### 1.1  AccountClosure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An account holder can request the bank to close the account at any point of time. The bank verifies the activities in the account before initiating the closure process.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.BLOCK.CLOSURE`, `AC.PENDING`, `AC.PRE.CLOSURE.DETAILS`, `ACCOUNT`, `ACCOUNT.CLOSURE`, `ACCOUNT.CLOSURE.PARAM`, `ACCT.ACTIVITY`, `FUNDS.TRANSFER` ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An account holder can request the bank to close the account at any point of time. The bank verifies the activities in the account before initiating the closure process.

An account is not closed in Temenos Transact , if it meets any of the following criteria:

- Part of a SEC.ACC.MASTER
- Direct Debit
- If it is a liquidation account
- Interest compensation account
- Charge account
- All-In-One account
- Part of a sweep account
- Part of a cash pool
- Not in current company
- Part of collateral
- Unauthorised AC.PENDING exists
- Blocked using AC.BLOCK.CLOSURE
- If the account is in suspense


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the system usage for closing the account in Temenos Transact .


##### Simulation of Account Closure

The account closure can be simulated through the AC.PRE.CLOSURE.DETAILS application. When this application is verified (V-function), the system calculates the settlement amounts, produce a list of errors or override messages that prevents an account from being closed by the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE application.

In order to simulate the account closure before actually marking the account for closure, select the Account Closure menu item and give the account number that has to be closed.

Click on the icon highlighted below to initiate the simulation through the AC.PRE.CLOSURE.DETAILS application.

Once the AC.PRE.CLOSURE.DETAILS is verified the details are displayed as shown in the below screen shot.

The simulation enables the bank user to decide upon the action (if any) to be taken by the account holder or the bank, for a hurdle-free account closure.


##### Account Closure – During COB or Online

The ACCOUNT.CLOSURE application is used to close accounts in online or during the Close of Business (COB). The account number is used as the record ID and the system calculates the outstanding interest, premium interest and charges. The capitalisation date, settlement account and posting restriction placed on the ACCOUNT record can be amended.

Interest and charges are calculated on the value dated balances and on the account activity statistics stored in the ACCT.ACTIVITY table, taking into account all entries over the account up to and including the last end of day processing. When an account is flagged for closure, any entries in the account has an override.

During end-of-day processing on the following working day, if both the Open Actual Bal and Open Cleared Bal fields are zero, the account is closed. If the account must be closed online, the Closed Online field is set to Y in the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE application.

In addition to this, the user must decide which of the following applications must be used for the settlement of balances in the account, in the CLOSE.MODE field:

- FUNDS.TRANSFER (FT)
- TELLER
- ACCOUNT.CLOSURE
- PAYMENT

If FUNDS.TRANSFER is used after the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE record is input, then the system automatically raises an FT record and place it on hold. The ID of the FT is stored in the Ft Id field. Once the FT is authorised, both the Open Actual Bal and Open Cleared Bal fields are zero. Then the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE record is authorised, and the account is closed and moved to history.

If TELLER is specified in the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE record, the system raises a TELLER.DEFAULT record and the ID is the ACCOUNT number. This record holds information that is used in the TELLER transaction and passes the entries. The user is required to input a TELLER record. The ID of the TELLER.DEFAULT record is populated in the Our Reference field in the TELLER application (once the TELLER.DEFAULT record has been processed, it cannot be reused) then this populates the transaction with the details from ACCOUNT.CLOSURE . Once the TELLER is authorised, both the Open Actual Bal and Open Cleared Bal fields are zero. Then the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE record is authorised, and the account is closed and moved to history.

The below screen shot is a sample of ACCOUNT.CLOSURE record for closure during COB.


##### Account Closure Parameter

The ACCOUNT.CLOSURE.PARAM application defines additional checks for the account closure simulation and account closure process.

- Definition is done at three levels. System Company Category (category can also be specific to a company)
- Applications can be defined which are to be checked during account closure request and simulation.
- Local applications that are to be checked can also be defined.
- Local API for checking the local application can be attached.

If the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE.PARAM is defined, the application level checks as defined in the parameter table are performed in addition to the core checks. This is done for account closure online as well as during COB.

The LIMIT application is enabled for the additional check and a provision is given to define other applications that are to be checked during the closure process. When an account which is attached to a LIMIT is marked for closure, an override is triggered stating that the account is linked to limit along with the limit product that is impacted. The below screen shot shows the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE.PARAM application.

The below screen shots show the ACCOUNT linked to LIMIT and the override raised after additional check on LIMIT application during the online account closure.


##### Account Closure and Payment Order

The Po Product Type Ac and Po Product Type Bc fields in the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE.PARAM application defines the payment order product that is used during account closure.

The Po Product Type Ac field indicates that the settlement happens between accounts held within the bank, whereas the Po Product Type Bc indicates that the settlement account is maintained external to the bank. In case of external settlement, the Pay Through Beneficiary field is set to Yes in the respective product for the payment order to be processed.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Account and Deposit Processes (Retail)

Account Closure feature allows the user to perform the closure of an account. When performing an account closure, all the overrides and errors are displayed, so that the user can do the necessary corrections in the respective applications and then proceed to do the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE .


##### Workflow

This section helps the user to perform the below tasks:

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
|  | Account Closure . |
| Account Closure | Enter or select the required values in the fields available and click FIND icon. Click the Simulate Pre-Closure icon. The system opens the account record to be simulated for pre-closure. |
| Ac Pre Closure Details Input | Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon to submit the record. Click the Verify icon to check the interest accrual as on date and updated online balance. |


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Account Closure feature.

#### 📖 Introduction

Accounts can be classified as customer accounts and internal accounts. Customer accounts belong to external customers, who have an arrangement with the bank to transact financial business. The customer accounts can be individual or corporate account. The servicing and maintenance of the accounts varies based on the nature of the account. Hence, the accounts are grouped by the bank in a logical manner to achieve operational efficiency. It is possible to retrieve the account using the alternate account ID (based on the legacy system or International Bank Account Number (IBAN)) and mnemonic codes.

Other than individual and corporate customer accounts, there are nostro and vostro accounts to transact payments with other banks and financial institutions. Internal accounts are created for bank’s own internal purpose. These accounts are not customer based. The bank needs internal accounts for cash management, capturing their fixed and movable assets, capital accounts (includes owner’s equity, statutory or other reserves retained earnings), provision accounts and so on.

> **⚠️ Note:** Interest and charges are not applicable for internal accounts.

Multi GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) accounts are internal accounts required for performing multiple financial reporting like:

- International Accounting Standards (IAS)
- International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)

Specific setup is required for distinguishing these accounts and their entries from the other reporting systems. Contingent accounts are sometimes required to maintain the balance information pertaining to off-balance sheet items, also referred as contingent items. Some banks have the practice to calculate and apply interest or charge on the utilised or unutilised portion of the contingent item. This facility is available for both customer and internal accounts.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The strength of Temenos Transact lies in the flexibility in which new account types can be created in order to meet the bank’s ongoing requirements. Once Temenos Transact is installed, part of the implementation process is to configure the types of accounts the bank wishes to offer and their characteristics. Typically, this includes:

- Debit or credit interest conditions.
- Interest and charges capitalisation frequencies.
- Statement production cycle.
- Other account group conditions.

Once these key files are setup, the creation of a new customer account is very simple.


##### Customer Accounts

Follow the below steps to create or open a customer account:

1. The individual or corporate must be registered as a CUSTOMER of the bank. Temenos Transact is a customer orientated system. An account is connected to a CUSTOMER record and thus the owner and address details are not entered on the individual account.
2. The account must have an operating CURRENCY in which the balance is maintained.
3. The account is mapped to the appropriate banking product like: Savings Account (resident or non-resident) Current Account (simple or overdraft) Privilege Account (gold or silver)

This mapping is done through the CATEGORY and ACCT.GEN.CONDITION (grouping condition table).

For creating a basic customer account, the fields in CUSTOMER , CURRENCY and CATEGORY are mandatory. These are validated against the respective applications in Temenos Transact . Other than these fields, certain add-on fields are used to capture other relevant details pertaining to the account like:

- Mode of operation.
- Alternate account number.
- Interest liquidation mode.
- Event alert requirements.
- Mandates.

An individual customer account is owned and operated in a single name or joint name. In case of joint account, each of the joint account holders must be registered as a customer of the bank. The relationship of main customer with the joint customer must be mentioned along with the documentary information (if any) about the joint holder. Signatures of the joint holder must be captured for verification. The joint holder relationship is one of the pre-defined values in the RELATION application in Temenos Transact .

Mnemonic is an alternate name for an account. The account can be referenced using the mnemonic across any Temenos Transact applications, where the account number has to be used. The user can type the mnemonic and the system automatically fetches the corresponding account number while validating the application.

There is another concept similar to mnemonic. It is the alternate account number. In practice, where Temenos Transact has replaced an existing system, the system allows the access to customer accounts using the old account numbers for a short-term. Alternate account number feature was enabled to support this functionality. Later, this feature was extended to generate International Bank Account Number (IBAN) numbers when a new account is created. So, different alternate account numbers can be created for different purposes.

The nature and type of alternate account numbers are configured before the account is created. The parameters and applications related to alternate account number are as follows:

The structure of alternate account is defined and validated in this parameter application. It contains the following information:

- Account number type
- Check digit validation
- Minimum and maximum length of the alternate number
- Display mask

If the bank wants to allow the users to reference the Temenos Transact accounts using the alternate account numbers, the Alternate Acc Ids field is set to Y and the applicable alternate account ID formats (defined in ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER ) must be included in the Alternate ID field.

After configuring the ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER and ACCOUNT.PARAMETER applications, the user is allowed to capture the alternate account ID while creating an account. The alternate account type is defaulted from the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application in the Alt Acct Type field. The user can capture the alternate account number, either manually or through an API using the Alt Acct Id field.

In the preceding screenshot, the user manually captures the alternate account ID for type LEGACY; whereas for type T24.IBAN, the system automatically generates the alternate account ID through an API that is linked.

This is an index application which stores the T Temenos Transact account number for the alternate account number. This is used for faster retrieval of the Temenos Transact account number when the alternate account number is used to refer other Temenos Transact applications.

The standard maximum length of account number is 16 digits. However, length of some of the alternate account types like IBAN is more than 16 digits. The EB.OBJECT application is configured to enable the extended alternate account number. For the ACCOUNT record in EB.OBJECT , the Max Length field can be defined with a value greater than 16 digits.

For example, if the user defines the Max Length field in EB.OBJECT as 36 characters, the Alt Acct Type in ALT.ACCT. PARAMETER can be defined with the Max Length field upto 36 characters.

The customer can instruct the bank to use one of his other accounts or group account for liquidating the interest and booking the charges, if any. Temenos Transact allows to define the interest liquidation account in any currency other than the account currency. The customer of the interest liquidation account can be different from that of the account customer. The customer can also specify which type of interest (CR/CR1/CR2/DR/DR1/DR2) they want to liquidate through the interest liquidation account. Some customers may opt to route the interest on their joint account to their savings account, while some customers may opt to route the interest on their account to their spouse’s account or kid’s account. The corporate current account holders may opt to route the interest to their funding account. Similarly, the account to which the charges are booked can also be different but the currency of the charge account must be the same as this account. The interest liquidation and charge liquidation accounts can be defined in the Int Liqu Type , Int Liqu Acct and Charge Account fields. The Int Liq Ccy is defaulted to the currency of account in Int Liqu Acct field.

There can be a requirement for the customer in an account record to be modified with that of another customer. For example, in case of death of the primary customer in an account record with the joint holder, Temenos Transact allows the modification of the main customer ID for an account record with Joint Holder ID to any one of the existing Joint Holder ID in the account record.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not allow modification of the main customer if there are limits linked to the customer.

Modification of the main customer is validated against the CATEGORY range as defined in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application in the SYSTEM record. The following screenshot shows the example setup of CATEGORY range in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER .

> **⚠️ Note:** Modification of the main customer ID for an ACCOUNT record with a single holder is allowed only for nostro accounts, even if the nostro CATEGORY range is specified in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application.

The customer can subscribe or unsubscribe for alerts, through SMS or e-mail or secure messages, for one or more events. The event may be pre-determined (like account getting overdrawn or customer address change) or time based (like, a loan maturing in nn days or repayment scheduled in nn days). The events can be initiated by the user or the system. The alerts can be activity alerts, transaction alerts, balance alerts, transfer alerts or portfolio alerts.

The individual or corporate customer can issue mandates mentioning the details of the authorised signatories and their signing powers to approve transactions in specific currency and amount on behalf of the customer. This is recorded in EB.MANDATE application. Each of the authorised signatory must be registered as a customer in Temenos Transact and must be linked to the EB.SIGNATORY.GROUP with the details of currency and amount upto which they have the signing powers.


##### Internal Accounts

Internal accounts can be opened manually or automatically. For certain types of internal accounts (like cash accounts, suspense accounts, inter-company accounts and AL currency position accounts), where the category is parameterised in the respective application, the system generates the accounts automatically.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is recommended to create the internal accounts manually for the local currency accounts, based on which the system can automatically open any foreign currency account, as required. The accounts have to be manually created for the non-parameterised internal account categories like fixed or movable assets account.

The internal accounts are not customer based accounts and hence is not linked to any customer. The currency and category are defaulted from the ID of the account. For example, if the ID of the internal account is EUR1122100010001, the Currency field is defaulted to EUR and Category field is defaulted to 11221. Customer is not updated for internal accounts so it is mandatory to define the following fields while creating the account.

- Account Title
- Short Name
- Mnemonic
- Account Officer

The automatically created internal account has the text RECORD.AUTOMATICALLY.OPENED set in the Account Title.1, Account Title.2 and Short Title fields. These can be amended later by the bank users. As the internal accounts are created and maintained for bank’s internal operations, the interest and charge conditions do not apply to them. Some internal accounts are used for special processing like inter-branch or inter-company accounts, position accounts and multi-GAAP accounts.

These accounts are used as parking accounts to perform the financial transactions on accounts belonging to a different branch or company. In this setup, each branch holds an inter-branch account with the other branch or branches or one branch is identified as the inter-company routing branch through which all the inter-branch transactions are routed. The routing branch details are defined in INTERCO.PARAMETER application. The format of the internal account differs according to the company setup.

In the case of multi-branch or multi-book setup, the format of inter-branch account is CCYCCCCCNNNNBBBB, where:

- CCY is the swift currency code of the account, for example EUR, USD.
- CCCCC is a category code defined in the INTERCO record of ACCOUNT.CLASS application.
- NNNN is sub division code (defined in the COMPANY application) of the other branch in the transaction.
- BBBB is the sub division code (defined in the COMPANY application) of the branch.

The transaction is done in Branch A (sub division code 0004) for an account belonging to Branch B (sub division code 0008). The ID of the inter-branch account is USD1280000080004 for Branch A and USD1280000040008 for Branch B.

In the case of multi-company setup, the format of inter-company account is – CCYCCCCCNNNN, where:

- CCY is the swift currency code of the account, for example EUR, USD.
- CCCCC is a category code is defined in the INTERCO record of ACCOUNT.CLASS application.
- NNNN is the sub division code (defined in the COMPANY application) of the other company in the transaction.

The sub division code of Company A is 0002 and Company B is 0003. The format of inter-company account for Company B in Company A is USD128000003 and for Company A in Company B is USD128000002.

Banks can opt to capture the currency position movements for reporting purposes. This is done through the Position Entry field in the CONSOLIDATE.COND application. If this field is set to ACCOUNT , the currency position movements are captured in the internal accounts based on the category defined for this purpose in the EB.POSITION.PARAMETER application.

In case of multi-book or multi-company setup, the format of currency position internal account is CCYCCYCCCCCDDSSBBBB, where:

- The first CCY is the currency code of the account.
- The second CCY is the other currency of the position relationship.
- CCCCC is a category code in the range 10000–19999.
- DD is the Dealer Desk (default value is 00, captured from the EB.POSITION.PARAMETER application) for which the accounts are maintained.
- SS is a sequential number that allows access to sub account processing, if required
- BBBB is the sub division code of the company the account belongs to.

> **⚠️ Note:** For CCYCCY, if the local currency is USD and there is a transaction in EUR, then two accounts need to be updated (EURUSD and USDEUR). The EURUSD account is the EUR account with the amount based on the sign of EUR in the transaction that updates the position. The USDEUR account is a local currency account with the opposite sign to that of the EUR.

If the ID is EURUSD1902201030001, then:

- EUR is the currency code of the account.
- USD is the position relationship currency.
- 19022 is the category code.
- 01 is Dealer Desk
- 03 is the sequential number
- 0001 is the Sub Division Code of the company

In a single company setup, the format of currency position account number is CCYCCYCCCCCDDSS, where:

- The first CCY is the currency code of the account.
- The second CCY is the other currency of the position relationship.
- CCCCC is a category code in the range 10000 – 19999.
- DD is the Dealer Desk (default value is 00, captured from the EB.POSITION.PARAMETER application) for which the accounts are maintained
- SS is a sequential number, which allows access to sub account processing.

If the ID is EURUSD190220103, then:

- EUR is the currency code of the account
- USD is the position relationship currency
- 19022 is the category code
- 01 is Dealer Desk
- 03 is the sequential number

To setup multiple financial reporting in Temenos Transact , internal accounts are required. For example, IAS, IFRS or other forms of local reporting. To distinguish these accounts and their entries from other reporting systems, they must be setup with the appropriate Position Type (in the CATEGORY application) to match the reporting system defined in the FX.POS.TYPE application. The used for the internal account must have the correct Position Type value to match the reporting system.


##### Nostro Accounts

The key of nostro accounts is similar to customer account. It is the shadow or mirror account of the vostro account maintained by the correspondent bank. So, the nostro Account is opened with the correspondent bank as the customer. For validating the nostro accounts, the NOSTRO record in ACCOUNT.CLASS application should be updated with the Category (marked for nostro accounts) and Sector (pertaining to corresponding banks).

The nostro account is identified based on the Category and Limit Reference field in the Account application. The system defaults the Limit R eference field as NOSTRO, based on the setup in ACCOUNT.CLASS . These accounts are marked for reconciliation. The statements and advices to these accounts are re-directed to the nostro reconciliation department for reconciliation purposes.

The following screenshot shows a sample nostro account.


##### Contingent Accounts

Banks, in certain cases, may have to maintain the balances of the off-balance sheet or contingent items for reporting purpose. To facilitate this, contingent accounts are created. These accounts are created for customer accounts or internal accounts. For example, contingent customer accounts are created for guarantees held. Posting to these accounts is done through the DATA.CAPTURE or FUNDS.TRANSFER applications of Temenos Transact . The category range for contingent accounts is defined in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application as shown in the following screenshot.

The customer contingent accounts are also used to capture the unutilised or utilised amount of the sanctioned limit on which the interest and charges are applied. The LIMIT record is monitored for changes and the unutilised or utilised amount is updated to the contingent account as and when the amount changes. Accounting entries are raised to show the movements from or to the contingent accounts. Internal contingent accounts are used to offset or balance the accounting entry movements to the customer contingent accounts.

The Contingent Int field is mandatory for setting up the contingent Account. This field denotes how the interest on the contingent account is treated in Temenos Transact . The following are the possible values in this field.

| Possible Values | Description |
|---|---|
| B | Indicates non-contingent interest to be reported in balance sheet. The interest and charge liquidation account needs to be a non-contingent account, in order to report the interest or charge as a balance sheet item. |
| C | Indicates contingent interest, which must not appear on the Balance Sheet. The interest or charge liquidation accounts can also be contingent accounts. |
| O | Indicates non-contingent interest but reported as an off balance sheet item. |
| I | Indicates an internal contingent account, which is used to counterbalance contingent accounts. This must not appear on the balance sheet |

The Procs Limit Sweep field in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application must be set to Y to enable the sweeping of unutilised or utilised limit amount into a contingent account. The Allow Unutil Cr field in the LIMIT.PARAMETER determines whether the unutilised portion of a partially utilised limit can be transferred to the contingent account. The Default Max Total field determines whether, the INTERNAL.AMOUNT or the ADVISED.AMOUNT of the limit is to be used for the calculation of unutilised limit amount.

The contingent account to which the sweeping of unutilised or utilised limit amount is specified in the Unutil Acct or Util Account fields in the LIMIT application. The current unutilised or utilised amounts are considered based on these fields. There is an option to override the LIMIT.PARAMETER application based on the setting of whether credits to the contingent account should occur when the unutilised amount is reduced. The following screenshot shows an individual LIMIT settings for contingent accounts.

The contingent accounts are updated at the end of day. The accounts can also be updated through the DATA.CAPTURE and FUNDS.TRANSFER applications. Funds transfer is possible only when both the accounts are non-contingent accounts or when both accounts are contingent. Similarly, in DATE.CAPTURE , the entire batch must be of the same type.

#### 📖 Introduction

The bank may impose charges for maintaining and servicing the accounts. These charges may be classified broadly as interest based charges and ledger fee or transaction based charges. These charges may be applied monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With


##### Calculating Account Interest

- Group specific interest and charges are configured using GROUP.DEBIT.INT (GDI) and GROUP.CREDIT.INT (GCI) applications.
- Account specific interest and charges are configured using ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT (ADI) and ACCOUNT.CREDIT.INT (ACI) applications.

These interest related applications support the following features:

- Defines fixed or floating interest rate. Floating interest rate refers to BASIC.RATE.TEXT and BASIC.INTEREST application to get the rates. The float or margin can be added or subtracted from the basic interest rate to give the applicable floating rate.
- Defines two levels of interest rates (referred in Temenos Transact as DR and DR2 for debit interest or CR and CR2 for credit interest) and different interest capitalisation cycle for each of these.
- Defines different interest day basis for calculating interest depending on the methods followed for calculating the number of days and days in a year. Example Interest Basis A 360/360 denotes that for interest calculation purpose, the number of days in a month is considered as 30 and number of days in a year is considered as 360. Validation Rules Interest Basis A 360/360 B 366/360 C 366/366 D 360/366 E 366/365 F 360/365 NONE No interest is applicable GENERAL Applicable only to ADI or ACI , where it is used to refer or restore the interest condition defined for the group in GDI or GCI .
- Tax on interest can be linked through the respective GDI or GCI or ADI or ACI applications.


##### Configuring Negative Interest

The negative interest rate and negative margin are defined in BASIC.INTEREST application. This is used mainly in MONEY MARKET (MM), SWAP (SW) and DERIVATIVE (DX) applications. This can be applied to any kind of account by linking the BASIC.INTEREST application and appropriate configuration of the Negative Rates field in the GDI or GCI or ADI or ACI applications.

The following options are available in the Negative Rates field.

- Blank or No – Indicates that negative rates cannot be input and if a rate becomes negative as a result of the application of a margin, then the rate is set to zero.
- Yes – Indicates that negative rates can be input and if the application margin makes the rate more negative, then the more negative rate is used.
- BLOCK.MARGIN – Indicates that negative rates can be used but the following conditions apply: If the rate is positive and the margin makes the rate negative, then the rate is set to zero. If the rate is negative and the margin makes the rate more negative, the margin is ignored and the original negative rate is used. If the total debit interest on capitalisation is a debit to the customer, then AC.PENDING application is updated. If the total debit interest on capitalisation is a credit to the customer, then the interest is posted directly to the customer account. If correction takes place for a debit interest which results in a credit to the customer account with an AC.PENDING record, then AC.PENDING record is updated with the negative amount and the interest pending processing then does the correct interest posting based on the dates defined.


##### Understanding Interest Compensation Account

Interest can be calculated and applied based on the balances of several accounts. These accounts are identified using the main account, whose number is defined in the Interest Comp Acct field in each of the account other than the main account. All the accounts involved must be in the same currency or the same fixed currency group. The group or account interest conditions pertaining to the main account is applicable on the consolidated balance. The main account referred to in this field must not be a sub-account of another group of accounts to be combined for interest purposes.


##### Interest Rounding Rules

The rounding rules indicate the type of rounding applicable to the individual interest calculation. Separate rounding rules can be defined for debit and credit interest using the ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION application.

Temenos Transact supports various types of account interest calculations:

- Natural rounding – Rounding to the nearest unit as defined in the CURRENCY record is performed for system calculated value.
- Round up – Rounding up to the nearest decimal place as defined in the CURRENCY record is performed for system calculated value.
- Rounding down – Rounded to the nearest decimal place as defined in the CURRENCY record is performed for system calculated value.
- Ryoha Kataha – This rounding method is for the Japanese market.

Read Account Interest Rounding for more information on interest rounding rules.


##### Re-calculating Interest

Interest rates need to be modified based on the market conditions and regulations from the Central Bank, with retrospective effect.

Temenos Transact has the facility to re-calculate the interest automatically and apply the interest corrections with value dates prior to the last interest processing dates.

- When previously calculated interest is recalculated, the old values are stored in CORR.ACCT.CR , CORR.ACCT.DR , CORR.ACCT.CR2 or CORR.ACCT.DR2 tables as appropriate.
- The re-calculated interest information is stored in STMT.ACCT.CR , STMT.ACCT.DR , STMT.ACCT.CR2 or STMT.ACCT.DR2 tables as appropriate.
- Necessary accounting entries are processed for the difference amount of interest.
- The TABLE.CAPITALIS.CORR application is used for requesting the recalculation and interest correction.
- Interest correction can be requested for specific accounts or a group of accounts. In each case, the date from which the interest re-calculation should take place must be defined.
- Correction entries are generated with the correct value date for each of the interest period and is taken into account on the recalculation of subsequent periods.


##### Understanding General Charge

Interest related charges include add-on interest charges, government margin and interest statement charges. These charges are applied on the Debit1 interest capitalisation date. The transaction based charges include:

- Balance requirement
- Number of credits
- Number of debits
- Turnover of credits
- Turnover of debits
- Non-immediate transaction charges based on the transaction codes

The following table explains the various interest and transaction based charges and the details of configuration.

| Field Name | Details | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| Debit Int Addon | This is an add-on charge levied on the overdraft (OD) interest on the interest capitalisation date. Either this or highest debit charge can be taken on the OD interest but not both | Configured in DEBIT.INT.ADDON application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Government Margin | This is a supplementary charge on debit balances calculated by the system on debit interest capitalisation date and collected on behalf of the Government | Defined in GOVERNMENT.MARGIN application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Highest Debit | This is a charge calculated on the highest debit balance during each capitalisation period | Defined in HIGHEST.DEBIT application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Interest Statement | Some customers require a detailed interest statement each time interest is applied. The interest statement charge is a fixed amount which may be applied each time debit interest is applied | Defined in INTEREST.STATEMENT application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Int Chg Bal Type; Int Chg Def Bal; Int Chg Ccy; Int Chg Bal | These fields are used to specify a balance for waiving Debit Interest Addon , Highest Debit and Interest Statement Charges fields If the balance is based on minimum or average balance for the interest period as defined in Int Chg Bal Type field If this balance is greater than the Int Chg Bal or Int Chg Def Bal , the above mentioned charges will be waived |  |
| Calcul Step Period | Specifies whether charges in Bal Requirement , Number Of Credit , Number Of Debit , Turnover Credit , Turnover Debit , Highest Debit Chg and Statement Charge should be calculated once to cover the full charge period, as specified in the COMPANY record, or in MONTHLY steps If MONTHLY is specified, free, minimum and maximum amounts apply to charges calculated for each month, otherwise the free, minimum and maximum amounts are only applied to the total charges for the period |  |
| Bal Requirement | Maintenance charge depending on the balance in the account | Defined in BALANCE.REQUIREMENT application |
| Number Of Credit; Number Of Debit; Turnover Debit; Turnover Credit | Transaction charges can be levied either based on the number of debit or credit transactions or the turnover value of the debit or credit transactions | The charge is defined in NUMBER.OF.CREDIT , NUMBER.OF.DEBIT , TURNOVER.DEBIT , TURNOVER.CREDIT applications respectively |
| Statement Charge | Determines the charges for the issuing account statements | Defined in ACCT.STATEMENT.CHARGE application |
| Trans Code Charge; Comb Trns Chrg Cde | One or more transactions in the TRANSACTION application can be made chargeable by defining a TRANSACTION.CHARGE in the TRANSACTION application and is applied using these fields | Defined in the TRANSACTION application |

The Comb Debit Credit field in the GENERAL.CHARGE application defines if the debit and credit entries specified in the following applications should be calculated separately or combined.

- NUMBER.OF.CREDIT and NUMBER.OF.DEBIT
- TURNOVER.CREDIT and TURNOVER.DEBIT

If set to No, the debit and credit charges are calculated separately, otherwise a combined charge is calculated using the credit charge details specified in NUMBER.OF.CREDIT or TURNOVER.CREDIT . An entry is chargeable if the transaction code in the TRANSACTION application contains Y in the Turnover Charge field. Reversal entries are not considered for this.

Notional credit interest for offsetting charges can be calculated using the credit balances during the application period. The balance type (average or minimum) is specified in Offset Bal Type field and the percentage rate is specified in Perct For Offset field. This can be offset against the charges specified in the following fields:

- Bal Requirement
- Number Of Credit
- Number Of Debit
- Turnover Credit
- Turnover Debit
- Statement Charge

It is also possible to define specific required balance for waiving the charges. The default balance requirement for waiving charges can be defined using the following fields:

- Default Min Av Bal
- Default Day Basis
- Def Bal No Offset
- Def Low Amt Charge

Currency specific balance for waiving charges can be defined using following fields:

- Offset Currency
- Min Av Bal
- Day Basis
- Bal No Credit
- Low Amt Charge

The average or minimum balance for the application period is calculated based on the Offset Bal Type field and if the result is not less than the Default Min Av Bal field , then all charges specified in following fields are waived:

- Bal Requirement
- Number Of Credit
- Number Of Debit
- Turnover Credit
- Turnover Debit
- Statement Charge

It is possible to define account maintenance charges and commissions through FT.COMMISSION.TYPE application and linking it to the appropriate GENERAL.CHARGE . This enables the definition of minimum and maximum charge either as absolute amount or percentage of transaction amount.

These charges may be applied monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually as specified in the COMPANY record. The GENERAL.CHARGE application defines the account maintenance and servicing charges by linking the applicable charges in Temenos Transact . The ID format is - .

The ID of is

1.20170316 as shown in the below screenshot.

The charge conditions are linked to the group(s) of accounts through the respective GROUP.DEBIT.INT (GDI) application or to the specific account through ACCOUNT.DEBIT. INT (ADI) application.


##### Understanding Independent or Adhoc Charges

The AC.CHARGE.REQUEST application is used as an inter-bank facility for requesting or advising many types of charges from other financial institutions. This application also generate the charges as independent transactions either to request payment of charges, interest and/or other expenses or to advise of a debit/credit to the account owners’ account. It posts the accounting entries and/or generates MTn90 or MTn91 SWIFT messages where appropriate. The four options available in this application are:

- ADVICE – This raises an MTn90 advising a customer of a charge, interest or adjustment, already debited from their account. No accounting entries are produced from this transaction.
- BOOK – This raises accounting entries when payment of an unknown charge is received.
- CHARGE – This can raise both accounting entries and SWIFTMTn90/MTn91.
- REQUEST – This raises an MTn91 requesting charges, interest or other expenses from another financial institution, which were previously unknown to them. No accounting entries are produced from this transaction.

The Status field should be set to PAID, if accounting entries are required to be generated. The options available in this field are:

- PAID – Triggers accounting entries to be raised.
- TAKEN – Account entries for the charge have been raised through another application.
- UNPAID – Awaiting payment.
- W/O – If the charge request is refused.

When the Status field is set to UNPAID, the transaction stays in the live file indefinitely. All the other status will move the transaction to the history file during the Close of Business (COB) process.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Account Interest and Charges feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Interest and charges are accrued, amortised and capitalised at regular intervals. These are charged to the bank’s customer account in case of income and paid to bank’s customer account in case of expense.

#### 📖 Introduction

A client account may be granted with a credit limit. This is mostly the case with current accounts where the bank provides the facility to overdraw the current account balance to the extent of the credit limit granted to the account. An override is generated whenever the account balance is overdrawn beyond the sanctioned limit. The limit facility is linked to the account through the Limit Ref field. Limit check is carried out for every transaction that impacts the account during online and COB processing. Limit is not applicable for nostro and internal accounts. The Limit Ref field is updated as NOSTRO, indicating it as nostro account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the system usage of the account limits feature.


##### Using Single Limit

The credit limit facility can be linked to one or many accounts of the customer. This is set in the Single Limit field in the Account. If an account is linked to a limit and the Single Limit field is set to Yes, the same limit cannot be linked to any other account of the customer. If the Single Limit field is set as No, the same limit can be linked to multiple accounts of the same customer. The default value for Single Limit field is defined at a group level in the ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION application. However, this can be overridden at the account level.

For certain types of limit products, it is possible to net credit account balances and debit account balances (the usual practice is to only include debit balances for limit checking). If an account with a credit balance is to be included in the limit checking, the Allow Netting field must be set to Yes in both LIMIT and ACCOUNT applications.


##### Credit Checking

A credit check is made whenever a debit transaction is validated and authorised at the same time. An option is available to set credit checking for an account against working balance and cash flows or available balance through the Credit Check field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER . The following are the options available in this field.

| Field Value | Description |
|---|---|
| Null or Working | The update of available funds ignores unauthorised credits. Overdraft checks use only working balance. Future cash flow check uses the available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date of the transaction. |
| Forward | Same as above, except that overdraft uses the value in the Working Bal field (in the ACCOUNT ) plus current bank day forward movements. |
| Available | The update of available funds uses the Available Bal Upd field (in the ACCOUNT ) to decide how the available balance is to be updated. There is no overdraft check. Future cash flow check uses available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date. |
| Availwork | The update of the available funds uses Available Bal Upd field (in the ACCOUNT ). The overdraft check uses Working Bal field (in the ACCOUNT ) only. Future cash flow checks use available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date. |
| Availfwd | The update of available funds uses Available Bal Upd field (in the ACCOUNT ). The overdraft check uses Working Bal field (in the ACCOUNT ) plus today's forward movements. Future cash flow check uses available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date. |
| Blank | If this field is left blank the Working option is applied. |

The Credit Check field is also available in the ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION and ACCOUNT application in the following order:

- ACCOUNT – The flag set here always takes precedence over a flag set elsewhere.
- ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION (If ACCOUNT is blank).
- ACCOUNT.PARAMETER (If all of the above applications are not been set).

If this field is set to Available, then all credit checks are made against the available balances and working balance is ignored although the available funds movement are still populated to the account.

If an account is linked to a limit then a limit check takes place; otherwise an available balance check takes place. If an account is linked to a shared balance, then the system still considers the available balance, and the shared balances are not included. The Available Bal field used for credit checking is made up of the movements as defined by the Available Bal Upd field.


##### Using the Link to Limit or Overdraft facility

The Link To Limit field in the ACCOUNT application defines whether account particular limits are to be linked to the LIMIT application. If this field is set to Yes, the debit interest conditions for the account is set according to the current value of the allocated limit amount ( Online Limit ) for the lowest defined record in the limit structure. The agreed overdraft limit can be specified either as an ACCOUNT.DEBIT.LIMIT record in conjunction with the GROUP.DEBIT.INT record, or as the first band of the ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT record.

Where an ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT record is defined for the account, the first band of the Dr Int Rate field is set to the available amount in the end of day processing, effective from the date the limit value changes. Where it is not defined for the account, the LIMIT amount is set to the limit amount available, effective from the date the limit amount changes.

When the Link To Limit field is set to Yes initially, the system creates an ACCOUNT.DEBIT.LIMIT record for the system date based on the existing limit value, if ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT record is not defined for the account. This ACCOUNT.DEBIT.LIMIT application allows overdraft limits to be specified for individual accounts which can then be used as the limit for the first rate of debit interest specified in the appropriate GROUP.DEBIT.INT application. If a GROUP.DEBIT.INT record contains two rates, but no limit for the first rate, the overdraft limit specified for each account in this application is used as the limit for the first rate.

In this way, it is possible to specify a different limit for the first rate for each account, without specifying separate ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT records. If there is no limit specified in this application for a particular account, a limit of zero is assumed, and the second rate specified is effective for all balances.

> **⚠️ Note:** Using this facility, it is not possible to specify more than two rates in the GROUP.DEBIT.INT record.


##### Understanding Account Overdrawn

An account is overdrawn when:

- An account with no limit goes into overdraft
- An account with limit, where the limit goes into excess

The ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN application stores information about the overdraft details for the account or the limit, which include:

- Account officer
- Customer
- Currency
- Cleared balance Limit
- Actual balance total out
- Date the account was first overdrawn
- Date the last movement occurred on the account
- Overdrawn excess narrative
- Moved narrative

The application is updated during the Close of Business (COB) after the account or limit goes into excess.

The following set of fields contain information that is used during the overdraft ageing process for retail accounts, if configured in the property class for limit.

- Curr Od Status
- Curr Od Start Date
- Curr Od Days
- Overdrawn Amt
- Threshold Amt
- Od Fee Date

When the current overdraft is cleared or the balance is returned under the tolerance amount, the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN record is written to the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.HIST table.

The following example shows an account overdrawn record, where the account is subject to overdraft ageing. This account went overdrawn on the 22 April and the current overdraft status is OD1. An overdraft fee was taken when the account went into excess.

If the account remains in overdraft, it progresses through the aging status depending on the configuration. The following screenshot shows that the account remains in overdraft. The overdraft status is updated along with the date when it changed.

This internal table is used to record the following overdraft ageing details for accounts:

- Year
- Number of overdrafts in the period
- Total number of days in overdraft, in the period
- For a specific period of overdraft: The number of days, the account was in overdraft The start date of the overdraft The end date of the overdraft ID to the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.HIST record

This table can be used to query on the accounts overdrawn history details.

Temenos Transact limit structure caters to multi-customer limits, the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.CUST table is created and updated to maintain the overdrawn or limit excess information at each individual customer level that is part of the limit structure.

Each record holds one multi-value field containing the limit IDs and account IDs present in existing ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN table for the given customer.

All the details for each exceeded limit and overdrawn account already present in the existing ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN table are mapped directly from this table and used to build a report with the overall view of a customer’s exceeded limit(s) and overdrawn account(s). Each customer has only one record in this table.

Similar to ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN , this table also gets updated during Close of Business (COB).

Consider limit LI1710705030 with customer 190200 and 190201, and we utilise it by creating an arrangement for user 190200 which exceeds the limit’s secured amount, the system includes the respective limit ID in the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.CUST table:

- Limit record – LI1710705030.
- Arrangement which fully utilises limit record’s (LI1710705030) secured amount of 40,000 and exceeds it by 5,000.

- Record ID 190200 is updated in ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.CUST table with limit LI1710705030.

- Information from ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN and ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.CUST tables is then consolidated in the Customer Exceeded Limits & Overdrawn Accounts enquiry in order to display all the exceeded limits and overdrawn accounts of a customer.


##### Accounts Ageing based on Ledger Balance

The ageing of the overdrawn balance in the overdraft account can be monitored and reported from the day the ledger balance of the account moves to negative. This means that the ageing of the overdraft account is monitored not from the time it exceeds the overdraft limit facility but from the time the ledger balance of the account moves to negative.

The ageing days for the overdraft account is calculated based on the configuration of the Ac Overdrawn Bal field in the AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM application, as shown in the screenshot below.

The allowed values in the Ac Overdrawn Bal field are:

- Actual.balance – Indicates monitoring of the overdrawn balance is based on the booked or ledger balance of the account. The overdraft limit is not considered when calculating the ageing days.
- No or Null – Indicates monitoring of the overdrawn balance is based on the cleared outstanding balance for accounts not linked to an overdraft limit. For those accounts linked to overdraft limits, ageing begins from the day the overdraft limit is utilised in excess.

> **⚠️ Note:** The values in this field can be modified from No or Null to Actual.balance, but not vice versa.

To monitor the ageing of overdrawn balances based on the ledger balance,

1. Set the Ac Overdrawn Bal field as Actual.balance in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM , to allow the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN table to be updated when the ledger balance of the overdraft account is overdrawn.
2. During the close of business process, the system creates and updates the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN table with the ageing details, the overdrawn ledger balance, and ageing status. The ID of the record in this table is the respective account number that is overdrawn.
3. The Account Officer monitors the ageing of the overdrawn balance in the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN table for the respective account.
4. Configure a tolerance time period for AR accounts to allow the ledger balance to go below zero without being monitored for overdrawn ageing. Overdrawn ageing can be computed even at this stage, and after the tolerance days are exceeded, the details are stored in ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN .
5. The overdrawn status, as defined for various account products, is updated in the ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN table for the respective account based on the overdrawn ageing of the account.
6. When the ledger balance of the account moves from negative to positive, the overdrawn ageing details are moved to ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN.HIST . If the balance moves to negative again, the system recalculates the ageing.

Below is a sample scenario, where a record is created in ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN , based on the ledger balance of the account despite the account being linked to a limit.

- Set the Ac Overdrawn Bal field as Actual.balance in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM .
- The account 10012268002 has a ledger balance of zero and is linked to the limit.
- The screenshot below shows the available limit as USD 15000.
- Initiate a transfer of USD 3000 from this account, making the ledger balance in the account as USD 3000.
- As the ledger balance of the account is overdrawn, a record is created and monitored during the close of business in ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN with the overdrawn details.

Account Limits enquiry fetches the details of overdrawn accounts that are not covered by a credit limit and the accounts for which the credit limits are exceeded. This enquiry is based on information stored in ACCOUNT.OVERDRAWN application.

The details includes the amount of the overdraft or excess utilisation of limit, the date on when the account initially became overdrawn and last overdrawn or limit exceeded amount.

This enquiry helps the user to view the details of the overdrawn accounts and exceeded limits for the given customer Id. In addition, the user can view the limit transactions and overdrawn accounts in detail using drilldown options provided.

#### 📖 Introduction

The account becomes operational once it is created. Funds start moving to and from the accounts depending on the nature of the transaction. Every movement of fund impacts the balance in the account. Temenos Transact maintains the balances in different fields in the ACCOUNT application, denoting that they are updated at various stages for different purposes. Not only the balances but also the credit and debit movements are maintained for calculating interest and charges and for reporting purposes.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the system usage of the account maintenance feature.


##### Maintaining Account Balances

The following balances are held in ACCOUNT and EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES for the individual account, based on setup in the Retain Ac Balances field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER . If this field is set to No, the balances are maintained only in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table.

This field contains the actual non-cleared balance or ledger balance of the account at the start of the day.

This field contains the cleared balance of the account at the start of the day. This includes the value of all entries over the account except any credit entries or reversed debit entries with exposure dates in the future. For credit and reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future, this field is updated in the start of day processing on the appropriate date.

This field contains the most up to date actual balance of the account. This is the same as the actual balance at the start of day ( Open Actual Bal ) and the value of all fully authorised entries since the start of day.

This field contains the most up to date cleared balance of the account. This is the same as the cleared balance at the start of day ( Open Cleared Bal ) and the value of all fully authorised entries since the start of day excepting any credits or reversal debit entries with future exposure dates.

For credit and reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future, this field is updated at start of day processing on the appropriate date. For multiple future exposure dates and associated amounts, the Online Cleared Balance field is updated at the start of the day processing on the appropriate date. To capture multiple exposure dates, set the Split Exposure field to Yes in the FT.TXN. T YPE .CONDITION application.

This field contains the current balance of the account, which is used for checks done by the LIMIT application in the start of day. This balance is the same as the cleared balance (Online Cleared Bal).

For nostro and internal accounts, the field is updated by all accounting entries when they have been fully authorised. For other customer accounts, it is updated by debit entries when they are validated and by credit entries when they are fully authorised excluding any credit or reversal debit entries with Exposure Dates in the future. For credit and reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future, the Working Balance field is updated at the start of day processing on the appropriate date.

| Transaction | Booking Date | Txn Ref | Value Date | Txn Amount (In USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Transaction-1 | 21 Apr 2017 | FT17111CN2Z1 | 24 Apr 2017 | -2000 |
| Transaction-2 | 21 Apr 2017 | FT1711188QZF | 21 Apr 2017 | -1000 |
| Transaction-3 | 21 Apr 2017 | FT17111XRCLY | 21 Apr 2017 | -2000 |

All the transactional balances and movement data of an account are held in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table. The ACCOUNT record holds static information, like Customer , Currency , Category and so on, pertaining to the account. It is optional to maintain the balances in the respective Account record. The following information is inferred from the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table:

- The Account Balances - open (actual and cleared) or online (actual and cleared) or working balance.
- The current ( Curr Asset Type ) and previous ( Prev Asset Type ) asset type in which the account is reported in the General Ledger (GL).
- The break-up of balances ( Open Balance ) held in the various asset types ( Type Sysdate ) and movements (debit or credit) for the respective asset type.
- The Auth Pay Mvmt , Auth Receive Mvmt and Trade Dated GL B alance fields are used in Trade Dated General Ledger (TDGL) processing for reporting the payable and receivable movements and the resulting balance.
- Total unauthorised debit and credit movements along with the unauthorised transaction reference.
- Total unauthorised forward debit and credit movements along with the forward unauthorised transaction reference.
- Date and time on which the account balance and EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record was last updated.


##### Maintaining Trade Dated GL Balances

For future dated movements under the TDGL accounting treatment, the customer's balances are updated on the value date. However, the balance sheet and GL is updated on the trade date but under payable or receivable. These movements are recorded and a TDGL balance is also maintained in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table to show the effect of these movements:

- Auth Pay Mvmt – Holds the authorised future-dated movements under PAY.
- Auth Receive Mvmt – Holds the authorised future-dated movements under RECEIVE.
- Trade Dated G L Bal – Holds the sum of the following fields. Online Actual Bal Auth Pay Mvmt Auth Receive Mvmt

The following screenshot shows an example of the future-dated movements under PAY.

In a TDGL accounting setup, the account balances are not updated with the future dated movements until the value date. They are updated under PAY or RECEIVE movements till the value date. However, it is still possible to include these movements along with the account balance for credit checking.

The Tdgl Credit Check field in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application must be set to Yes to include the PAY and RECEIVE movements to the account balance for credit check purpose.

With this setup, the balance used for credit checking on the current balance (not on the future cash flows) includes the values from Auth Pay Mvmt and Auth Receive Mvmt fields. The Limit Summary/Customer Liability enquiry shows the account balance including the Auth.Pay.Mvmt and Auth.Receive.Mvmt .


##### Maintaining Activity Based Balances (ACCT.ACTIVITY)

ACCT.ACTIVITY is an internal table containing the details of account balances and activity used to calculate interest and charges. Details are held in separate records for each account for each month in which there has been any activity over the account or in which the value dated balance changes. The details held in this table for the calculation of interest include value dated balances and total debit and credit turnover for each value date.

The details held for the calculation of charges include the total number of entries with each different transaction code processed during the month, and the total value of the entries with each transaction code. These details are held in the record for the month in which the entries are processed, regardless of the value dates of the entries.

- Interest is calculated on value dated balances. All entries over an account are considered to have a value date, which is the date on which the entry affects the (value dated) balance for interest purposes.
- If value date is not entered in a transaction, it may be added automatically by the system, depending on the rules specified in the TRANSACTION application , or rules specified in the application which generated the transaction (for example, Money Market).
- If value date has not been entered or generated in an entry, a default of the booking date is assumed, that is, the entry is considered to affect the balance for interest purposes on the same day as it is processed.
- The value dated balances are also used for calculating balance requirement charges and for determining whether sufficient balance has been maintained for waiving charges and for calculating credit interest to offset charges.

- Interest is calculated on cleared funds for credit movements of an account. This is based on the exposure date (date greater than current bank day).
- If exposure date is not entered or generated in an entry, a default of the booking date is assumed, that is, the entry is considered to affect the balance for interest purposes on the same day as it is processed.

The ACCT.ACTIVITY table uses the exposure date of credit movement based on the accounting system, using the configuration of Exp Upd Acct Activ , Exp Cat Start , Exp Cat End , and Exp Upd Acct Activ Cat fields in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER . The transactions initiated after the configuration of the above-mentioned fields updates the Tdgl Details field in the STMT.ENTRY table as EXPOSURE.DATE or VALUE.DATE based on the configuration.

The Exp Upd Acct Activ field is a system level configuration field, which can be set to Yes or No. If set to Yes, all the transactions that impact the account are updated with the value as EXPOSURE.DATE in Tdgl Details field of the STMT.ENTRY . If set to No, all the transactions that impact the account are updated with the value as VALUE.DATE in Tdgl Details field of STMT.ENTRY . It is possible to configure the exposure date update of ACCT.ACTIVITY table for specific categories using the Exp Cat Start , Exp Cat End and Exp Upd Acct Activ Cat fields in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER .

- Exp Upd Acct Activ is set to No
- Exp Cat Start is 1000
- Exp Cat End is 9999
- Exp Upd Acct Activ Cat is set to Yes

In this example, the ACCT.ACTIVITY is updated based on EXPOSURE.DATE to entries raised for accounts in the category range 1000 to 9999. For all other category of accounts, the ACCT.ACTIVITY is updated based on the VALUE.DATE, which is the default setup.

If these fields are not configured, the default setup is VALUE.DATE.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Consolidate Entries field is used to set the consolidation level to be used while rebuilding the transaction using AC.REBUILD.EXPOSURE application. When this field is set to Yes, it is not possible to set values in the Exp Upd Acct Activ and Exp Cat Start to Exp Upd Acct Activ Cat (multi-value) fields.


##### Processing of Unauthorised Entry for Accounts

Updates for unauthorised entries from transactions are stored at account level. The following are the benefits of these updates.

- Helps in account closure validation when closing an account that has unauthorised transactions.
- Rebuilds an available funds ladder properly if unauthorised transactions exist for an account.
- Produces a report and enquiry to show the list of unauthorised entries for an account.

The threshold for storing the number of unauthorised entries is parameterised in the No Unau Keys field in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application.

In the above example (screenshot), the maximum threshold limit for storing unauthorised keys in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table is set to three.

- The EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES is updated with the unauthorised entries with the current processing date and future or forward processing date in separate fields, Unauth Key and Fwd Unauth Key respectively, to the extent of the threshold defined in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER .
- The unauthorised entries with current processing date beyond the threshold number is updated in the AC.UNAUTH.TRANSACTION table, with the transaction ID.
- The unauthorised entries with future or forward processing date beyond the threshold number is updated in the AC.FWD.UNAU.TRANSACTION table, with the transaction ID.
- Once the AC.ACCOUNTING.SERVICE is run, the information in the Unauth Key field and any transaction written to the AC.UNAUTH.TRANASCTION table are merged and written to the AC.UNAUTH.ENTRY table. The information in the Fwd Unauth Key field and any transaction written to the AC.FWD.UNAU.TRANSACTION table are merged and written to the AC.FWD.UNAU.ENTRY table. The Unauth Key and Fwd Unauth Key fields in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES , and the AC.FWD.UNAU.TRANSACTION and AC.UNAUTH.TRANSACTION tables are cleared.
- The EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table stores the unauthorised transactions for an account. The following fields are updated with the unauthorised transaction data. Tot Unauth Cr – Holds the total unauthorised credit balance. Tot Unauth Db – Holds the total unauthorised debit balance. Tot Fwd Unau Cr – Holds the total unauthorised forward credit balance. Tot Fwd Unau Db – Holds the total unauthorised forward debit balance. Unauth Key – Multi-valued set of transaction IDs that updates the unauthorised balances, which links to the internal ENTRY.HOLD table. Fwd Unauth Key – Multi-valued set of forward transaction IDs that updates the unauthorised balances, which links to the FWD.ENTRY.HOLD table.


##### Processing Available Funds

The available funds functionality enables the identification of movements or transactions that generates a deficit of cash in a client's accounts, and anticipates the impact of a new transaction on pre-existing client commitments. The available funds ladder is updated or constructed based on the following order of dates, depending on whether the account is impacted due to debit movement or credit movement.

For credit transactions, the following order is applied:

- Exposure Date
- Value Date (if Exposure Date is blank)
- Booking Date (if Value Date is blank)

While for debit transactions, the following order is applied:

- Value Date
- Booking Date (if Value Date is blank)

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| Exposure Date | Indicates the date on which a credit entry is included in the cleared balance of an account |
| Value Date | Indicates the date from which the entry is included for calculation of interest. Where there is no exposure date on the transaction, the value date is used as the date when the transaction affects the available funds |
| Booking Date | Indicates the date on which the transaction has been processed |
| Available Funds window | Contains the available funds balances for all forward dated and value dated account movements up to the number of calendar days forward from current bank day as specified on Cash Flow Days field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER |

It is possible to define the type of unauthorised movements that needs to be updated to available funds processing. This is defined in the Available Bal Upd field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER or ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION or ACCOUNT applications. The order of precedence is ACCOUNT , ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION (if ACCOUNT is blank) and ACCOUNT.PARAMETER (if ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION is blank). The following options are available in the Available Bal Upd field:

- Both – Unauthorised debits and credits to update available balance.
- None – No unauthorised movements to update available balance.
- Debits – Only unauthorised debits to update available balance.
- Credits – Only unauthorised credits to update available balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** If unauthorised debits or credits are excluded from the Available Bal field, the movements are updated unless they are blocked in EB.AF.PARAM table.

The EB.AF.PARAM.CHANGE application allows the input of blocking parameters for available funds processing for an application. The Avail Bal Nau Dr and Avail Bal Nau Cr fields define the blocking for the application. In the below screenshot, blocking parameters are set for the DATA.CAPTURE (DC) application.

The following fields define the blocking parameters for the application.

- If the Avail Bal Nau Dr field is set to blank, all unauthorised debits for DC must update the available funds movements and the available balances and also perform credit checks.
- If Avail Bal Nau Cr field is set to No, that none of the unauthorised credits for DC must update either available funds movements or available balances.

If a blocking parameter that is different from the application needs to be defined for a transaction code, then these parameters can be set specifically for the transaction code. In the above EB.AF.PARAM.CHANGE screenshot, any DATA.CAPTURE record which uses the Tranx Code as 1 (miscellaneous debits) is blocked from updating any unauthorised debits.

All other transaction codes used in DATA.CAPTURE considers the blocking parameters set for the application. If the Avail Nau Dr field is set to No, then no unauthorised miscellaneous debits in DATA.CAPTURE update the available funds movements and the available balances. Hence, credit checking is not performed for that unauthorised transaction.

The Effective Date field defines the date at which the parameters take effect. By default, it takes current bank day unless a future date is entered. Once the parameters are set in EB.AF.PARAM.CHANGE , depending on the effective date, the transactions are written to EB.AF.PARAM during the Close of Business (COB).

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Available Date | Indicates the date on which there is a projected movement. |
| Av Auth Db Mvmt | Indicates authorised debit movement for the date. |
| Av Nau Db Mvmt | Indicates unauthorised debit movement for the date. |
| Av Auth Cr Mvmt | Indicates authorised credit movement for the date. |
| Av Nau Cr Mvmt | Indicates unauthorised Credit movement for the date. |
| Forward Mvmts | Indicates authorised forward movements for the date. |
| Available Bal | Indicates the available balance for the available date. |

| Override message | Description |
|---|---|
| Available balance excess | Raised if an account is linked to a limit and an online debit transaction has caused the overdrawn available balance on value date of the transaction to exceed its limit. |
| Available balance overdraft | Raised if an account is neither linked to a limit nor to a shared balance pool and if an online debit transaction causes the available balance to be negative as of the value date of the transaction. |
| Available balance limit excess | Raised if an account is linked to a limit and the available balances of all the accounts in limit falls below the limit amount. |
| Available balance limit expired | Raised if an account is linked to a limit and the transaction falls beyond the expiry date of the limit. |
| Available balance below locked amount | Raised if an account’s balance that has an AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record falls below the level of the locked amount. |

In order to use the available funds functionality, the available funds ladder must be built for accounts with the existing future transactions; otherwise only new transactions are reflected in the available funds. The AF.REBUILD.REQUEST application allows the rebuild at three different levels:

- Individual accounts
- Account group level
- All accounts

This below screenshot shows the AF.REBUILD.REQUEST for the account 19027.

The AF.REBUILD.REQUEST is also used to rebuild the available funds ladder if any data corruption is suspected. The rebuild takes place during the COB in the online batch SOD.AVAILABLE.FUNDS.

The Account module allows the user to create, maintain, and control all types of accounts handled by Temenos Transact. Account becomes operational after its creation. Funds start moving to and from the accounts depending on the nature of the transaction. Every movement of fund impacts the balance in the account. These credit and debit movements are maintained for calculating interest and charges for reports. #### 📖 Introduction

A referral is the reporting of an account movement or balance to an account officer ( DEPT.ACCT.OFFICER ), when certain conditions are met. It is a Close of Business (COB) report containing the details of the transactions and balances to be reported or referred to the account officer.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following conditions are set to cover:

- One or more transaction codes or ranges thereof.
- Specific movements like debit, credit or reversal.
- Minimum and/or maximum amount of movements.
- Combination of transaction codes, movement type and amount. For example, miscellaneous debits reversed for amounts over USD 500.
- Balances at the COB for accounts that had movement during the day. For example, closing debit balances greater than USD 50000 created today.
- A posting restriction (a stronger form of referral) should be used, if an override message at input is required.

The REFERAL application contains the pre-defined referral conditions. Then these are loaded into the ACCOUNT record in the Referal Code field. Multiple referral codes can be specified in an account.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Account Referral feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Account Referral feature.
