#### 📖 Introduction

Account statements show the details of all entries over the ACCOUNT since the last statement. Entries are listed in transaction date sequence and can show both transaction date and value date. There are various parameters which controls the creation, frequency and content of the account statements. They are:

| Parameter | Level of setup |
|---|---|
| AC.STMT.PARAMETER | High level Parameter |
| STMT.GEN.CONDITION | High level parameter |
| ACCOUNT.STATEMENT | Account level |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic covers the system usage of account statements in Temenos Transact .


##### ConfiguringAC.STMT.PARAMETER

This is a high level parameter application used by the system to create default ACCOUNT.STATEMENT records, when new accounts are opened in the system. Various flags can be set within this record, which is used to determine whether the default ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record is configured to do the following:

- Produce statements when there has been no movement.
- Produce descriptive statements.
- Produce interest and/or charges statements and advices.
- Produce tax advices.
- Calculate the minimum number of months for a statement to be produced if at all.
- Provision to call a local API to populate extra handoff details (mainly to populate sub items in tag 61 and tag 86).

If no record exists, the default value is NO and the minimum frequency is six months. These settings can be overridden in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record itself.

The Fwd Mvmt Reqd field is used in a value dated account system only. If this field is NO or NULL, then real forward entries with a value date equal or less than the next statement date, which is booked during the statement period alone is reported in the statements. If it is desired that all the real forward entries irrespective of value date booked during the statement period are to be printed in the next statement, then this field has to be set to YES.

- Last statement date is 15/03/2008.
- Next statement date is 31/03/2008.
- Booking date is 15/03/2008 – Value date is 28/03/2008.
- Booking date is 31/03/2008 – Value date is 05/04/2008.

If this field is NO or NULL, then the entry with a value date 28/03/2008 is only reported in the next statement due on the 31/03/2008. However, if this field is set to YES, both the entries are reported in the next statement due on 31/03/2008.

Interest and charges statements can be suppressed through the Int Stmt And Adv field in the AC.STMT.PARAMETER application. The options are YES, NO or NONE.

- YES – Statements are produced regardless of what is input in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT .
- NO and NONE – Statements are not produced in the normal fashion.

> **⚠️ Note:** For any internal account marked with the Hvt Flag as “Yes” during the time of account creation, the system defaults the Stmt Fqu field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application to “BSNSS” along with the business date. However, the bank can choose to change the Stmt Fqu field based on their requirement.

The Split Maximum field is used to configure the maximum number of entries after which the record is split and stored in the STMT.PRINTED and ACCT.STMT.PRINT tables. Temenos has released a model record for AC.STMT.PARAMETER with the Split Maximum set as “200”. The bank can either use this configuration from the released record or can choose to define its own configuration.

The screenshot below shows the Split Maximum field configured as 200.


##### ConfiguringSTMT.GEN.CONDITION

When a new ACCOUNT is opened, an ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record specifying the date and frequency for printing account statements is generated automatically by the system. The default frequency is determined by the STMT.GEN.CONDITION application. The STMT.GEN.CONDITION accepts the records with the following frequencies.

- DAILY (every working day)
- WEEKLY
- WEEK2 (will accept two till nine)
- MONTHLY
- TWMTH
- QUARTERLY
- SIX.MONTHLY
- YEARLY

The following screen shot shows the STMT.GEN.CONDITION record for SIX.MONTHLY.

The STMT.GEN.CONDITION application allows the users to define the criteria for which the Print Stmt field is defaulted as NO in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application. The criteria is defined in the STMT.GEN.CONDITION and it is based on the conditions set in the CONDITION.PRIOITY The Print Stmt field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application is set to YES to make any changes in the frequency.


##### ConfiguringACCOUNT.STATEMENT

A record is created automatically in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application by the system for each new account that is opened. This record controls the date and frequency for printing statements, whether statements are to be printed if there have been no movements and various other statement production options for each account. Defaults are taken from other parameter applications such as the STMT.GEN.CONDITION and AC.STMT.PARAMETER , but these can be overridden by user input in this application. The key to this application is an ACCOUNT number.

Account statements are produced periodically as specified by frequencies in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application or online on an ad hoc basis. The following are the SWIFT message types available:

- MT940 – Customer statement
- MT941 – Balance report
- MT942 – Ad hoc statement
- MT950 – Statement

Statements can be produced every working day, for 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or for 1-12 months (using any day of the month as the anniversary or on the month end date).

Two statement cycles can be specified for each account, for example, weekly and monthly.

These cycles can be independent or combined:

- Separate – Statements for each cycle show the details of all entries since the last statement in the same cycle, regardless of the other cycle.
- Combined – Statements are produced on the dates specified by both cycles, but only contain the details of entries since the last statement from either cycle.

If there have been no entries since the last statement, the statement may be suppressed unless six months have elapsed.

Special interim statements showing the details of all entries since the last regular cycle 1 statement, can be produced any day without affecting the regular statement cycles. When a duplicate or interim statement is produced on request, a charge is applied for the issue of the statement. This charge is usually deferred until the next time the statement is printed in accordance with the statement frequency. The charge is made immediately, together with the production of a debit advice, detailing the charge made when the duplicate statement is produced.

The Managed by AA field specifies whether the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record belongs to an account created in the legacy AC or AA application. If the defaulted field value is Yes, then the record belongs to an AA account. In such a case, the statement account record cannot be amended manually in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT (for example, frequency cannot be amended manually). However, it can be amended through an OFS string. If the value is blank, the record belongs to an account opened in the AC application and can be amended manually.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section covers the processing of account statements in Temenos Transact .


##### Statement Processing

The record in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT defines the frequency of statement production, for a high volume account (HVT) using SWIFT. This is typically generated on every business day.

Temenos Transact supports 950 and 940 statement message types, also specified in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application. The default statement type is 950. Although a SWIFT message type is used to identify the type of statement required, the system does not necessarily generate it in SWIFT format.

Through Temenos Transact delivery, the DE.PRODUCT application specifies the carrier that the statements should be produced through SWIFT or PRINT. For PRINT statements, an additional setting in DE.PARM application ( Print Bypass field) identifies that the printed statement is formatted outside of delivery.

The following are the frequently used fields in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application.

This field is used to request a special statement on any day for cycle 1 without affecting the regular statements of the cycle. A user may not want his statement to be produced at any fixed frequency, instead wishes to foresee the list of statement unique dates and want them to be printed only on these days. For this purpose the Special Statement Frequency field is multi-valued to accept the list of unique dates.

The Special Statement Frequency field allows the user to specify an ad hoc date on which a statement needs to be generated. For example, in the Special Statement Frequency multi-valued field the user can specify unique dates like 23 Aug 2017, 03 Sep 2017, 24 Sep 2017, 09 Oct 2017.

With the above set up, the statement generation dates are as follows:

- The statement generated on 23 Aug 2017 would be from account opening date to 23 Aug 2017.
- The statement generated on 03 Sep 2017 would be for the movements from 24 Aug 2017 to 03 Sep 2017.

The entries included in a given special statement would be from the day after the last statement was produced within that statement cycle. However, with the Special Statement Frequency field set the statement generated because of the frequency related field does not affect the statement generated out of the Special Statement Frequency dates.

This field generate a statement if there is no movement, but the account ledger balance is not 0 (the account ledger balance in Temenos Transact is stored in the Online Actual Bal field). This should suppress the creation of a statement with no activity and account ledger balance is 0.

If no movements and account balance is 0 as set in the

, the system can suppress the creation of statement with no activity and account ledger balance is 0.

However, if account balance is not 0 with the above setting, the user is instructing the system to generate statements, even if there has not been any account moments.

This field stops regular statements being printed and follows only the dates given in the Special Statement Frequency fields.

This field controls if the Special Statement Frequency field should be printed even if is no movement in the account.

The current account balance and the settings in the

application is shown in the following screen shots.

In case of Account 84468, there were no balance moments from 24 Aug 2017 to 04 Sep 2017. However, because of the previous transactions, the account balance is not 0. In this situation, a special statement is printed from 24 Aug 2017 to 04 Sept 2017.

This is a no input field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application. On AA when a combined statement is defined and committed, the system synchronises the statement frequency of the participant accounts with that of the lead account.

This is a no input field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application. This multi-valued field can be accessed by AA to specify the participant accounts for a combined statement. When a combined statement is defined and committed, the system synchronises the statement frequency of the participant accounts with that of the lead account.

The Mapping Routine field in the STATEMENT.CONTROL application is used to attach a routine, which is called while preparing an account statement. This can be used only for the statements sent through SWIFT format.


##### Producing Account Statement using Segmentation Process

The service - AC.STATEMENT.SERVICE picks up all the accounts from the detail record and uses the segment technique in job list preparation to distribute and process a pre-determined set of entries per account, across multiple agents. Each agent follows the generic statement process and updates the delivery applications ( DE.O.HANDOFF , DE.O.HEADER and so on) for the entries processed in that session. The activation application for formatting service is not updated, so they are not picked by the delivery SWIFT formatting service for processing, as the final statement is not completed.

The AC.MERGE.SEGMENT.HANDOFF job takes all the segmented delivery records per account number (delivery references generated by previous job), sorts in order by segment number and merges them into a single handoff record.

The final delivery reference is updated in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT , which refers to the single DE.O.HEADER record that also has frames after going through SWIFT formatting service. This single merged delivery is the handoff record that is picked up and formatted by SWIFT service.


##### Non-printing of Internal Account Statements

The Print Stmt field in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT is an optional input field and can only be made for internal accounts. The value of this field can be Null, Yes or No. The following screen shots are the examples for an internal account and for a customer account.

If the Print Stmt field is set to Null or Yes, the statement is printed as normal. If this field is set to No, the printing of the account statement is bypassed (that is, this indicates that the statement is not physically printed out but all associated applications are updated normally, as if the statements are printed).


##### Interim Transaction Report – SWIFT MT942

The ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application allows the generation of SWIFT MT942 messages. The following fields in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record control MT942 message generation.

- Message Time – Multi-valued field containing the time duration of when the message is to be generated.
- Dr Floor Limit – The minimum value of a debit transaction that is to appear in the statement. Any transactions below this amount is not included in the statement.
- Cr Floor Limit – The minimum value of a credit transaction that is to appear in the statement. Any transactions below this amount is not included in the statement.
- Message Type – Holds the 942 message type.
- Send Msg Type – Indicates the option of Yes or No, whether to send or not the generated messages.

> **⚠️ Note:** These message types can also be produced on an ad hoc basis.


##### Ad hoc Interim Transaction (MT942) Reports

A customer may authorise another financial institution to receive statements and transaction reports of his accounts. Temenos Transact has a facility to produce interim transaction reports (SWIFT MT942) online on ad hoc basis. The requests are entered through the DE.MT942.REQUEST application, where Temenos Transact produces interim transaction report on the account specified.

> **⚠️ Note:** The V function is required to invoke the message creation.


##### Configuring Statement Narratives

Banks may require additional transaction descriptions or customised narratives to meet specific business needs or individual customer preferences, even when the underlying transaction remains the same. Temenos Transact enables the definition of customized transaction descriptions in the statements using the two below applications.

Start

- STMT.NARR.FORMAT
- STMT.NARR.PARAM

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| File | Indicates the file from which information is to be extracted to form the narrative. |
| Text Data | Indicates the element of text, or field whose content is to form part of the narrative that is defined. |
| Format | Indicates the special formatting to be applied to fields extracted from the specified file. |

End


##### Statement Print Mask – Masking of Entries in Statement

Accounting entries can be masked when the entries are posted incorrectly and are reversed out, or for other financial postings that customers do not want on their statements.

Masking is also necessary because some customers reconcile directly against the statements they receive from the banks and unexpected entries can cause confusion to their reconciliations. This is happens when the statement is delivered electronically and the customer uses it to reconcile internally within their computer systems.

The masking applies only to statements. The entries are not removed from the account and the transactions are not deleted, but the entries are not shown in the statement.

The Mask Print field in the STMT.ENTRY application indicates whether certain statement entries should be masked from printing. To update the Mask Print field, the AC.PRINT.MASK application allows the users to manually flag the statement entries that need not be displayed in their statements. The selection of entries to be masked for a particular account is assisted by STMT.ENTRY based enquiries.

Once the statement entries have been captured into AC.PRINT.MASK application, the system performs routine validations on the selected entries, to ensure the integrity of the selected items and to make sure that the net movement of the selected entries is zero.

Once all the routine are validated, the statement print programs or formatting enquires checks the Mask Print field in STMT.ENTRY . If the value of the field is true, then the entry is not displayed in the statement.

The AC.PRINT.MASK application allows the users to manually flag certain statement entries that have to be omitted from customers’ statements. The rules and validations of this application are:

- Run the AC.PRINT.MASK application and capture an ID which can be automatically generated by setting up an AUTO.ID.START record for AC.PRINT.MASK and also make sure that the application exists in the COMPANY record under the Pgm Autom Id fields .
- Once the ID is captured the customer account number and the current date in Mask Date needs to be captured.
- Enter the dates in Enq Start Date and Enq End Date . These dates are captured to ensure that the statement entries that are to be masked, fall within the start dates and end dates. If the user does not enter any dates into these fields, a default date of current bank day is captured in those fields.
- The Mask field indicates whether the statement entries should be masked and unmasked. It should be set to YES or NO, as this is a mandatory field.
- The Matched T o field is used to capture all the statement entries the user wants to mask or unmask. However, they must all be debit or all credit entries. Debit and credit entries cannot be mixed in the same field.
- The STMT.ENTRY enquiries is used to pick the entries which needs to be updated with the relevant fields in STMT.ENTRY . The below example explains how to run the enquiries and copy paste the relevant entries into the Matched To and Matched From fields.

The screenshot shows all the statement entries that are associated with account number 1189. To launch this list, the user has to run an enquiry in the STMT.ENTRY application of all entries that belong to the particular account that needs to be masked.

- Once the user finds the statement entry that needs to be masked or unmasked for printing on the enquiry list, the user can double-click on the statement entry and the full record of the statement entry is displayed (as shown in the preceding screen shot). Select the statement entry ID (at the top of the record) and copy the ID (right click on the mouse).
- After copying the statement entry ID, paste the ID in the Matched To or Matched From field in the AC.PRINT.MASK application (move the mouse to either fields and right click on them to paste the ID into the field) and click Enter .
- Then the To Total , From Total and Net Total fields are updated with the total of STMT.ENTRY .
- When all the entries are captured, the user can commit and authorise the record, but the system ensures that the net movement between the statement entries captured is zero.
- After authorising, the relevant records in STMT.ENTRY it is either masked or unmasked for printing at a later stage.


##### Generating MT940 Messages for Customer or Counterparty Reconciliation

MT940 is a standard structured SWIFT customer statement message. It is an end-of-day statement file that details all entries booked to an account. The bank can use this functionality to:

- Generate MT940 messages for customer or Vostro banks – these messages are usually sent to the customer or counterparty through SWIFT or, bank specific interfaces.
- Generate MT940 messages for internal or Nostro banks – these messages are usually sent to the bank reconciliation system which the bank uses to reconcile the entries on such accounts.

To generate an MT940 for customer or counterparty statement messages,

1. Set the current bank date to April 18, 2023 in the Today field in the DATES application as shown in the below screenshot. The screenshot below shows the transactions that have been processed in the new customer account.
2. Create a record in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT table and specify the Swift Statement Type field as MT940 in the Account Parameter menu.
3. Create a record in DE.PRODUCT for the account with the Carrier Addr No field set as SWIFT.
4. Run COB to update the AC.STMT.SERVICE.DETAIL table and generate the statement.
5. After the COB is run, the bank date in the Today field is changed to April 19, 2023.
6. Check the record in AC.STMT.SERVICE.DETAIL for the statement period.
7. Run the BNK/AC.STMT.DELIVERY.SERVICE and BNK/SWIFT.OUT services to generate and format the delivery message.
8. After running the service, DELIVERY.REF field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application gets updated with Delivery Reference for the newly generated statement for the account number. Using the delivery reference, view the record in the DE.O.HEADER application. The Carrier Addr No field must be set as SWIFT.
9. As shown above in the screenshot, the final generated swift statement can be viewed through the DE.MSG.SUM or DE.PREVIEW enquiry using the delivery reference updated in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application.

To generate an MT940 for reconciliation of internal or Nostro accounts,

1. Set the current bank date to April 18, 2023 in the Today field in the DATES application as shown in the below screenshot. The internal account details are displayed as shown in the below screenshot. The screenshot below shows the transactions that are processed in the account.
2. Create a record the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT table and specify Swift Statement Type field as MT940.
3. Create a record in DE.PRODUCT for the account with the Carrier Addr No field set as RECS.
4. Run COB to update the AC.STMT.SERVICE.DETAIL table and generate the statement.
5. After the COB is run, the bank date in the Today field is changed to April 19, 2023.
6. Check the record in AC.STMT.SERVICE.DETAIL for the statement period.
7. Run the BNK/AC.STMT.DELIVERY.SERVICE and BNK/RECS.OUT services to generate and format the delivery message.
8. View the DE.O.HEADER generated for the statement messages. The Carrier Addr No field must be set as RECS.
9. As shown above in the screenshot, the final generated swift statement can be viewed through the DE.MSG.SUM or DE.PREVIEW enquiry using the delivery reference updated in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application.


##### Archiving Statement Details

The user can archive the account statement details recorded in the ACCT.STMT.PRINT , ACCT.STMT2.PRINT , STMT.PRINTED , and STMT2.PRINTED applications using the Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) or Transact standard archival methods.

The T24 Data Lifecycle Management Application (DL) module reduces the size and improves the performance of a transactional database by moving non-transactional, historical data to a separate Read-Only (RO) database. When the DL module is installed, the system stores the statement record copy in the RO database (RO.COPY.KEYLIST) and deletes the records from various applications. The STATEMENT and ACCT.STMT.PRINT records in the ARCHIVE application serves this purpose.

The Retention Period or Purge Date fields must be defined by the user in the specific records in the ARCHIVE application to retrieve the deleted records.

Below are the sample screenshots of the ARCHIVE application records.

The above records from the ARCHIVE application should be linked to ARC.GENERIC.REQUEST as shown below.

The ACCT.STMT.PRINT.DATES table stores the ACCT.STMT.PRINT and ACCT.STMT2.PRINT IDs with their minimum and maximum date. This table helps in identifying the statements that are archived based on the purge date or retention period available in the ARCHIVE application records.

To enable the ACCT.STMT.PRINT.DATES table, the user must install the DL Module, and set the Enable Asp Date Online field as Yes in the AC.STMT.PARAMETER table, as shown below.

This table is updated initially with a one-time service (UPDATE.ACCT.STMT.PRINT.DATES) and post this service is run, the table gets updated for every new ACCT.STMT.PRINT record (for new account during first transaction) and for every split of new ACCT.STMT.PRINT record (for an existing account).

A sample screenshot of ACCT.STMT.PRINT.DATES after running the service is shown below.

The system identifies the records to be archived with inputs from ACCT.STMT.PRINT.DATES table.

> **⚠️ Note:** Any record with a minimum date less than the purge date is archived.

When the ARC.GENERIC service is run, the STATEMENT record initially runs in the ARCHIVE application, which results in the copy generation of the files mentioned in the Arc Filename field. This copy is archived and stored in the RO.COPY.KEYLIST file. Upon running the ACCT.STMT.PRINT record in the ARCHIVE application, the system deletes the record from various applications.

In the case of standard archival, the user must run only the archival for the STATEMENT record in the ARCHIVE application, and after running the archival service, the records are moved to the $ARC file.

The ARCHIVE.DATA field should be set as ‘Y’ in the ARCHIVE application to archive the record. If it is set as ‘N’, then the system deletes the record instead of archiving, which results in loss of data. Hence, this field is set as ‘Y’.

### 1.10  ACFA


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In various scenarios, the payment transactions can fail due to various reasons like insufficient funds, posting restrict, stop requests. In case of such failures, Temenos Payments, Payment Order, Generic Accounting Interface, NSF processing have capabilities to create a funds authorisation request, ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `RC.CONDITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Approval Code*, *Allowed Funds Decision*, *Allowed Reservation*, *Dda Funds Check*, *Funds Decision*, *Update Activation File*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In various scenarios, the payment transactions can fail due to various reasons like insufficient funds, posting restrict, stop requests. In case of such failures, Temenos Payments, Payment Order, Generic Accounting Interface, NSF processing have capabilities to create a funds authorisation request, providing the bank enables this option, that can be reviewed and retried later.

The funds authorisation requests raised by the business application are initially created in hold, till the user or the Transaction Recycler module approves or rejects them.

The funds authorisation request can also be captured by a user to record funds authorisation approval (pre-approval).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The funds authorisation requests are processed based on the parameterisation in the ACFA.TYPE application. The ID of this table is formed by RequestSource*[RequestCode]. A record with the ID = DEFAULT is used to define the conditions for catch all.

When an ACFA ( AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION ) record is created manually or by a business application, the system combines the values supplied in the RequestSource (populated with the system ID assigned to the business application) and RequestCode and determines the appropriate setup in ACFA.TYPE . If not found, then the setup in the DEFAULT record is used.

The following table explains the fields present in ACFA.TYPE :

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Update Activation File | This field is used to decide if the internal activation file must be updated or an external event must be emitted when the AC.FUNDS.AUTHOIRISATION record is authorised. It holds the following values: If set to Yes, the system updates the activation file with the status of the funds authorisation request. If set to No, the system does not update the activation file with the status of the funds authorisation request. If set to External, the system updates the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE application and an Integration Framework event is created. If set to BusinessEvent, a first-class business event is emitted. |
| Dda Funds Check | This field checks if ACFA performs the funds check when the record is committed. For example, when an ACFA record is created as an investigation item for transaction stop, the funds check is not required. |
| Allowed Funds Decision | This field decides if the funds authorisation request is to be manually approved and/or sent to the Recycler. For example, the funds authorisation requests for insufficient funds and/or posting restricts are normally sent to the Recycler, but those for transaction stop are manually reviewed by the bank staff. |
| Allowed Reservation | This field defines if funds are automatically locked on the account when an ACFA record is approved. When an ACFA record is created as an investigation item for the bank staff to review transaction stop or non-sufficient fund (NSF) decisions, it should not reserve funds. |
| Allow Approval Code | This field defines if the respective ACFA type can be manually authorised or authorised by the Recycler. |

The RC.CONDITION and RC.CAPTURE applications are used to define the capture conditions for ACFA records.


#### 🔧 Working With

The AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION records created manually by a user, capture a funds authorisation approval, the user can indicate the reason. The Funds Decision field can only be set to Pres-approved.

The decision to reserve the funds depend on the configuration in the DEFAULT record of ACFA.TYPE .

> **⚠️ Note:** The manual funds authorisation requests are not considered by the Transaction Recycler module and can only be authorised manually.

The below screenshot shows a funds authorisation request captured by the account officer to record the approval.

ACFA created by a business application has more additional details:

- The source (RequestSource, for example, TPH).
- The original transaction (original transaction reference, for example, the TPH reference).
- The request code (indicates the reason for which the source has created the ACFA, for example, 01 – insufficient funds).
- Transaction sub-type (sub-type sent by the business application, in the form of SystemID-Subtype).
- Cut-off date (represents the cut-off date until when the system should retry the ACFA).
- Cut-off time (represents the cut-off time until when the system should retry the ACFA).
- Transaction code (represents the transaction code sent by the business application, relevant for funds check and posting restrictions).

In case, an ACFA record is created in the system containing a cut-off date and time for a specific request, this takes precedence over the cut-off time defined in the RC.CONDITION application for the specific retry request type or sub-type.

If the business application sends the transaction code in the ACFA record, the system checks if this code is mapped under a specific activity under Balance Availability property class for balance checking. In this way, there is a possibility to configure the system to check different balance types for different transaction codes and whether or not to include the limit granted to the customer, if necessary.

For the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION records created by the business application, the decision to check the funds, reserve the funds, the funds decisions and the update of the activation file or external system depends on the setup of the corresponding ACFA.TYPE record. Read Configuring Account Funds Authorisation (ACFA) for more details.

If the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION record is rejected either by the user or by the Transaction Recycler Module, funds are not locked on the account.

If the funds authorisation records are created based on requests from an external business application, outside Transact (for example, a standalone Temenos Payments platform) the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION can either emit an IF event or a first class event when the record is authorised, depending on the setup in the corresponding ACFA.TYPE record.

ACFA.TYPE Set up for Generating Entries in Integration Framework Event is explained in the below example.

The record in ACFA.TYPE for TPH application (PP) is being set up with the Update Activation File field set to External.

A debit transaction of 500 EUR is being posted by TPH against account 10014870001.

As the account does not have enough funds, the system creates a record in AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION and RC.DETAIL .

The Recycler tries to recover the amount from the debit account each time the COB or online process is executed.The debit account 10014870001 is being funded with 50,000 USD, making its balance positive.

When the online Recycler process is run, the system tries to recover the amount captured in the record in ACFA.

As sufficient funds are available in the account, the amount is recovered and the records in AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION and RC.DETAIL are updated.

As ACFA.TYPE is set up to update IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE , an entry is added after the ACFA record is processed.

### 1.11  CAMT Statements


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks that participate in Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments (both credit transfer and direct debit) which is acting for the ordering party or the beneficiary are required to generate the CAMT053/052/054 messages, which are standard account reports based on movements across the account over a...*
> 
> **Applications:** `STMT.ENTRY`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks that participate in Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments (both credit transfer and direct debit) which is acting for the ordering party or the beneficiary are required to generate the CAMT053/052/054 messages, which are standard account reports based on movements across the account over a specified period of time.

These are part of the family of cash management messages (CAMT) format of the ISO20022 (also known as UNIFI) standard using an XML based schema. The format should include full details of the SEPA payment in the statement detail, as well as details of other non-SEPA financial transactions. This is mandatory in many European countries since February 1st 2014.

The following are the CAMT messages generated in Temenos Transact .

- The CAMT053 (bank to customer statement) message is a statement of account(s) sent by the bank to the account holding customer (or nominated representative) on a periodic basis. .
- The CAMT052 (bank to customer account report) is used for intra-day account reporting upon request by the account owner. It is an intra-day version of the CAMT053, showing movements generated since the last CAMT052 or CAMT053 was generated.
- The CAMT054 message (bank to customer debit credit notification) is a report of selected transactions processed across the account during the requested period and does not include account balances.

The CAMT messages are the ISO20022 equivalent of the MT9nn series:

- CAMT053 is the ISO20022 equivalent of MT940, which is an account statement sent by the bank to the account holder on periodic basis.
- CAMT052 is the IS020022 equivalent of MT942/MT941, which is an intra-day version of the Camt053 reporting intra-day transactions and balances.
- CAMT054 is the IS020022 equivalent of MT900/MT910, which is a notification of selected transactions but no balance data.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

A CAMT message has a nested structure with the building blocks (as shown in the following diagram). The Temenos Transact CAMT module is responsible to assemble the data necessary to produce a CAMT message for each statement triggered. CAMT052, CAMT053 and CAMT054 messages have the same structure, except for the header name that is different and CAMT054 does not have balance details.

The CAMT053 – Bank to customer statement has the following structure:

- Group Header
- Statement
- Entry
- Transaction details

CAMT052 – Bank to customer account report has the following structure:

- Group Header
- Report
- Entry
- Transaction details

CAMT054 – Bank to customer debit or credit notification has the following structure:

- Group Header
- Notification
- Entry
- Transaction details

The Group Header block of the CAMT message provides the information related to the statement and is specified once for the CAMT message. This section of the message is mandatory.

It contains the information such as the message identification, pagination, message recipients and so on.

> **⚠️ Note:** (1..1) – Denotes that this section is mandatory and occurs only once in the CAMT message.

The Statement section of the CAMT message provides the details of the account(s) for which the statement(s) is produced.

The CAMT message may contain information related to more than one account statement. However, Temenos Transact is producing one CAMT message for a single account statement.

Details required at this level are built from the Temenos Transact account and related statement production details. This includes the details of the statement period, account identification, opening, closing and other account balances.

> **⚠️ Note:** (1..n) – Denotes that this section is mandatory and may occur multiple times in the CAMT message.

An account statement can contain multiple account movements (a statement may have zero entries during the period). Information at this level is derived from the individual account movement from the Temenos Transact STMT.ENTRY table.

> **⚠️ Note:** (0..n) - Denotes that this section is optional and may occur multiple times in the CAMT message.

Provides additional information for each entry displayed in the entry level section.

The additional information includes:

- Additional details for an individual entry.
- Additional details for SEPA related transactions.
- The underlying entries for an individual entry, which is a net movement representing multiple debits and credits or a batch entry (this is supported at a later stage).

> **⚠️ Note:** (0..n) – Denotes that this section is optional and may occur multiple times in the CAMT message.

The following diagram shows the XML view of the CAMT053 message.

Read CAMT messages for more information on CAMT statements.

### 1.12  CustomerSSI


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Standard settlement instruction (SSI) can be defined for a particular customer, which is then used to default settlement account fields such as drawdown account, principal liquidation account and interest liquidation account, in various Temenos Transact applications.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.SYS.CODES`, `ACCOUNT.PARAMETER`, `CUSTOMER.SSI`, `LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS`, `MM.MONEY.MARKET`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Code*, *Company*, *Customer*, *Default*, *Order*, *Ssi*, *Sys*, *Sys Code*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Standard settlement instruction (SSI) can be defined for a particular customer, which is then used to default settlement account fields such as drawdown account, principal liquidation account and interest liquidation account, in various Temenos Transact applications.

The CUSTOMER.SSI application is used to define the standard settlement instruction (SSI) for a particular customer. The customer can instruct the bank to link a specific account as the default settlement account for the different type of transactions. In cases where customers have accounts in several branches, an appropriate default settlement account can be defined specific to the branch during the settlement process.

For example, if a bank creates a Forex (FX) transaction for a customer in Mumbai, the settlement account defined in CUSTOMER.SSI for Mumbai’s branch will be used as the default settlement account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application the Sys Code field holds the combination of application-activity or ALL, based on which the settlement accounts such as drawdown and liquidation are defaulted in the LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS (LD) and MM.MONEY.MARKET (MM) applications. In the AC.SYS.CODES application, the above application activity combinations can be defined along with the relevant description. The required Sys Code field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER can be selected through the linked AC.SYS.CODES application and the enrichment as given in AC.SYS.CODES appears here.

The record ID is LD-INT, which refers to the interest liquidation account in the LD application has a record in

, as shown in the below screen shot.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Customer Ssi field is used to define the standard settlement instruction (SSI) for a particular customer, which is then used to default settlement account fields such as drawdown account, principal liquidation account and interest liquidation account in applications such as:

- LD.LOANS.AND.DEPOSITS (LD)
- MM.MONEY.MARKET (MM)
- FOREX (FX)
- MG.MORTGAGE (MG)
- NETTING
- BL.BILL
- PD.CAPTURE
- PRE.SYNDICATION.FILE

The Customer Ssi field in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application is used to control the above feature.

If this field is set to YES (along with the Default Order field of the required Sys Code field set as blank), then during contracts input for the above applications, the system first checks for a matching record (combination of Customer, Currency or Sys Code) in Customer Ssi to default in the relevant settlement account fields. During capture of a contract, the SSI defined have the highest priority for defaulting.

In case where the counter party does not have a record for the above combination in Customer Ssi , then overrides are generated at the application level and the settlement accounts are defaulted as per existing functionality of the respective application.

If the Customer Ssi field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER is set as blank, then the system does not allow input in the CUSTOMER.SSI application and uses the existing functionality of the respective application for defaulting settlement accounts.

Create the following record in

application for customer 1025.

While inputting a LD contract in USD for the above customer, using the above setup the settlement accounts are defaulted, as shown in the below screen shot.


##### Defining Settlement Account Specific to Branch Company

The bank can configure default settlement instruction to the customer for one or more specific company or branch where the transaction may get initiated. The default settlement account associated with the company or branch can belong to the same company or a different company.

The Company field in the CUSTOMER.SSI application allows the user to capture the company for which the associated account acts as the default settlement account.

If the Company field is left blank for a specific settlement account, it is deemed as the generic default settlement account for all the companies for which specific definition does not exist for the given transaction type and currency. It is possible to define the account of a different branch as the default settlement account of a specific branch. For example, the account in Branch 2 can be configured as the default settlement account for Branch 3.

If no default settlement account is defined for a company and no generic default settlement account is defined for the transaction type and currency in CUSTOMER.SSI , the user should manually enter the settlement account at the time of transaction initiation.

The user cannot define multiple settlement accounts for the same system code and company for a specific currency. In such a scenario, a duplication error is displayed while validating the record in CUSTOMER.SSI .

The following screenshot shows the CUSTOMER.SSI application set up for Customer 151763.

The account 10015176301 is in the BNK Company (US0010001) and 10015176203 is an account in branch company (US0010100). The user has configured the account (10015176301) in BNK Company as the default settlement account for the branch company.

When an LD-DD transaction is initiated for Customer 151673 in BNK Branch Company, 10015176301 is defaulted as the settlement account.

As per the CUSTOMER.SSI setup in the above example, the Company for Sys Code “ALL” is left blank. In that case, Account 10015176101 will be considered as the generic default settlement account for all the other transaction types in the USD currency.

So, when an FX transaction is initiated for Customer 151763, 10015176101 is defaulted as the settlement account.


#### 📋 Tasks

Standard settlement instruction (SSI) can be defined for a particular customer to default the values in the settlement account fields such as drawdown account, principal liquidation account and interest liquidation account, in various Temenos Transact applications.

Set Customer SSI

The CUSTOMER.SSI application is used to define the standard settlement instruction (SSI) for a particular customer. The customer can instruct the bank to link a specific account as the default settlement account for the different type of transactions. In cases of customers who have accounts in several branches, an appropriate default settlement account can be defined to a specific branch during the settlement process.


##### Workflow

### 1.13  Daylight Overdraft


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Daylight Overdraft represents the intraday and end-of-day overdraft risks the bank is willing to take for a given customer. An Intraday Overdraft may be higher than the end-of-day overdraft as the bank expects any intraday credit extension to be cured by end of day.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Time Zone*, *Use Local Time*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Daylight Overdraft represents the intraday and end-of-day overdraft risks the bank is willing to take for a given customer. An Intraday Overdraft may be higher than the end-of-day overdraft as the bank expects any intraday credit extension to be cured by end of day.

Daylight Overdraft is set up to temporarily allow Intraday Overdrafts that are not going to turn into end-of-day overdrafts. Therefore, the Daylight Overdraft can be used by a client when there are Forecasted Credits that are known by the banking system. The Daylight Overdraft is uncommitted or unadvised, and therefore, it can vary day to day and throughout the day, as seen fit by the bank.

Forecasted Credits represent funds expected to be credited against the customer’s account but which are not fully booked yet. These can be set up to be taken into consideration against the intraday exposure. The system allows the aggregation of the Forecasted Credit and of the intraday exposure posted against the customer’s accounts.

The exposure of the multiple cash accounts belonging to the same customer is monitored in the Temenos Transact environment using a specially created off-books Summary Account for each customer. This exposure is reset on a daily basis per calendar day, not business day. Each customer’s account is linked with the Summary Account, and the exposure created against the customer’s account is automatically transferred to the Summary Account. The exposure of the Summary Account is created on the booking date irrespective of the value date of the transaction – working balance of the account is used in calculating the exposure.

The validation of balances is performed on the account and Summary Account. A special off-books (memo) balance has been introduced to hold the Forecasted Credits on the level of accounts and the Summary Account. Special types of credit checks can be performed by the system when the debit transaction arrives to the account. While performing the credit check, the system now considers both funds fully posted against customer accounts and those booked as Forecasted Credits.

While the system validates the transaction, balance checking is performed both on the level of the account and on the Summary Account level in real time. Depending on the results of such credit check, the transaction is either accepted or diverted for Dispo. After funds recorded as Forecasted Credit are fully settled, the relevant portion of the Forecasted Credit is removed while posting funds against the principal balance of the customer’s account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To create accounts which may have Forecasted Credits assigned to them, the following steps must be performed:

- AA Products have to be created for the Summary Account (SA) and its underlying Transaction Accounts (TR).
- A new balance must be added in the AC.CREDIT.CHECK application which defines how credit check will take place in case of Forecasted Credits. This will be used in the BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property of the respective SA and TR accounts as shown in the following screenshot:

The Base Balance Type field should be configured as WORKING or AVAILABLE based on the accounting treatment (Trade Dated or Value Dated Accounting) followed by the bank.

The Sign Restricted field in the AC.BALANCE.TYPE application has the following options:

- No/Null (default option) – Represents existing functionality, where the balance under the balance type is moved from credit to debit or vice-versa.
- Credit Only – Allows the respective balance types to hold only amounts equal to or higher than zero, meaning that the balance under the balance type cannot be moved from credit to debit.
- Debit Only – Allows the respective balance type to hold only amounts equal to or less than zero, meaning that the balance under the balance type cannot be moved from debit to credit.

The Sign Restricted field allows the user to restrict Forecasted Credits at the TR or SA account level to go in debit.

For these two types of accounts, the following new balance types must be introduced:

- TR account balance type

- SA account balance type


##### Cross-company Accounts

In case of cross-company accounts, where the off-books memo SA account is open in a different company than the one of TR cash accounts, the system does not post any intercompany accounting entries. However, for the system to be able to recognise the SA from a different lead company, the Summary Account reference suffixed with company mnemonic must be set up.

For example, if the TR account is opened in BNK company and linked to SA account in EU1 company, the Parent Account field from the ACCOUNT property is set up with the Summary Account reference suffixed with company mnemonic EU1:

> **⚠️ Note:** Summary Account defined with a company mnemonic as suffix should only be a memo account.


##### Summary Account Daily Exposure Reset

To have the exposure of the Summary Account reset on daily basis per calendar day, the system must consider the bank’s local time. This implies the following configuration steps must be made:

- In SPF application, the Use Local Time field must be set to Yes:
- In the respective bank’s record from the COMPANY application, the Time Zone field must be set up with the value corresponding to the bank’s local time zone:


#### 🔧 Working With

The following example will be split into 2 days to show how the forecasted exposure is reset with the starting of next business day and how Forecasted Credits are updated with new values.


##### Day 1

In the following scenario, the bank has three TR accounts with a customer. Their opening credit balances and Forecasted Credits on day 1 are listed in the following table:

| Ac.1 | Cr | 10 | 30 |  |

Also, overdraft amount (OD), which is the minimum floor amount representing the level of risk exposure the bank accepts regardless of the amount of Forecasted Credits, and the Daylight Overdraft amount (DLOD), which is the maximum ceiling amount representing the maximum level of risk exposure the bank is willing to accept out of the customer’s Forecasted Credits on the SA or TR account level.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Day.1 | OD | 20 |
| DLOD | 50 |  |

When creating the account structure for the customer, the SA is created first, under the designated AA Product for such accounts.

The Act Credit Check field from the BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property must be set to the balance that has been defined for Forecasted Credits in the AC.CREDIT.CHECK application.

The OD and DLOD amounts as well as their currency are defined in the following fields in BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property:

- Cc Com Currency – Represents the currency of both OD and DLOD amounts.
- Cc Com Maximum – Represents the DLOD amount, meaning the maximum ceiling amount consisting the maximum level of risk exposure the bank is willing to accept out of the customer’s Forecasted Credits.
- Cc Com Minimum – Represents the OD amount, meaning the minimum floor amount consisting the level of risk exposure the bank accepts regardless of the amount of Forecasted Credits.

Because the SA is an off-books memo balance account, it has to be marked as such. Therefore, in the ACCOUNT property, the Balance Treatment field must be set to Memo.

The TR accounts can be created under the designated AA Product for such accounts, with the SA set as the parent account. The following screenshot shows a TR1 account:

The BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property is set up similar to the one from the SA account:

Because TRs are on-books balance accounts, in the ACCOUNT property, the Balance Treatment field must be left blank. Also, in the ACCOUNT property, the Parent Link Type field must be set to Exposure. This is done to consolidate the exposure of TR accounts at the SA account level by including the Forecasted Credits in it. The SA maintains total balance of Forecasted Credits as a memo balance in addition to its principal balance.

If the Parent Link Type field is left blank, then only the actual balances of TR accounts is consolidated. The user can set up the Parent Link Type field only when the Parent Account field is also set up, and in the example, this has to hold the reference ID of the SA account.

The Link Type Exception field is associated with the Parent Link Type field and can be set up only if Parent Link Type is set as Exposure. Link Type Exception is a multi-value field which accepts the list of arrangement activities that are exempt from the following Parent Link Type configurations. This means that all the activities mentioned here will follow the default method of aggregating balances to the SA account, by aggregating to it the entire transaction amount.

### 1.14  DeferringInterestCharges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Deferring of interest and/or charges is allowed either as statutory banking requirement or for internal review procedures in certain financial institutions. Interest and/or charges on the capitalisation date are posted to a suspense account until a pre-defined event date till they are cleared from s...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Deferring of interest and/or charges is allowed either as statutory banking requirement or for internal review procedures in certain financial institutions. Interest and/or charges on the capitalisation date are posted to a suspense account until a pre-defined event date till they are cleared from suspense and posted to the customer account. This allows the opportunity for either the customer to query the amounts; or the bank to amend or even cancel the interest.

> **⚠️ Note:** The code of banking practice in UK states that the bank should give all private individual customers 14 days’ notice before debiting their accounts with interest and/or bank charges relating to overdrafts.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.

### 1.16  GenerationScalableAccountNumbers


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *After an Account Officer captures the necessary customer details and initiates the account creation process, the system must generate a unique account ID. In a typical banking environment, multiple Account Officers can be working simultaneously, initiating the request to create an account from their...*
> 
> **Applications:** `ACCOUNT`, `AUTO.ID.START`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Additional Info*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

After an Account Officer captures the necessary customer details and initiates the account creation process, the system must generate a unique account ID. In a typical banking environment, multiple Account Officers can be working simultaneously, initiating the request to create an account from their respective systems.

When they attempt to create accounts at the same time, each session sends a request to generate an account ID leading to a locking situation. This may lead to,

- Delay: Other sessions must wait until the locking is released.
- Timeout and Slowness: The sequential nature of the process leads to performance degradation, causing timeouts during periods of high activity when several officers are creating accounts simultaneously.

This can be avoided by generating scalable account numbers.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following steps need to be followed to generate scalable account number.

1. Add .PRE in the Additional Info field in the ACCOUNT record to indicate that the account numbers are pre-generated.
2. Setup TSA.SERVICE record for new service.
3. Check if the Digit Type and Account Mask used for the branch companies are the same as those of the lead company. This ensures that the branch companies follow the same rules as their parent or lead company for generating account IDs.
4. Configure the AUTO.ID.START application for the lead company, and the same configuration is automatically applied to all the associated branch companies. Essentially, branch companies do not require individual configuration for ID generation, as they inherit the settings from their lead company.
5. Configure the files specific for branch companies. If the branch companies have unique requirements (for example, different check digit types, account number lengths, or AUTO.ID.START settings), the system must handle them separately.

In this case, the ACCOUNT.ID.LIST and ACCOUNT.ID.REQUEST files are converted to FRP type (file resource partitioning), meaning that each branch has their own separate files for managing account IDs. This ensures that the pre-generated ID lists and requests are managed independently for each branch.


#### 🔧 Working With

To avoid locking issues while generating account numbers, the AC.PRE.GENERATE.ID background service pre-generates the account numbers and stores them in a list file. When there is a request to open a new account, the session fetches the account number from this list for the respective session number (unique random number assigned by Transact for each request).

The account numbers are pre-generated as shown below:

1. The service generates IDs for the session based on rules set in the company’s configuration. The service pre-generates batches of account numbers and stores them in a file linked to the session. Each session in T24 has a unique session ID. This session ID is used to pick the pre-generated account numbers from the list.
2. When a session needs an account number, it checks the list for its session and picks the first available ID.
3. If a session runs out of account numbers (for example, less than 5 IDs left), it updates the ACCOUNT.ID.REQUEST file, prompting the background service to generate more account numbers for that session.
4. Instead of locking the F.LOCKING file during each account creation request, the session simply reads from the pre-generated list. Only the background service updates the F.LOCKING file, and since the service is single-threaded, it doesn’t face locking collisions.
5. When a session fetches an account number, it locks only its own session-specific list file, reducing the chance of multiple sessions locking the same resource and avoiding the delays caused by sequential processing.

The following screen shots show the creation of current accounts using Legacy AC module.

Initially, run the service with the desired number of agents to pre-generated account IDs for all possible session numbers (that is, from 00001-99999).

After the service is finished, check the ACCOUNT.ID.LIST internal table in the back end.

Now try to create an account, where the system can use the pre-generated ID for ACCOUNT application.

The following screen shots show the creation of current accounts using Arrangement Architecture.

The following screen shots show the creation of Accounts Arrangement using simulation.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Generation of Scalable Account Numbers feature.


#### 📊 Outputs
