### 1.17  HVT Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Certain types of financial transaction require account postings to be made to the same account, where the volume of these transactions are high, the result is a high number of postings across the account. Typically this scenario can occur when one side of the transaction is the bank itself, so an in...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT`, `AC.CONSOLIDATE.COND`, `AC.HVT.PARAMETER`, `AC.HVT.TRIGGER`, `ACCOUNT`, `ACCOUNT.PARAMETER`, `ACCOUNT.STATEMENT`, `ACCT.ACTIVITY` ... +6 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Ac*, *Consolidate Ent*, *Deferred Balance Update*, *Deferred Consolidate Ent*, *Deferred Ids To batch*, *Deferred Status*, *Do Check*, *Ent* ... +23 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Certain types of financial transaction require account postings to be made to the same account, where the volume of these transactions are high, the result is a high number of postings across the account. Typically this scenario can occur when one side of the transaction is the bank itself, so an internal account (or nostro account) is updated as the other side of a customer transaction. This can also happen when a bank has Corporate or Retail accounts that attract high volumes of transactions.

When an account posting takes place, a number of applications related to the account are updated with details of the posting and account balances. The high volume account solution provides standard account functionality in a seamless manner to the end user, avoiding any concurrency issues and allows the system to be scalable.


##### When to Use HVT

HVT is used when there are significant volume of movements generated across the account that needs to be completed in shortest time frame. The possible candidates are:

- Internal accounts used for collection of tax and charges – These are frequently high volume operations both online and as part of the Close of Business (COB).
- Internal suspense accounts – Bulk payments are frequently processed through individual suspense accounts. For example, a company salary payment batch typically results in a debit to the corporate account initially and a credit to a suspense account. Then each child payment is made to the individual staff member by debiting the suspense account.
- Nostro accounts – Where the bank needs to make a payment externally, a nostro account is usually credited by the transaction issuing the payment. High volumes of transactions can be processed both online and offline.
- High volume customer accounts – Certain accounts owned by customers may also process high volumes of transactions, both online and offline.

Temenos Transact has a mechanism to enable high volume processing for accounts. The Hvt Flag field in the ACCOUNT record controls whether an account is high volume or not. A value of No or Null indicates that it is not a HVT. If this field is set to Yes, it indicates that this account has a high volume of transactions every day. HVT processing is supported for AC Accounts and Arrangement Accounts (AR) Product Line. Customer Accounts that are flagged as High Volume Transaction accounts does not undergo funds check including limit check.

Once an account is flagged as a HVT and when the transactions are processed the details of the transactions are written to the AC.HVT.TRIGGER table. The ID to this table is ACCOUNT.ID!SESSION.NO!DAY!TIME.

This record also contains the IDs to the files that have been updated by the transaction. For example:

- Stmt Val Id
- Ent Fwd Id
- Ac Violation
- Fwd Stmt1 Id

If a merge is triggered, the information from the AC.HVT.TRIGGER records are merged and the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record is updated. The other accounting applications where multiple entries have been created with suffixes for the high volume processing, such as STMT.PRINTED are also merged at this time, creating one record for the account.

The merging service runs automatically at defined intervals during the online phase and is forced to run at critical points during COB, to ensure that all relevant data for a HVT is merged. During COB, data from non-stop transactions with a booking date of next working day is not merged until the start of day processing begins. The defined interval is set through the Hvt Merge Interval field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER , which can be from 1 to 99 minutes. The default interval for online merging is 15 minutes. The following are the types of merging:

- Notional Merge – The balances are merged online for enquiry purposes.
- Online Merge – The service can be run online. This merge does not include entries in the current defined period.
- Real Merge – This is done during the COB and the system process all the records.

The following diagram explains the flow for HVT.


##### Deferred Balance Update

High Volume Internal Account can be selected to defer its updates to improve the Accounting Transaction performance.

Certain financial transactions require account postings to be made to the same account such as a cash withdrawal. In this scenario, one side of the transaction is the customer account but the other side of the transaction is the banks own internal contra account, thus resulting in high volume of transactions posted to this internal account.

For accounts (like internal contra accounts) the actual timing of the balance updates and tables is not critical when the transaction volume is huge, and the balances and tables change continuously. The user can select an HVT internal account to defer its balance updates and entry creation to a background service. Accounting Transaction performance is significantly improved by saving on IO and processing time, by deferring entries.

> **⚠️ Note:** When an internal account is selected to defer its updates, the user must accept that the balances and enquires are not up to date. HVT notional merge, where the user can view correct balances in real-time including the pending updates to the account balances is not possible.

The deferred entries are processed by a continuous background service. This background service posts the entries as NON-HVT. Online transactions do not change and are posted as HVT to the HVT Trigger table.


##### Pre-Reservations during Credit Check

Any transaction to a HVT account, must be split into two database updates to perform accurate credit check and skip lock on ECB:

- A notification of the intended debit transaction to the account (pre-reservation). The application that is initiating the request must ensure that the pre-notification is created and available before the actual transaction is processed.
- The actual funds check and reservation.

Pre-reservation (AC.RESERVATION) is a notification of an upcoming reservation on an account. A pre-reservation:

- Is a very light transaction that updates a key-only table.
- Does not check if funds are available on the account.
- Does not reserve funds on the account.

The format of the record Id is, HVTRES-AccountNo-TransactionSign-SessionNumber-Amount-UnqiueKey. The Pre-Reservation ID must be passed with the reservation request for the system to avoid lock, else it continuees to lock the HVT account during a credit check.

During credit check, the valid pre-reservations are added to the Locked Amount, which if configured is used to calculate the Credit check Balance. Any pre-reservations that exist beyond the virtual lock time are not considered for credit check and are deleted by a background service.

Consider an account with:

- Account’s working balance = 100$.
- Locked amount = 10$
- Account’s available balance = 100$ - 10$ = 90$

There are three transactions T1, T2, and T3 posted to an account A1 in three different sessions at same time for 40$,50$, and 60$. All the transactions create pre-reservations as HVTRES-A1-D-S1-40-U1, HVTRES-A1-D-S2-50-U2, and HVTRES-A1-D-S3-60-U3 respectively. When the transactions are processed,

- T1 transaction passes, as the transaction amount 40$ is covered within the account’s balance of 90$ and there are no active pre-reservations prior to this transaction.
- T2 transaction passes, as the transaction amount 50$ + pre-reservation created in S1 40$ = 90$ is within the account balance of 90$.
- T3 transaction fails, as the transaction amount 60$ + pre-reservation created in S1 40$ + pre-reservation created in S2 50$ = 150$ is greater than the account balance of 90$.

The credit check balance in the above example is calculated as shown below:

Credit check balance = Account Balance – Locked Amounts – total amount of existing active pre-reservations in the time-order, excluding the supplied pre-reservation (as the transaction amount is already subtracted).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic covers the configuration of necessary Temenos Transact applications for high volume account processing.


##### ConfiguringAC.HVT.PARAMETER

HVT are designed to be totally transparent to the bank's customers and the bank's business users. The default configuration settings delivered with the system need not be change for the majority of implementations, however the implementation team or the banks system administrators can configure and fine tune high volume processing at system and company level without changing the settings on individual accounts.

The AC.HVT.PARAMETER application provides the configuration options at system and company level, with a company level record taking precedence over the system record. The key options are to set all accounts to HVT or non HVT and then set exceptions to the default by category code range. This application is used by the system implementers and Temenos Transact database administrators to fine tune performance.

In below screenshot shows that the entire

system has been set to default for all accounts to be processed as HVT except accounts with the product category codes in range of 1000 to 4999 and 6000 to 6999, which generally equates to customer current and savings accounts.

If individual accounts need to be set opposite of AC.HVT.PARAMETER default, then Hvt Flag in the ACCOUNT record is set to the appropriate value, which takes precedence over the AC.HVT.PARAMETER settings. As an alternate, the user can set all accounts to non-HVT and then enter the product category code ranges for the HVT accounts.

5000 to 5999 for nostros and 10,000 to 19,999 for internal (that is, non customer accounts).

In a multi company environment, if certain companies have different requirements then records can be setup for those companies, which overrides the SYSTEM record.

The above example screenshot shows that for company GB0010001, the accounts in the category code range 1008 and 1009 have also been set to be processed as HVT. For example, corporate customer accounts.

The Non HVT Job field defines the jobs that can be run safely with the default HVT processing turned off. That is, the read for account balances and write to account balances bypasses the HVT processing, and updates the relevant applications directly. Then this bypasses the notional merge processing when getting account balances and updates the account balances applications directly.

> **⚠️ Note:** While using this setting, the user needs to exercise caution, as any job that runs with HVT turned off must ensure that account balances cannot be updated from any other source.

A local reporting job that runs in the system or reporting stage of the COB and reads account balances. Any account updates from non-stop processing transactions are booked as if they were entered the next day, so they do not affect the current bank day balances.


##### Configuring Account Lock Retry during Merge Service

As a part of AC.HVT.MERGE service, the following fields in the AC.HVT.PARAMETER provide flexibility for the user to configure retry values when encountering locks on EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES for Accounts.

- Max Pass Back – Specifies the maximum number of times unmerged triggers can be passed back to Batch Job Control due to a lock on the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record.
- Read Max Retry – Specifies the maximum number of retries allowed when attempting to resolve a lock on EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES .
- Sleep Lock Time – Specifies the time in seconds to wait before retrying a lock on EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES .


##### ConfiguringHVT.ACTIVE.TIME

The interval time can be defined at ACCOUNT.PARAMETER level, system AC.HVT.PARMETER level and/or company AC.HVT.PARAMETER level. If defined in all, then the following logic applies:

- System - AC.HVT.PARMETER overrides the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER level.
- Company - AC.HVT.PARMETER overrides the system AC.HVT.PARMETER level.

If not defined anywhere, then the default time is 15 minutes.

> **⚠️ Note:** A new record in AC.HVT.TRIGGER is updated only if any transaction hits the underlying account. For example, with the default merge interval of 15 minutes, if the account hits with one transaction in an hour, then only one trigger record is created and not four with each 15 minutes.

- The AC.HVT.TRIGGER table stores consolidated accounting updates with one record for each online session and active time period. The HVT merge service processes these records and merges the data into the account related tables, for example, EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES and ACCT.ACTIVITY .
- The Last Merged Time field in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES application holds the time when the balances for the HVT account is merged and updated.
- When the HVT merge service is running as online processing. That is, not in the COB, then all AC.HVT.TRIGGER records except the currently active ones are merged into the relevant account related tables and then deleted.
- If a balance request is made for an HVT account, then a notional merge takes place where the data is merged including the currently active record but no database updates take place. To balance the system performance, the merge service keeps the number of AC.HVT.TRIGGER records restricted to the currently active records, so that the notional merge process does not have to process large numbers of trigger records.
- During implementation performance testing, the HVT active time can be adjusted from the default 15 minutes to determine whether any performance benefits can be made.

The following are the exceptions to default parameterisation:

- The default HVT logic can be overwritten manually at individual account level.
- During upgrade, all the master accounts are converted as HVT by default, and the rest of the accounts that are not converted during the upgrade process follows the rules set in the new parameter design. If the account does not have any value in the Hvt Flag field, then during transaction the system decides whether HVT processing is applicable for this account based on the new parameter setup.
- If the parameter is not setup, the existing design decides the default HVT field. That is, the following accounts are only set as HVT by default and the other accounts needs to be set manually. Local currency internal accounts Position accounts Nostro accounts

The following are the exceptions to the parameter setup:

- AZ – ALL IN ONE accounts cannot be set as HVT, even if the default value in the parameter is YES, because AZ needs sub- accounting process.
- AA – Only Arrangement Accounts (AR) can be set as HVT, all other product lines are not supported.
- When account is set to have passbook, that is, saving book accounts cannot be set as HVT accounts.
- Teller cash accounts (defined in TELLER.PARAMETER ) cannot be set to HVT accounts, because there will be only one internal till account per cashier.


##### Configuring Deferred Balance Updates

This section covers the configuration of Temenos Transact applications to defer updates for an internal account. The internal account must be configured to be a High-Volume Account.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Deferred Balance Update | Switches the deferred balance updates on or off for the specific company or for all companies where ID is SYSTEM. |
| Deferred Ids To batch | Spcifies the number of pending deferred IDs to process in a transaction boundary. The default is 50. |
| Deferred Consolidate Ent | Specifies the AC.CONSOLIDATE.COND ID that is used to default the consolidation of statement entries if not defined for the account. |

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Deferred Balance Update | Switches the deferred balance updates on or off for the account. |

A TSA service is required to perform the balance and entry updates.

The AC.MERGE.STMT.ENTRY.PENDING TSA service must be running. One service per lead company is required to run the deferred updates.


##### Configuring HVT Processing for Internal Accounts

The user can configure HVT processing for internal account categories by following the below steps:

1. Set the Hvt Flag as Yes or No in the ACCOUNT application.
2. Set the Hvt Flag as Yes or No in the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application at the internal account category level. The record ID corresponds to the category code of the internal accounts that need to be enabled for HVT processing.
3. Set the Hvt Flag as Yes or No in the INTERNAL record of the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application. Temenos has released a model bank record which is available as an exception in the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application the record ID “INTERNAL”. The bank can either use this record or create a record with ID “INTERNAL”.
4. Define a specific category of internal accounts in the AC.HVT.PARAMETER application.

For internal accounts, the system processes the HVT Flag in the following sequence:

- Checks the Hvt Flag in the ACCOUNT application.
- Checks the configuration in AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT for the specific category record, if the field is blank in the ACCOUNT application. If it does not find a matching category record, it then checks if the record “INTERNAL” is available with the HVT Flag enabled.
- Checks the AC.HVT.PARAMETER configuration, if there is no specific configuration in AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT . If the internal account category is configured here, it then considers the same for HVT processing.


##### Consolidating Entries for Internal Account during HVT Processing

The user can configure the consolidation rules in AC.CONSOLIDATE.COND application and link the created rule to consolidate the entries at the following applications:

- The Consolidate Ent field in the ACCOUNT application.
- If the Hvt Flag of the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application is defined, the user can define the consolidation rule in the Consolidate Ent field of the same application. The record ID is the category code of the internal accounts to be considered for consolidating entries.
- If the Hvt Flag of the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application is defined for the “INTERNAL” record, the user can define consolidation rule in the Consolidate Ent field of the same record in the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application.
- The Consolidate Ent field in the CATEGORY application.

For internal accounts, the system processes the consolidation of entries in the following sequence:

- Checks whether the Consolidate Ent field in the ACCOUNT application is defined.
- Checks the configuration in AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT for the specific category record, if the field is blank in the ACCOUNT application. If it does not find a matching category record, it then checks if the record “INTERNAL” is available along with a value in the Consolidate Ent field.
- If the value of the Consolidate Ent field is not defaulted from AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT , the system checks for the configuration of the Consolidate Ent field in the CATEGORY application for the internal account category.

The screenshot below is an example of the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application created for a specific internal category account with the Consolidate Ent field set as CLDEFAULT and Hvt Flag field set as Yes.

The below screenshot shows that internal account USD1400300020001 created gets Hvt Flag and Consolidate Ent updated with the values from “14003” record of the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Hvt Flag and Consolidate Ent fields in AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT are applicable only for internal account categories and the “INTERNAL” record. The system uses the “INTERNAL” record to configure the default Hvt Flag decision for most internal accounts. It can create variations to this decision for specific internal account categories as separate records in the AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT application. If there is a category specific record available in AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT , when an internal account is created for the same category, the system defaults the configuration of the category record from AC.AUTO.ACCOUNT instead of the “INTERNAL” record.

For any internal account marked with the Hvt Flag as “Yes” during the time of account creation, the system defaults the Stmt Fqu field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application to “BSNSS” along with the business date. However, the bank can choose to change the Stmt Fqu field based on their requirement.

##### Configuring Pre-reservations and Skip Lock on ECB

This section explains how to configure Transact applications to consider pre-reservations and skip lock on ECB during credit check.

Configure the following fields in the AC.HVT.PARAMETER application to consider pre-reservation and skip lock on ECB.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Hvt No Lock | When set as ‘YES’, allows the debit transactions for HVT customer accounts to skip lock on ECB, provided a pre-reservation is created as part of the transaction. |
| Virtual Locked Time | Specifies the time in milliseconds until which the pre-reservation can be active in the system and can be considered during credit check. Any records that cross this time is deleted by a background service. Default time is 500 ms. |

##### Check for Sufficient Balance before Debiting an Account

The system provides a series of flexible options that allow the bank to control the ability to apply a fund availability check when processing HVT transactions.

- For any customer account that is not identified as requiring HVT processing, the system default behavior is to perform a funds availability check before a posting is made. For any debit movement the system makes a check for available funds. For non-HVT accounts there is no option provided to make the check optional.
- For any internal account not identified as requiring HVT processing the system does not perform a funds availability check before posting.
- The Temenos Transact business applications have a fixed behavior determined by its business rules that control whether failure of a funds availability check results in the cancelling of the transaction, warning the user or force the movement through.

- For internal accounts that are identified as requiring HVT processing there is no option provided to allow a funds availability check. Funds availability is never checked for internal accounts of any type.
- For customer accounts that are flagged for HVT processing, the bank is able to specify whether debit movements are required to perform a funds check. The bank is able to define the following options: By default all debit movements require a funds check. By default all debit movements do not require a funds check.
- These options can be defined at the system and company level.


##### Check for Sufficient Balance when Performing Funds Reservation for Payment Request Through TPS

This topic covers the process in checking the sufficient balance when performing funds reservation for payment request through TPS.

- The Temenos TPS product has a separate funds check step in the payment process that results in the reservation of funds if the funds are available.
- Based on the type of payment transaction that is processed this step can be configured.
- If the payment transaction type requires a funds check and reservation, the funds availability checking process ensures that any pending movements across an HVT account are included. When the funds availability check is performed, the system locks the account exclusively for the process that is performing the check. This ensures that the funds availability checked always include the latest movements and it is accurate as funds availability checking is sequential.

- For HVT customer accounts, the system provides additional flexibility so that the bank can define exceptions to the default behavior to check funds availability.
- It is possible to define which type of posting identified by the transaction code are exceptions to the default rule.
- It is possible to define which type of posting identified by an external code supplied from the source application are exceptions to the default rule.
- The ability to specify an external identifying code is added to the Temenos Transact generic accounting interface. This is used by some of the bank’s SEPA interface and other posting interfaces to allow the source application which indicates whether the posting requires a funds availability check for specific type of movement.
- The SEPA interface processes the requests for refund of direct debits from the creditor accounts held in Temenos Transact . These types of request are processed irrespective of the availability of funds and the account is always debited and does not require a funds check. These direct debit refund transactions indicate the type of posting to consider if the availability check is required or not.

For credit movements posted to an HVT account there is no option to provide a funds availability check as crediting an account does not require funds availability check.


##### Perform Standard Temenos Transact Funds Availability Check

This topic covers the funds availability check for HVT accounts.

The system determines if a funds availability check is required for each movement raised for the account. If the funds availability check is required, the system follows the standard Temenos Transact funds availability check process based on the configuration of the account product and account system.

Apart from allowing the funds availability check to be optionally controlled for an account set as HVT, additional requirement is not raised for the existing Temenos Transact funds availability check process, and all existing options are supported. This includes:

- The available amounts from any credit line associated with the account.
- The impact of any locked amounts or reservation from other transactions.
- The impact of unauthorised debit from other Temenos Transact transactions.

If a payment transaction is required to make a funds availability check, it follows the standard Temenos Transact funds availability check process. There is no additional requirement above the standard process.


##### Display Accurate Current Balance and Related Account Movements

This topic covers the current balance and related movements of HVT accounts. When an account is flagged as HVT, the actual updates to the account are deferred to a background service which takes place periodically. This means that if the account and related records are viewed directly they may not reflect all the latest movements processed as the update is still pending.

The user can view the correct balance in real-time and the movements that have caused the balance to be updated for any HVT flagged account. This ability is provided for the standard Temenos Transact account enquiries, to reflect the pending updates to the account balance. The same capability is available to locally developed queries and views by using the standard method to access the account balance delivered with Temenos Transact .


##### Generate SWIFT Standard Statements

Temenos Transact supports the ability to generate standard SWIFT statements for any account. This includes accounts that are flagged as HVT.

MT940 or MT950 statements are generated for any account including HVT accounts. The statement contains all entries raised as a result of processing Temenos Transact transactions. The system ensures that all movements for HVT accounts pending update are applied before the statement is generated.

An intraday MT942 SWIFT statement is generated for any account, including those that are flagged as HVT. This is produced on manual request, based on a timed frequency or on receipt of an MT920 request.

The statement contains all movements that are processed across the account at the time of receiving the request. This includes any movements for HVT accounts that are pending at the time of generating the request.


##### Updating Deferred Balance

This section explains the working of deferred balance updates.

1. The AC.HVT.PARAMETER application is configured for deferred balance updates.

1. Internal account is configured for deferred balance updates.
2. A transaction is processed to credit a customer account and debit the internal account.

1. The entry for the customer account is processed and created.

1. Internal account entry is deferred and AC.STMT.ENTRY.PENDING is updated.

1. AC.HVT.TRIGGER is not updated for the internal account.

1. The background service picks up the entry and processes it. A record in STMT.ENTRY is created and the balances of the internal account are updated (other associated updates are done).
2. The STMT.ENTRY has Deferred Status as Posted.


##### Ability to perform Credit Check by considering Pre-Reservations

This section explains the working of credit check on an HVT account by considering pre-reservation created in another session.

To perform credit check by considering pre-reservations,

1. Set the Do Check and the Hvt No Lock fields in the AC.HVT.PARAMETER application as ‘Yes’.
2. Consider an account with a working balance and set the Hvt Flag as 'Yes'. The pre-reservation is created by the application that initiated the transaction.
3. Post the payment order transaction, after which it considers the created pre-reservation and performs credit check. Working balance = 1000$ Transaction amount = 1000$ Pre-reservation = 100$ Credit check balance = 1000$ - 1000$ - 100$ = -100$. This results in failure as the transaction tries to withdraw 100$ more than the available balance. The Payment Order considers the pre-reservation and throws an override as shown below.

#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact has the functionality to lock funds on an account (also known as blocked or held amounts). Defined amounts can be locked for specified periods of time, with an override when a transaction takes an account below the value of the locked funds.


##### Understanding Future Dated Debit and Credit Reservations

Based on the configuration , the user can include or exclude future dated debit and credit reservations while determining the available or usable balance of an account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration


##### Configuring Credit Reservation

Credit Reservation of expected credit takes place through AC.LOCKED.EVENT . A credit check balance, the CREDIT.RESERVE record provides the user the option to include credit reservations in the available balance calculation.


##### Configuring Merchant Return

The transaction code used in the OFS Clearing message indicates if the respective credit reservation is to be considered as merchant return or not.

The merchant return-specific transactions are configured using the Merchant Flag field in the TRANSACTION application.

The allowed values are:

- Yes – A credit reservation associated with this transaction code is considered as merchant return. Credit Reservation Balance and Available Balance are affected by a merchant return reservation.
- No or Blank – A credit reservation associated with this transaction code is not considered as merchant return. Credit Reservation Balance and Available Balance are updated by a reservation using this transaction code.


##### Configuring Future Dated Debit and Credit Reservations

The user decides if the future dated debit and credit reservations must be considered for calculating the available or usable balance of an account using Lock Reserve Condition in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM . This field allows the following values.

| Field Value | Description |
|---|---|
| lock.funds.date | Indicates that only Active* debit reservations or debit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of an account. |
| credit.reserve.date | Indicates that only Active* credit reservations or credit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of an account. |

Active* - Indicates the reservations or locked events with From Date as the current date or previous date.

This is an optional configuration. The user can set any of the above values, both, or Null in Lock Reserve Condition . This configuration applies to component and non-component based credit check accounts.


##### Configuring AC Locked Event Type

Users can do the below configurations in the AC.LOCKED.EVENT.TYPE application.

| Field Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Account Link | If the user selects: Yes – Block is propagated to accounts. The propagation of funds reservation is related to the Parent Account and Linked Ac No fields in the ACCOUNT property. No – Funds are blocked only on a single account where the transaction is applied. |
| Check Notice | Allows the user to check any existing withdrawal notice request for the arrangement. |
| Expiry Type | Start of Day – Locked Amount is released at the next start of the day after the expiry date. Close of Business – Locked Amount is released on the expiry date before the close of business process. |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Block or Unblock Funds (Corporate)

Temenos Transact provides control over locked amounts, with each amount being recorded as an EVENT in the AC.LOCKED.EVENTS application, which stores the details of each amount to be locked for an account with start and end date.

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

Account is an integral part of banking business. The functional components of the Account (AC) module involves the creation, maintenance and closure of accounts. The AC and Interest and Charges (IC) module together caters the creation, maintenance and control of all types of accounts handled by Temenos core banking.

Temenos Transact AC module is Non-Stop (NS module) compatible. If NS module is installed, the account balances are updated real-time to ensure that the latest transaction impact is fully included from the customer perspective. Read Non-Stop Processing User Guide for more information on the specific applications compatible with NS processing.


##### Product Configuration

This topic covers the setup and usage of the applications used in AC module.

| Field Name | Usage |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash Flow Days | Specifies the number of calendar days forward for which the cash flow balances are to be maintained for the purpose of accounting overrides and cash flow processing. The number of days entered here determines the window period that cash flow balances are to be maintained on each account record. Each forward dated entry generated for an account impacts the cash flow balances, if the date of the entry falls within this period. If the number of days entered is 10, then any forward dated entry raised online that has the value date less than 10 calendar days from current date will update the accounts cash flow balances. If this update causes either a limit to be exceeded or an unauthorised overdraft to occur, then an override message appears on the transaction input. All entries raised online that fall outside the window do not update the account balances immediately and no override messages appear. But when their value dates fall within the window, the start of day process (SOD.CASH.FLOW) updates the account cash flow balances. If an exception occurs at this stage, then the CASH.FLOW.EXCEPTION table is updated to indicate this. If the value is not entered in this field, then only the nostro accounts have cash flow maintained and a default of 10 calendar days is used for this. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Value Dated Acctng | A switch to set value dated accounting as On or Off or Trade Dated General Ledger (TDGL). If a value dated accounting system is required, then this field must be set to Y. In trade dated accounting system, the cash based transactions update the customer’s account and the bank’s position on the date in which the transaction is processed in the system, irrespective of the value date assigned to the transaction. In value dated accounting system, the cash based transactions update the customer’s account and the bank’s position on the value date assigned to the transaction. It is held as off balance sheet until the value date. In TDGL accounting system, the cash based transactions update the customer’s account and the bank’s position on the value date assigned to the transaction. It is held under payable or receivable until the value date. Cash based transactions follow the accounting treatment based on this setup. However, the accounting treatment can be switched from one system to another and the system permits any of the following switch. Switching of Accounting System Treatment of cash based transactions can be switched from one system to another, any combination of the setup is possible. Original Accounting Setup Target Accounting Setup Trade dated Value dated Trade dated Trade dated GL Value dated Trade dated Value dated Trade dated GL Trade dated GL Trade dated Trade dated GL Value dated The new accounting system switch applies to new transactions only. The existing cash based transactions with a future date follows the setup applied when the transaction were raised. The Tdgl Details field in the STMT.ENTRY application holds the details of the accounting method followed for the transaction. Exceptions to the above is SEC.TRADE – Actual Settlement: If contract input is in existing setup and authorised in the modified setup, then the system follows the modified setup. | Original Accounting Setup | Target Accounting Setup | Trade dated | Value dated | Trade dated | Trade dated GL | Value dated | Trade dated | Value dated | Trade dated GL | Trade dated GL | Trade dated | Trade dated GL | Value dated |

| Trade dated GL | Value dated |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Use Pay Receive | This field is used to flag the suspense processing at system Level, in the case of value dated or TDGL accounting setup. Under these accounting setup, the value of the transaction is suspended in a temporary account till the split value date is reached. The allowed values are : Yes – Suspended to GL accounts pay or receive as special entries and reported as on-balance sheet item in the general ledger (GL) report. No – This is the default setup where the suspense processing posts the entry to the internal suspense account. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Pay Rec Allwd | This field works in conjunction with Use Pay Receive . It is used when a customer wants to decide if payable or receivable are to be reported with account attributes or against underlying customer attributes based PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE application. Value in this field should be valid record ID of AC.DEFINE.PAY.RECV.ALLOWED application. This field is available at different levels such as System level, System Id (sub-system) level, Category level and System ID with Category level. In the AC.DEFINE.PAY.RECV.ALLOWED application, the users can create their own records using any of the following options in the Pay Recv Options field. The ID of the application record can be a meaningful alpha-numeric name. Broker – This option decides the customer to whom the payable or receivable is to be booked in the PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . If this option is set, the payable or receivable is booked against the third party customer (for example, broker) passed from the application. If this option is not set, the payable or receivable is booked against the customer passed in the original entry from the underlying application. Contract – If this option is selected, all the payables or receivables are reported under the PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . Customer – If the target account passed from the underlying application is a customer account and the Customer option is set, then the payables or receivables are reported under PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . Internal – This option works similar to Use Pay Recv set to Yes. If the entry is posted as an internal (suspense) account and the target account is passed from the application, then the original STMT entry to internal (suspense) account is converted to special entry with asset type as PAYSUS or RECEIVESUS. Nostro – If the target account passed from the underlying application is a NOSTRO account, and the Customer option is set, then the payables or receivables are reported under PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . NULL – If no option is set, then the system continues to work as usual. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Val Date Sys Id; Val Date By Sys ; Use Pay Rec Sys | Enables the definition of accounting treatment for specific cash-based applications, where it is different from the default accounting treatment. If the default accounting system is trade dated, for the application mentioned in Val Date Sys Id , a different accounting system can be defined. For example, if SEC.TRADE is to follow TDGL accounting system, the Val Date Sys Id is defined as SCTR and Val Date By Sys is defined as TDGL. The Use Pay Rec Sys field can be flagged as Yes or No, which is used in the suspense processing for the specific application. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Vd Cat Start; Vd Cat End; Val Date By Cat; Use Pay Rec Cat | Enables the definition of accounting treatment for specific category or range of categories, where it is different from the default accounting treatment and application specific (if defined) accounting treatment. The category level definition takes precedence over the system level and application level definition. The Use Pay Rec Cat field can be set to Yes or No, which is used in the suspense processing for the specific category. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Vd Cat Sys Id; Vd Cat Sys Start; Vd Cat Sys End; Val Date By Cat Sys; Use Pay Receive Cat Sys | If the accounting system for specific categories of an application is different from the default accounting system, it can be setup using these set of fields. The application can be defined in Vd Cat Sys Id , the category or range of categories can be defined in the Vd Cat Sys Start and Vd Cat Sys End fields. The accounting system applicable to this setup are defined in the Val Date By Cat Sys field. The Use Pay Receive Cat Sys field can be set to Yes or No, which is used in the suspense processing for the specific category. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Entry Category; Sus Category; Suspense Txn In; Suspense Txn Out; Suspense History | The format of Entry Category can either be CATEGORY-FX.POS.TYPE or CATEGORY, which determines the suspense account to be used when operating in a value dated accounting system. If the position type for the Entry Category does not exist, then the entry category alone is used to determine the suspense category. Else, the default suspense category is used. When a split value dated transaction is processed in a value dated accounting system then the first leg is balanced against a suspense account. This is washed out when the second leg reaches its value date. The suspense account that is used is determined by the category of the second leg entry. The Entry Category field and its associated field Sus Category defines this relationship. Example XX.1 ENTRY.CATEGORY YY.1 SUS.CATEGORY 19998 XX.2 ENTRY.CATEGORY 5000-XX YY.2 SUS.CATEGORY 19999 Entry Category is a start of range value. Hence in this example, second leg entries with a category in the range 0 - 4999 uses account LCL199980001 (where LCL is the local currency code) and entries with a category 5000 and above uses LCL199990001 for suspense processing. To define a default suspense account for all the entries, configure as shown below: XX.1 ENTRY.CATEGORY YY.1 SUS.CATEGORY 19998 The purpose of defining different suspense category is to allow the splitting of suspense movements, for value dated accounting, within the CRB. For example, it is possible to report suspense entries for nostro accounts separately from suspense entries for current accounts. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sys Code; Nostro Default; Def Override; Use First Acct; Default Order | These set of fields are used for defaulting the settlement nostro account applicable to the transaction defined in the Sys Code field. The Sys Code field is a combination of Application-Nature of transaction, for example, LD-PRIN or LD-INT. These values must be defined upfront in AC.SYS.CODES application. The Nostro Default field is used to specify how settlement accounts are defaulted when using a nostro account for the associated Sys Code . A null value implies that the nostro account is always defaulted. The following are the options in this field: AGENCY – Defaults only when agency conditions exist. NONE – No nostro account is to be defaulted. The Def Override field defines whether an override is required when the default account number does not match the account number entered on the deal. Additionally, if the account with bank, intermediary bank or beneficiary account number differs from the default derived from the information on the agency file, then an override is raised if this field is set to Yes. The Use First Acct field defines whether an account is to be defaulted when more than one possible default account exists. The following options are available in this field: Yes – First account of the customer in any company is defaulted. No – If more than one account is present in the current company, then no defaulting takes place. In a multi-book setup, the following additional options are available for this field: CUR – First account of the customer in current company is only defaulted. FRS – First account of the customer in the current company as first choice followed by first available account in any company is defaulted. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Cheque Register; Chq Dep Txn; Def Coll Susp; Chq Col Txn; Chq Ret Txn; Def Ret Susp; Return Txns; Return Susp Cat | The Cheque Register field indicates whether or not the cheque issue and management functionality within Temenos Transact has been activated. The Yes or No value entered in this field controls the defaulting of cheque type in DATA CAPTURE (DC) or FUNDS TRANSFER (FT) or TELLER (TT) application as well as payment stop processing. The list of transaction code for cheque on collection, clearing and returned cheque and the corresponding suspense accounts where the value of cheque needs to be parked in the clearing process can be defined in these set of fields. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Net Od Appl; Net Od Override; Net Locked Override | The Net Od Appl field specifies the Temenos Transact application for which debit and credit entries to an account in a transaction must be netted for displaying the overdraft and cash flow overrides. The allowed applications are LOANS AND DEPOSITS (LD), TELLER (TT), COLLATERAL (CO), FUNDS TRANSFER (FT), ARRANGEMENT ARCHITECTURE (AA) or ALL. When this field is set to ALL, the functionality is applied for all transaction irrespective of the application. The pre-condition for the suppression of overrides is to set the Net Od Override field as Yes. If Net Od Appl holds the value ALL, the system does not permit any other multi-value to be input. Either applications are manually input in a multi-value block or ALL value is used. For example, if the Net Od Appl field is set to ALL and the Net Od Override field is set to Yes and a transaction is made using the same account as both debit and credit account, no override is generated for any excess amount. Suppression of Unnecessary Overrides: If a single contract creates both credits and debits to an account, if the net effect of the contract is to credit the account, it is possible to suppress the override generated for the debit side of the transaction. Example If a discounted loan is arranged for a customer, whereby the customer has a balance of £10, receives a credit of $1000 for the loan, but also a debit of $100 for the upfront payment of interest. The system usually generates an override specifying that the customer is debited $100 and the customer is being overdrawn by $90. However, it is possible by configuring the Net Od Appl as LD and Net Od Override fields as Yes in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER to net off the differences, so as the credit of $1000 exceeds the debit of $100 and the override is suppressed. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Retain Ac Balances | Defines whether balances need to be maintained in ACCOUNT or not. When set to Yes the balances are updated in ACCOUNT and EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES . When set to N the balances are not updated in ACCOUNT , but updated only in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES . Default value is Yes. Changing this setup from Yes to No clears the existing account balances automatically. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Booked Balance | Defines which booked balance is recorded in the STMT.ENTRY record when the transaction is booked. The following are the options available in this field. Online Actual Bal – Records the account balance from the GL perspective, this means that future dated movements are not included. Traded Dated Gl Bal – Records the account balance from a customer perspective, which means that future dated movements recorded as PAY or RECEIVE are included. The enhanced transaction search uses the value in this field to display the output in Booked Balance column of the enquiries |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

- Residence
- Sector
- Language

- Status
- Joint holder’s name
- Signature(s)

The operating currency is the currency in which the account is operated. It must be one of the currencies defined in CURRENCY application. Once the account is authorised, the currency cannot be changed as the balances of the account is maintained in this currency. In other words, the account holder can make or receive payments in any currency other than the operating currency but when the account balance is updated for these payments, it is converted into the operating currency of the account.

The operating currency of account 84506 is EUR. If the customer wants to make a payment to the beneficiary in USD from the account 84506, it is possible. The balance in account 84506 would be impacted to the extent of EUR equivalent of the payment amount in USD.

The account specific interest and charge conditions are defined in the ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT (ADI), ACCOUNT.CREDIT.INT (ACI) and ACCT.CAPITALISATION applications. The ID format of this application is - . For example, 12165-20170321.

Bank may want to specify a differential interest and charge condition for specific accounts in the group. For such accounts, the interest and charge conditions can be defined in the ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT and ACCOUNT.CREDIT.INT applications. This supersedes the conditions defined at the group level.

On a later date, if the account has to be reverted to the group specific conditions, the Interest Day Basis field in the ADI or ACI record must be set to GENERAL. This change is effective from the date on the ID of the ADI or ACI record. Similarly, some account holders may request for an interest capitalisation date different from that of the group. For such accounts, the interest capitalisation date and frequency can be defined in ACCT.CAPITALISATION application.

##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as ‘Yes’, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Account Funds Authorization (ACFA) table.

| deposits.updatefundsAuthorization.fundsAuthorizationRejected | Event to be emitted when bank user rejects funds authorisation for deposits |


##### Archival of Account and Related Tables

The closed account and the related data can be archived using the Transact Standard archival or Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) archival.

The DL module must be installed for the user to initiate the archival service to archive the closed account and the related data records to a Read-only (RO) database. Otherwise, the user moves the data records to the $ARC file using the Standard archival method. If the closed account crosses Retention Period (defined in ARCHIVE ), it is archived along with the related data. The retention period is calculated from the closure date of the account.

A sample screenshot of ARCHIVE for the ACCOUNT record is shown below.

When Retention Period ends and the user runs the archival service, the files mentioned in Arc Filename are archived.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user must set Archive Data as Y to archive the record. If the user sets it as N, the record is deleted instead of archiving, which results in loss of data.

Read Archiving for more details regarding Transact Standard archival process. Read Data Life Cycle Management for more details regarding DLM Archiving process.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level specifications required for ACCOUNT .

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | ACCOUNT.PARAMETER | It has the information pertaining to cash flow, accounting method, generation of alternate identifier to account number, account level balance maintenance, netting and cheque issue management and so on. |
| 2. | CUSTOMER | To create a user account, the account holder should be registered as a customer in Temenos Transact . The information like name, address, age, residence, sector, language, industry, signature and so on, pertaining to the user is captured in the application. |
| 3. | CATEGORY | Based on the business needs, category codes defined in Temenos Transact has to classify financial transactions. Use of the codes together with personal customer characteristics enables the bank to produce balance sheets and returns reflecting a coordinated and structured view of its operation, by directing business transactions to their appropriate report. |
| 4. | CURRENCY | It allows the user to capture the operating currency of the account and it should be a record or value in the currency application. Account currency cannot be changed once the account is authorised as the balances are maintained in the currency. |
| 5. | ACCT.GEN.CONDITION | It allows the user to define the grouping condition for accounts for which the same conditions of interests and charges apply. Based on the business needs, category codes along with CUSTOMER attributes like Sector and Residence enable grouping of accounts. These attributes and their order of priority is defined in CONDITION.PRIORITY application for ACCOUNT record. |
| 6. | ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION | It allows the user to define the rules for accounts belonging to a group and specific currency mentioned in the table. Some examples for rules defined are Notice withdrawals, account violations, deferring interest and charges, rounding rules for interest and premium interest, automatic IBAN generation and so on. |
| 7. | ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT | It allows the user to define special debit interest conditions when the corresponding group interest conditions are not suitable. The user can define Interest to be calculated on daily, average using value dated balance and interest rate to fixed or linked to basic rates. |
| 8. | ACCOUNT.CREDIT.INT | It allows the user to define special credit interest conditions when the corresponding group credit interest conditions are not suitable. Credit interest rates can be specified for different balance levels. Rates can apply to the entire balance or a part between the two-balance levels. |
| 9. | ACCT.CAPITALISATION | It allows the user to specify the next date and subsequent frequency of application of debit and credit interest capitalisation for a specific account. |
| 10. | GROUP.DEBIT.INT | It allows the user to specify the calculation method of debit interest for a group of accounts and provides the link to the GENERAL.CHARGE , where the charges applicable to the same groups of accounts are specified. The user can also specify negative interest and tax on interest. |
| 11. | GROUP.CREDIT.INT | It allows the user to specify the calculation method of credit interest for groups of accounts. The user can also specify second interest on the account with different capitalisation frequency. |
| 12. | GROUP.CAPITALISATION | It allows the user to specify the next date and subsequent frequency of application of debit and credit interest capitalisation for a group of accounts. |
| 13. | ACCOUNT.CLASS | It allows the user to define the account class records, which can be used by other Temenos Transact applications to construct account number or to check the account number for a particular group. |
| 14. | ACCOUNT.ACCRUAL | At company level, it provides the system with information on how and when to process accruals of interests and charges on customer accounts. Accrual process can be specified at Account Category and Account Group for which the associated interest accrual parameters are defined. |
| 15. | SAVINGS.PREMIUM | It enables the user to pay premium on the savings deposits if the savings account qualify the eligibility criteria defined in this table. |
| 16. | AC.FUNDS.DIVERSION.PARAM | The funds diversion is setup from the off-balance sheet Transaction Account to the on-balance sheet Diversion Account. The system provides flexible options that allows the bank to control the ability to suppress the funds diversion processing for specific transactions for Transaction accounts setup for funds diversion. The bank will be able to define the following options for funds diversion: The default funds diversion behaviour. To suppress Funds Diversion processing for specific activities by mentioning or defining the associated transactions code as an exception to the default rule. |
| 17. | ACSWIT.PARAMETER | This parameter table stores the validity period decided by the bank for the switch out service. The validity period can be defined in days or months. The ID of this record represents the Temenos Transact Company ID. |
| 18. | DDA.SERVICE.PARAMETER | This table helps the bank to decide whether the payment made by the account holder in a specific currency is allowed or not. Also, enables the Bank to change the core decision for Account Currency and to return the Payment Currency. |
| 19. | AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM | This table helps to parameterise the accounting related processes based on the Max No Of Splits defined. |
