### 1.22  NSF ExceptionProcessing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Non-sufficient funds (NSF) is the status of an account that does not have enough money to cover debit transactions. If a bank receives a debit item on an account with insufficient funds, the bank can pay or refuse payment and charge the account holder an appropriate fee.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PRD.DES.BALANCE.AVAILABILITY`, `AC.ACCOUNT.LINK`, `AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM`, `AC.BALANCE.COMPONENT`, `AC.CASH.POOL`, `AC.CREDIT.CHECK`, `AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION`, `AC.NSF.ACFA.XREF` ... +6 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Aaa Chg Amt*, *Aaa For*, *Act Credit Check*, *Action*, *Activity Class*, *Auth*, *Bal*, *Balance* ... +80 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Non-sufficient funds (NSF) is the status of an account that does not have enough money to cover debit transactions. If a bank receives a debit item on an account with insufficient funds, the bank can pay or refuse payment and charge the account holder an appropriate fee.

There are different facilities that are checked by the bank before declaring an item as NSF.

- Typically, banks provide a small amount, up to which the account can be overdrawn to post a debit item and there is no charge for posting the item. This is referred to as grace limit.
- If the checking account customer has multiple accounts with the bank like savings, investment and line of credit, and also has a setup of sweeping facility to cover the checking account, then the bank considers the balance available in the linked accounts to post the debit item. This is referred to as overdraft protection.
- For certain accounts, banks can pre-approve an overdraft limit, up to which the account can be overdrawn depending on the customer’s choice to OPT-IN or OPT-OUT. This is called a courtesy overdraft limit. There are regulations in place, which protect the customer from processing charges on electronic transactions. In case of certain bank configured electronic transactions (ATM and debit card purchase), the customer can specify if a courtesy overdraft has to be used to post the transaction or not.

In Temenos Transact , the NSF processing is enabled for Arrangement Accounts (AR Accounts).The NSF processing covers the following functionalities:

- Configurable available balance for NSF credit check.
- OD processing for AR Accounts using NSF functionality.
- Pooling funds (sweep) for credit checks.
- Opt-In or Opt-Out of limit facility for credit check.
- NSF exception handling.
- Assessment of NSF item and decision management.
- NSF closing evaluation process.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic covers the system usage of NSF exception processing.


##### Balance Components –AC.BALANCE.COMPONENT

The AC.BALANCE.COMPONENT application defines the balance components that can be configured for the NSF credit check. These balance components are classified as BASE and OPTION.

This application can only be viewed and cannot be modified as they are released and maintained by Temenos. The balance components can be used to configure the available balance for credit check during the NSF processing. The below screenshot shows the list of balance components released by Temenos.


##### Configuring the Available Balance –AC.CREDIT.CHECK

This AC.CREDIT.CHECK application creates different combinations of balance components, which can be used in credit check processing when the transaction is initiated.

It gives the flexibility to define and use different balance components for credit checking based on the transaction or activity.

This is configured in two parts.

This type is a mandatory single value field and should be defined with one of the base type balance components released by Temenos (in AC.BALANCE.COMPONENT ).

This type is an optional multi-value field which allows the bank to configure any number of option type balance components released by Temenos (in AC.BALANCE.COMPONENT ).

The below screen shot shows an example of AC.CREDIT.CHECK , which is used to define the Base balance type as WORKING and Option balance types as SWEEP and LOCK.FUNDS.


##### NSF Exception Processing Parameter –NSF.PARAMETER

This parameter is a pre-requisite for NSF processing.

The information pertaining to the order of processing the debit and credit items to the account, settlement types, expiry date and default decisions for the respective settlement types is configured in this parameter application.

The NSF.PARAMETER can be defined at the system or company level. In the absence of company specific parameter, the system level configuration is used.

The order of processing debit and credit items to the checking account is configured in the Order field. It is defaulted to Creditdebit, which indicates that the credit items to be processed first and the debit items to be processed in the order of time. The other option is Time, which indicates that the credits and debits are to be processed in the order of time.

The fields from Settle Type to Chrg Negotiable is a set of associated fields which defines the default rules for funds decision for approval, rejection and reversal. The usage of these fields are described in the below table.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Settle Type | The possible values in the field are: PTL (Payed Through Limits) – Account balance including transaction amount is within the limit available at the time of posting the entry. POL (Payed Outside Limit) – Either account balance including transaction amount is in excess of the limit available at the time of posting the entry or the limit is not applicable (Opt-Out) for the respective debit transaction or activity. SET (Automatic Settlement) – Force settled with NSF. This debit transaction or activity is forced to be settled at the activity class definition. |
| Expiry Days | Indicates the cut-off period for manual decision making. This is the number of days within which the bank user should either approve or reject the NSF item and negotiate the NSF fee or charge. If the decision is not actioned manually, the default decision (if defined in the NSF parameter) applies on the COB of the expiry date of the NSF exception item. |
| Def Fund Decision | Hold the value approved or rejected. |
| Fund Decision Upd | Hold the value system or manual, to indicate the fund decision update. |
| Fund Deci Approve Act; Fund Deci Rej Act; Rev Approve Act; Rev Rej Act | Arrangement activity to be triggered for the default decision processing for fund approval/rejection or reversal approval/rejection. |
| Charge Negotiable | Hold the value YES or NO, to indicate if the NSF fee or charge is negotiable. |
| NSF Decision Hook | Configure the user exit routine to overrule the rule-based NSF decisioning of account transactions. |
| NSF Start Balance | Indicates the starting balance that must be used when calculating the accounts available balance used for the NSF evaluation process. It belongs to a set of associated fields. The allowed values are: Open.booked Open.valued If there is no value defined, Open.valued is the default value. |
| NSF Balance Type | Defines the inclusion of active debit holds and active credit holds in the available balance calculation during the NSF Evaluation process. It belongs to a set of associated fields. The allowed values are: Lock.funds Credit.reserve If there is no value defined, the available balance is calculated by including all the balance components. |
| NSF Lock Reserve Condition | The allowed values are: Lock.funds.date - Includes active debit locked events Credit.reserve.date - Includes active credit locked events. If there is no value defined for the associated balance type, the system refers the definition in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM . |
| NSF Process Type | The allowed value is: Exclude.return - Excludes the debit transaction amount from calculating the running balance when the default decision of the entry is set as RETURN or REJECT. |


##### NSF Exception Processing Parameter –NSF.PARAMETER

To enable the Grace Period NSF Charge Waiver process, the user must configure the required fields in NSF.PARAMETER as shown below.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Grace Period Type | Indicates the balance cure method applied when Grace Period functionality is enabled. The supported values are: Full – The account must have an available balance and tolerance greater or equal to 0 for the NSF charges to be waived. Partial – Each NSF exception is evaluated to determine if the positive movement of the available balance is sufficient to cover that item. |
| Grace Start Balance | Indicates the starting balance used for calculating the accounts available balance (used for grace period waiver). The allowed values are: Actual.booked - Indicates the account’s booked balance for today. A transaction is considered booked once it is completed and the balances are updated. Transactions with a forward processing date (for example, non-stop transactions entered at the close of business) are not included in this balance until the bank’s system date matches the processing date of the transaction. Actual.value - Indicates the account’s value-dated balance for today, which is used for interest calculation. Transactions with a forward value date are not included in today’s value-dated balance until the specified value date arrives. If the balance is not defined, then Actual.value is considered as the default value. |
| Grace Balance Type | Indicates the debit locked events and credit locked events are included when calculating the account available balances used for grace period waiver. The supported values are Lock.funds and Credit.reserve. The user can select one or both the options. |
| Grace Locked Reserve Condition | Indicates if current day’s active locked events should be used or if the maximum or minimum amounts should be used when debit locked events and credit locked events are included in the account available balance calculation. The supported values are Lock.funds.date and Credit.reserve.date. The user can select one or both the options. If the field is left blank for the associated Grace Balance Type , then the system uses the setting defined in Lock Reserve Condition in AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM as default. |


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the workflow of Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) exception processing.


##### NSF Transaction workflow inTemenos Transact

The NSF transaction workflow is shown in the below screenshot.

- In a transaction workflow, the system checks if the account has sufficient balance to post the debit item presented.
- The system makes use of the respective balance component depending on the type of transaction presented for credit check.
- If funds are available, the transaction is posted.
- In case of insufficient funds, the system allows the transaction to be processed. This is to allow customers to make deposits until Close of Business (COB) to their account and cover the overdraft balance.
- The system checks for limits based on Opt-In or Opt-Out chosen by the customer and exceptions are created only for accounts that have overdrawn balance in excess of limit.
- NSF exceptions are created for each transaction that is breaching the limit and represent the whole transaction amount, not just the overdrawn amount.
- The NSF exception items are assessed for charges and the account officer can negotiate the charges, if allowed.


##### Overdraft Processing Using NSF Functionality

The NSF functionality is available only for Arrangement Accounts (AR module).

The specific fields for NSF processing should be defined in the BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property class. The fields are detailed below:

- The Overdraft Processing field should be set to Yes, to process the debit items to the account based on NSF functionality.
- The Credit Check field should be defined as Component, to consider the balance components for credit checking during the transaction processing.
- The fields from Activity Class to OD Charge Action is a set of associated fields, which defines the rules for the activity defined in the activity class. Activity Class and On Activity – Defines the arrangement activity class or activity that is triggered by the transaction processing. Act Credit Check – The balance components that needs to be checked during the credit check processing for this specific activity. This should be a valid record in AC.CREDIT.CHECK application. Limit Check – Checks whether limit check is to be carried out or not. If the Opt-in option is chosen, limit check is performed. If Opt-out or Blocked option is given, limit check is not performed during the transaction processing. Overdrawn Action – Defines the action to be performed by the system for the given activity or activity class, in the event of insufficient funds while performing balance check. The possible values are Post, Reject or Settle. OD Charge Action – Checks whether the activity should be assessed for charges or the charges are waived. The possible values are Assess or Waive.

An example of BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property class is shown in the below screen shot.

Based on the above screenshot, the transaction that triggers the ACCOUNTS-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT activity class:

- Performs the credit check based on the balance components configured in the AC.CREDIT.CHECK for DEBIT.ARR.
- If the Limit Check field is defined as Opt-In, then the transaction considers the limit available to the account if the balance components are not sufficient to cover the transaction amount.
- After limit check, if the account balance still remains overdrawn, it gets posted (#Overdrawn.Action) with the override message 'Overdraft on Account &1 for &2 &3', (where, &1 is account that is overdrawn, &2 is the currency of the overdrawn account and &3 is current overdrawn amount for the account, calculated based on the credit check setup for the transaction). The debit item is updated in the NSF exception application ( AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION ) in IHLD status.
- If the OD Charge Action field is set as Assess, then this transaction is assessed for applying NSF charges.


##### Optional Balance Components

The following optional balance components are supported while performing the credit check along with the base balance, during the NSF processing.

- SWEEP
- FLOAT
- FORWARD.OPTION
- LOCK.FUNDS
- TDGL
- SHADOW
- SUPPRESS.CREDIT.PROJECTIONS

One or more optional balance components can be added to the base balance component for credit check in AC.CREDIT.CHECK and linked to the appropriate arrangement activity or transaction.

Retail sweeping is normally performed during COB. However, if sweep is included as one of the optional balances for credit check in AC.CREDIT.CHECK , then the balance available in the linked accounts are shared with the checking account during the online transaction processing.

The following fields in AC.ACCOUNT.LINK should be configured appropriately, to share the balances for online transaction processing.

- Yes – Represents that balances can be shared across accounts involved in sweep during transaction processing.
- No/Null – Represents that balance are not shared during online transaction processing.

- Full – The amount to be swept must be covered in full using only one of the linked accounts.
- Partial – More than one linked account can collectively donate the balance required for passing a transaction.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Shared Balance can be set to Yes only for maintenance sweep. The linked (donor) account cannot be a receiver account in another AC.ACCOUNT.LINK or corporate cash pool through the AC.CASH.POOL application.

Account A is the checking account having Account B and Account C, as linked accounts for sweeping funds in case of shortfall.

A debit transaction is processed for Account A for USD 100. Account A has a balance of USD 30. Account A is short of USD 70.

Account B has a balance of USD 50 and Account C has a balance of USD 120:

- If Shared Balance is Yes and Sweep Coverage is Partial, then the shortfall of USD 70 in Account A is shared by Account B to the extent of USD 30 and Account C to the extent of USD 40.
- If Shared Balance is Yes and Sweep Coverage is Full, then the shortfall of USD 70 in Account A can be shared only by Account C as the balance in Account C can fully cover the shortfall. Whereas the balance in Account B cannot cover the full amount of shortfall.

In continuation to this scenario, if the balance of Account C is USD 60 instead of USD 120 and the Sweep Coverage is Full, neither Account B nor Account C could contribute to the shortfall of funds to process the debit transaction and the entire amount. That is, USD 70 is debited to Account A resulting in Account A getting overdrawn.

The balance swept from the linked (donor) accounts and checking (recipient) account is updated in the respective EB.CONTRACT.BALANCE application, as projected amounts using the following fields.

- Sweep Account – Indicates the donor or receiver account.
- Projected Cr Amt – Indicates the projected sweep amount that is summed and used for credit checking purposes.
- Projected Dr Amt – Indicates the projected sweep amount that is summed and used for credit checking purposes.
- Projected Locked Amt – Indicates the projected sweep as a result of the locked amounts.

The value in these fields are calculated when a subsequent debit transaction is processed on these linked accounts.

- The FORWARD optional balance component is applicable only when the base balance component is WORKING.
- It is the sum of all authorised and unauthorised forward entries raised for the checking account within the cash flow days defined in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER .
- This information is stored in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES in the available balance ladder and unauthorised forward movement fields.

- FLOAT optional balance component is applicable only when the base balance component is WORKING.
- It is the sum of all authorised and unauthorised real entries raised under the trade dated system with future exposure date (including future value date).
- This information is stored in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES in the following fields: Auth Fut Exp Bal – Indicates the sum of all authorised future exposure dated credit entries for the account. Unau.Fut.Exp.Bal – Indicates the sum of all unauthorised future exposure dated credit entries for the account. Both the above fields hold the balances for any future exposure date irrespective of cash flow ladder days defined in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER .

- TDGL optional balance component can be used in combination with any of the base balance components.
- It is the sum of all authorised pay movements and authorised receive movements.
- Both authorised pay movements and authorised receive movements are stored in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES .

- LOCKED optional balance component can be used in combination with any of the base balance components.
- It is the maximum of locked amounts for the checking account from the locked amounts ladder.
- This information is also available in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES .
- The locked amount is deducted from the base balance.

This is an optional component, which can be used in addition to a base component:

- It is calculated by the system if the Ifp Balance field for the corresponding balance category is set to Yes in AC.BALANCE.TYPE .
- It represents an off-balance sheet amount (reporting balance), which is calculated by the system if this is used by a business application and will be deducted from the base balance when calculating the available balance.

The AC.CASH.POOL application uses the SHADOW component to calculate the amount that was swept in or out of an account, which is part of a Cash Pool Group, if the IFP option is set up (that is, the Ifp field in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application is set to Yes) when the Group was defined.

- This optional component represents the suppression of the amount that is calculated by the system as a sweep projection.
- This option is used to cancel the sweep credit projection at the account level if this need not be considered when calculating the available balance.

When an account (set up as an account from/linked account) involved in a maintenance sweeping transaction (retail or corporate) receives a debit transaction and does not have sufficient funds, the system checks the available amount at the level of the sweeping account/account to. If that account has enough funds, the transaction is approved and the amount necessary to cover the deficit on the linked account is reserved as a debit sweeping projection at the sweeping account level. The same amount but as a credit projection (to be received in a sweeping transaction) is updated on the linked account. This amount is considered in the Cover Control process on both accounts. The SUPPRESS.CREDIT.PROJECTIONS optional component ignores the credit sweep projection if attached to the balance type.


##### Limit Check – Opt-In or Opt-Out Model

The credit checking process considers limit available during the balance checking process, based on the condition or option chosen by the customer.

The customer can choose to:

- Opt-In – Which considers the limit facility, if available for the Account Arrangement.
- Opt-Out – Which does not consider the limit facility, even if available for the Account Arrangement.
- Opt-In No IDL – Provides the ability to configure the system to disregard the intraday limit when doing a credit check, in case this is granted on the account.

This is captured at the arrangement in the Limit Check field in the BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property class for each activity or transaction.

For any reason, if the bank wants to block the limit check for any specific arrangement, they can do so by choosing the Block option in the Limit Check field. This blocks the usage of limit available to the account while processing the credit check.

When the Opt-In option is chosen, the credit check processing for the transaction performs the balance check in the following sequence:

1. Balance in the checking account (based on base balance and optional balance configured in AC.CREDIT.CHECK ).
2. Shared balance, if sweep is configured as one of the optional balance components.
3. Limit check, based on the limit available to the checking account.

The below example details how Opt-In No IDL option works.

Opt-In No IDL (only limit amount is considered by Limit Check , without IDL).

The BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property for debits posted to an account is set to include only standard limit amount and not the IDL in the Credit Check (Opt-in No IDL), as shown in the below screen shot.

A standard limit amount of 1000 USD and an intraday limit amount of 500 USD is granted to customer 182154 and attached to the account 02000000365.

The account 02000000365 balance is 3000 in credit.

A Funds Transfer (FT) transaction is posted to the account for a debit of 5000 USD.

In this case, the system has posted the FT transaction with an override. The account is in debit of 1000 USD, as the system did not consider the intraday limit.


##### Transaction Processing Using the Configured Available Balance

- An Arrangement Account is created with the NSF functionality enabled, as shown in the below screen shots.

- The BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property class is updated for the above arrangement.

- A FT transaction is initiated with a debit to the above arrangement account resulting in overdrawing the account. The override message 'Overdraft on Account 85316 for USD 10000' is prompted indicating that the account is overdrawn.

- The STMT.ENTRY is updated with the base and optional balance components for information in the Credit Chk Dtls Name and Credit Chk Dtls Value fields.

- AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION is created in IHLD status.

The following processes can also support the configurable available balance, to determine the account balances, if the Credit Check field in the BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property class of the account is configured as component.

- Creation of locked funds.
- Clearing cover request.
- Payment order check funds.
- TPH funds check.
- Standing order retry mechanism.
- Core enquiries that return the available balance.


##### NSF Processing using Start Balance Configuration

The NSF evaluation process calculates the available account balance by including the open balance with the entry amount. The NSF Start Balance field in NSF.PARAMETER helps to configure whether the Open.booked or Open.valued balance option is to be considered. The below illustrations explain how the open balance is derived.

| 1 | -200 | 20230419 | 20230419 | 800 | 800 |
| 2 | -900 | 20230419 | 20230419 | -100 | -100 |
| 3 | -500 | 20230419 | 20230419 | -600 | -600 |

##### NSF Processing using Active Holds Configuration

The NSF Evaluation process calculates the account available balance using the below formula.

When NSF Balance Type is configured in NSF.PARAMETER , the optional balance components are suppressed and the locked amounts are directly added to the running balance.

If the value in NSF Balance Type is,

- LOCK.FUNDS – Indicates that debit locked events is considered when calculating the account available.
- CREDIT.RESERVE – Indicates that credit locked events is considered when calculating account available.

If the value in NSF Lock Reserve Condition for the respective balance type is,

- LOCK.FUNDS.DATE – Indicates that debit locked events with start date as ‘Today’ or ‘Earlier’ is considered.
- CREDIT.RESERVE.DATE – Indicates that credit locked events with start date as ‘Today’ or ‘Earlier’ is considered.

When there is no value defined in the NSF Lock Reserve Condition for the respective balance type, the system refers the value defined in Lock Reserve Condition field in the AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM application. ##### NSF Processing Using Process Type Configuration

During the NSF evaluation process, when the funds decision for an NSF entry is updated as Rejected, the debit transaction amount is included in the running balance and subsequent debit movements are assessed in the NSF process.

When the NSF Process Type field is set to ‘Exclude.return’ in NSF.PARAMETER , a debit transaction amount of the NSF entry for which funds decision is updated as Reject, is not included in the running balance and subsequent debit items are assessed accordingly.

##### Handling NSF Exception

The NSF exception items represent the debit transactions to the account that moved the account to overdrawn status or resulted in further debit to the overdrawn balance.

NSF exception processing serve the following purposes:

- Funds Decision – To decide if the original transaction is to be approved or rejected.
- Charge Assessment – To take action on the charge that needs to be posted to the account, as a result of overdrawing the account balance.

NSF exceptions are created during the COB process and recorded in the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION (ACFA) application.

ACFA is used for different types of processing. The ACFA.TYPE application is created to ascertain the type of processing for ACFA.

An example of

record created for NSF processing is shown in the below screenshot.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Debit Account | Holds the account number. |
| Account Ccy | Holds the account currency. |
| Requested Ccy | Indicates the currency of the transaction - account currency. |
| Requested Amt | Indicates the transaction amount - amount in account currency. |
| Request Date | Indicates the booking date of the transaction. |
| Orig Trans Ref | Holds the Temenos Transact transaction reference. |
| Funds Decision | Contains the option, approved or rejected. |
| Xx Descision Reason | Holds the narrative describing the reason for rejection by the account officer. |
| Funds Auth Status | Indicates the status based on which level of authorisation is the lifecycle of the ACFA record. |
| Request Source | Indicates the source product creating the ACFA record. For NSF, this is defaulted to AC. |
| Request Code | Identifies the type of ACFA record. For NSF, this is defaulted to NSF. |


##### NSF Charge Assessment

Charge for each entry marked as NSF is calculated and updated to the exception record while the exception record is created.

The BALANCE.ACTIVITY property class in the Account Arrangement can be configured to Assess or Waive the charge for the transaction. If it is marked as Waive, the charges on the transaction are waived if it turns out to be an NSF item.

On the other hand, if it is marked as Assess, the transaction is assessed for charges if it turns out to be an NSF item. The charges can be defaulted based on the charge configured for this purpose in Account Arrangement. If the charge is configured to be negotiable, the account officer or bank user can negotiate the charge amount and manually update the negotiated charge amount in the NSF exception for further processing.

The following fields in ACFA are used in NSF funds decision.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Od Amt | Indicates the amount that the account is overdrawn before limit. |
| Set Type Or Orig Dec | Contains the option PTL, POL, SET or REJ. |
| Chg Waived | Contains the option Yes or No. This field is set as YES, only if the Od Charge Action field in the corresponding NSF entry is set to Waive (which is based on the activity). If this field is set as YES, then the Chg Decision field in ACFA is updated as SYSTEM. This field is not allowed for user input. |
| Chg Decision | Indicates if the charge is waived by the system. |
| Def Chg Amt | Holds the proposed charge amount configured in AA. This field holds the default charge amount calculated by the system during the creation of the exception record. This field is not allowed for user input. |
| Chg Amt | Holds the charge amount negotiated by the user. If not manually input, it gets defaulted from the default charge amount. This field is defaulted with the system calculated charge amount, if the Chg Decision field is not set as SYSTEM. The bank user can negotiate charge amount defaulted in this field. An override is raised if the Chrg Negotiable field is set to NO, for the respective funds type in NSF.PARAMETER and the user has amended the defaulted charge amount. The amount defined in this field is finally passed, while triggering the respective charge activity. After authorisation, this field cannot be amended. |
| Aaa Chg Amt | Updated by AA after posting the NSF charges. This field is updated with the actual charge amount posted by the system subsequent to posting of charge activity. The Aaa For Chg field holds the charge activity reference and is not allowed for user input. |

The Arrangement Activities defined in NSF.PARAMETER corresponding to the settlement type are triggered, based on the values in the Funds Auth Status and Funds Decision fields for funds decision and charge assessment. The activities that are triggered are summarised below.

| Funds Auth Status | Funds Decision | Field Reference in NSF.PARAMETER |
|---|---|---|
| Authorised | Approve | Fund Deci Approve Act |
| Authorised | Reject | Fund Deci Rej Act |
| Cancelled | Approve | Rev Approve Act |
| Cancelled | Reject | Rev Rej Act |

| S.No | Transaction | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TXN1 - Debit transaction | -1100 |
| 2 | TXN2 - Credit transaction | 1000 |
| 3 | TXN3 - Debit transaction | -100 |
| 4 | TXN4 - Debit transaction | -200 |


##### NSF Closing Evaluation Process

The closing evaluation process includes:

- Processing NSF exception items actioned by the user.
- Processing NSF exception items not actioned during the cut-off period.
- NSF charge revaluation for back value dated credits.

| Funds Auth Status | Funds Decision | Field Reference in NSF.PARAMETER |
|---|---|---|
| Authorised | Approve | Fund Deci Approve Act |
| Authorised | Reject | Fund Deci Rej Act |
| Cancelled | Approve | Rev Approve Act |
| Cancelled | Reject | Rev Rej Act |

The cut-off period for user decision is defined in the Expiry Days field in NSF.PARAMETER for the corresponding settlement type. The expiry date is derived as the number of days configured in the Expiry Days field from the date of creation of the NSF exception in ACFA.

The account officer or bank user can action the funds decision and charge negotiation (if applicable) during this period. If the NSF item is not actioned during this cut-off period, the default funds decision (configured in NSF.PARAMETER ) and default charges configured for the transactions are applied and processed on the expiry date.

In the event of receipt and authorisation of a back value-dated credit to the account on which the NSF item is processed, the NSF charge processed is re-evaluated.

For this purpose, the ACFA records created and processed for the NSF items for the account are recorded in a quick reference AC.NSF.ACFA.XREF table, in the order in which they are processed.

When a back value-dated credit is authorised for the account, a processing is triggered to get the processed ACFA records in the order in which they are processed and stored in AC.NSF.ACFA.XREF and make necessary adjustments to the charges collected on the NSF items.

The Od Charge Rev Action field in BALANCE.ACTIVITY property class determines the action to be taken during the re-evaluation of charges.

- If it is set to Reverse, the charges that are covered to the extent of the back value-dated credit are processed for reversal.
- If it is set to Re-book, all the charges collected after the back value-dated credit are reversed and re-booked considering the back value-dated credit.

When an account is closed, any unauthorised NSF exception gets waivered automatically by the system and the below details are updated in the exception record.

- Chg Waived is set to YES.
- Chg Decision is set to ACCOUNT.CLOSED.
- Chg Amt is set to zero.
- Grace Status is cleared & set to NULL.


##### Cover Control Processing Based on Two Different Balance Types

The system can perform two different types of cover controls (credit checks) for an arrangement account for the same debit transaction. The Cover Control setup at the arrangement level can contain different balance types. The system considers both the credit checks for all balance types before approving the transaction.

At the level of the Balance Availability Property for each arrangement, the user can configure the type of balances the system should consider before approving a debit transaction and also if a bank limit or an internal limit should be added.

A Financing Cash Pool is set up between three accounts as shown in the following screenshot:

Account 10012729102 (master account) has one cover control, IFP5, set up at the arrangement level.

The IFP5 record in AC.CREDIT.CHECK is set up to consider the available working balance and the sweep projections.

At the arrangement level, the cover control (credit check) is done considering the below setup and the bank’s limit (the Limit Check field is set to Opt-in).

Accounts 10012729103 and 10012729104 are set up to consider two balances for the same transaction (Activity Class):

- IFP4 is set up to consider the available working balance and the shadow balance (IFP balance) and to cancel any credit sweep projections and the internal limit.
- IFP5 is set up to consider the available working balance and the sweep projections and the bank’s limit.

A Cash Pool Group is created with the Ifp field in the AC.CP.GROUP.PARAM application set to Yes.

Two maintenance sweep records are created under the group to maintain the balances of accounts 10012729103 and 10012729104 at a minimum of 100,000 USD.

A debit transaction of 700,000 USD is posted on Day 1 against account 10012729103.

The system does two cover controls:

- IFP 4: Available working balance (0), shadow balance (0) and internal limit amount (1,000,000). Credit check is passed.
- IFP 5: Available working balance (0), sweep projections (0) and bank’s limit (5,000,000). Credit check is passed.

Transaction is posted. After the transaction is posted, the accounts’ balances are updated as below:

| Account | Available Working | Sweep Projection | Shadow Balance (IFP) | Internal Limit | Bank Limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10012729102 | 0 | -800,000 |  |  | 5,000,000 |
| 10012729103 | -700,000 | 800,000* | 0 | 1,000,000 | 0 |
| 10012729104 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1,000,000 |  |

*The projected amount is 800,000 because the system must keep the balance of account 10012729103 at a minimum of 100,000 USD. In this case, the system will sweep 800,000 USD at the EOD process.

After the sweep is triggered in the system, the accounts’ balances are updated to:

| Account | Available Working | Sweep Projection | Shadow Balance (IFP) | Internal Limit | Bank Limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10012729102 | -800,000 | 0 |  |  | 5,000,000 |
| 10012729103 | 100,000 | 0 | -800,000 | 1,000,000 | 0 |
| 10012729104 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1,000,000 |  |

On Day 2, another debit transaction of 400,000 USD is posted against the account 10012729103:

The system does two cover controls:

- IFP 4: Available working balance (100,000), shadow balance (-800,000), and internal limit amount (1,000,000). Credit check is not passed as the available amount is only 300,000 USD.
- IFP 5: Available working balance (100,000), sweep projections (0), and bank’s limit (5,000,000). Credit check is passed.

Transaction is not posted as the first cover control did not pass.


##### Overriding Rule-Based NSF Decisioning

All the transaction entries posted for the account are evaluated as a part of the Close of Business (COB) NSF evaluation process. Based on the sequence of rules, the list of debit entries that have been paid more than the account available balance, excluding the limits, are classified as NSF entries.

Based on the rules defined in the user exit routine, the system transfers the list of transaction entries classified as NSF to the hook routine.

Required local logic can be built within the user exit routine for further evaluation of the transaction entries. Based on the evaluation, in the user exit routines, the system allows the hook routine to:

- Update the overdraft amount for each entry (reduce the amount or mark it as zero).
- Update the Settlement Type field for each entry with one of the options below: POL – Paid Outside of Limit PTL – Paid Through Limit SET - Settle only

> **⚠️ Note:** Reducing the overdraft amount for an entry implies that the entry is classified as non-NSF. The AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION application creates the exception record for the entries marked as NSF by the hook routine.

| Position | Component | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | OdAmount | Indicates the overdraft amount for each respective entry. It can be reduced or made to zero. The amount is marked as zero by the user routine to make the entry as non-NSF. The value cannot be increased. The core decision values are considered if the values are increased in the local routine. |
| 2 | ChargeActivity | Indicates the charge activity for overdraft. Any changes in the value by the user routine is not considered for the process. |
| 3 | WaiveCharge | Indicates the flag on waiving the charge for overdraft. Any changes in the value by the user routine is not considered for the process. |
| 4 | SettlementType | Indicates the type of settlement from the list of defined values (POL or PTL or SET). If the value given does not match the predefined values, then the local routine changes is not considered and only the core decision values are considered. |
| 5 | OptionalCompBal | Indicates the multivalued list of optional components such as locked funds, credit reserve, sweep, and so on. Any changes in the value by the user routine is not considered for the process. |


##### Charge Waiver usingOverdraft GraceConfiguration

Grace Period Waiver is enabled using Overdraft Grace in AA.PRD.DES.BALANCE.AVAILABILITY and is defined as 1D, 2D, or Null. It indicates the number of working days within which the customer must clear the debit balance in order to waive the NSF charges on the account.

When the Grace Period Waiver is enabled for an arrangement account or product, additional information is updated in the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION record by NSF processing during close of business.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Grace Period | Indicates if the Grace Period Waiver functionality is enabled for the account. It is defaulted from the Product/Arrangement Balance Availability property class. |
| Grace Run Date | Indicates as the sum of current working day and number of working days defined by the Grace Period . |
| Previous Day Balance | Indicates the arrangements available balance as defined on the NSF Parameter for Grace Period Waiver when NSF is created. |
| Grace Status | Indicates if the system has reviewed and evaluated the NSF exception for grace period waiver. It is set to 1. |

Grace Period Waiver process reviews all the unauthorised AC Funds Authorisation record with Grace Run Date equal to or greater than current working day and with Grace Status as 1. The user is not allowed to authorise the exception record when the Grace Status is set to 1.

The NSF exception record with Funds Decision as Rejected and Charge Decision as Waived is not considered during Grace Period Waiver process. If the account is funded with sufficient balance with grace period and based on Grace Period Type as Full or Partial, below details are updated in the exception record.

- Chg Waived is set to Yes.
- Chg Decision is set to GRACE.WAIVER.
- Chg Amt is set to zero.
- Grace Status is updated from 1 to cleared (Null).

| Field Name | Value 1 | Value 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Grace Start Balance | Actual.booked |  |
| Grace Balance Type | Lock.funds | Credit.reserve |
| Grace Locked Reserve Condition | Lock.funds.date | Credit.reserve.date |

### 1.23  Payment Currency Validation for Multicurrency Accounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) and System Applications and Products (SAP) are two standalone processing systems. TPH is used for payment processing and SAP is used for reporting and accounting purpose. Generally, customer accounts are maintained in SAP and their basic details are mirrored on the TPH sta...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Multi Currency Check API*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) and System Applications and Products (SAP) are two standalone processing systems. TPH is used for payment processing and SAP is used for reporting and accounting purpose. Generally, customer accounts are maintained in SAP and their basic details are mirrored on the TPH standalone platform to validate the account details for payments processing, but the booking requests are sent directly to SAP.

As part of debit or credit party determination, TPH invokes the getFullAccountInfo API exposed by the embedded Demand Deposit Account (DDA) component to validate the details (mirrored from SAP) of the supplied debit or credit account.

TPH can supply the payment currency as one of the input parameter to the getFullAccountInfo API to check if the account currency is an accepted currency for the supplied account number. However, as Temenos Transact does not support multicurrency accounts, the decision if the payment currency is allowed or not is handled by the bank.

The DDA component enables the bank to parameterise a local API which is invoked before the getFullAccountInfo API returns the details to TPH and it can change the core decision regarding the payment currency. Based on the supplied details, TPH decides if it can send the booking requests to SAP in the payment currency or in the account currency.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The DDA.SERVICE.PARAMETER application contains the hook API for multicurrency check, as shown in the following screenshot:

The ID of the parameter table can only be ‘System’. The Multi Currency Check API field acts as a hook to attach the local API to return the account currency to the getFullAccountInfo API. The attached local API should be validated against the EB.API table.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Payment Currency Validation for Multicurrency Accounts feature.

#### 📖 Introduction

The payment netting facility provides the ability to automatically net payments with a counter party in the same currency and with the same value date. Netting is permitted only when a NETTING.AGREEMENT is held with the counterparty. The netting agreement has a finite life and indicates the currencies that may be netted with this counterparty.

Net payments must be agreed and approved before the payment is generated. This is done using the NETTING application. Temenos Transact automatically consolidates the payments eligible for netting into a netting group which appears as a single record in the NETTING application. Then this record may be reviewed and confirmed with the counter party. The NETTING record generates the single netted payment upon authorisation.

During the review of the NETTING record, individual payments can be rejected for inclusion in this net payment. Thus, any payments rejected remains in suspense and is automatically included in the next netting group created for the same currency, customer and value date. Once a payment has been selected for netting, it can only be made using the NETTING application.

Netting groups are created during the Temenos Transact overnight processing (based upon forward deals) or online (using the CREATE.NETTING application) for spot deals.

The accounting entries for payments that are to be passed across a suspense account, should have a zero balance once all net payments have been sent.

Individual payments that are to be netted are recorded in the NETTING.ENTRY table.


##### Multilateral Netting Settlement

The Foreign Exchange transactions involve a settlement risk. As the exchange of the two currencies involved is not simultaneous, the party that sells a currency before receiving the currency purchased from the counterparty is exposed to risk. The Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) eliminates the settlement risk through a Payment vs Payment (PvP) mechanism.

Forex CLS trade is settled through the multilateral netting settlement process where the Forex CLS trades for a given value date and currency are netted and processed as a single settlement for the currency through the identified Nostro account for the respective currency.

The NETTING application is integrated with the Payment Order to process the payment through the Temenos Payment Hub (TPH).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic covers the configuration of netting applications.


##### Payment Netting Suspense Account

The payment netting facility requires suspense accounts. These accounts are setup in two stages, an ACCOUNT.CLASS record is created and then a suspense account is opened, which acts as a template for all the suspense accounts.

The ACCOUNT.CLASS record to be established has a key of NETTING. Temenos Transact uses this record to determine the characteristics of the suspense accounts to be setup which holds the netted payments. Before setting up the record, a new CATEGORY code should be created for netting suspense accounts. This code is referenced by the ACCOUNT.CLASS parameter.

Then, the internal netting suspense accounts is opened using the ACCOUNT application. The ID of these accounts is the same as any other internal account, that is, the CURRENCY, CATEGORY, and a four digit identifier. For example, USD149550001.

The Nett Payments field in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER must be set to YES for netting the payment.

The NETTING.PARAMETERS application controls the payment netting facility. There is only one record with the ID as SYSTEM. It specifies the TRANSACTION codes to be used for netting payments, the number of days prior to the payment value date that NETTING records should be created, and the period of history that should be kept before netting information is purged from the system.

All contracts whose payments may be netted contains Netting Status field. This field is used at contract input time to stop the payments arising from this contract being netted.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the system usage of the payment netting feature.


##### Details of Agreements with Counterparties –NETTING.AGREEMENT

The NETTING.AGREEMENT application contains agreements with counterparties to net payments of the same currency and value date. An agreement can be made with each counterparty (CUSTOMER) and the agreement may specify that only payments of particular currencies may be netted and only payments arising from particular Temenos Transact applications may be netted.

The agreement lasts for a finite period as specified in the Start Date and End Date fields. The agreement can be input and amended at any time.


##### Details of the Entries to be Netted –NETTING.ENTRY

The NETTING.ENTRY table contains the details of all entries being netted. Records are created upon authorising the original contract. When an individual payment is successfully included in a net payment, then it is updated in this table. The ID of the records is the original contract ID. The record contains the details of each payment arising from the contract where the payment is being netted.

The NETTING.ENTRY record also holds the details of the status of each individual payment. Each individual payment can have one of the below status:

- Waiting to be included in a net payment.
- Included in a net payment.

The status is recorded in the Np Ref field. If this field does not contain a value, then the individual payment is waiting to be netted. Once the individual payment has been included in a net payment, then this field is updated with the reference of the Netting record.


##### Netting Payments –NETTING

The NETTING application is the main control over the net payments process. All individual payments selected for netting are combined into a single Netting record for the counterparty, currency and value date combination. Then this record is reviewed and amended, if necessary. Once the net payment is correct, the Netting record is authorised and Temenos Transact creates the single net payment or receipt accounting and delivery messages.

Individual payments may be dropped from a net payment at this point. If dropped, they remain in suspense until captured in another net payment. Therefore, once a payment has been selected for netting, it can only be paid using the NETTING application. Individual payments may be removed from netting, by reversing and re-inputting the source contract and ensuring that the Netting Status field is set to NO on the re-input.

The CREATE.NETTING application creates the Netting records automatically during the overnight batch run or online. These records are created with the status as hold ready for review and possible input. If a Netting record is confirmed as valid (possibly following confirmation with the counterparty) it should be authorised. Then Temenos Transact generates the single net payment. The following screen shots shows the authorised Netting record.

Settlement details (such as bank-to-bank information) are added to the Netting record and is used on the resultant net payment. Additionally individual payments are removed from the Netting record, if necessary, through the Netting field. Payments removed from the record remain in suspense until another Netting record is generated (either in the Temenos Transact batch or by the CREATE.NETTING application).


##### Netting Payments Online –CREATE.NETTING

This application is used to create netted payments online. Verification of a CREATE.NETTING record activates the payment netting process. This combines all outstanding payments that match the specified criteria into Netting records. Then these can be reviewed, amended and authorised for the net payments. Payments can be netted for any combination of counter-party, currency and value date. Thus a record can net all outstanding payments for a single counter-party, only those for a single currency for that counter-party and so on. The specification of counter party is mandatory.


##### Accounting for Net Payments

Accounting entries are raised for payments that are netted pass across a suspense account.

| DR or CR | Account | Amount | CCY | Value | Generated by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Credit | Nostro | 15M | USD | Spot | Contract |
| Debit | Nostro | 12M | USD | Spot | Contract |


##### Integration of Netting to Payment Order

The netted settlements processed through the NETTING application are integrated with the Payment Order, so that, the payment system (TPH) can process the payments based on the settlement instructions provided by the Netting application. This is enabled based on the Treasury product configuration to settle trades through the Payment Order.

The TM.PO.INTEGRATION (parameter application) enables the processing of regular and netted settlements of treasury trades through Payment Order. The Payment Order hands over the processing of the payment through the respective payment system (TPH).

The PO details are referenced with PAYMENT.ORDER application using Po Reference in NETTING application.

TM.PO.INTEGRATION is configured at the company-level and the decision applies to all the treasury trades including the netted trades processed in that company. A sample screenshot of TM.PO.INTEGRATION application is shown below:

The Acc Trans Thru Po field in the parameter application decides if the Account Transfer settlements from the Treasury or Netting application must be processed through Payment Order (PO). If the Acc trans Thru Po field is set to

- Yes, the account transfer settlements are processed through PO. The necessary accounting entries and settlement instructions are processed by payment system (TPH).
- No, the account transfer settlements are processed in the Netting application itself and are not be handed over to PO.

The netted treasury trade settlements through Nostro are processed by the payment order, if the TM.PO.INTEGRATION parameter is configured for the company.

When the Payment Order is generated from the NETTING application, the Payment order reference is updated in the Po Reference field for cross reference.

When the Payment order is generated for the netted settlement, the accounting entries and delivery messages are processed by the associated payment system (like TPH).

> **⚠️ Note:** If the TM.PO.INTEGRATION application is not configured for a company, the netted trade settlements in that company are processed by the NETTING application itself. That is, the accounting entries and the delivery messages for the netted settlement are generated by the NETTING application.

The following screenshot show the PO Reference for the Nostro settlement in the NETTING application.

The following screenshots show the Payment Order details that are referenced for the Nostro settlement in the NETTING application.


##### Multilateral Netting Settlement

The FOREX application captures and maintains Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) Forex trades in Temenos Transact. The trade with the counterparty is captured as a ‘CLS deal’ and the settlement of the CLS deal is processed by the CLS bank, thereby, eliminating the settlement risk.

The Forex CLS trade triggers the settlement through multilateral netting process by setting the Allow Cls Netting field to Yes in the FX.CLS.PARAMETER application, as shown in the screenshot below:

If the Allow Cls Netting field is not set to Yes, the CLS trades are not netted and is settled individually using the FOREX application.

When the FOREX (FX) application triggers the multilateral netting process, the following actions are performed in the system for the trade settlement.

- A record in NETTING.ENTRY is generated indicating that the Forex trade is a CLS deal (the Cls Deal field is set to YES).
- The Create Netting process generates the Netting record in FHLD status, consolidating the settlement amounts based on Value Date and Currency of the settlement. The Counterparty is not considered as a consolidation criterion for multilateral netting. The Create Netting process can be triggered manually or is handled automatically during Close of Business (COB). The manual process of create netting is initiated using the CREATE.NETTING application and the Cls Settlement field is set to Yes if the user requests for a multilateral netting settlement. Counterparty is not required or considered when the Cls Settlement field is set, as shown in the screenshot below. The automatic process of create netting is performed by configuring the Days Ahead field in the NETTING.PARAMETERS application and if the Value Date of the Forex CLS trade falls within this period, it is considered for multilateral netting.
- The following details are updated in the record created in the NETTING application in FHLD. The Cls Settlement field is set to Yes. The Nett Amt Settle field consolidating the CLS settlement amounts based on the Value Date and Currency of the settlement. The details of Forex CLS trade that are netted for settlement. The multilateral netting suspense account used in the CLS settlement process, as configured in the Cls Susp Categ field in the FX.CLS.PARAMETERS application. Settle Account is defaulted from the Cls Nostro Account field in FX.CLS.PARAMETERS for the respective settlement currency. The system defaults the settlement routing information for multilateral netting as given below: If the processing bank is a direct participant, the Beneficiary Bank (Tag 58A in MT202) and Acc With Bnk (Tag 57A in MT202) is the CLS bank, as defined in the FX.CLS.PARAMETERS application. If the processing bank is third-party participant, the Beneficiary Bank is defaulted from the Cls Rep Bank field in FX.CLS.PARAMETERS and Acc With Bnk field is defaulted from the Cls Rep Corr Bank field (if provided) in FX.CLS.PARAMETERS . If the Cls Rep Corr Bank field is blank, then Acc With Bnk is defaulted from the Cls Rep Bank field. The user can manually change the defaulted values in Beneficiary Bank (Tag 58A in MT202) and Acc With Bnk (Tag 57A in MT202) fields of the NETTING application before authorisation.
- Once the user verifies NETTING details and authorises the same, the following actions take place: The SWIFT delivery advice for payment (MT202) or receipt (MT210) with the settlement instructions are triggered. The settlement accounting entries are raised to the Nostro accounts by debiting or crediting the multilateral netting suspense accounts in which the FX application has the settlement amounts. The Cls Settle Status field in the corresponding Forex CLS trade(s) is updated as Settled. This field in the Forex CLS trade is initially set to pending, which indicates that the trade is yet to be picked up for netting. Once the trade is picked up for netting by the create netting process, the Cls Settle Status field is updated to Processing. Once the netting is authorised, the Cls Settle Status is updated to Settled.
- A sample Cls Netting record is shown below.
- Accounting entries are generated when Netting record is authorised. In this case, F-entries (Forward entries) are raised because the Value date (that is, settlement date) is forward.
- As the net amount of settlement is less than zero, net amount must be received and hence MT210 advice is generated as shown below.
- On reaching the Value date , the following accounting entries are generated for the settlement.

The Netting application is integrated with Payment Order to process the payment through the Temenos Payments Hub (TPH).

The Netting application refers to TM.PO.INTEGRATION , Treasury-Payment Order integration parameter to process the netted payments through the Payment Order application. If TM.PO.INTEGRATION is configured for Treasury trade settlements for the processing company, the same is used for settlement of Forex CLS trades through multilateral netting.

When the TM.PO.INTEGRATION is configured for the company that processes the multilateral netting settlement, the payment is routed through the Payment Order application. The Netting application passes the settlement details to the Payment Order application, which generates the delivery advice for payment (MT202) and settlement accounting through the TPH.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the netted amount is a receipt, the delivery advice (MT210) is generated by the Netting application itself. If the netted amount is a payment, the settlement details are handed over to the Payment Order.

Once the Payment Order is created for the netted payment, the Po Reference field is updated in NETTING for cross-reference.

The below example shows the settlement of multilateral netting payment through Payment Order.

1. Netting record with the Po Reference updated after handing over the payment details to the Payment order application is shown in the below screenshot.
2. Payment Order created for settling the payment is shown in the below screenshot.
3. The following screenshot shows the processing of payment order through TPH using POR.TRANSACTION . Accounting entries generated by TPH for payment settlement are shown in the following screenshot. Delivery advice (MT202) generated for the payment through TPH is shown in the below screenshot.

The user suppresses the settlement instruction for payment or receipt of the netted settlements manually before authorising the Netting record. The Suppress Payment field in the NETTING application is used to indicate if the settlement instruction must be suppressed. The user updates this field to Yes to indicate that the settlement instruction must be suppressed.

If the Suppress Payment field is set to Yes, the delivery messages are not generated and payment details are handed over to the Payment Order. The necessary accounting entries for the settlement are generated by the NETTING application but the delivery advices are not sent out.

- The following screenshot shows the Netting record with Suppress Payment set to Yes.

> **⚠️ Note:** Po Reference is not updated (indicating that the payment details are not handed over to Payment Order application) and the delivery instructions are also not generated in the Netting application (indicating that the delivery message for payment is not generated by the Netting application).

- The following screenshot show the accounting entries raised by the Netting application (when Suppress Payment set to Yes).

The following amendments are performed on the underlying Forex Cls Trade till the Netting in FHLD status is authorised:

- Change the nature of settlement from Cls settlement to a regular Forex settlement.
- Reverse the FX Cls trade.
- Amend the Nostro account for the Our Account Pay and/or Our Account Rec fields.

In this case, the Netting entry for the trade is updated for the above changes and the Netting in FHLD is rebuilt during the next create netting process to reflect the impact.

However, once the Netting record is authorised, the amendments mentioned above are not possible on the Forex Cls trades that are part of the netted settlement and the system prompts an error if the user attempts to modify.

> **Purpose:** *The POSTING.RESTRICT application defines various types of restrictions, such as, post no debits, whereabouts unknown, and the like. #### 📖 Introduction

The POSTING.RESTRICT application defines various types of restrictions, such as, post no debits, whereabouts unknown, and the like. The restrictions can be given at the customer or account level. When a posting restriction is given for an account and transactions are done impacting the account, an override message is triggered stating the posting restriction on the account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic covers the system usage of the posting restriction feature.


##### General Posting Restriction

Posting restrictions can be imposed on selective transactions by setting values in the Allow Txn and Transaction Code fields in the POSTING.RESTRICT application. The following are the possible values:

- If Allow Txn is set to N, posting restrictions are applied only on the transaction codes listed in the Transaction Code field.
- If Allow Txn is set to Y, posting restriction functionality is applied on any transaction code except those listed in the Transaction Code field
- If Allow Txn field is Null, posting restrictions are applied on transactions based on the Restriction Type field.
- If Allow Txn and Transaction Code are set, the Restriction Type need not be input. However, when both Restriction Type and Transaction Code fields have values input, the Transaction Code takes precedence and posting restriction is applied only based on the Allow Txn and Transaction Code setup.


##### Posting Restrictions at Account Closure

The system automatically closes any ACCOUNT that has a posting restriction in the range of 90-99 as soon as all balances are zero. Posting restrictions in the range 80-89 are used for ACCOUNTS, which are pending closure. During the closure of the ACCOUNT, the value of the Posting Restrict field set in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER defines the availability of the existing POSTING.RESTRICT messages in the ACCOUNT.

When the Posting Restrict field in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER is set to Multiple or None and when an account is subjected to the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE processing, the POSTING.RESTRICT code for closure 90 is appended to the existing set of POSTING.RESTRICT messages in the account (as shown in the following screen shot).

When the Posting Restrict field is set to Single in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER and when an ACCOUNT is subjected to the ACCOUNT.CLOSURE processing, the POSTING.RESTRICT code for closure 90 overwrites the existing set of POSTING.RESTRICT messages in the account (as shown in the below screen shot).


##### Restriction using Customer Mass Block

The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK application is used to place a posting restriction on a range of accounts at the same time through predefined selection criteria. The following features are also available when using this application:

- Blocking code – Code shows the value linked to record in POSTING.RESTRICT .
- Blocking reason – Free text field.
- Start date – Current bank day or future date blocking action effective from.
- Expiry date – Date on which the mass block is removed.

The following fields are used to determine which fields from the CUSTOMER and ACCOUNT applications are used as the selection criteria for the block.

- Sel Application – Customer/Account.
- Sel Field – Sector/Residence/Nationality/Industry/Category/Currency.
- Sel Value – Valid range of input for Sel Field .

The following are the only Sel Field value used from customer and account as selection criteria.

- Sector
- Residence
- Nationality
- Industry
- Category
- Currency

The

is configured to select a range of accounts which satisfy the following selection criteria.

- Customer with Sector as 1000
- Nationality as US

This section details the types of applying mass block with exclusion.

It is possible to exclude specific customer or specific accounts of the customer from the block even if it satisfies the blocking criteria. This is achieved by using the multi-value fields for capturing the customer and account numbers to be excluded.

The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK is configured to select a range of accounts which satisfy the selection criteria of Customers with Sector as 1000 and Nationality as US. In the example below, among other customers who satisfy the selection criteria, the following customers and accounts are marked to be excluded from blocking - all accounts of CUSTOMER 10012 and Account 00001001301 of CUSTOMER 10013.

Mass blocking with Funds Transfer (FT) between blocked and excluded accounts raises an override as shown in the below screen shot.

The override displayed is only for the blocked account. The excluded customer account remains unblocked.

It is also possible to setup blocking for specific customers individually, with or without exclusion, as shown in the below screen shot.

The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK with FT between two excluded accounts is shown in the below screen shot.

Override is not displayed when the transaction happens between excluded accounts. There are no changes in the Posting Restri ct fields of the CUSTOMER record which are affected by CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK .

The Include Ac Accounts field in the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK application enables the flag, if the legacy accounts are also eligible to be included or excluded for mass block. Legacy accounts refer to all Temenos Transact customer accounts that are not created through Arrangements (AA module). If this field is flagged as YES, the legacy accounts qualify for the selection and if left blank or flagged as NO, only the Arrangement accounts qualify for the block criteria.

The Include Ac Account flag is set to YES, to indicate that the restriction also applies to legacy accounts.

The system is configured to produce notifications for the following events for a CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record when:

- A record is created.
- An existing record is approaching the start date.
- The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK has started.
- An existing record is amended.
- An existing record is reversed.
- The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record is approaching the expiry date.
- The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record has expired.

The following fields are used to set the notification parameters in the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK application.

This optional field is used to set the number of working days prior to the start of the block when the system should produce a notification for future dated CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK records only. The system calculates this based on the present date (when the block is created) and the start date of the mass block record. If the field is left blank then no notification is sent before the start of the block.

If the date on which a

record is created is 1st December 2016, the start date of the block is in the future, 8th December 2016, and the

field is 2, this means that on 6th December 2016 (two working days prior to 8th December 2016) a notification is produced. (6th and 7th December are working days).

This optional field is used to set the number of working days prior to the expiry of the block when the system should produce a notification only when the expiry date is defined. It is calculated between the start date of the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record and the expiry date. If it is left blank then no notification is sent before the expiry of the block.

If the date on which a CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record started is 8th December 2016, the expiry date of the block is 31st December 2016 and the Expiry Notify Days field is set to four , this means that on the 27th December 2016 (four working days before 31st December 2016) a notification is produced.(as 27th to 30th December are working days).

This system generated field is updated automatically when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record is created based on the information previously defined by the user, it represents the next calculated date when the system triggers an event.

The CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record is created on 1st December 2016 with the start date as 8th December 2016. The Start Notify Days field is set to two. After authorising the record on 1st December 2016, the Next Event Date field contains the value of 6th December 2016. This represents the next date when a notification is produced (two working days before the start of the record).

This system generated field automatically populates the current status of the block which is associated to the current business reason for generating the event. The status of a record can be:

- FORWARD – Applied when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record has a start date in the future.
- FORWARD-NOTIFIED – Applied when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record triggers an event due to the setting in the Start Notify Days field.
- CURRENT – Applied when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record reached its start date.
- EXPIRY-NOTIFIED – Applied when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record triggers an event due to the setting in the E xpiry Notify Days field.
- EXPIRED – Applied when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record reached its expiry date.
- REVERSED – Applied when the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record is reversed.

EXPIRED. The REVERSED block status is not dependent on the above sequence. Notification events are triggered through Integration Framework in the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE . These are then used by the bank to generate the actual alerts.

#### 📖 Introduction

The PRINT.STATEMENT application holds the definition of the formatting enquiry or Application Programming Interface (API) that produces the statement output. For example, if the system is setup to bypass DELIVERY module from statements production, the PRINT.STATEMENT application can be used to produce printed statements directly from the Temenos Transact environment either manually or within the daily Close of Business (COB).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

The records created in the PRINT.STATEMENT application have a reference to the statements formatting enquiry in the Format field and to a relevant REPORT.CONTROL record in the Report Control Id field.


##### Refer To Product

Using this field the system can be instructed to control the format of combined customer statements to the AA product or arrangement. In order to do this, the Refer To Product field in the PRINT.STATEMENT application that is used in the COB job PRINT.STATEMENT$RUN in the batch process AC.REPORTS, (normally with the ID as SYSTEM) needs to be set to YES.

Thereby, the references to various types of combined statements as defined in the PRINT.STATEMENT application. Records can be selected in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT property either on the level of the product definition or on the arrangement level as required by the product.

#### 📖 Introduction

A provider API can retrieve credit and debit movements of accounts excluding masked movements for any specified dates. Banks can use this API for their local development purpose to produce the customer summary reports and queries.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Provider API – AC.API.BALANCE.MOVEMENT

- Provider API to retrieve credit and debit movements of accounts and account booking balance for a specific date. This API will return credit and debit movement for the day with and without masked entry movements in separate tags.
- API Details, o URI - /v1.0.0/holdings/accounts/{accountId}/balanceMovements/{bookingDate}
- Method – GET


#### 🔧 Working With

The Account Balance Movement (AC.BALANCE.MOVEMENT) enquiry artefact is used for the AC.API.BALANCE.MOVEMENT provider API:Accout Balance Movements enquiry is used to retrieve credit and debit movements of accounts and account booking balance for a given period or a specific date. It displays credit and debit movements with and without masked entry movements in separate columns.

User has the option to enter either the account number or arrangement as a reference and will have to enter a start date from which the account balance movement is required. In addition to start date, user can also optionally enter an end date:

- If an end date is defined, this enquiry will display balance movement for the account for those days, which has movements within the given period, irrespective of whether the movement is masked or not.
- If an end date is not defined, this enquiry will display balance movement for the day given as the start date, irrespective of whether there is a movement.

The following screenshot shows the Enquiry Selection screen.

The following screenshot shows the Enquiry Output screen.

- Column – Net Credit Movement and Net Debit Movements excludes the balance movements which are masked from being printed in account statement.
- Column – Gross Credit Movement and Gross Debit Movements includes all the balance movements for the account including those movements that are masked from being printed in account statement.

### 1.30  Non-Stop Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Financial transactions can happen any time round the clock. This document explains how Non-Stop (NS) processing is supported in Temenos Transact .

In NS mode, there is no restriction for:

- Modifying, reversing or deleting existing contracts
- Back values, forward values and so on.

There is no impact on transactions in unauthorised state (like INAU, RNA and so on) before the COB is initiated. Such contracts are automatically moved to HLD.

The non-stop processing functions for both new and existing contracts as explained below.


##### New Contracts Only

Core banking can enter, amend and authorise new contracts in this mode. However, back valued transactions are not allowed. The contracts unauthorised before the COB are moved to HLD during the COB process, but new contracts are not impacted.


##### New and Existing Contracts

Customer and contract balances are updated real time to ensure that the latest customer transaction is included. For Securities, the customer positions is updated real time.

Non-stop transactions do not impact financial closing position of the bank as:

- GL (CAL/CPL) include no movements from these transactions, which are included in the next COB
- Currency positions are updated to include the impact of cross-currency non-stop transactions, but the COB revaluation excludes the value of these transactions.

### 1.31  Account Interest Rounding


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact supports various types of account interest calculations:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact supports various types of account interest calculations:

| Rounding method | Description |
|---|---|
| Natural rounding | Interest (System-calculated value) is rounded to the nearest unit, as defined in the currency record. |
| Round up | Interest (System-calculated value) is rounded up to the nearest decimal point, as defined in the currency record. |
| Rounding down | Interest (System-calculated value) is rounded down to the nearest decimal point, as defined in the currency record. |
| Ryoha Kataha | This rounding method is used for the Japanese market. |

To give an accurate interest total, it may be required to sum the un-rounded individual interest amounts and then to round down or up the total interest amount. The method of rounding the individual interest amounts and the total interest amounts is configurable for credit and debit interest, and is linked to the EB.ROUNDING.RULE application.
