The message format is one of the family of cash management messages (camt) of the ISO20022 (also known as UNIFI) standard. Th...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The camt.053 (Bank to Customer Statement) message is a statement of account(s) sent by the bank to account holding customer (or nominated representative) on a periodic basis. The message format is one of the family of cash management messages (camt) of the ISO20022 (also known as UNIFI) standard. The camt.052 message is an intraday version of the camt.053, only showing movements generated since the last generation of camt.052 or camt.053.

Banks that participate in Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payments (either credit transfer or direct debit) acting for the ordering party or the beneficiary must be able to generate the camt.053 or camt.052 electronic statement if requested by the account holding customer or bank. The format must include complete details of the SEPA payment in the statement detail and details of other non-SEPA financial transactions.

This capability is mandatory in many European countries from February 1, 2014.

- The camt.053 and camt.052 are part of the cash management messages set by ISO20022 using an XML based schema.
- The camt.053 (Bank to Customer Statement) is sent by the bank to an account owner or a party authorised by the account owner on a periodic basis.
- The camt.052 (Bank to Customer Account report) is used for intra-day account reporting upon request by the account owner.

The CAMT messages are the ISO20022 equivalent of the MT9nn series:

- Camt.053 is the ISO20022 equivalent of MT940, which is sent by the bank to the account holder on a periodic basis.
- Camt.052 is the IS020022 equivalent of MT942 or MT941, which is an intraday version of the camt.053.


##### Product Configuration

The camt solution is packaged into the Temenos Transact ISO20022 XML Account Statement Module (IX - ISO20022 Statement). The IX product must be installed to use the camt statement functionality.

The camt message produced by Temenos Transact is aligned with the Dutch-specific usage rules, as set by the Dutch Banking Association (NVB).

The NVB guidelines include the usage rules for the reporting of SEPA credit transfers and Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) direct debits. The SEPA details required under NVB are reported in the camt statement if the required information is available in Temenos Transact .

> **⚠️ Note:** Other country-specific regulations need to be requested with requirements to evaluate if those usage rules can be accommodated.

A camt message has a nested structure with the building blocks as shown in the image below. The Temenos Transact Camt module is responsible to assemble the data necessary to produce a camt message for each statement triggered.

The camt.053 and the camt.052 messages both have the same structure, except that the header name is different.

- Camt.053 message has the following structure:

Bank to Customer Statements:

- Camt.052 has the following structure:

Bank to Customer Account Report:

- Group Header Report Entry Transaction details

The following image shows the structure of a camt.053 message.

- Group Header (Statement Level Information):

The Group Header block of the camt message provides the information related to the statement and is specified for the camt message. This section of the message is mandatory.

It contains information like Message Identification, Pagination, Message Recipients and so on.

> **⚠️ Note:** Group Header block is mandatory and is specified only once for the camt message.

- Statement or Report (Account Level Information):

The Statement section of the camt message provides the details of the account(s) for which the statement(s) is being produced.

The camt message may contain information related to more than one account statement. However, Temenos Transact is producing one camt message for a single account statement.

Details required at this level are built from the Temenos Transact account and related statement production details. This includes details of the statement period, account identification, opening, closing and other account balances.

> **⚠️ Note:** Statement section is mandatory and may occur multiple times in the camt message.

- Entry-Level Information:

One account statement can contain multiple account movements (a statement may have zero entries during the period). Information at this level is derived from the individual account movement from the Temenos Transact statement entry table.

> **⚠️ Note:** Entry Level section is optional and may occur multiple times in the camt message.

Transaction-Level Information:

This section provides additional information for each entry displayed in the Entry Level section. The additional information may include:

- Additional details for an individual entry.
- Additional details for SEPA related transactions.
- Underlying entries of a netted entry which represents multiple debits and credits or a batch entry (this will be supported at a later stage).

> **⚠️ Note:** Transaction Level information section is optional and may occur multiple times in the camt message.

The following screenshot shows the xml view of the camt.053 message.

This table is used to define the default details for an account statement when opening new accounts. It also holds the high-level parameter that is applicable to account statement at the system level.

The AC.STMT.PARAMETER application is also used to define the following:

- Provide the link between an entry and the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS table, which would hold the SEPA details from an external SEPA system.
- Provide a hook to plug-in APIs to filter and consolidate the list of entries for a specific camt message.

Link between the Entry and the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS table:

To identify the corresponding EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS record that holds the SEPA details for a STMT.ENTRY , the STMT.ENTRY and the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS record should be linked.

A hook is available based on each implementation to attach a local API with the logic to link the STMT.ENTRY record to the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS . The API returns the key to the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS table.

The External SEPA Link API field in AC.STMT.PARAMETER application is the hook that gets the link from the entry to the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS table. It is a valid key to EB.API to hold the API that returns the link key to the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS table.

Different variations of the camt.054 message are generated by filtering the list of entries to be reported. A filter API is invoked to exclude entry details based on the criteria the bank requires.

Entries for the statement or report period are combined into consolidated entries for the statement. The criteria and consolidation method used is determined by message types and decisions made through an API routine. This consolidates entries together according to the required rules and ensures that the consolidated entry is shown in the statement.

The following screenshot shows the hook in AC.STMT.PARAMETER to plug-in an API to return the link between the entry and the EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS table.

The camt account statements and reports are generated using the standard account statement functionality.

ACCOUNT.STATEMENT table is used to specify the dates and frequencies for producing account statements. A record is automatically created with the default settings when an account is set-up. It can then be defined specifically for each account based on the customer’s requirements. User can define up to nine statement cycles, and within each cycle, a combination of different types of messages can be generated.

The Xml Stmt Type field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application is used to request a camt or MT type message for the first cycle for an account.

The Swift Statement-2 Type field is used to define the message types for the additional statement cycles.

The following screenshot shows the set-up for camt and MT type messages for two statement cycles.

### 1.33  User-Definable Content of the Camt Message


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration


##### Filtering Entry Content

The Filter Routine field in AC.STMT.PARAMETER allows the entry list for the report cycle to be filtered. A filter API can be invoked by the statement processor that will be able to exclude entry detail based on the criteria required by the bank. This will allow the inclusion and exclusion of information based on the recipient receiving the report. It is typically used to restrict the list of entries reported under camt.054 (Debit or Credit notification).

The API is passed at the entry, and it returns a flag to indicate if the entry can be included in the account report. A test API, IX.TEST.FILTER.RTN, has been released as an example of how the API should be built.

The following screenshot shows the set-up to plug-in an API to filter the entries for camt.054 account report.


##### Consolidating Selected Entries

Entries for the period under consideration can be combined into consolidated entries for the statement. The criteria and consolidation method used is determined by message type and the decision is made through an API routine. The Consolidate Routine field in AC.STMT.PARAMETER provides the hook to plug in the API. This will consolidate entries together according to the required rules and ensure that the consolidated entry is shown in the statement.

The default consolidation grouping uses the following elements from the entry:

- System ID
- Transaction Code
- Booking Date
- Reversal Marker

The API is passed to the entry and the consolidation group. The API can alter or clear the consolidation group. It can also change the transaction code, if a specific transaction code is preferred for a consolidated entry. This allows the system to show a specific transaction description in the camt message.

While the statement shows the consolidated entry in the statement, the actual entries are held in detail in the system. This is typically used when an account report is generated for a selected list of entries with all the details, but in the statement, the entries are reported as one consolidated entry. A test API, IX.TEST.CONSOLIDATE.RTN, is released as an example of how the API is built.

The following screenshot shows how an API may be plugged in to consolidate entries for a camt.053 account statement:


##### Suppressing Information

The XML.TAG.DEFINITION application allows an individual tag or group of tags defined as Optional under camt, to be suppressed for a specific message type or entry from a specific application. Additionally, it is possible to make more complex suppression decisions through a developed API routine to handle specific bank’s criteria.

The following screenshot shows the suppression set-up for a group tag for batch details. The suppression can be set by default for the group, or by message type as shown here, or under the application or transaction type for the message type. The following image shows the suppression for camt.053 by setting the Suppress Flag as Yes and for camt.054a, the suppression is based on a logic defined in SUPP.BATCH.DTLS API.

The following screenshot shows how the suppression set-up for a data tag can be defined.

### 1.34  Passbook Printing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Passbooks can be issued to savings accounts (see ACCOUNT.CLASS and ACCOUNT ). When an entry is passed across a passbook account from any application, the details are recorded and the TELLER system updates the passbook when it is presented.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Passbooks can be issued to savings accounts (see ACCOUNT.CLASS and ACCOUNT ). When an entry is passed across a passbook account from any application, the details are recorded and the TELLER system updates the passbook when it is presented.

The layout of the passbook has to be defined in the TELLER.PASSBOOK application. This describes the physical dimensions of the book in addition to header type information. For example, customer name and address, and positions of the debit or credit columns. The entire content of the passbook is user definable. Read TELLER.PASSBOOK for more details.

### 1.35  AC Funds Auth Process


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The funds authorisation requests AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION (ACFA) application created by various business applications are handed off to transaction recycler based on the parameterisation in the ACFA.TYPE table.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The funds authorisation requests AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION (ACFA) application created by various business applications are handed off to transaction recycler based on the parameterisation in the ACFA.TYPE table.

The capture mechanism uses the rules defined in the RC.CAPTURE application for the business application that created the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION request to determine the retry conditions (the retry options are Partial and End Partial defined in the RC Condition application) as well as the payment processor (in this case, AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION).

The funds authorisation request created through AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION remains on hold status until the bank staff or the transaction recycler approves or rejects that record.

### 2.1  Cancel Chq Dep Clearing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks use the Temenos Transact front-end application ( TELLER ) to record the details of the cheques deposited by their customers that must be sent for collection. The Cheque Collection record is created with status as Deposited for every cheque deposited through front-end applications. The front-en...*
> 
> **Applications:** `ACCOUNT.PARAMETER`, `CHEQUE.COLLECTION`, `CQ.PARAMETER`, `TELLER`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks use the Temenos Transact front-end application ( TELLER ) to record the details of the cheques deposited by their customers that must be sent for collection. The Cheque Collection record is created with status as Deposited for every cheque deposited through front-end applications. The front-end application captures the basic details such as Customer Account Reference, Cheque Number, Exposure Date, and Value Date and passes on to the CHEQUE.COLLECTION application.

The CHEQUE.COLLECTION application in Temenos Transact manages the outward cheques that are presented for collection through front-end application TELLER , which handles all the workflows and accounting, associated with outward cheque collection like Deposit, Collection, Returns, and Cancellation. The cheque collection processing is triggered-off by setting the relevant configurations in the CQ.PARAMETER or ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application that are used to specify a list of transaction codes that invoke the processing related to depositing, collecting, or return of cheques.

The user can cancel or revoke a deposited cheque before it is sent for collection. As part of this cancellation process, the system reverses the associated accounting entries that are raised originally as a part of the cheque deposit transaction.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 📋 Tasks

Cheque cancellation helps the user to cancel a cheque that is not yet sent for clearing. The the bank to mask the entries raised on the client account related to the respective cheque.

### 2.2  Card Management


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The card management life cycle includes processes like issuing of new card, monitoring the card usage, blocking the cards, card expiry, and re-issuing the cards (expired, lost or stolen).*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The card management life cycle includes processes like issuing of new card, monitoring the card usage, blocking the cards, card expiry, and re-issuing the cards (expired, lost or stolen).

Card Management System (CMS) is the software system that administers and controls the card life cycle. The Cards Fulfilment Service receives the card related requests from various user agents (like channels, branch and so on) and sends these requests to the CMS using adapters. Based on the responses received from CMS, the cards fulfilment service updates the details of the issued cards in Temenos Transact .

Temenos Transact supports the above functionality that can be used to provide an overview of their card details to the customers.

The following applications are used to manage the card issue details in Temenos Transact :

- CARD.TYPE
- CARD.STATUS
- CARD.CHARGE
- CARD.ISSUE


#### ⚙️ Configuration


##### Card Type

The CARD.TYPE application holds the details for each type of card supported by the card control system.

A card type is defined by a four-letter code, for example:

- AMEX – American Express cards.
- VISA – VISA cards.

Each card would normally be valid for a set length of time. The renewal date of cards is calculated from the Renewal Date and the Renewal Fqu fields. These are separate fields, so that cards may be renewed based on a standard frequency field if all cards expire on a given date or on a frequency period based on their date of issue.

The following significant fields in CARD.TYPE should be input when a new card type is input.

- Billing Day – Format (D-nn) means date minus ‘nn’ (where nn is a numeric). Date here implies REPAY date input in the card issue application. When a repayment date is input in card. Issue – the billing date is nn days before such date. (that is, repayment date –nn (nn is a numeric)
- Az Product – No change or no input field. When Card Type field in az product parameter is input –then in card type, this field is populated. For a valid Az. Product. Parameter – if field card. Type is mentioned then this field in card. Type is automatically populated with the AZ product parameter. NO change/ no INPUT field.
- Forward Backward – This field defines the method to be followed by the system when the derived date of a generated schedule is a non-working day. The following values can be updated in this field: Forward – The system goes forward to the next working day. Backward – The system goes back to the last working day. Fw Month – The system takes the next working day, if it is within the month and if it is not within the same month then the system goes backward to the last working day. Calendar – The system date is the same whether it is a holiday or not.


##### Card Status

The CARD.STATUS application is used for defining various card statuses. The following four-card statuses are hard coded in the CARD.ISSUE application and cannot be altered. Any new status other than the ones that are hard coded can be input using this application.

- 90 – Issue
- 91 – Re-issue
- 92 – Scrap
- 93 – cancelled


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Card Management feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Card Management feature.

The bank can capture the charges based on the charge type or may not based on the charge type, depending on the requirement and situation. Moreover, at the time of realization of a foreign cu...*

#### 📖 Introduction

Charges can be levied on cheques or drafts at the time of issue or based on the status of cheque processing. The bank can capture the charges based on the charge type or may not based on the charge type, depending on the requirement and situation. Moreover, at the time of realization of a foreign currency draft, a suitable exchange rate must be considered based on the draft currency and local currency of the bank to obtain the realization amount. This exchange rate is normally based on the currency market and currency rate system, but the user can also capture a specific exchange rate at the time of realization of drafts.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.

### 2.4  Cheque Draft Return


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The cheque or draft returns can be processed at the counter or through clearing using Temenos Payment Hub (TPH).*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Clrd Chq Rtn*, *Allow Clrd Chq Rtrn*, *Cheque Return*, *Incr Return Cnt*, *Return Count*, *Return Reject Reason*, *Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The cheque or draft returns can be processed at the counter or through clearing using Temenos Payment Hub (TPH).

- When the bank teller finds that the cheque or draft presented by the payee at the counter cannot be paid for reasons such as signature mismatch, validation errors, insufficient funds and cheque stop, teller initiates a process to update the Temenos Cheque Management System that the cheque or draft has been returned.
- When the payments operator from TPH or TPH finds that the cheque or draft presented through clearing cannot be paid for reasons such as signature mismatch, validation errors, insufficient funds and cheque stop, the operator or TPH initiates a process to update the Temenos Cheque Management System that the cheque or draft has been returned.
- When a cheque is issued, it can be cleared, returned or stopped. Normally, once a cheque is cleared, it cannot be returned. But there are clearings and situations where a cleared cheque can be returned. So, every time a cheque is returned, the reject reason is updated. Due to some operational errors, the reject reason can be updated incorrectly. Such operational errors need to be rectified by modifying the reject reason.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section covers the applications used to configure cheque return and modification of rejection reasons.


##### Returning a Cleared Cheque or Draft

The user must set the Allow Clrd Chq Rtn field in the CHEQUE.TYPE application to Yes to allow a cleared cheque to return.

The Status of the cheque in CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT is updated as Cleared.

When the user tries to clear a cheque, a record is successfully created in CHEQUE.RETURN .

The user sets the Allow Clrd Chq Rtrn field in the CHEQUE.TYPE application to No.

The Status in CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT is updated as Cleared.

While trying to create a Cheque Return record, an error is displayed indicating that the cheque is cleared and cannot be returned as the Allow Clrd Chq Rtrn field in CHEQUE.TYPE application is set to No.


##### Modifying Rejection Reason(s) of a Rejected or Returned Cheque

The Incr Return Cnt field in the CHEQUE.RETURN application allows the user to indicate whether there should be an increment in the Return Count or not. When a cheque is being returned with the Return Reject Reason as Account Closed and the Incr Return Cnt field is left blank in the CHEQUE.RETURN applicaion, the Return Count is incremented in the CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT application and updated as 3.

The following screenshot shows the records after authorsation in the CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT application:

But due to an operational error, the Return Reject Reason must be modified from 'Account Closed' to 'Stale Cheque'. The Incr Return Cnt field in the CHEQUE.RETURN application is set to No. After authorisation, Return Count in the CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT application displays the same value (that is, 3) without any increment.


#### 📋 Tasks

Currently, a cleared cheque cannot be returned. However, there are situations and clearings that permit such process. Whenever a Cheque or Draft is returned, a new Cheque Return record is created where the reason for the return is updated. At times, due to operational errors there is a need to modify the reject reason.


##### Workflow

This section allows the user to perform the below activities:

1. Input Cheque Return .
2. In the Contract screen, enter a value that starts with ‘CHRE’ in the Cheque Return field and then click the Edit icon.
3. Enter values in the below fields: Cheque Number Cheque Type Account Number Cheque Return Code
4. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
5. Click the Commit icon to create the record.

This enquiry allows the user to view, amend or delete the existing Cheque Return records.

To amend a Cheque Return record, follow the below steps:

3. In the Cheque Return screen, enter or amend values in the fields that require amendment.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for overrides and errors.
5. Click the Commit icon to create the record.

To delete a Cheque Return record, follow the below steps:

2. In the Cheque Return Amend/Delete screen, click the Delete icon corresponding to a record.

To view a Cheque Return record, follow the below steps:

1. Cheque Return Amend/Delete .
2. In the Cheque Return Amend/Delete screen, click the View icon to see the respective record in detail.

This enquiry allows the user to authorise the records created for Cheque Return.

2. In the Authorise Cheque Return screen, click the Authorise icon corresponding to a record, to authorise the existing Cheque return record.

### 2.5  Cheque Issue Management


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks provide cheque books to Individuals or corporates. Cheque books can contain 25, 50 or 100 cheque leaves depending on the nature of their relationship with the bank. For example, the bank may provide a cheque book with 25 cheque leaves for savings account, whereas it may provide a cheque book w...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account No*, *Cheque Amount*, *Cheque amount*, *Cheque currency*, *Choose Clearing Type*, *Credit Account*, *Debit Account*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks provide cheque books to Individuals or corporates. Cheque books can contain 25, 50 or 100 cheque leaves depending on the nature of their relationship with the bank. For example, the bank may provide a cheque book with 25 cheque leaves for savings account, whereas it may provide a cheque book with 100 cheque leaves for Current Account. This calls for printing of cheque and stocking of the same at the bank, before it can be issued to customers.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section covers the applications used to configure Cheque Issue and Management.


##### ConfiguringSTOCK.PARAMETER

The STOCK.PARAMETER is the top-level parameter for creating and maintaining different types of stock of:

- Cheques
- Bankers cheques
- Drafts
- Fixed Deposit receipts
- Credit cards

The following screenshot shows the STOCK.PARAMETER for cheque.

The accepted IDs for this application are:

- CHQ for Cheque
- BCHQ for Bankers Cheque
- DRAFT for Demand Drafts
- FDR for Fixed Deposit Receipts
- CARD for Credit / Debit cards

The Stock Reg Id field in the STOCK.PARAMETER application can be used to define a combination of values using which the stock is updated in STOCK.REGISTER . This field can contain the following values:

- Company Code
- Department Code
- Local Table
- Co Code-dept Code
- Dept Code-local Tab
- Co Code-local Tab.

This provides the convenience of maintaining stock at different levels within the organization.

The Stock No Mask field identifies the mask the user wants to apply to the instrument numbers for the instruments (Cheque, Bankers cheque, Drafts, Fixed Deposit Receipts (FDR) or Credit cards). Input in this field must contain '#' characters. Number of '#' characters defines the maximum length of the instrument. First character can be R, which means that the account number is right justified and it can contain leading zeros.

- If the Cheque Number is 1234 and the Mask is #####, the display is 1234.
- If the Cheque Number is 1234 and the Mask is R#####, the Cheque Number is displayed as 01234.


##### ConfiguringCHEQUE.TYPE

This application holds the details of each type of cheque supported by the Cheque Control System.

The following screenshot shows the CHEQUE.TYPE record CURR (for Category 1001).

A Cheque Type is defined as a four-letter code.

- CURR – Current Account Cheque
- EURO – Euro Cheque

Each cheque type can be assigned a maximum and minimum holding, a default issue quantity (number of cheques in a book) and a notice period to allow reports to be produced for accounts requiring automatic reissue.

A list of account categories to which cheque can be issued is also recorded for each cheque type. Auto Reorder Type is defined if the reorder has to be based on a cheque number of the cheques held by the account holder. The Max Represent Number field in CHEQUE.TYPE defines how many times a cheque can be represented following a return.


##### ConfiguringSTOCK.ENTRY

The STOCK.ENTRY application is used to record inward or outward printed stock of stationery like cheque and Fixed Deposit Receipts (FDR). Any successful entry updates the STOCK.REGISTER table. Through this application, the stock details like Cheque Type , Stock Series , Stock Start Number , Stock Quantity and Stock Account Number are captured.

Given below is an example of STOCK.ENTRY for a corporate account.

Movement from one stock register to another can also be entered. It also forms the Stock Series based on CHEQUE.TYPE*STOCK.SERIES*STOCK.ACCT.NO, if the account number for which the stock has been received is noted in the STOCK.ENTRY . An example for inclusion of account number at the STOCK.ENTRY level would be interest or dividend warrants to be issued by a corporate.


##### ConfiguringSTOCK.REGISTER

The following screenshot shows the STOCK.REGISTER updated as CHEQUE.TYPE*SERIES*ACCOUNT.NO.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Issue of LCY Draft (Retail)
- Process External Cheque (FCY)
- Process Cheque Clearing (Outstation)
- Cheque Collection or Clearing Processes

The CHEQUE.COLLECTION application is used to post the cleared cheques from the suspense accounts to the customer accounts on collection or from the collection suspense account to the returned suspense account on return of cheques in Temenos Transact .

CHEQUE.COLLECTION is one of the two central applications of the cheque and card control system. Banks provide chequebooks to individuals or corporates. The issue of cheques to an account is controlled by the entry of records on this table. When the issue record is authorised, the cheque register for the account is updated with the number issued. Banks levy charges for the issuance of cheques based on the number of cheque leaves requested (BAND or LEVEL).

### 2.6  Draft Issue Management


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Demand Drafts (DDs) issue is handled using the FUNDS.TRANSFER and TELLER applications in Temenos Transact . Retail Banks that issue DDs maintain an inventory of the drafts for audit purpose, because they are written orders issued by the bank to its correspondents and the details need to be cross che...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Stock Reg Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Demand Drafts (DDs) issue is handled using the FUNDS.TRANSFER and TELLER applications in Temenos Transact . Retail Banks that issue DDs maintain an inventory of the drafts for audit purpose, because they are written orders issued by the bank to its correspondents and the details need to be cross checked at the time of payment. The bank and its agents will pay the beneficiary when the demand draft is deposited and cleared by the beneficiary bank.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section contains detailed setup information and other information pertaining to functions like receipt of stock, issue, charges and stop payment instructions for drafts. The setup for receipt and update of stock into Temenos Transact is similar to cheque issue with a few differences.


##### ConfiguringSTOCK.PARAMETER

This application allows the user to define top-level parameters for different types of drafts.

The following screenshot shows the STOCK.PARAMETER record with ID as DRAFT.

The Stock Reg Id field in the STOCK.PARAMETER application can be used to define a combination of values, using which the stock is updated in STOCK.REGISTER . This field can contain the following values:

- Company Code
- Department Code
- Local Table
- Co Code-Dept Code
- Dept Code-Local Tab
- Co Code-Local Tab.

This provides the convenience of maintaining stock at different levels within the organisation.


##### ConfiguringCHEQUE.TYPE

A unique CHEQUE.TYPE for drafts needs to be created.

The following screenshot shows a record in CHEQUE.TYPE for draft issue.

As the credit is to an internal suspense account, the Assigned Category field is populated with the related Category and Internal field is set to Yes.

The format of the Internal Category code is CCYCCCCCSSSS, where:

- CCY indicates the Currency
- CCCCC indicates the Category
- SSSS indicates the Subdivision code from the Company

Usually, demand draft issued by a bank has a limited period of validity. This information is provided in the Validity field to enable the system to track expired drafts. Any buyer of a draft has to either cancel or renew the draft that exceeds the validity period.

The payee name of an incoming draft (issued by the same bank) can be validated when the same is presented through local clearing. For this, the Validate Payee Name field has to be set as Yes. This serves as a basic security feature against forged drafts.


##### ConfiguringSTOCK.ENTRY

Stock of draft can be maintained at various levels within the bank. This functionality is similar to STOCK.ENTRY for cheque. Please refer to the STOCK.ENTRY section under Cheque Issue Management.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Issue of LCY Draft (Retail)

The FUNDS.TRANSFER and ACCOUNT application uses a customer’s account to perform debit or credit into any bank’s customer account or in other words from customer account to bank’s internal account and vice versa.


##### Workflow

The user can perform the below activities corresponding to draft issuance in the core banking system.

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
|  | Issue Drafts . |
| User Prompt | Click the Issue Draft – Local option. |
| Issue of Local Currency Draft | Enter values in the following fields: Debit Account Draft number Draft Amount Issue Cheque Type Payee Name Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. |

There are no Outputs available for Draft Issue and Management feature.

### 2.7  FCY Draft Processing Drawee


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This section explains the processing of Foreign Currency (FCY) drafts from the drawee bank’s perspective. When the drawer bank issues an FCY draft on its Nostro account maintained with the drawee bank, drawer bank can inform the drawee bank by sending a draft issue notification using the MT110 or CB...*
> 
> **Applications:** `CHEQUE.ADVICE`, `CQ.PARAMETER`, `EB.MESSAGE.111`, `STOP.REQUEST.STATUS`, `SWIFT.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Default No Stop Answer*, *Default Stop Answer*, *Drawee Bank Pref*, *Payment System*, *Send MT112*, *Send Stop Request Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

This section explains the processing of Foreign Currency (FCY) drafts from the drawee bank’s perspective. When the drawer bank issues an FCY draft on its Nostro account maintained with the drawee bank, drawer bank can inform the drawee bank by sending a draft issue notification using the MT110 or CBPR+ camt.107.001.01 messages.

At a later stage, the drawer bank can send any of the following messages requesting the drawee bank to stop the payment of the draft or cheque due to various reasons like customer request or operational exceptions.

- MT111 (Request for Stop Payment of a Cheque)
- CBPR+camt.108.001.01 (Cheque Cancellation Or Stop Request)

The drawee bank sends an MT112 (Status of a Request for Stop Payment of a Cheque) or CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (Cheque Cancellation Or Stop Report) message to the drawer bank as response.

When the draft is presented for payment, the drawee bank verifies the status of the draft. If the advice is not received, the drawee bank raises a warning. Depending on the drawee bank's procedures, it may request the drawer bank to confirm the status of the draft. If the bank is notified about the draft but it is marked as stopped based on a request from the drawer bank, the bank rejects the payment of the draft.

The adoption of ISO20022 CBPR+ messages for cheque transactions is mandatory starting from November 2025. To support these messages, the bank must license the SWIFT CBPR+ Cheques (PPSWCQ) and Cards and Cheques (CQ) modules and activate the CBPR 2023 rulebook in SWIFT.PARAMETER . However, until November 2025, the bank can continue using existing MT messages for cheque transactions even after obtaining the required license and activating the CBPR 2023 rulebook.

If the user responds to the stop requests with the generic version, the system generates any of the following.

- MX camt.109 messages - If the CBPR November 2023 rulebook is activated.
- MT112 messages – If CBPR November 2023 rulebook is not activated.

If the user responds with the version dedicated to MT messages, the system sends MT112 messages or no messages (for example, the bank uses this for a proprietary interface).

- If Drawee Bank Pref is set to Temenos Payments in CQ.PARAMETER , then the system follows the TPH setup.
- If Drawee Bank Pref is blank in CQ.PARAMETER , then the system follows the Delivery configuration.

The bank can receive MT or CBPR+ cheque related messages from its counterparties till November 2025. The below diagram explains the Temenos solution for the drawee bank flow.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

If Payment System in CQ.PARAMETER is blank, then the payments processing is done through Full Funds Transfer module (FTFULL).

The drawee bank account or counterparty is determined using the configuration in TPH ( Drawee Bank Pref is set to Temenos Payments) or the Delivery configuration.

The SWIFT MT112 does not contain a dedicated tag to indicate if a message is rejected or accepted. The following parameters enable the system to take a decision based on the answer code. The following fields in CQ.PARAMETER are explained below.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Default Stop Answer | Used to default the answer code which notifies the drawer bank that the draft is stopped. This field is parameterised with /13/, indicating that the stop instructions are fully recorded. |
| Default No Stop Answer | Used to default the answer code which notifies the drawer bank that the draft is not stopped. This field is parameterised with /12/, indicating that the stop instructions are not acceptable. |

The following screenshot shows CQ.PARAMETER with Default Stop Answer and Default No Stop Answer fields with parameters /13/ and /12/ respectively.

> **⚠️ Note:** ISO20022 has a dedicated element to indicate the accept or reject of the requests. The system provides a generic user workflow that allows the bank to use a version to answer the stop requests received from the counterparties and indicates the accept or reject.


#### 📋 Tasks

In drawee bank perspective, when the bank receives the FCY cheque and stop payment of cheque (either MX or MT) from drawer bank, the details can be captured and also sends the status of stop payment of cheque with the below versions.


##### Workflow

The user can perform the below activities corresponding to FCY Draft Processing as Drawee Bank in the core banking system.

This version allows users to capture the received drafts or cheques using MT110.

Create Received Advice of Cheques-CAMT107 .

This version allows users to capture the received drafts/cheques using camt.107.

This enquiry allows the user to authorize the records created for received drafts/cheques.

This version allows the user to capture the received stop payment request of the cheques/draft received using MT111.

Create Stop Payment of Cheque(Inward) -Generic .

This generic version allows the user to capture the received stop payment request of the cheques/draft received camt.108/ MT111.

View /Respond Unauthorised Stop Payment request of Cheques .

This enquiry allows the user to view the unauthorised the EB.MESSAGE.111 records with the DIRECTION as INWARD and can perform the following.

- View EB.MESSAGE.111 record
- View Cheque Reg Supplement
- Respond to Stop Request with MT/MX message (Generic Version) ( Send Stop Request Status is Defaulted if PPSWCQ licence is installed)
- Respond to Stop Request with MT message ( Send MT112 is set to YES)
- Respond to Stop request with No message
- View Inward Delivery Message received
- View Inward Delivery reference

Authorise/Delete-Request/Response Stop Payment of Cheques .

This enquiry allows the users to authorise and delete the inward unauthorised Stop Requests (the EB.MESSAGE.111 records) for the drafts/cheques and the user can perform the following.

- View Amend, Delete the record.
- View Cheque Reg Supplement
- View Delivery Header
- View Delivery Message

The user can view the below list of enquiries and reports pertaining to Drawee Bank FCY Cheques.

This section allows the user to view the below enquiries and reports:

### 2.8  FCY Drawer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The drawer bank functionality describes the processing of Foreign Currency (FCY) drafts from the perspective of the drawer bank.*
> 
> **Applications:** `CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT`, `CHEQUE.TYPE`, `CQ.PARAMETER`, `DE.ADDRESS`, `DE.I.HEADER`, `DE.O.HEADER`, `EB.MESSAGE.111`, `IF.EVENT.INTERFACE.TABLE` ... +8 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acceptance Status*, *Account Number*, *Account Number or Drawee Bank BIC*, *Action Request Status*, *Answer Status Code*, *Answers*, *Cheque Amount*, *Cheque CCY* ... +41 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks


#### 📖 Introduction

The drawer bank functionality describes the processing of Foreign Currency (FCY) drafts from the perspective of the drawer bank.

When the drawer bank issues a FCY draft on its NOSTRO account maintained with the drawee bank, they can inform the drawee bank by sending an MT110 or camt.107.001.01 message. These messages are used to advise the drawee bank about the draft being issued.

Payment Order and Temenos Payments handles the issuance of Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunications (SWIFT) MT110 (advice of cheques) or Cross Border Payments and Reporting Plus (CBPR+) camt.107.001.01 (cheque presentment notification) messages.

Read International Payments (SWIFT CBPR+ ISO20022) for more information.

The drawer bank may request the drawee bank to stop the payment of the draft or cheque at a later stage. This can occur for various reasons, such as a customer request or operational exceptions. In such cases, the drawer bank can send an MT111 (request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.108.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop request) message to the drawee bank, requesting to stop or cancel the payment.

The drawee bank sends an MT112 (status of a request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop report) message to the drawer bank in response to the stop payment request. This message informs the drawer bank about the actions taken by the drawee bank regarding the stop payment request.

The table below defines the SWIFT definitions for CBPR+ cheque messages.

| Message | Description |
|---|---|
| Cheque Presentment Notification (camt.107.001.01) | Sent by a drawer bank, or a bank acting on behalf of the drawer bank to the bank on which a / several cheque(s) have been drawn (the drawee bank). It is used to advise the drawee bank or confirm the enquiring bank on the details concerning the cheque(s) referred to in the message. |
| Cheque Cancellation Or Stop Request (camt.108.001.01) | Sent by a drawer bank, or a bank acting on behalf of the drawer bank, to the agent on which a cheque has been drawn (the drawee bank) to request for the cancellation of the presentment and / or stop the payment of the cheque referred in the message. |
| Cheque Cancellation Or Stop Report (camt.109.001.01) | Sent by the drawee agent (on which a cheque is drawn) to the drawer agent or the agent acting on behalf of the drawer agent to indicate the actions taken to cancel the presentment and / or stop the payment of the cheque referred to in the message. |

> **⚠️ Note:** The adoption of ISO20022 CBPR+ messages for cheque transactions is mandatory starting from November 2025.

Banks must have licenses for the SWIFT CBPR+ Cheques (PPSWCQ) and Cards and Cheques (CQ) modules and the activation of the CBPR+ 2023 rulebook in SWIFT.PARAMETER is required to support these messages. However, until November 2025, banks can use the existing MT messages for cheque transactions even after obtaining the required license and activating the CBPR 2023 rulebook. The preference to send MT messages, MX messages, or no messages is defined in Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) at the counterparty level. The system considers the activation of November 2023 rulebook in SWIFT.PARAMETER . The CQ module follows the TPH setup for the counterparty and can stop sending the message at the request level for stop payment of cheque messages.

> **⚠️ Note:** Banks can receive both MT or CBPR+ cheque related messages from their counterparties till November 2025.

The following diagram explains the Temenos solution for the drawer bank flow:


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following tables are configured for Foreign Currency (FCY) drafts processing as drawer bank:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Drawee Bank Pref | Indicates if the counterparty determination and advice preference is given by the configuration in Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) or by the delivery preference. The following are the possible values: Temenos Payments - Send CBPR+ cheques messages. Blank - Raise an override if Payment System is ‘Tps’. The PP license code is required for the banks to select Temenos Payments. |
| Answer Status Code | Indicates the answer codes that are received in the Answers field (Tag 76) from the incoming MT112 message. Based on the received code, the system performs the action defined in the Action Request Status field. |
| Action Request Status | Indicates the action performed by the system on receiving an answer code in MT112. The answer code is configured in the Answer Status Code field. The available option for this field is Stopcheque. |

The Debit Credit Advice field allows the bank to select the drawee bank preference advice. The field is also referred while deciding the stop payment of the cheque message when,

- Debit credit advice includes camt.107.
- Drawee Bank Pref field in CQ.PARAMETER is set to ‘Temenos Payments’.
- CBPR+ 2023 rulebook is activated in SWIFT.PARAMETER .

Then camt.108 is generated from the EB.MESSAGE.111 application, provided the bank does not specifically indicate that no advice should be sent.

> **⚠️ Note:** The bank must ensure Debit Credit Advice is set to ‘camt.107’ to avoid sending MT messages after November 2025.

The basic equivalent SWIFT Code Word for Iso Reason Code are added when the generic model bank version initiates the stop requests and MT messages are handed over. The equivalent SWIFT code word are populated in the Queries field of EB.MESSAGE.111 application and the same is sent out in the MT111 messages. Banks can modify these records in the application anytime.


#### 🔧 Working With

This sections covers the process of drawer bank CBPR+ cheque stop requests and report messages.


##### Capturing Stop Requests

The drawer bank request the drawee bank to stop the payment of the draft or cheque. This can occur for various reasons, such as a customer request or operational exceptions. In such cases, the drawer bank can send an MT111 (request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.108.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop request) message to the drawee bank, requesting to stop or cancel the payment.

> **⚠️ Note:** The EB.MESSAGE.111 application allows the users to capture the stop payment requests of cheque or drafts.

The table below defines the fields used in EB.MESSAGE.111 .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Account Number | Identifies the account number to whom the cheque belongs. |
| Customer No | Identifies the receiver of the SWIFT message. |
| Drawee Bank BIC | Indicates the BIC of the receiver or drawee bank. |
| Cheque Amount , Cheque CCY , Cheque Number , Date of Issue , Value Date | Indicates cheque details. |
| Cheque Type | Indicates the cheque type used by the bank when the draft is issued. |
| Send Notice | Indicates whether the message is to be generated. |
| Orig Instruction Id | Indicates the unique identification number to unambiguously identify the original instruction. |
| Queries | Indicates the reason for stopping the payment of the cheque for MT111. |
| Chq Stop Originator | Indicates the party who originated the stop request of the cheque. |
| Stop Req Reason Code | Indicates the Iso reason code to initiate the stop request of the cheque. |
| Stop Req Additional Info | Indicates the additional information on the cancellation request reason. |
| Payee Name , Payee Address , Payee Country , Private and Org Details , Payee Town | Indicates the details of the Payee. |

Depending on the Model Bank versions used by the clients, either the Stop Req Reason Code and Stop Req Additional Info or Queries is displayed.

The Cheque Type field is mapped along with the Cheque Number (ChequeType / ChequeNumber) in the following:

- tag 21 of the outward MT111 message.
- tag ChqNb of outward camt.108 message.

Based on the information mapped in the outgoing MT111 (request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.108.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop request) message, the system identifies the cheque number and cheque type based on the same reference present in tag 21 or ChqNb when it receives an inward MT112 (status of a request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop report) message.


##### Validations for Capturing Stop Request

- If the Payee Country is populated and Payee Name is not captured, an error is raised that Payee Name is mandatory when Payee Country is specified.
- If the Payee Town is populated and Payee Name is not captured, an error is raised that Payee Name is mandatory when Payee Town is specified.
- For SWIFT MX Messages, SWIFT rejects the messages if the Payee Town and Payee Country or Payee Address is populated along with the Payee Name . The system raises a warning, if the bank decides to send only MX messages they can set up the warning as an error.

The screenshot below explains the processing of the outward SWIFT MT111 (request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.108.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop request) message.

If the Drawee Bank Preference field in the CQ.PARAMETER application is set to ‘Temenos Payments’, the following actions occur within EB.MESSAGE.111 :

- Drawee Bank BIC is captured, and the Account Number is not specified - Temenos Payment Hub (TPH) checks for the configuration in the PP.LORO.NOSTRO.ACCOUNT table and validates if the bank is a correspondent. If so, the NOSTRO account of the counterparty is retrieved and populated in the Account Number field.
- Drawee Bank BIC is not captured, but the Account Number is captured and it is a NOSTRO account - TPH checks the configuration in the PP.LORO.NOSTRO.ACCOUNT table and determines the BIC of the counterparty associated with the Account Number and populates it in the Drawee Bank BIC field.
- Account Number is not a NOSTRO account - The Drawee Bank BIC or Customer Number is populated. The Customer Number is optional if Drawee Bank BIC is present.

If Drawee Bank Pref is set to ‘TPS’ in CQ.PARAMETER , the system uses the TPH configurations to fetch the Drawee Bank BIC else it is determined from the Temenos Transact configuration (SWIFT DE.ADDRESS defined for the counterparty customer).


##### Model Versions for Capturing Stop Requests

The following options are provided for the bank to initiate a stop payment request, which is sent as:

- MT messages - The ‘EB.MESSAGE.111,INP’ version captures the field specific to MT messages.
- camt.108 messages or MT111 messages - The ‘EB.MESSAGE.111,OUT.GENERIC’ version captures the fields available in the ISO20022 CBPR+ messages. If the counterparty preference indicates cheque advice in MT format, the Delivery module translates the CBPR reason codes to the equivalent MT codes. The values captured in the other fields that are not specific to MT messages (for example, structured address, private or organization details, and so on) are ignored while sending the message.


##### Capturing Stop Request MT111

Banks can access EB.MESSAGE.111,INP version in the path below and enter the mandatory fields to initiate the stop request and the message to the drawee bank.

Create Stop Payment of Cheque(Outward)-MT111 .

Given below are the mandatory fields:

- Account Number
- Cheque Number
- Cheque Type
- Date of Issue
- Cheque Currency
- Cheque Amount
- Direction = OUTWARD
- Send Notice

> **⚠️ Note:** The value for Send Notice is set to Yes.


##### Capturing Stop Request - Generic (camt.108 or MT111)

The EB.MESSAGE.111,OUT.GENERIC version is designed to simplify the process for banks to initiate a stop payment request. With this version, the banks can input the necessary information to request a stop payment. After recording the stop payment request, the system automatically generates either MT111 message or camt.108 message based on the DebitCreditAdvice field in PP.BANK.CONDITIONS and other parameters. Read Configuration for more information. Banks can access the EB.MESSAGE.111,OUT.GENERIC version in the path below and enter the mandatory fields to initiate the stop request and the message to the drawee bank.

Create Stop Payment of Cheque(Outward)- Generic .

Given below are the mandatory fields:

- Account Number or Drawee Bank BIC
- Original Instruction Identifier
- Cheque Number
- Cheque Type
- Date of Issue
- Cheque Currency
- Cheque Amount
- Cheque Stop Request Reason code
- Send Notice

> **⚠️ Note:** The value for Send Notice is set to Yes.


##### Generating MT111 Messages

The EB.MESSAGE.111 application hand over the details to delivery after the record is authorized to generate DE.O.HEADER , considering the stop request status captured in the Capture stop request MT111 section.

Bank runs the BNK/SWIFT.OUT service to generate the SWIFT MT messages and set the status of the Disposition field in DE.O.HEADER to ‘Formatted’.


##### Generating camt.108 Messages

The process given below are followed to generate camt.108 messages:

1. The EB.MESSAGE.111 application hand over the details to delivery after the record is authorized to generate DE.O.HEADER , considering the stop request status captured in the Capture stop request Generic (camt.108/MT111) section.
2. Bank runs the XMLISO.OUT and INTEGRATION.SERVICE services to generate the SWIFT MX messages and set the status of the Disposition field in DE.O.HEADER to ‘Formatted’.
3. The details of the IF event are updated in the IF.EVENT.INTERFACE.TABLE application.
4. Banks can now view the outward camt.108 delivery message of the EB.MESSAGE.111 record through the EB.MESSAGE.111.OUT.ENQ enquiry. Enquiry View: Delivery Message:

> **⚠️ Note:** For outward camt.108 through EB.MESSAGE.111 , the Delivery modules check whether Relationship Management Application (RMA) is available in PP.RMA and PP.NO.RMA with Drawee Bank BIC . If the RMA is not available, an override gets populated while authorizing the EB.MESSAGE.111 record. Read Working with RMA for more information.


##### Capturing Stop Request Status

The drawee bank responds by sending either an MT112 (status of a request for stop payment of a cheque) or a CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop report) message to the drawer bank when it receives a stop payment request. This message informs the drawer bank about the specific actions taken by the drawee bank in response to the stop payment request.

The STOP.REQUEST.STATUS application allows the banks to store the inward MT112 (status of a request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop report) message from the drawee bank. The following are the fields in STOP.REQUEST.STATUS.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Drawee Bank BIC | Indicates the BIC of the receiver or drawee bank. |
| Drawer Bank Account | Indicates the account number of the drawer bank. |
| Drawer Customer Number | Indicates the customer number of the drawer bank. |
| Cheque Number, Cheque Type, Cheque Currency Cheque Amount | Indicates the details captured for the cheques. |
| Payee Name , Payee Address , Payee Country , Private and Org Details , Payee Town | Indicates the details of the Payee. |
| Instruction Id | Indicates the unique reference number to unambiguously identify the instruction |
| Orig Instruction Id | Indicates the unique identification number to unambiguously identify the original instruction. |
| Answers | Indicates the answer codes in MT112. |
| Chq Stop Originator | Indicates the party who originated the stop request of the cheque. |
| Stop Status | Indicates the status of the cancellation request. |
| Stop Req Stat Additional Info | Indicates the additional information on the cancellation request status. |


##### Receiving and Storing Inward MT112 or camt.109 Message

The screenshot below explains the processing of the inward MT112 (status of a request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop report) message.

The system determines the NOSTRO account depending on Drawee Bank Pref recorded in CQ.PARAMETER . The NOSTRO account is determined based on the TPH configuration if Drawee Bank Pref is set to ‘Temenos Payments’ else delivery configuration is used.

The inward MT112 (status of a request for stop payment of a cheque) or CBPR+ camt.109.001.01 (cheque cancellation or stop report) messages received from the drawee bank are processed by the Delivery module to the STOP.REQUEST.STATUS application. The Delivery module creates a DE.I.HEADER with Disposition in the unformatted status for each message.

Bank must run the BNK/SWIFT.IN service for MT messages and BNK/XMLISO.IN for MX messages, which sets Disposition of the DE.I.HEADER record to the ‘Formatted’ status and creates the corresponding records in STOP.REQUEST.STATUS.


##### Updating Draft or Cheque Status

The draft or cheque status is updated in Inward MT112 and Inward camt.109.

The system checks the values of the following fields and process accordingly:

- Answer Status Code – Decides on the action taken to the draft if the answer code received in the MT112 message matches with one configured in the Answer Status Code field in CQ.PARAMETER .
- Action Request Status - The PAYMENT.STOP record for the NOSTRO account is created or updated to indicate the draft is stopped when the value is StopCheque.

> **⚠️ Note:** Ensure to run OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE to create or update the PAYMENT.STOP automatically.

The corresponding record from CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT (where the status of drafts is stored) is updated with the Status as ‘Stopped’ after the PAYMENT.STOP record is created.

The system performs the following activities once the STOP.REQUEST.STATUS record created for the inward camt.109 is authorized:

- Identifies the EB.MESSAGE.111 record linked to the STOP.REQUEST.STATUS through the Orig Instruction Id field.
- Updates the Acceptance Status field within the identified EB.MESSAGE.111 record with the value present in the STOP.STATUS field of the STOP.REQUEST.STATUS . This ensures that the status information aligns across both the originating stop request and its associated response.
- If the Stop Status field holds the value ‘ACCEPTED’, the PAYMENT.STOP record is created or updated for the NOSTRO account to indicate the draft that is stopped.

> **⚠️ Note:** Ensure to run OFS.MESSAGE.SERVICE to create or update the PAYMENT.STOP automatically.

After the PAYMENT.STOP record is created the corresponding record from CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT (where the status of drafts is stored) is updated and the Status is updated to Stopped (refer the screenshot).

The corresponding record from CHEQUE.REGISTER.SUPPLEMENT (where the status of drafts is stored) is updated with the Status as ‘Stopped’ after the PAYMENT.STOP record is created.


##### Cheque Type in Outward and Inward Messages for Cheque Stop Request

The Cheque Type Prefix field in the CQ.PARAMETER application indicates if the cheque type is to be prefixed to the cheque number in the cheque number tag (Tag 21 of the MT message or Tag ChqNb of the CAMT message). The allowed values in this field are Blank, Yes or No, where blank is considered as ‘Yes’.

The screenshot below is an example of the CQ.PARAMETER application displaying the Cheque Type Prefix field.

In this message type, update Tag 21 for MT111 or Tag ChqNb for CBPR + camt.108.001.01 as below:

- When the Cheque Type Prefix field is set to Yes or Blank, Tag 21 or Tag ChqNb is populated with the Cheque Type prefixed to the Cheque Number delimited by ‘/’.
- When the Cheque Type Prefix field is set to No, Tag 21 or Tag ChqNb is populated only with the Cheque Number .

#### 📋 Tasks

In drawer bank perspective, when the bank issues the FCY cheque from Payment Order and sends a message out to drawee bank (either MX or MT), it also sends the stop payment of issued cheque and receives the status of the stop payment of the cheque with the below versions.


##### Workflow

The user can perform the below activities corresponding to Foreign Currency Drafts Processing as Drawer Bank in the core banking system.

Create Stop Cheque Request .

This enquiry allows users to create the stop payment request for the drafts which are issued from the payment order application directly through generic version with the mandatory values pre-populated on the screen.

Create Stop Payment of Cheque (Outward)-MT111 .

This version allows the users to manually create the stop payment request for the drafts or cheques and generate Outward MT111 message.

Create Stop Payment of Cheque (Outward)- Generic .

This generic version allows the users to manually create the stop payment request for the drafts or cheques and generate Outward MT111 message or camt.108 message.

View / Amend unauthorised Stop Payment Requests - Sent .

This enquiry allows the users to view, amend the outward unauthorized Stop payment requests (the EB.MESSAGE.111 records) for the drafts or cheques. The user can perform the following.

- View, Edit, and Delete the record
- View ChqRegister Supplement

Authorise/Delete Stop Payment of Cheques - Sent .

This enquiry allows the users to authorize, delete the outward unauthorized Stop payment request (the EB.MESSAGE.111 records) for the drafts or cheques. The user can perform the following.

- Authorise or Delete the record.
- View ChqRegister Supplement

Create received Stop Request Status-Generic .

This generic version allows the users to manually create the records Stop request status of cheques/drafts for the received MT112/camt.109 message.

View / Amend Unauthorised Stop Request Status - Received .

This enquiry allows the users to view, amend ,delete the inward Unauthorised Stop Request Status (the STOP.REQUEST.STATUS records) for the drafts or cheques and the user can perform the following.

- View, Amend, Delete the record
- View ChqRegister Supplement
- View Delivery Header
- View Delivery Message

Authorise/Delete Stop Request Status - Received .

This enquiry allows the users to authorise, delete the inward unauthorised stop request status (the STOP.REQUEST.STATUS records) for the drafts/cheques and has following options

- Authorise, Amend, Delete the record
- View ChqRegister Supplement
- View Delivery Header
- View Delivery Message

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs

A cheque (or check) is an instrument that orders payment of money from a bank account. The person writing the cheque, the drawer, usually has an account with a bank where the money was previously deposited. The drawer writes various details (including the amount, date and a payee name) on the cheque and signs it, ordering the bank (known as the drawee) to pay that person or company, the amount of money stated.

A Demand Draft (DD) is a negotiable instrument issued by the bank, similar to a bill of exchange. Bank issues a DD to a client, directing another bank or one of its own branches to pay a certain sum to the specified party.

The Card Management feature supports the issue and maintenance of various types of cards. The card management life cycle includes processes like issuing of new card, monitoring the card usage, blocking the cards, card expiry, and re-issuing the cards (expired, lost or stolen).


##### Product Configuration

The first step in cheque or draft issue management involves managing the stock. This is common for banker’s cheque, drafts, fixed deposit receipts and credit cards as well as cheques issued to customer accounts.

For cheques, it is possible to record receipt of stock, receiving requests for cheque book from customers, sending a cheque for further local printing and actual issue to customers.

The following flowchart shows the process of stocking and issue of cheque or draft.

The following flowhcart shows the cheque stocking and issue process in Temenos Transact .

| S.No | Parameter | Description |

| 1. | STOCK.PARAMETER | Allows the user to create and maintain different types of stocks such as cheques, bankers cheques, drafts, fixed deposit receipts, and credit cards. |
| 2. | STOCK.ENTRY | Allows the user to record inward and outward printed stock of stationeries such as cheque and fixed deposit receipts. Details such as cheque type, stock series, stock start number, stock quantity, and stock account number are captured. |
| 3. | STOCK.REGISTER | Helps the user to view details such as Stock Register ID, Series ID, Stock Start No, and balance stock. |
| 4. | CHEQUE.TYPE | Allows the user to define the types of cheques supported by the cheque control system. |
| 5. | CHEQUE.STATUS | Allows the user to define various types of cheque statuses issued in the Cheque Issue application. |
| 6. | CHEQUE.CHARGE | Allows the user to define the charging structure to be applied to all cheque types for issues and periodic usage charges. |
| 7. | PAYMENT.STOP.TYPE | Allows the user to define maximum 99 reasons for payment stop instructions such as cheque lost and cheque destroyed. |
| 8. | CQ.PARAMETER | Allows the user to parameterise the transaction and category codes related to CHEQUE.COLLECTION application. It is referred while creating or amending records in CHEQUE.COLLECTION and also helps to define whether account or cheque currency to be considered for raising suspense entries account. |

### 3.1  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The International Banking Account Number (IBAN) is an international standard that allows to uniquely identify bank accounts across national borders. Based on the IBAN, it is possible to identify both the country and the bank where the account is maintained.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services
- Uploading IBAN Directories
- Centralised Reference Data

The International Banking Account Number (IBAN) is an international standard that allows to uniquely identify bank accounts across national borders. Based on the IBAN, it is possible to identify both the country and the bank where the account is maintained.

In Temenos Transact or Standalone TPH, the IBAN module (IN):

- Manages the IBAN Structure rules for the countries that have adopted the IBANs.
- It optionally handles the IBAN National Identifiers
- Provides a set of REST APIs through which the IBAN reference data can be accessed

A set of public methods are available under the System Table (ST) module to access or validate the IBAN-related data against the reference directories.

SWIFT provides the IBAN-related data as part of the following directories:

- SWIFTRef IBAN Plus – This directory includes the IBAN structure rules for the countries that adopted IBAN, the IBAN National Identifiers used in the countries and their corresponding BIC, and the list of IBAN National Identifiers that cannot be used in Payments. From November 2026 SWIFT discontinues support for this directory, which is replaced by the SWIFT Identifiers All
- SWIFTRef Identifiers All – This directory includes all the entity identifiers. This includes BIC, LEI, IBAN National IDs, and national IDs which are not used in IBANs.

SWIFTRef IBAN Plus Upload

- Temenos supports the upload of the SWIFTRef IBAN Plus directory published by SWIFT. The upload processes for the SWIFTRef IBAN Plus files into the Temenos IBAN Structure, IBAN Plus, and Exclusion List are part of the Centralised Reference Data module (RD).
- Clients upgrading from a release before 201907 who have already licensed Delivery (DE) or IBAN module (IN) in the prior release, can get the RD license code at no additional cost. Before starting the upgrade, the customers should request the license code of the RD module from their account manager.
- From November 2026, SWIFT discontinues support for this directory. SWIFT clients can upload the SWIFTRef Identifiers All which replaces SWIFT IBAN Plus

SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory

- Temenos supports the upload of the Identifiers All directory published by SWIFT. The upload of the SWIFTRef Identifiers files is part of the Temenos SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory (SFRD25) module.
- From R25 clients that have licensed the Centralised Reference Data module (RD) will automatically receive the SFRD25 module
- Upgrading clients to R25 which have licensed SFRD25, will automatically receive the RD module
- Based on the configuration of the RD module:
- The IBAN National IDs can be referred from the IBAN Plus or from the Centralised Bank Directory
- The upload process can optionally update the IBAN National ID into the IBAN Plus Directory

Read SWIFTRef Identifiers Directory user guide for more information.

> **Purpose:** *A standing order (or a standing instruction) is an instruction given by a bank account holder (the payer), to their bank to pay a specific amount at regular intervals to another (the payee or beneficiary) account.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services
- Transaction Type Condition, Charge Type and Commission Type
- Asset Reference Details – Stock Register
- Receive Request for Standing Order
- Set up Standing Order
- Execute Standing Order
- Cancel Standing Order Instruction

A standing order (or a standing instruction) is an instruction given by a bank account holder (the payer), to their bank to pay a specific amount at regular intervals to another (the payee or beneficiary) account.

Within the Funds Transfer module, a fully operational sub-module is designed for effective regular payments. Entries are made in the STANDING.ORDER application. This user guide should be read in conjunction with the Funds Transfer user guide.


##### Product Configuration

For each account, a maximum of 9999 standing orders can be defined. During the creation of new standing orders, the system generates this number. Balance Maintenance (BM) STANDING.ORDER types must have a number between 900 and 999 and must be entered by the user accordingly. Therefore, the numbers generated for all other standing orders reach 899 and then proceed from 1000 to 9999.

- 111112.1 – The first STANDING.ORDER existing on the account 111112.
- 222224.7 – The seventh STANDING.ORDER existing on the account 222224.
- 444448.900 – The BM STANDING.ORDER existing on the account 44448, where a minimum balance must be maintained, so that the amount can be transferred from another internal account to restore the balance.
- 444448.901 – The BM STANDING.ORDER existing on the account 444448, where a maximum balance has been defined above which the system transfers the funds out of the account.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The high-level configuration available in the Model Bank is given below:

| S.No. | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | STO.TYPES | Allows the user to define the types of standing orders that can be used by the account holder. |


##### Illustrating Model Products

Different types of standing order are listed below:

| Products | Description |
|---|---|
| Balance Inward | Allows transfer of funds from other internal accounts to restore the minimum balance required. |
| Balance Outward | Allows withdrawal of the excess amount (other than the minimum balance) and makes the payment as specified in the instruction. |
| Balance Principal | Allows transfer of funds during the start of the day process; hence, the system considers the account balance as the opening balance of that day. |
| Fixed | Executes instruction to pay a fixed amount to the bank on a regular basis and debit the customer’s account. |
| Periodic Payment | Allows payment of bills to third parties upon presentation of the bills defined in the standing order. The amount varies and there is no definite frequency. |
| Diary | Maintains a tracer system for ad hoc or regular actions that cannot be defined in a transaction. Users can specify the conditions in which the transactions can be executed in the Diary Details field by attaching a User Routine. |
| Direct Debit | Allows transfer of funds based on the direct debit mandate request received on the account. |

#### 📖 Introduction

Introduction to Retail Sweeping ⓘ Content migrated: Old structure mapped (To be planned)

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

Retail Sweeping provides the functionality to move funds automatically from one account to another, based on a pre-determined set of rules. The main features of Retail Sweeping are:

- Maintaining accounts at a particular balance
- Moving excess funds to another account
- Repaying loans automatically through account sweep. For example, settling Arrangement Loans through Sweeping.

This functionality uses the parameter tables to configure the type of sweep and the accounts to be used for sweeping. It updates the account balances after sweeping the funds and maintains a history for reference.


##### Product Configuration

This topic covers the configuration of AC.SWEEP.TYPE application.


###### Configuring the Sweep Type –AC.SWEEP.TYPE

The AC.SWEEP.TYPE application is used to create the rules for the sweep types. Multiple AC.SWEEP.TYPE records can be created with different combinations of rules for each sweep type.

Screenshot of AC.SWEEP.TYPE application is shown below:

The below table details some of the important configurations in the AC. SWEEP .TYPE application.

| S.No. | Field Names | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Sweep Style | Retail sweep can have one of the following sweep styles: Maintenance Surplus Two-way |
| 2. | Cr Txn Code ; Dr Txn Code ; Ret Cr Txn Code ; Ret Dr Txn Code | Different transaction codes can be defined in the AC.SWEEP.TYPE records to differentiate the entries raised. For a Maintenance sweep, Cr Txn Code and Dr Txn Code fields must be defined. For a Surplus sweep, Ret Cr Txn Code and Ret Dr Txn Code fields are required. For a Two-way sweep, all four fields are required. |
| 3. | Amt Sweep Routine ; Rtn With Sw Amt | The Amt Sweep Routine field can be used to attach a local routine, which returns a locally calculated sweep amount. In the absence of a local routine, system uses the amount from the AC.ACCOUNT.LINK records to determine the amount of funds to be swept. If the Rtn With Sw Amt field is set to Yes, then the sweep routine is called after the sweep amount is calculated by Temenos Transact , thus allowing the Temenos Transact -calculated sweep amount to be modified based on a local condition. |
| 4. | Use Limits | This field allows the system to check the overdraft limit on accounts. It can be set to Yes or No. If set to Yes, then, the limit attached to the From Account is checked. If set to No, then, the system disregards any limit on the account. |
| 5. | Return At Sod ; Prioritise Od | If the Return At Sod field is set to Yes, the system automatically returns the funds swept during the COB process to the From Account during the SOD processing. For return sweeps, the funds are always credited to the first account in the From Account field of the AC.ACCOUNT.LINK record. However, by setting the Prioritise Od field to Yes, the user can specify the sweep to clear any overdrafts among the list of ‘From Accounts’. |
| 6. | Restrict Sweep | This field is used to either stop or override the Posting Restriction rules set at either CUSTOMER or ACCOUNT level. The allowed values are Yes or No or Null. (Read Configuring Posting Restriction in Retail Sweep for more information.) |
| 7. | Restrict Charges | If the field is set to Yes, validation in FUNDS.TRANSFER and STANDING.ORDER applications will generate an error if any charges or commissions are entered. |
| 8. | Balance To Use | This field controls the balance type used by the system when calculating the sweep amount. The current options for account are Online Actual, Online Cleared and Working Balance; and the balances are available in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES record for the account. For Retail Accounts or Arrangement Contracts, the option is the balance type defined in AC.BALANCE.TYPE . |
| 9. | Acct Mode | This field identifies the accounting mode used for executing sweeps. Acceptable values are: SAO – System accepts the overrides encountered while executing a sweep and processes it. Successful sweeps are stored in AC.ACCOUNT.SWEEP.HIST table. SNP – System rejects the overrides encountered while executing a sweep and does not process it. Rejected sweeps are stored in AC.ACCOUNT.SWEEP.ERROR table. The default value is SAO. |


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level specifications required for Retail Sweeping.

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|

| 2. | AC.ACCOUNT.LINK | This application allows the user to create and execute retail sweeps for the accounts. To process retail sweep, user has to capture the Sweep Type , Frequency , From Account and To Account details. An advantage of sweeping is that many ‘from’ and ‘to’ accounts can be defined in the same transaction and the accounts can be of different currencies. |

### 4.2  Posting Restriction in Retail Sweep


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**

> **Key Fields:** *Restrict Sweep*

#### ⚙️ Configuration

The condition set in Restrict Sweep field in AC.SWEEP.TYPE application is used to either stop or override POSTING.RESTRICT (Posting Restriction) rules set at either CUSTOMER or ACCOUNT level.

If the Restrict Sweep field is set to No or Null, the sweeping process ignores the posting restriction and allows the sweep transaction to pass. The process generates the relevant overrides on the respective STMT.ENTRY records.
