### 5.2  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Direct Debit Mandate is an authorisation given to the creditor by the debtor, to collect future payments using direct debit. This mandate allows the creditor to initiate DD collections to debit the debtor’s account and at the same time, it allows the debtor bank to accept and process these instructi...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Applied To*, *Charge Reason Code*, *Charge Return Activity*, *Reason Code*, *Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

Direct Debit Mandate is an authorisation given to the creditor by the debtor, to collect future payments using direct debit. This mandate allows the creditor to initiate DD collections to debit the debtor’s account and at the same time, it allows the debtor bank to accept and process these instructions on the debtor’s account.

Direct Debit (DD) is the most efficient way for an organisation to collect regular or occasional payments from their customers. It has the following advantages:

- Saves time
- Reduces the cost of collection
- It is initiated by the organisation itself rather than expecting the customer to make the payment

The amounts and the DD collection can be fixed or variable (for example, the amount of collection for a monthly phone bill varies from one month to another but a collection to fund a savings account is normally a fixed amount).

From a processing point of view, the DD Mandates are further classified as:

- Debtor DD Mandates – These are the debtor’s view of the mandates. Their purpose is to protect the debtor account and is used for processing inward DD collection. External DD collections – These are received through a clearing interface, from creditors being participants under the scheme. In house DD collections – These are received from creditors who have their collection account within core banking (both credit account and debit account are within core banking).

The clearing channel through which the DD collections are received is irrelevant for the DD Mandate check. For example, a bank can move from one SEPA DD clearing provider to a different clearing provider. A creditor can move from an external bank to the Temenos bank or vice-versa.

- Creditor DD mandates – These are the creditor’s view of the mandates. These type of mandates are used in the outward DD collections process.

From a core banking perspective, such mandates are used by lending and deposit products in the DD collection process for loan repayments and deposit funding. In this context, the creditor is the bank itself and the Creditor Mandate is registered on the loan or deposit account and attached to the settlement conditions.

Previously, the DD module generated and processed the payment files. These were sent to clearing and the inward DD collection files were processed from clearing. The DD module provided a mechanism to generate or receive a text file. The specific formats of the inward and outward files were usually covered by the country or local implementations.

Most of the banks now have a payment system like Temenos Payments Hub, which ensures the payments and direct debit processing. DD module is used to manage the DD Mandates and send the DD collections initiated by Temenos business applications to the payment system.


##### Product Configuration

This is covered as part of feature configuration. There is no specific product configuration.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level specifications required for the Direct Debit (DD) module.

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | DD.EVENTS | This application allows the user to define the list of events to be used by DD module, which can be used in the Status field of the DD module applications like DD.DDI , DD.STANDALONE and DD.ITEM . |
| 2. | DD.REASON.CODES | This application allows the user to define the reason codes applicable for the clearing module and linked through DD.CODES application with various possible events. In addition, it allows the users to define various clearing codes in outward claim file based on the underlying events in DD.ITEM or DD.DDI . |
| 3. | DD.CODES | This application allows the user to define various codes with the respective events for a clearing system. These codes can be mapped to the outward file format when the Reason Code field is defined in DD.OUT.FORMAT application. Banks can charge the customer for all the failed DD collections or Original Collection by setting the Applied To field to All or Original. Charge Reason Code and Charge Return Activity fields are used to define appropriate AA Charge activity and return reason code. |
| 4. | DD.TXN.CODES | This application allows the user to specify the transaction codes that has to be used while generating accounting entries from DD Module for various events. |
| 5. | DD.OUT.FORMAT | This application allows the user to define the prescribed file format for Outward Claim Submission and Return. For outward claim generation, format details have to be attached with the relevant DD.PARAMETER record. |
| 6. | DD.IN.FORMAT | This application allows the user to define the prescribed file format for Inward Claim Submission and Return. |
| 7. | DD.PARAMETER | This application allows the user to define the details related to direct debit system. It contains details like Clearing Account category, Suspense Account category and Standalone Mandate category. It is also used to specify the following: Claim date period for generation of Direct Debit header file can be specified. The number of days after which a file is moved to history. If standalone mandates are allowed, and the currencies and holiday regions to be checked. |
| 8. | DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY | Italian Banking Association (ABI) publishes the Creditor Directory file daily at the end of each day and it must be uploaded regularly in Temenos Transact . This file has the following details of each Creditor: SEDA service to which they have subscribed Activation date Creditor Bank (Alignment PSP in SEDA Terminology) If the Creditor Id is waived or not from remuneration |
| 9. | DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY.PARAMETER | It is used to configure the upload file and date details of the DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY record, which is uploaded by country layer. |
| 10. | DD.MANDATE.SERVICE.REASON.CODE | It is used to map the errors raised from DD mandate with the ISO error codes. User needs to configure these codes. If any error raised other than the configured one, the default error code is mapped. |
| 11. | DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER | It helps to define the parameterisation for bulk or de-bulk SEDA messages. The DD module de-bulks the incoming file in individual requests and applies a transformation to store the bulk and individual request details. |

### 5.3  Outward DD Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos DD module also supports the DD Initiation workflows. Temenos Transact captures the dematerialised information of DD Mandates signed by the loans and deposit customers. These mandates give permission to banks to collect loan repayments and the regular funding for deposit accounts through DD. ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `DD.OUT.FORMAT`, `DD.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Address Format*, *Applied To*, *Block Closure*, *Charge Reason Code*, *Claim Date Prd*, *Cred Bldng Name*, *Cred Bldng No*, *Cred Cntry Sub Division* ... +64 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos DD module also supports the DD Initiation workflows. Temenos Transact captures the dematerialised information of DD Mandates signed by the loans and deposit customers. These mandates give permission to banks to collect loan repayments and the regular funding for deposit accounts through DD. The DD mandates are attached to the loan or deposit settlement conditions and are used to generate the Outward DD collections.

> **⚠️ Note:** The DD module provides options to create SEPA DD Mandates. The country and local implementations cover the requirements for the DD Mandate management requirements specific to the country, clearing or bank.

The module allows the bank to capture their creditor information (Temenos Bank is the creditor), register and maintain own creditor DD Mandates for loans and deposit accounts.

The bank can also setup standalone DD mandates, which indicate a fixed amount and a fixed collection date.


##### Outward DD Collections through TPH

The DD collections are sent to TPH using TPH neutral PAIN.08 format, where country and local implementations can customise this specific to clearing and bank requirements. Returns are processed in TPH and sent to the DD module using an embedded API, which creates DD returns. Once the DD returns are processed, the original DD collections are marked as returned. The following diagram shows the Collection of Loan Repayments/Deposit Funding using DD.


##### Outward DD Collections Through External Payment System

Pain.008.001.02 instructions are generated when the DD collections are sent to the external payment system. The incoming pain.002.001.02 instructions received from the payment system are processed in core banking and the original DD collections are marked as returned. The following diagram shows the Collection of Loan Repayments using DD.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following flowchart shows an overview of the interaction of different applications part of the DD module to ensure the Outward DD processing.

The parameterisation tables are explained below.


##### DD.EVENTS

The DD module can understand and process a set of finite events. Each event is mapped to codes used by the local clearing. Multiple clearing codes can be mapped to a DD.EVENT .

The events defined here can be used by the DD.DDI and DD.ITEM applications. These events control the generation of accounting entries related to claim, reversal and resubmit.

The following table shows the events used by DD.DDI application.

| Activity | Remarks |
|---|---|
| NEW | New mandate created or entered |
| ADVISED | Mandate sent to customer’s bank for approval |
| AVAILABLE | Mandate approved by the Customer’s bank and ready for use |
| ACTIVE | First claim sent or claim already sent to customer’s bank* |
| RETURNED | Mandate returned with a reason code |
| REJECTED | Mandate rejected |
| RESUBMITTED | Mandate resubmitted |
| HOLD | Mandate put on hold (due to some problems) |
| CANCELLED | Mandate cancelled |
| MATURED | Mandate matured –termination date reached* |
| * Status is updated by the system. |  |

The following table shows the events used by DD.ITEM .

| Activity | Remarks |
|---|---|
| NEW.ITEM | Claim Item created* |
| FIRST.ITEM | Claim Item sent for first time* |
| CLAIMSENT.ITEM | Claim file generated for underlying item* |
| CLAIMED.ITEM | Claim accounting raised for the item* |
| DELETED.ITEM | Item deleted because claim is changed to MORTGAGE or standalone claim* |
| CANCELLED.ITEM | Claim item cancelled |
| EXTERNAL.ITEM | External claim |
| HOLD.ITEM | Claim item put on hold |
| LAST.ITEM | Last claim |
| PASTDUE.ITEM | Claim item moved to past due |
| PROCESSED.ITEM | Claim item processed fully |
| REJECTED.ITEM | Claim item rejected |
| RESUBMITTED.ITEM | Claim item resubmitted* |
| RETURNED.ITEM | Claim item returned* |
| CONFIRMED.CANCELLED.ITEM | Claim item is cancelled based on the notification received from TPH* |
| * Status is updated by the system. |  |


##### DD.REASON.CODES

Various clearings identify the DD collection through transaction codes, which indicates that transaction is a DD collection as well as a sequence (that is, claim presentation after DDI lodgement), subsequent claim or return of an item and the reason codes are indicated in returns. The reason codes related to DD for a clearing system are defined here along with the description, which is displayed as enrichment when these codes are referred to in other DD applications.

A dedicated record is released for SEPA. These codes are based on the EPC SDD Core C2B IG 2017, which are published, and banks can customise this list and add additional reason codes if the payment system notifies additional reject or return reasons.


##### DD.CODES

The DD.CODES application links the codes defined in the DD.REASON.CODES application with the events defined in DD.EVENTS application. Based on this, the appropriate reason code is defaulted in either DD.DDI or DD.ITEM based on respective events.

> **⚠️ Note:** There are usually more codes in the local system than the events in Temenos Transact . For example, there are many reasons for a payment to be returned and the local code provides a more detailed reason.

The bank can define the processing of DD.RETURN based on its reason codes:

- Hold Reason Codes - Indicates the reason codes for which the DD.RETURN is placed on Hold. The bank manually investigates the reject or return reason, follows up with the customer and eventually posts the DD return. For example, if the DD collections is returned with reason code AC04 rather than processing the return STP, the DD.RETURN record can be placed in an exception queue. The bank staff then investigate this and follow up with the customer.
- Resubmit Exclude Codes - Allows the bank to parameterise the reason codes for which the DD.RETURN is not resubmitted (provided the auto-resubmit is enabled in DD.PARAMETER ).
- Charge Reason Code - Allows the bank to add the return reason codes for which the charge activities are defined. It must be a valid code defined in DD.REASON.CODES .
- Return Charge Activity - Indicates the AA Activity that is applied to collect the charge. Multiple activities are allowed and are associated with the Charge Reason Code field.
- Applied To - Indicates if the charge is applied to all failed DD collections (original collections and resubmitted collections) or if it applies only to the original.


##### DD.TXN.CODES

This application specifies the transaction codes used when generating accounting entries from DD module for various events such as new, claim, return, resubmit, reject, refuse, and claim resubmitted. A transaction code defined here is applicable for all clearing systems.

> **⚠️ Note:** For contracts based DD collections, forward accounting entries are not raised. Real accounting entries are created only at auto-settlement and when returns are processed. The exceptions are the resubmitted DD collections, for which forward entries are created (as they are not controlled by AA framework but by the DD module).


##### DD.OUT.FORMAT

Each clearing system has their prescribed file format for outward claim submission and return. To create the format to suit the local DD layout, Temenos Transact allows the user to create customised layouts with user configurable parameters.

The Outward and Inward DD collections processing is done by TPH or an external payment system. However, the DD Clearing files will still be maintained for the banks which are migrating from older releases but not improved in future.

When the DD collections are sent to the external payments system, in the outward format linked to the DD parameter, Raise Delivery Msg field must be set to Y. This indicates that a PAIN.008 message is sent to the external payment system through delivery, rather than sending a file.

When the DD collections are sent to TPH, the Local Mapping Routine indicated here can be used to customise the outward message sent to TPH.

Message Version in DD.OUT.FORMAT is specifies the schema version for outgoing pain.008 messages, ensuring compatibility with the SEPA EPC messaging standards.

- V2- pain.008.001.02 format
- V8- pain.008.001.08 format

The validations are given below.

- If the user sets Raise Delivery Msg as Y and Message Version is NULL, the system updates Message Version to V2.
- If Raise Delivery Msg is not YES, and the user sets Message Version as NA, the system throws an error.

For pain.008.001.02, the address lines of the debtor and creditor party are mapped as below.

- If the user enters values for the address line fields are populated, then the system maps address lines to the message.
- If the user does not enter values for the Address Line fields, the system checks if structured address fields are populated and forms the Address Line as below. AddressLine1 - By concatenating Building Name, Post Box, Building Number, Street Name, Room AddressLine2 - By concatenating Town Name, Post Code, Country Sub Division

For pain.008.001.08, the address lines of debtor and creditor party are formed and mapped as below.

- If the user enters Country and Town Name, the system maps the structured address (Country and Town Name) including the optional address fields (Department, Sub Department, Street Name, Building Number, Building Name, Floor, Room, Post Box, Post Code, Town Location Name, District Name, Country Sub-Division) to the message.
- If the Town Name is blank, then the system maps unstructured address to the message including Country (If it is captured).


##### DD File Generation

The custom formats defined in the DD.OUT.FORMAT application covers three basic sections:

- Header
- Data
- Footer

In the header, data and footer sections, details can be specified either as a static information related to file or can be linked to other applications:

- A free text
- A field on DD.ITEM application
- A field linked from DD.ITEM application
- Data derived using a subroutine or a few specific control characters for line control

The ID of the DD.OUT.FORMAT is formed by the clearing system identifier (the id used for the DD.REASON.CODES ) and a numeric sequence. This allows several formats to be defined, so the bank can have a current format in the daily usage and the format being created for a scheduled changeover date. The customised format settings are linked to the relevant DD.PARAMETER application.

This application is similar to DE.FORMAT.PRINT that is used for formatting printed messages.

A limited formatting option is permitted in the following fields:

- Hdr Len Mask
- Data Len Mask
- Ftr Len Mask

The formatting can also be used for spacing the data into columns shown in the examples.

It is also possible to use fields that are used for data retrieval and are not themselves displayed.

The following example shows the setup of an outward claim file format using the DD.OUT.FORMAT application.

| 1-15 | Free Text information Example – Header Details: |  | Y |
| 18-30 | Free Text information Example – VOL1DDSUSD001 | 15R | Y |

|  | CR |  | Y |

##### DD.PARAMETER

This is a high-level parameter application, which contains details related to DD processing. The following are relevant to outward DD collections initiated by the bank as a creditor:

- The Type field is set to OWN.
- The DD control account category ( defined in the Ddi Acct Class field in case of DD Collections raised by contracts or the Std Acct Class field in case of DD Collections raised for Standalone DD Mandates) and suspense account category that are used for auto-settlement.
- The payment system to which the DD collections are sent (the Outward Format field is set to None, TPH or External). If none, the legacy behaviour is used and a file is generated, provided the necessarily details are captured.
- The number of days before the value date when the DD collection must be sent for execution to payment system is defined in the Claim Date Prd field.
- The outward format (set in the Dd Out Format field) that is used when the DD collections are sent for execution.
- The payment service level (set in the Paymnt Srvc Lvl field) which identifies the clearing.
- The DD scheme (set in the Local Inst Code field), if the clearing supports multiple DD schemes.
- The number of days to be considered for the value date of resubmitted DD collections (implicitly indicates the auto resubmit process is enabled) is defined in the Resub Date Prd field.
- Option to immediately make the status of the mandate available (the Mandate Avl Imed field is set to Yes).
- Maximum resubmit number (set in the Max Resumit No field) for failed DD collections.
- Creditor Identifier – Identifies the bank as creditor. Also referred as Service User Number.
- Creditor Name - Indicates the name of the creditor
- Creditor Address - The user can enter the following address details Creditor Party Cred Dept Cred Sub Dept Cred Street Name Cred Bldng No Cred Bldng Name Cred Floor Cred Floor Cred Post Box Cred Post Code Cred Town Name Cred Town Locn Name Cred District Name Cred Cntry Sub Division Creditor Country Model Bank Address
- Creditor Settlement Account – This is not necessarily a Temenos Transact account as it can also store an external account.
- Creditor Originator Clearing Code – This field is captured in Creditor Agent Clearing Code .
- UMR prefix – This field is used while generating a unique mandate reference for the creditor mandates owned by the bank.
- PAIN Override Del Address (the delivery address for pain.008 messages) – If configured, this is captured for all pain.008 messages linked to DD.PARAMETER .
- The Block Closure field in DD.PARAMETER is used to update the cross reference between a standalone DD Mandate and the accounts. If it is set to yes, the internal account block closure file is updated every time a Direct Debit Mandate is created, cancelled or matured for the accounts which reside in Temenos Transact.

Address Format in DD.PARAMETER indicates the type of the address allowed in the outward pain.008 message and this field is allowed for Creditor Mandates ( Type is OWN)

- Structured
- Structuredorunstructured

For own creditor mandates ( DD.PARAMETER with Type as OWN)

- If the user sets Address Format in DD.PARAMETER to blank NULL then, Creditor Country is mandatory Creditor Address Lines is mandatory
- If the user sets Address Format in DD.PARAMETER to Structuredorunstructured for own creditors then, Creditor Country is optional Either Creditor Address Lines or Creditor Town Name is mandatory when Creditor Country is populated. Creditor Country is mandatory when Creditor Town is populated. If any elements in structured address fields ( Cred Dept , Cred Sub Dept , Cred Street Name , Cred Bldng No , Cred Bldng Name , Cred Floor , Cred Room , Cred Post Box , Cred Post Code , Cred Town Name , Cred Town Locn Name , Cred District Name , Cred Cntry Sub Division ) is populated, then Creditor Town and Creditor Country are mandatory.
- If the user sets Address Format in DD.PARAMETER to Structured for own creditors then: Creditor Country is optional Cred Town Name is mandatory when Creditor Country is populated Creditor Country is mandatory when Creditor Town is populated If the user enters any elements in structured address fields ( Cred Dept , Cred Sub Dept , Cred Street Name , Cred Bldng No , Cred Bldng Name , Cred Floor , Cred Room , Cred Post Box , Cred Post Code , Cred Town Name , Cred Town Locn Name , Cred District Name , Cred Cntry Sub Division ) is populated, then Creditor Town and Creditor Country are mandatory. Creditor Address Line is not allowed.

> **⚠️ Note:** From 2025 the structured address becomes mandatory in SEPA messages.

Whenever a foreign currency clearing system is referred, it is assumed that the files are sent either to a branch of the bank to be merged with the local direct debit claims or directly to another clearing system. The merging of any such claim files from a branch for onward transmission to the local clearing system is subject to local development.

The following parameters are specific to DD parameters that are used to process DD collections initiated by the bank as creditor:

- Service User Number – This is captured in the Creditor Id field.
- Creditor Name and Creditor Address

- Creditor Settlement Account – This is not necessarily a Temenos Transact account as it can also store an external account.
- Creditor Originator Clearing Code – This is captured in the Creditor Agent Clearing Code (field in DD.PARAMETER ).
- UMR prefix – This is used while generating unique mandate reference for the creditor.
- The Type field is set to OWN.

Where a foreign currency clearing system is referenced, it is assumed that the files are sent either to a branch of the bank for merging with their local direct debit claims or directly to another clearing system. The merging of any such claim files from a branch, for onward transmission to the local clearing system will be subject to local development.

Temenos Direct Debit (DD) module help the financial institutions to collect regular or occasional payments from their customers in an efficient way. The DD Mandates are captured in the DD module using DD.DDI table as Outward DD Mandates (Type is set to Outward). DD Mandate cannot be amended after authorisation.

Temenos Core Banking captures the electronic information of DD Mandates signed by the loans and deposit customers. These mandates give permission to banks to collect loan repayments and the regular funding for deposit accounts through DD.

Temenos Transact DD module helps to capture the Direct Debit Mandate Requests to collect the regular or occasional payments using DD.DDI application. The new DD.MANDATE.COLL.DETAILS application limits the maximum number of successful collections allowed under the single DD Mandate reference and defines the frequency of collections.

### 5.4  Restrictions on Inward DD Collections


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Under the SEPA Regulation, debtors are allowed to:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Under the SEPA Regulation, debtors are allowed to:

- Block direct debit collections on specified accounts. For example, the debtor can request the bank to allow Direct Debit (DD) collections from his current account but not from the savings or deposit accounts.
- Blacklist or white list specific direct debit creditors.
- Define a maximum limit for a DD collection processed under a given DD Mandate.

This type of services are also common in other markets.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Restrictions on Inward Direct Debit Collections feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Restrictions on Inward Direct Debit Collections feature.

### 5.5  Support for e-Mandates


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Various countries have implemented a Centralised Mandate Service that enables banks to exchange, process and route mandate-related information using ISO20022 messages.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acceptance Status*, *Account Field Extract*, *Application Name*, *Archive Days*, *Attribute Field Extract*, *Block All DD Posting Restrict*, *Bulk Criteria Routine*, *Bulk Id* ... +35 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Various countries have implemented a Centralised Mandate Service that enables banks to exchange, process and route mandate-related information using ISO20022 messages.

A Centralised Mandate Service is usually a dedicated service offered by the national or regional clearing system. The banks collect new mandate, mandate amendment and mandate cancellation requests from their creditors/debtors and, under this service, send these requests to the Centralised Mandate System directly or indirectly, through a direct participant of the service. The Centralised Mandate System performs the validations and forwards the valid requests to the instructed agents. The exchange of the messages between a direct participant and its indirect participants is done outside of this service.

Under the licensable feature DD E-mandate (DDEMAN), the Temenos Transact DD module provides a framework to a debtor bank for exchanging ISO20022 mandate management messages with a Centralised Mandate System. The functionality supports the e-mandates service as a debtor bank and covers the Creditor Driven workflow.

The system can receive files initiated by the creditor banks for registration, amendment and cancellation of Direct Debit Mandates from the Centralised Mandate Service and can send amendment and cancellation requests to the creditor banks for a Direct Debit Mandate which was previously registered through an E-mandate flow.

The following screenshot represents the flow of receiving the files from the creditor bank through the Centralised Mandate Service:

SEDA is a SEPA-compliant Electronic Database Alignment offered to banks in Italy by the STEP2 clearing. The SEDA-specific setup is also released as part of the product.

> **⚠️ Note:** Adaptations to formats or variations supported by other Centralised Mandate Services are not part of the module; they can be covered by local implementations or by country features using this framework.

The incoming files received from the Centralised Mandate System can contain multiple bulks, and each bulk could have multiple requests of the same type:

- pain.009 (registration of new DD Mandate)
- pain.010 (amendment of an existing DD Mandate)
- pain.011 (cancellation of an existing DD Mandate)

The framework provides the Direct Debit Transformation layer, which receives the files through queues and has an option to validate and transform the received files into a Temenos standard format. After the validation is passed, it de-bulks them and bulks the individual requests. The details related to the received files, bulks and received requests are stored in the following dedicated tables:

- DD Mandates Received Files
- DD Mandates Received Bulks
- DD Mandates Received Transactions

The DD.INWARD.MAPPING online service detects the DD Mandates Received Transactions with the status as ’Received’ and processes these transactions based on the request type (registration, amendment or cancellation), creating, updating or cancelling the DD Mandate (DD.DDI) records.

For each received request, the service stores the processing result into the DD Mandates Sent Transaction application . The DD.OUTWARD.MAPPING online service picks the DD Mandates Sent Transaction records with the status as ’New’, it determines each transaction in which bulk must be included and then it issues the messages to the Direct Debit Transformation Layer through Integration Framework. The requests are mapped to the Temenos standard format, bulked and transformed into the format expected by the Centralised Mandate System. A file (pain.012 format) is emitted containing the bulked requests into the queue dedicated to the Centralised Mandate Service.

The Centralised Mandate System sends pain.012S2 acknowledgement files representing the validation result for the received files. These files are received through queues by the DD Transformation Layer, which validates and transforms them into Temenos standard format which are then used to update the status of the DD Mandates Sent Transaction to reflect the acceptance or rejection from the Centralised Mandate System.

If the Centralised Mandate Service sends pain.012S2 which are not accepted, an exception handling flow will be followed and the file can be resubmitted. If a Direct Debit Mandate is created using the E-mandate flow (pain.009 incoming file), the debtor bank can initiate an amendment or a cancellation request and send to the creditor through the Centralised Mandate Service for confirmation.

In this case, these requests cannot be immediately applied. The debtor bank sends the amendment (pain.010) and cancellation (pain.011) requests to the creditor, considering its current creditor bank (the creditor can change their banks during the lifetime of the DD mandate). After the pain.010 and pain.011 files are sent to the Centralised Mandate Service, Temenos Transact receives a pain.012S2 file with the file acceptance confirmation from the Centralised Mandate Service.

The Centralised Mandate Service passes the valid amendment and cancellation requests to the instructed agents. After these requests are processed by the creditor banks, they send back pain.012 messages through the Centralised Mandate Service – E-mandates flow, with the acceptance or rejection confirmation. Based on the received acceptance report, the Direct Debit Mandate is amended or cancelled automatically, or no action is performed.

For each Direct Debit Mandate request (amendment or cancellation) entered in the system, a new record in DD Mandate Sent Transaction is created. The DD OUTWARD MAPPING service determines all the records according to the file type, which must be included in the bulk and issues the messages to the Direct Debit Transformation Layer through Integration Framework. The files are emitted with bulks of pain.010 and pain.011 and are sent to the Centralised Mandate Service.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the parameter setup required for delivery transformation layer.


##### Inward Processing

The inward processing in the Direct Debit Transformation Layer is governed by the setup in the QueueConfigInwardMandate.properties file. The DDInputQueue property identifies the queue where the incoming files are received, for example, DD.BULK.PAIN.QUEUE.

The source name associated with these messages is defined based on the name of this queue. This is used to determine the Mandate Service which is parameterised in Temenos Transact DD module. For example, DD.BULK.PAIN.QUEUE = SEDA. The backup queue where a copy of the incoming messages is stored for audit reason is indicated by the DDBackUpFolder.

-CountryAPIName indicates the country layer API which decides the logic that must be applied to the incoming message. If none is parameterised, then the transformation indicated by the TemenosFormatXslt property is applied to the incoming message to transform the content of the incoming file into Temenos standard format. In case of failures, the message is moved to the queue indicated in the DD.TRANSFORM.REJECT.QUEUE property. If the processing in the country layer API fails, the Delivery Transformation Layer moves the message to the DD.REJECT.QUEUE. If the message fails, the TemenosFormatXsd indicates the folder where the schema for the incoming message is stored.

The variable $XSD_ROOT_DIR indicates the folder where the schema are stored, the $XSLT_ROOT_DIR points to the folder where the transformation is located. The variable $PP_HOME defines the main folder structure, if the exchange and processing is file based instead of queue based.

Attached is a sample file QueueConfigInwardMandate.properties


##### Outward Processing

The outward processing in the Direct Debit Transformation Layer is decided by the setup in the QueueConfigOutwardMandate.properties file. The IFTransitQueue identifies the queue to which the acceptance report messages emitted through Integration Framework (IF) are sent to the Direct Debit Transformation Layer.

The backup queue where the incoming messages emitted from Temenos Transact are stored for audit reason is defined by the DD.BACKUP.QUEUE property. The transformation applies to the IF message to the standard Temenos DD format as indicated by the TemenosXsltFormat. In case of failures, the messages are moved to the queue defined by the DD.OUT.TRANSFORMATION.FAILURE property. If the CountryAPIName is defined, Delivery Transformation layer triggers this logic. If blank, then the transformation indicated by the ISOXsltName is applied to transform to the target format, and the message is validated with the schema defined by the ISOXsdName property. The final message is emitted into the FinalOutputQueue if valid with schema or to the DD.OUT.REJECT.QUEUE if the schema validation fails. The notification sent to the DD module to update the status of the sent transactions, bulks and files is sent to the queue defined in the T24Queue property.

Attached is a sample file QueueConfigOutwardMandate.properties

To process pain.009, pain.010, pain.011 and pain.012S2 electronic files, the Mandate Service field in the DD.PARAMETER application must be set to indicate the electronic mandate service used for a specific DD mandate scheme (for example, SEDA). This setup must be aligned with the source defined in the Delivery Transformation Layer.

The outgoing pain.012 must indicate if the incoming E-mandate request has been accepted or rejected. If it is rejected, it must specify the specific reason code. The reason codes can vary from one mandate service to another and can be parametrised in the DD.MANDATE.SERVICE.REASON.CODE application.

A record is created in this table for the Mandate Service to define for each message type, the reason codes associated with a respective Temenos Transact error or override.

If the error or override raised when DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTION processed does not match the defined error codes, then the default error code configured for the particular message type is returned and is populated in the corresponding record created in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTION .

If the mandate request is processed successfully, the system uses the success code parameterised in DD.MANDATE.SERVICE.REASON.CODE for the respective message type.

For the outgoing pain.010 and pain.011 requests, the amendment and cancellation reason codes must be defined based on the type of request and initiator. It is possible to select the reason codes when the DD Mandate request is created and send to the creditor to indicate the reason of the mandate amendment or cancellation.

Read the Tasks and Outputs section for information on the setup for the Mandate Service SEDA.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Inward Mapping Local Hook API | Allows to add a local routine |
| Max Transaction per Bulk | Indicates the maximum number of transactions that will be included in each bulk |
| Max Bulk per File | Indicates the maximum number of bulks which will be included in each pain.012 file |
| Bulk Criteria Routine | Indicates the local routine that decides the bulking criteria, file name convention and bulk ID convention |
| Archive Days | Indicates the number of days or months after which completed files, bulk and requests can be archived |
| Bulking Days | Indicates the number of days after which mandate sent transactions in New status can be bulked. This number is taken into consideration as a default if no bulking days is specified for the specific transaction type (pain.009, pain.010, pain.011, pain.012). For example, if the transactions to be sent record is created on 1 April in status New and bulking days is 2W (2 working days) and current day is 3rd of April, then this transaction is included in the file. If the transactions are of pain.012 type and no parametrisation specific to pain.012 type is done (see below), the file bulks the transactions to be sent in status New which have the process date as current business date minus Bulking Days. |
| Test Code | Allows the bank to parametrise the test code, which is sent in the Header file. For example, for SEDA, this is T for Test and P for Production |
| Mandate Service BIC | Indicates the BIC assigned to the Centralised Mandate System |
| Service Code | Identifies the Service Code associated with the Mandate Service |
| Message Type | Indicates the bulking type of the transactions which will be sent in the file (pain.009, pain.010, pain.011, pain.012) |
| Msg Bulking Days | Indicates the number of days after which mandate sent transactions in New status can be bulked according to the message type |


##### Transaction Stop Mapping Rules for DD Mandates

The bank can also define Transaction Stop Mapping Rules for Direct Debit Mandates for the system to apply stop instructions to Direct Debit Mandates. In this way, the customers can define stop instructions that can apply to Direct Debit Mandates. For example, they can stop the system to create DD Mandates from a specific creditor and/or with a specific reference.

For this purpose, the following setup is done in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES application.

| Field | Description or Logic |
|---|---|
| ID | DD.DDI*1700 (1700 represents the ID of the DD.PARAMETER record that describes the setup for processing the Debtor DD Mandates) |
| Application Name | DD.DDI |
| Stop Type | SDD |
| Account Field Extract | IBAN.INWARD.ACCOUNT |
| Matching Attribute | MandateReference |
| Attribute Field Extract | CLEAR.SYS.REF |
| Matching Attribute | CreditorId |
| Attribute Field Extract | CREDITOR.ID |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains the functionality of receiving pain.009, pain.010 and pain.011 files through e-mandates flow.


##### Receiving pain.009, pain.010 and pain.011

The incoming files (containing pain.009, pain.010 or pain.011) are received by the Direct Debit Transformation Layer. They are transformed into Temenos standard format, validated and de-bulked and then the details are stored in Temenos Transact DD module.

The processing steps are described in the following picture:

If the incoming file has multiple bulks, each bulk is decomposed in individual transactions:

- The DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES application stores the individual file details.

- The DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS application stores the details for each bulk within the file (the bulk record has a File ID , as a reference).

- The DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS application stores each transaction details within the bulk (the transaction record has the File Id and Bulk Id , as reference).

After the file is received and validated, the records in these files have the Status field set to Received. The DD.INWARD.MAPPING service identifies every record in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS with the status as Received and processes them according to the message type (new, amend or cancel a DD Mandate).

The following validations are done when processing the requests:

- If the file type is pain.009 (create New Mandate), then the system:

1. Checks if the DD Mandate (DD.DDI) exists.
2. If the DD Mandate exists and is Active, an error ’Duplicate Mandate’ is raised.
3. If the DD Mandate does not exist, then the DD Mandate is created using the supplied details.
4. If the DD Mandate is created successfully, it returns the success message, or if any error occurs, then it returns the specific error code.

The following validations are triggered when the DD mandate is created:

1. If debtor account is not found, an error ’Account not found’ is raised.
2. If debtor account is marked for closure, an error ‘Account is pending closure’ is raised.
3. If debtor account or customer has the posting restrict defined for this mandate scheme, an error ‘Account Blocked’ is raised, or if any Facility is defined at the product level (for AA arrangements), an error ‘Transaction forbidden’ is raised.
4. If debtor account or customer has a Transaction Stop Instruction that applies to the mandate and/or creditor ID, an error ‘Transaction Rejected by Customer’ is raised.

- If the file type is pain.010 (amend an existing mandate), then the system:

1. Checks if the DD Mandate exists using the Original Mandate Reference and Original Creditor ID.
2. If the DD Mandate does not exist, then error ‘Mandate Not found’ is raised.
3. If the DD Mandate exists but is cancelled, an error ‘Mandate Cancelled’ is raised.
4. If the DD Mandate is found, then the DD Mandate is updated using the supplied details. The Mandate Reference and Creditor ID are updated with the (new) Mandate Reference and Creditor ID (not with the original one).
5. If the DD Mandate is created successfully, the success message is returned, or if any error occurs, then the specific error code is returned.

> **⚠️ Note:** The same validations are triggered when the DD mandate is amended as in case of pain.009.

- If the file type is pain.011 (cancel an existing mandate), then the system:

1. Checks if the DD Mandate exists using the Original Mandate Reference and Original Creditor ID.
2. If the DD Mandate does not exist, then an error ‘Mandate Not found’ is raised.
3. If the DD Mandate exists but is cancelled, an error ‘Mandate Cancelled’ is raised.

1. If the DD Mandate is found, then the mandate is updated and its status is set as Cancelled.

The following validations are triggered when the DD mandate is cancelled:

1. If debtor account is not found, then an error ‘Account not found’ is raised.
2. If debtor account is marked for closure, then an error ‘Account is pending closure’ is raised.

When processing these transactions, the system checks if there is a posting restriction at the customer or account level that indicates that it does not accept Direct Debits. The Block All DD Posting Restrict field in DD.PARAMETER allows the bank to define this posting restrict.

When a DD.DDI record is created or amended, the system compares the posting restrict defined in the corresponding DD.PARAMETER , with those present at the customer or account level. If found, the system raises an error to indicate ‘Customer/Account doesn’t allow direct debits’.

After the transactions are processed, the status of the records in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES , DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS are changed to ‘Processed’.

The system maintains internally in the DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.CONCAT application a link between the received file, its bulks and transaction and their respective statuses.

When the records in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTION are processed and an error or override is raised, the system checks the values parametrised in the DD.MANDATE.SERVICE.REASON.CODE table. If the error or override is found, the respective reason code is mapped into the Error Code, else the default error code is updated. Once processed, the status of DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTION is changed to ’Processed’, irrespective of whether the corresponding DD mandate request has been successful or not.

A pain.009 file is received in the system for registering new DD Mandates. The incoming file is validated according to XSD schema, and it is stored in the DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES application with the status as Received.

- The system de-bulks the pain.009 message and creates a record for each bulk which is present in the message in the DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS application. For each transaction present in each bulk, the system creates a record in the DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS application.
- Only one bulk is present and inside the bulk, one transaction. The records are created in the above applications with status as Received.

- In this case, when the DD.INWARD.MAPPING process runs, it detects the DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS record with status as Received and checks if the respective Direct Debit Mandate already exists in the system in the DD.DDI application.
- In this case, the DD Mandate for which the registration request is received is not found, and therefore, the service creates the DD.DDI record for that specific DD Mandate.

- The ID of the DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS is stored in DD.DDI to track back to the latest request which has created or amended the DD mandate.
- The records created in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES , DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS are updated with status as Processed.

- The statuses of these records are changed to ’Confirmed’ once the pain.012S2 response file is received from the Centralised Mandate System.


##### Sending pain.012 Files

For each inward transaction updated in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS that has the Status field set to Processed, a record is created in the DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS application with the status as New. This record holds the details of the original message that was received (pain.009/010/011) and the processing result.

The outward processing is described in the picture below:

When the DD.OUTWARD.MAPPING service runs, it picks up all the records in the DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS application with the status as New and reads the DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER table to decide how to bulk the messages in the pain.012 file.

The records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS which have the status as New and the Processed Date equal or older than the date when the service runs minus the number of days mentioned in the Bulking Days field in DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER are considered for bulking.

This gives the bank the opportunity to review DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS and manually change the status of the record and make the relevant changes in the DD Mandate also.

The service forms the bulks considering the DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS which have the same Mandate Service, Message Type and Instructed Agent.

The

field in

is set to 3W (three working days).

Current Business Date is 22 January 2021.

If the DD.OUTWARD.MAPPING service is run on the current date, it considers current business date (22 January) minus 3W and picks up the records with the Processed Date equal or less than 19 January.

The records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS are created with the Status field set to Processed. The Bulk Reference ID represents: First six characters – Fixed identification number (for example, ISFBLK) Next 11 characters – BIC number (for example, ABNRNLNLXXX) Next 12 characters – Unique ID (for example, 421106433401) The DD.OUTWARD.MAPPING service also creates a record in the DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES application with the Status field set to Processed. The default logic for the file name generation is:: First seven characters are SE02SED. Then is the BIC (11) of the sending bank. ‘XxxxX’ – (optional reference) up to 12 characters – must be unique. The last character is .Z. After the records in the DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES applications are created, the status of the record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS is updated from New to Processed. The system also updates the DD.MANDATE.SENT.CONCAT application with the ID representing the File Reference and having the bulk reference and the transactions reference that are part of that bulk. For each outward transaction, the system emits a message into an Integration Framework queue, passing not just the transaction details but also the bulk details, header details and the number of transactions part of the bulk, according to the setup in the DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER application. A record is created in the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE when the outward service is run. The Direct Debit Transformation layer fetches the IF messages from the IF queue where they have been emitted (parameterised in the IFTransitQueue in the Delivery Transformation Layer property file for outward processing) and transforms them to Temenos DD format. Then, based on the file name part, the messages are bulked and the file content is formed. From the Temenos standard format, a final transformation is applied to the message and then the message is validated with the XSD schema. If the validation is successful, then the final message representing the file is placed into the outward message queue. If there are any errors, the messages are placed in the error queue. As a last step, a status update is sent back to Temenos Transact DD module. The Status field is updated as SENT in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULK and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES records. In the DD.MANDATE.SENT.CONCAT application, the status is also changed to Sent.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Max Transaction Per Bulk | 999 |
| Max Bulk Per File | 100 |
| Archive Days | 45D |
| Bulking Days | 2D |
| Test Code | T |
| Mandate Service | EBAPFRPAXXX |
| Service Code | SED |


##### Creating Direct Debit Mandate Requests

Debtor bank captures a Direct Debit Mandate request for amendment or cancellation of a DD Mandate which was previously created in the DD.DDI application, based on an incoming pain.009 file (creation through the E-mandate flow).

After the amendment or cancellation request has been registered, the system can send pain.010 (amendment) and pain.011 (cancellation) bulks to the creditor bank to get the approval or rejection of the requests and either modify or do not modify the existing record in DD.DDI .

The user can register the following information in a DD Mandate request:

- Request Type – Allows to select Amend or Cancel the request.
- Mandate Service – Allows to validate the amendment or cancellation reason codes (in case of an E-mandate). This is an optional field.

- Paymnt Srvc Lvl – Identifies the Payment Scheme (e.g. SEPA).

- Local Inst Code – Identifies the Local Instrument Code (e.g. SDD Core, SDD B2B).
- Mandate Reference – Specifies the Unique Mandate Reference.
- Creditor Identifier – Specifies the identifier associated with the creditor.
- New Debit Account – Specifies another account number maintained by the debtor bank and it is valid only for the amend request type to which the DD Mandate will be moved.
- New Debit Iban – Specifies the IBAN of another account number maintained at the debtor bank, valid only for the amend request type, to which the DD Mandate will be moved.
- Initiated By – Allows to select who initiated the request between Debtor and Debtorbank.
- Reason code – Allows to select the reason code supported by the Mandate Service for the respective request type (valid only for E-mandates) parameterised in DD.MANDATE.SERVICE.REASON.CODE
- Reason Details – Allows to enter the additional reason as a text.
- Orig DD Ddi Id – Specifies the original ID of the DD Mandate. It is a no-input field.
- Dd Mndt Sent Txn Id – Specifies the Sent Transaction record ID. It is a no-input field.

Before the request is created, based on the information added in the record, the system checks if the Debtor DD Mandate identified by Paymnt Srvc Lvl , Local Inst Code , Mandate Reference and Creditor Identifier is registered.

- If the DD Mandate does not exist, if the DD mandate is cancelled or if the Mandate service of the underlying DD mandate has a different Mandate Service, an error is raised.
- In case the request is an amendment, if the new account is not found or if it’s the same account as in the existing DD mandate, an error is raised.
- The system also checks if there is already a pending request for the DD Mandate and if there is, a warning is raised.

If none of the above conditions is found, the system creates the record in DD.MANDATE.REQUEST and updates the request ID of the DD Mandate request in the corresponding record in DD.DDI . The status of DD.MANDATE.REQUEST is then set to PENDING. After the Direct Debit request is created, the system validates if this is an E-mandate, and in this case, it creates a record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS with status as NEW.

At the same time, the system checks the creditor in DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY and if the creditor ID is found and it is active, it populates in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS the creditor bank from DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY and the instructed bank from CA.CLEARING.DIRECTORY .

> **⚠️ Note:** If the creditor is not active or not found in DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY , a warning is raised and the record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS is marked with an error status and will be on hold.

The DD.MANDATE.REQUEST and DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS applications can be updated manually with the status Cancelled. The user can manually cancel the DD Mandate request as the creditor bank is not active or does not exist. If the creditor bank is not a direct participant and no direct participant is found on the SEDA Bank Directory, then an error is raised.

> **⚠️ Note:** DD.CREDITOR.REGISTRY and CA.CLEARING.DIRECTORY are part of the L2 upload.

Whenever DD.MANDATE.REQUEST is created, the ID of the record is stored in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS as well as in the record in DD.DDI . Reversal or amending of a DD Mandate Request record is not allowed.

The following details have been added to a DD Mandate request. The user added the mandate details, the creditor ID, the reason code (as parametrised in DD.MANDATE.REASON.CODES for the Initiated By field) and the reason details of the cancellation.

The system updates the Orig Dd Ddi Id number with the existing DD Mandate record for which the cancellation request is created and the DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS record ID which has been created.

The system checks if this DD Mandate exists based on the added details and if it is an E-mandate. The following record in DD.DDI has been identified as an E-mandate (Mandate service is “SEDA”).

The DD Mandate request is authorised and a record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS is created for the message type as pain.011 (cancellation), with the status as New.

The system updates the DD.MANDATE.REQUEST ID , the cancellation reason codes, along with other details in the record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS .


##### Sending Pain.010 and Pain.011 Files

The records created in the DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS application with the status as New and message type as pain.010 and/or pain.011 are picked up by the DD.OUTWARD.MAPPING service and are bulked based on the setup in DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER , according to the message type, similar as for the pain.012 files.

For each record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , the system creates records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES with status Processed, updating the same status from NEW to Processed of the record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS .

For each outward transaction, the system emits a message into an Integration Framework (IF) queue, passing not just the transaction details but also the bulk details, header details and the number of transactions part of the bulk.

The Direct Debit Transformation layer fetches the IF messages from the IF queue where they have been emitted and transforms them to Temenos DD format. Then, based on the file name part, the messages are bulked and the file content is formed. If the validation is successful, then the final message representing the file is placed into the outward message queue. The status of the records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES is updated to Sent.

When a pain.010 or pain.011 file is sent to the Centralised Mandate Service and then to the creditor bank, the system expects to receive a pain.012S2 validation file (from the CMS – containing an acceptance or rejection response for the file formatting) and a pain.012 file from the creditor bank containing the acceptance or rejection response for each amendment or cancellation request sent. Only after the final response is received from the creditor bank (pain.012 file), the system amends or cancels the existing DD.DDI or no action will be done if the request is rejected.

A Direct Debit request is created for an existing DD.DDI .

The system creates a record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTION with the status as NEW.

When the DD.OUTWARD.MAPPING service is ran, all DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS in status New are picked up and bulked as per the setup in the DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER application for the specific message type (pain.011).

The system updates the record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS with status as Processed and creates records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES with status as Processed.

The DD.BULK.DEBULK.PARAMETER application is set up to consider “0C” days for message type pain.011, meaning that all the records processed today are picked up to be sent.

After the integration service is ran, the status in the records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES is changed to Sent.

The pain.011 bulk is sent to the Centralised Mandate Service and it is expected to receive a pain.012S2 file with a file format acceptance or rejection response. After the pain.011 is validated by the Centralised Mandate Service, it is forwarded to the creditor bank for sending pain.012 with the final response.

When the pain.012S2 file is received, a record is created in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILE in the system with the status as Completed. The record is updated with the Original File Name and Reference (pain.011, in this case, that was sent) and the acceptance or rejection code (in this example, the A00 code is an acceptance code).

If CMS accepts the file format, the status of the records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES is changed to Validated and the accepted status as Accepted.

The status of DD.MANDATE.REQUEST remains Pending until a final response is received in the pain.012 file. After the CMS validates the pain.011 file, it is sent to the creditor bank for a final response. The creditor bank sends a pain.012 file with a response for the pain.011 cancellation request.

When the pain.012 file is received, the records in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES are created in status Received.

When the DD Inward Process is ran, the system correlates the received files with the sent ones and if they are identified, the status of the records in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES is changed to Confirmed.

Based on the response received in the pain.012 file from the creditor bank, the status of the records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES is updated as Completed and the acceptance status as Accepted or Rejected. In the example below, the bank accepted the cancellation request.

The status of DD.MANDATE.REQUEST is also updated as Completed.

As the cancellation request was accepted by the creditor bank, the system cancelled the record in DD.DDI .


##### Receiving Pain.012S2 Files

For each pain.012 file sent by the bank, the Centralised Mandate System sends back a pain.012S2 file as a response, indicating if the messages in the outward file have passed or failed the Centralised Mandate System’s validation.

A pain.012S2 file contains the acceptance and/or rejection response for all the bulks or transactions that were sent in the pain.012 file.

Once the pain012S2 file is received in the system and has passed the XSD validation in the Direct Debit Transformation Layer, the system correlates with the sent file. A new record in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES is created for the received pain.012S2 with the Status field as Completed.

The record contains as the Orig File Name the name of the outward pain.012. According to the reject or acceptance reason passed by the Centralised Mandate System in the pain.012S2 file, the respective records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES are updated with the status as Completed.

The records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS also hold the Acceptance Status field (Accepted or Rejected) along with a code, as sent by the Centralised Mandate System. The DD.MANDATE.SENT.CONCAT application status is also updated to COMPLETED.

File status: When the pain.012S2 file is received, the system correlates it with the Sent File. If this is correlated, the status of DD.MADANDATE.SENT.FILES is updated as Validated; in case it is not, the status is updated as Not Found.

Bulk status: For each pain.012 DD Mandate Sent Bulk that has been fully accepted, its status is set to Completed, as no further details are expected and the Acceptance Reasons as Accepted. For each pain.012 DD Mandate Sent Bulk that has been partially accepted or fully rejected, its status is set to Validated and Acceptance Reasons will be Rejected or Partially Accepted. For any other type of DD Mandate Sent Bulk (pain.010, pain.011), its status is set to Validated, and Acceptance Reasons will be Accepted, Rejected or Partially Accepted .

Transaction status: For each pain.012 DD Mandate Sent Transaction that has been accepted, its status is set to Completed, as no further details are expected, and Acceptance Reasons as Accepted. The status of the correspondent DD Mandate Received Transaction is changed at this point in time to Confirmed. For each pain.012 DD Mandate Sent Transaction which has been rejected, its status is set to Validated and Acceptance Reasons is Rejected. For each pain.010 and pain.011 DD Mandate Sent Transaction that has been accepted or rejected, its status is set to Validated and Acceptance Reasons is Rejected or Accepted. The rejected transactions can be resubmitted. Read the Exception Handling section for more information.


##### Receiving Pain.012 Files

For each pain.010 or pain.011 file that is sent to the creditor bank to approve an amendment or a cancellation request, the system must receive a pain.012 file with a final response to proceed with the modification of the existing DD Mandate ( DD.DDI ) record.

When a pain.012 file is received, the system creates records in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.FILES , DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTIONS in status Received, which are correlated with the records in DD.MANDATE.SENT.FILES , DD.MANDATE.SENT.BULKS and DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS that were created for the pain.010 or pain.011 files.

When the final response is received from the creditor bank, the system also updates the status of DD.MANDATE.REQUEST and modifies or does not modify the existing DD.DDI , based on the response.

When the pain.012 file is received, if the corresponding DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTION is found:

- The status of the record in DD.MANDATE.RECEIVED.TRANSACTION is updated to Confirmed.

- The status of the record in DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTION is updated as Completed.
- It identifies the DD.MANDATE.REQUEST for the sent transaction and performs the following steps:

- If the Acceptance Status of the DD Mandate Request is Accepted and its Request Type is Amend: The underlying DD Mandate is cancelled. A new DD Mandate record is created on the new account, copying all its characteristics, including the related request.

- If the Acceptance Status of the DD Mandate Request is Accepted and its Request Type is Cancel: The underlying DD mandate is cancelled.

If the corresponding DD Mandate Sent Transactions is not found, the DD Mandate Received Transactions status will be set as Not Found, the Error Code and Error Reason will indicate the corresponding sent transaction was not found.

Exception Handling This section explains the flow of exception handling.

There might be the case that for a sent pain.010, pain.011 or pain.012 file, the Centralised Mandate Service will return a pain.12S2 file that contains transaction for which the validation failed due to technical , operational or formatting reasons.

In this case, the DD E-mandates module provides the bank an option to resubmit the rejected transactions within the file. The bank can use this option after addressing the technical or operational issue for which the file has been rejected.

The resubmission of the failed transactions can be done at the bulk level (DD Mandate Sent Bulk) by changing the status to Resubmit. A DD Mandate Sent Bulk can be resubmitted if its acceptance status is either Partially accepted or Rejected. A background process evaluates all the DD Mandate Sent Transactions included in that bulk which have the Status Validated and the Acceptance Status as Rejected.

After validation, it creates a new DD Mandate Sent Transaction with the same details for each resubmitted DD Mandate Sent Transaction, but with no reference to the Sent File and Sent Bulk; the Status of this is set to New and stores the ID of the original resubmitted transaction.

For the new resubmitted pain.010 and pain.011 DD Mandate Sent Transaction, the system validates the creditor bank and the instructed agent and will raise an error if they are not aligned with the directories. The outward process picks up again all the DD Mandate Sent Transaction with status New and resends the file to the Centralised Mandate Service in a pain.010 or pain.011 file.

A pain.010 file was sent to CMS containing three transactions and a pain.012S2 file is received, updating the statuses as Validated.

One transaction from the file was rejected. Its status is Validated and the acceptance status is Rejected.

The Bulk status is Validated and the acceptance status is Partaccept.

The user manually resubmitted the bulk by setting the status to Resubmit.

After the outward service is ran, the system creates a new Sent Transaction for the resubmitted transaction.

The transaction is then sent out in a new pain.010 file.

In a very exceptional circumstance, if a creditor bank, for some reasons, is not able to send an acceptance report (pain.012 file) for a sent DD Mandate request (pain.010/pain.011), the user, as a debtor bank, can complete manually a DD Mandate Sent Transaction.

The user can complete a DD Mandate Sent Transaction if its status is either Validated or Sent. The user can mark manually the DD Mandate Sent Transaction with the status Complete and the Acceptance reason as Accepted or Rejected.

> **⚠️ Note:** This flow must not be used as a normal practice and any manual modification to the status will result in automatic changes to the existing DD Mandate ( DD.DDI ).

If the Acceptance status is Accepted, then the related DD.MANDATE.REQUEST is marked as COMPLETED and the related DD.DDI record is either amended or cancelled based on the request type (details will be fetched based on the mandate request).

If the Acceptance status is Rejected, then the related DD.MANDATE.REQUEST is marked as COMPLETED but no changes are applied to (amend or cancel) DD.DDI .

> **⚠️ Note:** After marking DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS as COMPLETED manually, if either pain12 or pain12S2 is received for the same transactions, then that request will be updated in RECEIVED tables as Not Found.

There might be the case that when a pain.012 file is received from the creditor bank, due to some system validations, an error might occur (e.g. CURRENCY passed in message is not included in DD.PARAMETER ). In such situation, the record in DD.DDI will be in Hold and DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS in status VALIDATED with the respective error.

The user must correct the error, manually authorise the record in DD.DDI and then manually set the status of the DD.MANDATE.SENT.TRANSACTIONS to Complete.

### 5.6  Support Inward DD Processing Through TPH


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Temenos DD module provides the Direct Debit Mandate management solution. Debtor mandates are maintained in this module.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Block Closure*, *Check Mandate Unicity*, *Clear Sys Ref*, *Cred Idnfy Chk Rtn*, *Creditor Id*, *Date of Signing*, *GB Description*, *Local Inst Code* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Temenos DD module provides the Direct Debit Mandate management solution. Debtor mandates are maintained in this module.

While processing the inward or in-house DD collections, TPH invokes various DD Mandate APIs to identify if the bank has the authority to debit the customer account (mandate is present, AVAILABLE or ACTIVE) and further updates the date in DD Mandate when a successful collection is processed. The following diagram shows the DD Inward Collections Processing (Debtor DD Mandates).

When the DD processing takes place in Temenos payments or external processing:

- Temenos DD module provides the Direct Debit Mandate management solution. SEPA debtor mandates and local clearing DD Mandates are maintained in this module.
- While processing the inward SEPA DD collections, TPH or external payment system performs various mandate checks and amendments, by invoking a set of APIs exposed by the DD module.

The debtor bank can handle the Debtor DD Mandates in three different ways:

- Register the mandates based on the info provided by the debtor, which must happen before the first DD collection is received by the bank.
- Mandates are auto registered as part of the first DD collection received in the bank.
- Mandates are processed without being registered in the system. In some schemes like SEPA Core, the mandate check is not required as the scheme participant has the option to request a refund.

The DD Mandate ( DD.DDI ) application allows the user to set up a limit for direct debit collections that can be posted by a mandate to a customer’s account during a specific period of time. TPH invokes an API that checks, before the transaction is posted, if the limit is breached or not. In case the limit is breached, the transaction is rejected. A DD Mandate (record in DD.DDI ) can be amended or cancelled manually, automatically by TPH or by registering a DD Mandate Request.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The decision to auto-register a mandate is controlled by TPH through clearing settings. The DD Mandate management provides the following features:

- It manually registers a SEPA or local DD Mandate.
- Auto-registers a SEPA or local DD Mandate through an API invoked by TPS while processing an inward external or in-house SDD collection.

> **⚠️ Note:** For local clearings, Model Bank provides an option to create a generic Inward DD Mandate, which can be further customised by implementation projects or Country Model Bank solutions to accommodate the specific local clearing requirements.

The following actions can take place during the life of a SEPA debtor DD Mandate:

| Action | Mandate Status | Remarks |
|---|---|---|
| Amend Mandate | Active | An Inward DD Mandate can be amended for the following reasons: Amend creditor ID Amend mandate reference Amend creditor name Amend debtor account within the same bank Amend debtor bank The amendment can be done manually or using update DD Mandate API invoked by TPH when the Inward DD Collection indicates an amendment. When the mandate amendment refers to the debtor account that is changed to another account within the Temenos bank, it implies that the old DD mandate is cancelled and a new DD Mandate is created on the new debtor account. This is due to the technical restrictions as the ID of the Core Banking DD Mandate record is the debtor account. |
| Suspend Mandate | Hold | The mandate is registered but cannot be used until further notice. |
| Auto Cancel Mandate | Cancelled | A mandate is automatically terminated when: The mandate was not used for a certain period (for example, in SEPA, after 36 months). Expired, once an end date is reached. |
| Cancel Mandate | Cancelled | The mandate can been cancelled: Manually by a user. Automatically using Update DD Mandate API, following a request from payment system while processing a one-off or last collection for the mandate. |
| Re-open Mandate | Active | A cancelled mandate can be reopened : When the cancellation has been done by mistake. A cancelled mandate can be automatically re-opened using Re-open DD Mandate API. When the cancelled mandate is re-opened following a request from the payment system, it returns or refunds a specific or last DD collection for which the mandate has been marked as cancelled or terminated. In such cases, a new DD Mandate is setup and the cancelled DD Mandate moved to archive. |


##### Creditor Identifiers under SEPA

A creditor identifier is a unique reference for organisations that collect payments by SEPA DD. It must be included in each SEPA DD collection.

In SEPA, the creditor identifiers have a maximum of 35 characters and the format is defined using the following rules:

| Creditor Identifier | Number of Digits |
|---|---|
| Country code | two digits |
| Check digit | two digits |
| Creditor business code | three digits |
| Country specific part | up to 28 chars |

The creditor business code can be set as ZZZ by default and can be used where the creditor business code in the identifier is not considered for calculating the check digit (for example, IE47DUB304639 represents the same creditor ID as IE47ZZZ304639).

Moreover, creditor identifiers are space and case insensitive and are stored in the Creditor Id field of the Core Banking DD Mandate ( DD.DDI application).


##### Unique Mandate Reference in SEPA

This is a unique mandate reference that is assigned a specific DD Mandate by a creditor and is used throughout the lifetime of that mandate.

In SEPA, the following rules apply to the mandate reference:

- Content contains latin characters as shown below:

- Must not start or end with ‘/’.
- Must not contain a ‘//’.
- It is case insensitive (123AAa45678 and 123aaA45678).

- Must not start with / or //.

- Eliminate any space.
- Replace the characters from position 5 to 7 with ZZZ.

- If the Param Id cannot be determined, the Retrieve Register Mandate API will return an error.
- If more than one record is found, the one that has been most recently changed will be considered.
- The Block Closure field in DD.PARAMETER is used to update the cross reference between an inward or standalone DD Mandate and the accounts. If this field is set to Yes, the internal account block closure file is updated every time when a DD Mandate is created, cancelled or matured for accounts in Temenos Transact.

### 6.1  Account Interest Rounding


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact supports various types of account interest calculations:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact supports various types of account interest calculations:

| Rounding method | Description |
|---|---|
| Natural rounding | Interest (System-calculated value) is rounded to the nearest unit, as defined in the currency record. |
| Round up | Interest (System-calculated value) is rounded up to the nearest decimal point, as defined in the currency record. |
| Rounding down | Interest (System-calculated value) is rounded down to the nearest decimal point, as defined in the currency record. |
| Ryoha Kataha | This rounding method is used for the Japanese market. |

To give an accurate interest total, it may be required to sum the un-rounded individual interest amounts and then to round down or up the total interest amount. The method of rounding the individual interest amounts and the total interest amounts is configurable for credit and debit interest, and is linked to the EB.ROUNDING.RULE application.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Account Interest Rounding feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Account Interest Rounding feature.
