### 7.10  Limits in Multi-Currency Accounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks can sanction a limit for an Multi-Currency(MCY) account at the MCY and sub-account level. It is possible to control the exposure on a specific currency account (sub-account). This enables customer having MCY arrangements with limits sanctioned at the MCY level and/or the sub-account level.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Charge Account*, *Credit Check*, *Credit Chk Condition*, *Credit Chk Txn Type*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Entry Type*, *Expiry Date* ... +14 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks can sanction a limit for an Multi-Currency(MCY) account at the MCY and sub-account level. It is possible to control the exposure on a specific currency account (sub-account). This enables customer having MCY arrangements with limits sanctioned at the MCY level and/or the sub-account level.

The features pertaining to limits are currently not applicable for multi-currency (MCY) accounts in the TBC. Read here for more information on MCY accounts in the Deposits TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Banks can configure the limit property class at the Multi-Currency (MCY) account level, sub-account level (individually) and on both MCY account Level and sub-account level for a MCY account Product.

The Limit Property Class can be attached to the Multi-Currency (MCY) account product. As a result of this, the banks or users can sanction limit to MCY at the MCY arrangement level. A limit created through the LIMIT application can be attached to a MCY arrangement using Limit Reference along with the Serial Number or Limit ID . Further the user can set a secondary limit along with the limit sanctioned at the MCY account level, to act as a cap or ceiling.

The system can be configured to create a limit automatically while opening the MCY account. The Manage Limit and its related fields like Expiry Date and Review Frequency can be used to create a limit while creating the MCY arrangement.

The details such as administrative limit creation, cash flow check, limit style fields, time banding limits, limit maturity, maturity date and maintain limit balance are not applicable to MCY product line. The system raises the following errors if the above fields are added.

- Proofing error at product level
- Validation error at arrangement level

Read Limit Property Class for more information.


##### Maintaining Limit Balances

When the limit for the MCY arrangement is created and managed by AA, the Charge Account field can be used to maintain the limit balances. The details of limits sanctioned, utilised, unutilised and over utilised (or unauthorised overdraft) can be maintained for the MCY Arrangement in Charge Account . When limit for the MCY arrangement is created and managed by the LIMIT application, the Charge Account in the LIMIT application can be used to maintain the limit balances.

Read Limit Property Class for more information on charge account.

The user can create an account with the Limit Account attribute set as yes in Account Product condition.This limit account is updated in the Charge Account field of the limit product condition. This enables the limit account to maintain the limit balances for the MCY arrangement. The banks or users can configure the interest or charges based on the limit balances in the MCY arrangement as per their requirement.

> **⚠️ Note:** Limit balances are not maintained for the secondary limit updated in MCY arrangement.

Read Account Property Class for more information on Limit account.

Further through the limit property, banks or users can implement the credit check at the MCY arrangement Level. Read Credit Check in MCY structure for more information on Credit Check.

> **⚠️ Note:** The CURACCOUNTMCYINF balance type needs to have the Entry Type field set to Stmt for updating the utilised limit in the limit account (defined in the Charge Account field of the Limit property).


##### Suspension of MCY Arrangement

The MCY arrangement can be suspended when it has the overdraft status for certain ageing bucket. The automatic suspension of MCY arrangement is configured based on the limit amount utilisation and overdraft status. The user can also manually suspend the MCY arrangement.

The suspend activity of the MCY arrangement triggers a secondary activity, which suspends all the sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement. Similarly, for a MCY arrangement, that is resumed (automatically), triggers a secondary activity to resume all the sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement.

- New sub-account created under a suspended MCY arrangement results in an immediate automatic suspension.
- The sub-account in an MCY hierarchy cannot be automatically or manually suspended individually and the same can be achieved only through the Automatic and Manual suspension of the MCY arrangement.


##### Limit at Sub-Account Level

Banks or users can attach a secondary limit to a sub-account to capture and control the sanctioned exposure on a currency of an MCY arrangement. They can implement credit check at the MCY sub arrangement level, through Limit Property. Read Credit Check in MCY Structure for more information on Credit Check.

In a sub-account for limit product condition, the Credit Check , Transaction Type , Utilize Limit and Utilize Amount fields can be used. All the other features associated with the limit property class are not applicable for sub-accounts in a MCY hierarchy and the system raises an error during the proofing of MCY sub-account products or a validation error at the sub-account opening stage.

The system automatically maintains limit balances like Limits Sanctioned, Utilised, Unutilised and Over Utilised (or Overdraft), in the individual sub-account level using the Maintain Limit Balance set to yes.

> **⚠️ Note:** For sub-accounts in the MCY structure, the Maintain Limit Balance attribute should be set as yes, else the system raises an error during the creation of the arrangement.


##### Suspension of Sub-Account Arrangement

The sub-account can be suspended or resumed by triggering or resuming the suspension at the MCY level. The system raises an error if the suspend or resume activity is triggered at the sub-account level.


#### 🔧 Working With

Multi-Currency (MCY) account allows definition of limits in MCY and sub-account levels of the MCY arrangement. This is achieved by configuring the limit property and the associated product condition in the MCY arrangement and the sub-account arrangement of the MCY.

The banks or users can sanction a limit at the MCY arrangement level. This enables the user to withdraw more funds from the MCY arrangement.

When a limit is sanctioned for a MCY arrangement at the MCY level, the limit is available for the overall MCY arrangement. The MCY overview screen with the limit sanctioned is seen below:


##### Limit at Sub Arrangement Level

The banks or users can place a secondary limit in the sub-account of an MCY Arrangement to place a cover control on the allowed debit balance for an individual sub-account. This is achieved through the Utilize Limit and Utilize Amount field in the limit condition of the sub-account arrangement. The Credit Check , Transaction Type field can be used to disable the credit check for the selected internal transaction types.

For a MCY arrangement with a limit of USD 10,000 and the sub-accounts with a limit of 2000 USD, 1000GBP and 2000 EUR, the MCY Overview Screen as shown below.

For a sub-account, when the secondary limit is being sanctioned, the system ensures that the secondary limit is within the overall limit sanctioned for the MCY structure. If the secondary limit is greater than the Limit sanctioned, the system raises an override stating: Secondary Limit of sub-account is greater than the primary account MCY Limit.


##### Suspension in MCY Arrangement

The MCY arrangement can be suspended at the MCY level automatically or manually. This activity further triggers a secondary activity to suspend all the sub-accounts under the MCY hierarchy. The same holds good for resuming the arrangement activity at the MCY level. When the MCY arrangement is resumed, the secondary activity resumes all the sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement.

> **⚠️ Note:** Automatic or manual suspension of sub-accounts directly at the sub-account level is restricted.

Consider a Multi-Currency Arrangement having a 3 Sub-accounts in the currency of USD, GBP and EUR.

When the customer tries to suspend the sub-account under the MCY arrangement, the system raises an error.

When the MCY arrangement is suspended it in turn suspends all the sub-account under the MCY hierarchy as shown below.


#### 📋 Tasks

Limit can be sanctioned to MCY Accounts and associated Sub Accounts.


##### Workflow

In Limits, you can perform the following activities:

Limit Properties can be attached to MCY Arrangement and the Sub accounts associated with the MCY arrangement.

To attach limit to MCY account, perform the following steps:

1. Multi Currency Account-Gold .
2. Click the New Arrangement Activity icon for the Multi Currency Account-Gold.
3. Enter the required values in the following fields: Customer Currency
4. Click the Validate icon and check for any errors and overrides.
5. Click the Limit option to expand.
6. Enter the required values in the following fields: Limit Reference Limit Serial Limit Amount
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

To Attach limit to MCY Sub account, perform the following steps:

1. Find Multi Currency .
2. Enter the Arrangement and access the MCY Account Overview Screen.
3. Click the New Arrangement Activity icon for the appropriate Sub account in the MCY Sub Account - Gold option.
4. Enter required value in the Customer field.
5. Click the Validate Icon and check for any errors and overrides.
6. Click the Limit option to expand.
7. Enter required values in the following fields: Credit Chk Condition Credit Chk Txn Type Use Secondary Limit Secondary Limit
8. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
9. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

### 7.11  Migration MCY AccountDetails


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An MCY arrangement can be taken over from legacy system to Temenos' system through the Takeover Activity class. Post migration, the MCY account:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adjust Balance Type*, *Adjust Property*, *Base Ccy Product*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *MCY Orig Contract Date*, *MCY Product*, *MCY Sub Account Product* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An MCY arrangement can be taken over from legacy system to Temenos' system through the Takeover Activity class. Post migration, the MCY account:

- Retains its account number
- Is fully operational across our system
- Has its existing product conditions retained in our system
- Sub-account balances reflect as a memo balance at MCY arrangement level

When the user migrates a multi-currency account, through the provided API, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the migration process.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Balance Maintenance Property Class and its configuration are not required for the takeover as there are no separate bills or balances that can be captured during a migration.

During the migration of data from the legacy system to Temenos' system, it is possible to improve the performance of the takeover process by updating certain AA tables through a background service. Read Customer Arrangement Offline Update for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The migration of a MCY arrangement can be performed using the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT activity. The MCY arrangement and rest of sub-accounts in the MCY account have to be taken over manually and separately by the user for the MCY arrangement migration to complete successfully. The parent and sub-accounts can be taken over using the Accounts Takeover activity.

The capture balance activity should be triggered manually and per account for the MCY parent and existing sub-accounts. All sub-account balances captured should reflect as memo balances at the MCY arrangement level.

The following are the steps for triggering a takeover activity for a multi-currency account:

1. The user defines the following fields using the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT activity: Customer MCY Product Currency MCY Orig Contract Date (MCY Arrangement Opening Date) Base Ccy Product field should always be blank in the Multi-Currency Rules Condition for the takeover activity to be triggered manually for each sub-account
2. The ACCOUNTS-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT activity is used to capture the details of the sub-account(s) involved. The user captures the following: Customer MCY Sub Account Product Currency MCY Orig Contract Date (Sub-Account Opening Date) Master Arrangement ID
3. The user triggers the ACCOUNTS-CAPTURE.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activity to capture the balances of the newly-created sub-account . The following fields must be specified: Adjust Property - BALANCE has to be specified Adjust Balance Type - CURBALANCE has to be specified New Balance Amount

After committing, the system updates the new sub-account balance accordingly. Other currency sub-accounts can also be taken-over similarly using the ACCOUNTS-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT and the ACCOUNTS-CAPTURE.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activities and specifying the corresponding currency.

In case the MCY account takeover is backdated and there is an activity or scheduled charge in the interim period, the user must update the settlement account manually for such charge to get levied successfully. In case of an activity charge and after take-over, balance capture and settlement definition, the user must trigger the activity manually as backdated for the activity charge to get raised and collected accordingly. In case of a scheduled charge, the user should also update the settlement account manually for the system to raise the scheduled charge automatically.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Migration of MCY Account Details feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Migration of MCY Account Details feature.

### 7.12  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Multi-Currency Accounts (MCYAAR) is a module under the Arrangement Architecture (AA) umbrella of products and is part of the Temenos Retail Banking suite of products.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION`, `LIMIT.REFERENCE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adjustment Order*, *Def Credit Check*, *Def Credit Check, Avl Bal Update, Position Adjustment*, *Limit Serial*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs

Multi-Currency Accounts (MCYAAR) is a module under the Arrangement Architecture (AA) umbrella of products and is part of the Temenos Retail Banking suite of products.

The MCYAAR module provides multi-currency account capabilities and maintenance for a financial institution. The module allows the user to create a multi-currency account, making use of Retail Accounts to maintain the currency wise positions of any allowed currencies, without diminishing the existing accounts features and functionalities.

Some of the key features are:

- Create a multi-currency account (MCA) arrangement
- Create and link multiple sub-accounts with a single base currency account at any time
- Define base currency and allowed currencies
- Perform credit transactions for the multi-currency (MCY) account
- Route funds to proper currency accounts based on the payment currency
- Supports single or multiple ownership for the MCY account

- Link single/multiple debit cards to MCY sub-accounts
- Combined statement generation.

- MCY accounts are not enabled to be linked to Transaction Cycler for retrying bill settlements or payments.
- MCY accounts are not enabled to have periodic charges, calculated charges configured at the MCY level.
- MCY accounts are not enabled to invoice the charges, periodic charges that cannot be captialised.
- Unauthorised overdraft cannot be monitored under the MCY level when there is no limit attached to the account.
- To lock funds, the locked event should be placed at the sub-account level with the locked event type having that has account link set to yes. Funds should not be locked at the MCY account level.
- MCY accounts cannot act as settlement accounts in lending, deposit or account arrangements.
- MCY accounts cannot form part of a standing order.
- MCY accounts are not enabled to configure activity restrictions at the MCY level.
- MCY accounts are not enabled to configure dormancy.
- MCY accounts are not enabled to be configured as the liquidation account in contract based applications like LC, Forex, and so on.
- MCY accounts are not enabled to link to retail sweeping or cash pooling or notional pooling modules.
- Transactions to MCY account is enabled to be posted through Payment Order application or APIs through the GAI. Teller, Funds Transfer or Data Capture are not enabled for Transaction Processing in MCY accounts. TPH or Payment Order does not process the transaction from the MCY account level directly. The sub-account number is replaced in the PI or GAI level.
- Manual Funds authorisation request (using the AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION application) and automatic retry for funds (using Transaction Recycler module) is not applicable for MCY accounts including the sub accounts (for each currency). For a payments initiated through Payment Order or TPH, the system performs a funds check. In case of insufficient funds at the MCY account or the subaccount level (based on credit check configuration), the system raises error and payment is cancelled. Therefore, manual funds authorisation or automatic retry of funds is blocked for MCY accounts and its sub accounts.
- MCY accounts are retail accounts – HVT feature is not enabled for MCY accounts.
- MCY accounts are not enabled with passbook feature.
- Existing AR accounts cannot be added to existing MCY account structure.
- Currently one sub-account can be created per currency in a MCY structure.
- AR accounts cannot be changed to MCY accounts using change product. They are different product lines.
- Credit check is based on the working balance including the limit available. Advanced credit configuration using the Balance Availability condition is not possible for MCY accounts.
- Automatic position transfer is triggered only when account results in negative balance due to transactions. Automatic position transfer is not enabled for account moving to negative balance due to any interest or charge capitalisation.


##### Configuration

The AA.PRODUCT.LINE provides high-level definition of the business components (Property Classes) required to construct a product belonging to that line. The Product Lines are defined by Temenos and cannot be modified. The financial institution then uses these building blocks to construct the individual multi-currency products, which can then be made available for sale to its customers. The following Property Classes are enabled for the MCY Product Line.

- Account
- Activity API
- Activity Mapping
- Activity Messaging
- Activity Charges
- Activity Presentation
- Alerts
- Balance Availability
- Charges
- Closure
- Constraint
- Customer
- Eligibility
- Officers
- Statement
- Sub Arrangement Rules
- Settlement
- Payoff
- Payment Schedule
- Pricing Rules
- Limit

The AA.PROPERTY is an instance of AA.PROPERTY.CLASS and these components constitute an account product. The Property Classes and Properties are made mandatory or optional based on the AA.PRODUCT.GROUP level but subject to the Product Line definition. The AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER is used to create the account products required.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The product conditions of a Property Class are evaluated to bring out the features of the Property Class. The system defaults the values in the product condition in an arrangement during its creation. The negotiability or default values and other restrictions are also defined in the product condition. These product conditions along with the properties derived from the Property Classes are grouped together to build products.

The product conditions are dated and some of the product conditions have currency as part of their ID. When the currency forms a part of the product condition ID, the user needs to create different conditions for each currency in which the product is available. When a new condition is created or an existing one is amended, the product to which the condition is linked has to be proofed and published.

Multi-Currency Account Model Parameters are:

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Account | The Account Property Class is used by all account-based products. This Property Class primarily controls the description of the account. The ACCOUNT property allows the user to define and control Balance Treatment, Posting Restriction, Linked Account Number (for memo accounts), Currency Market, Date Convention related setup for the Account. Although account names are typically account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined. |
| Activity Charges | The Activity Charges Property Class defines the charges that has to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made-due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made-due from unallocated credit balance by setting the Auto Settle field to Yes. In accounts, charges are enabled for dormancy, settle payoff and ageing. This Property Class is also used for all AA related modules. Charges are set for various other activities. |
| Activity Mapping | The Activity Mapping Condition in Multi-Currency Product line is limited only to map the events in MCY arrangement to a named activity of Record Event Activity (a non-financial activity). There are no financial activities in MCY arrangements and the Activity mapping for transaction activities are also blocked. |
| Balance Availability | It is an optional property class that holds the settings related to available balance updates, credit checking at the MCY account level and automatic position transfer control (position transfer) for the MCY product line. For the MCY product line, only the Def Credit Check, Avl Bal Update, Position Adjustment and Adjustment Order fields are allowed for input. The system raises errors if the user inputs any field other than Def Credit Check, Avl Bal Update, Position Adjustment and Adjustment Order for the MCY product line. It also raises an error if the Component option in the Def Credit Check field is configured for the MCY product line. |
| Charge | The Charge Property Class is used for all charge calculations in AA. The primary purpose of this Property Class is to enable calculation of charge. The charge defined can be a scheduled charge, a periodic charge or an activity based charge. The charge can be fixed or calculated based on band or level. The currency in which the charge has to be applied can also be defined. It is possible to define a minimum charge and also waive the charge. |
| Closure | The Closure Property Class defines the rules and behavior for processing closure of an arrangement. An arrangement account can be closed automatically or manually and it is defined in the product condition. On reversal of a new arrangement, closure is triggered automatically. |
| Customer | The Customer Property Class is used by all products. This Property Class is used to define all the parties involved in an arrangement and their respective roles. The customer is always defined at the arrangement level. Each arrangement can have one or more legal owners defined in OWNER. |
| Eligibility | The Eligibility Property Class is used to evaluate eligibility of a customer for a specific product based on a set of rules. The eligibility evaluation is triggered at a given frequency or when there is a static change for the customer. First the EB.CONTEXT has to be created. Based on this, rules are defined using Rules Engine. Once these rules are validated, the EB.RULES.VERSION and EB.RULES are created in the system. |
| Officers | The Officers Property Class enables the user to define: Product Arrangement specific officers Officer’s roles Primary officer Additional officer Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single OFFICERS Property defined. |
| Statement | The Statement Property Class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each Account and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This Property Class also controls if advices are to be produced or not, when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced. |
| Sub Arrangement Rules | The Sub-Arrangement Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for currency accounts under a MCY structure. The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is available for the MCY Accounts Product Line. This Property Class enables to set rules for the sub-arrangements under a master arrangement. It is attached to the MCY Accounts product to control the allowed customers, currencies and products of the currency wise sub-accounts. |
| Settlement | The Settlement Property Class enables the user to indicate the settlement account for collecting charges at the MCY level. The system defaults it with the first created sub-account and it can be changed based on customer request. The settlement can be any AR account. Payin or Payout settlement account can be used to indicate payment type specific or property specific settlement accounts. During a live closure, the settlement account is used to liquidate the account funds before closing the arrangement. This account should not be one of the sub-account of the same MCA structure. |
| Payment Schedule | The Payment Schedule Property Class is used to define rules and default schedule of repayments for a product. At the arrangement level it specifies the exact repayment schedule to be applied for the arrangement contract |
| Payoff | The Payoff Property Class allows the user to perform a simulation of account closure and execute the same, if required. The Payoff property can be used to simulate a combined closure at the MCY arrangement level. The system calculates the settlement amount to generate a payoff bill (as an information type of bill) during the closure simulation of the MCY arrangement with its underlying sub-accounts. |
| Pricing Rules | The Pricing Rules Property Class handles the rules governing the selection of appropriate relationship pricing plan, the frequency of selection reassessment and updates the relationship pricing adjustment on the financial arrangement. |
| Limit | The Limit Property Class primarily controls the use of Limit module in the Product. We can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for specific product such that the system defaults the same in an arrangement or give the Limit Serial as NEW at the arrangement level for new limit. The MCY module can also have self-contained secondary limit without having an actual limit attached to it. Overdraft Status, notice credit check etc for the MCY module is handles through the Limit Property Class. Further limits can be set to use the Limit module or it can be managed in the arrangement architecture framework. Fields related to Facility Product Line and External Product Lines are restricted for MCY module. |

| 2 | Multi Currency Account - Gold | Sub-Accounts Allowed Currencies: Any Eligibility: Resident at least 18 yrs old, any Customer(s)/Owner(s) should apply for Parent and all sub-accounts, Customer a resident Sub-Account allowed products: MCY Sub Account – Gold Exchange Rate: Mid.rate |

### 7.13  MultiCurrency Account Creation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Financial institutions can create a Multi Currency Account (MCY) with sub-accounts in different currencies under the MCY account. The system auto-generates the account numbers for the MCY accounts and sub accounts opened in a MCY structure. This account number can be used by the banks and the custom...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acc Bkno Prefix*, *Account Mask*, *Account No Length*, *Acct Checkdig Type*, *Allowed Currency*, *Allowed Prd Group*, *Allowed Product*, *Alt Acct Type* ... +18 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Financial institutions can create a Multi Currency Account (MCY) with sub-accounts in different currencies under the MCY account. The system auto-generates the account numbers for the MCY accounts and sub accounts opened in a MCY structure. This account number can be used by the banks and the customer for all dealings. An account can have single or multiple owners.

When the user tries to create a multi-currency (MCY) account from the front end, the system is configured to trigger the corresponding activity in the TBC to complete the MCY account opening process. During this MCY account opening process:

- The eligibility of the customer for this MCY account product is evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.
- Currently, the functionality pertaining to limits is not applicable for MCY accounts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section orients the user on configuring multi-currency(MCY) account arrangements.


##### Designing Account Number

The user can validate the MCY account number format by the use of check digits or by the automatic inclusion of the CUSTOMER number and/or branch ID.

The COMPANY application defines the length and the check digit type used for a MCY account.

- Acc Bkno Prefix - Defines the bank code prefix which is a part of the local account number in countries like Belgium and Luxembourg and each bank receives a range or a unique identification numbers.
- Acct Checkdig Type - Identifies the check digit calculation method for the company being entered.

The following values are accepted:

- 1 - When the Local Currency starts with BE (that is, identifies Belgium).
- 2 - When the Local Currency starts with LU (that is, identifies Luxembourg).
- 3 - For 10 digit account numbers with a modulus 11 check.
- 4 - For 11 digit account numbers constructed with a 2-digit bank number prefix defined in Acc Bkno Prefix , followed by 7 identifying digits and a 2 digit mod 11 check digit. The prefix may contain leading zeros.
- 5 - For a standard check digit calculation with the account numbers zero filled to the Account Mask .
- 6 - For a 12-14, digit number with two check digits, the first 6 digits, and the second on the remaining digits. The check digits are calculated using mod 11.
- 99 - No check digit calculation, with the account number, padded with zero as per Account Mask.
- @routine name - Where a local subroutine performs the check digit calculation.
- Blank - In all other cases.

The MCY account number display can be controlled using the account mask feature. Account Mask - Identifies the mask that the user wants to apply to customer type accounts. It is a field in the COMPANY table and input in this field must contain at least four # characters to define the minimum length of the account number. It can be up to a maximum length of 20 characters with separators.

The first character can be R, which means that the account number is right adjusted and it can contain leading zeros.

- Mask = ##### - #####. No 1234 displayed as 1234
- Mask = ##### - #####. No 1234567 displayed as 12 - 34567
- Mask = R##### - #####. No. 1234 displayed as 00000 - 01234
- Mask = R##### - #####. No. 1234567 displayed as 00012 – 34567DD


##### Understanding INTERCO.PARAMETER

The following fields in INTERCO.PARAMETER govern the set-up of the branch ID of the bank in the MCY account number format:

- Branch Code Start - Indicates the digit in the MCY account number, at which the branch identification number starts.

- Branch Code Length - Indicates the length of the branch identification number in the MCY account number.

- Account No Length - Indicates the length of the customer MCY account. If the MCY account number length differs from this value, then it belongs to the initial company loaded namely master company.

- Company - Identifies the company whose details are entered in the Branch Code field.

- Fin Mnemonic - Indicates the company mnemonic for the company in the earlier field

- Branch Code - Indicates the branch codes that can be used in the customer MCY account for the company specified in the Company field.

A MCY account number can contain the customer number as part of the record ID. The following fields in the COMPANY table govern the set-up of customer ID as part of the MCY account number format:

- Customer Code Pos - Specifies the start position of the customer code within the MCY account number throughout the system.

- Cust Code Len - Defines the length of the customer number within the MCY account number(together with Customer Code Pos ).


##### Understanding Arrangement Number

The arrangement number is a unique identification number for the arrangement contract. The format of the ID is AAYYDDDXXXXX, where:

- AA - Arrangement Architecture module identifier

- YYDDD - Year and date of input in Julian date format

- XXXXX - A random string generated by the system

When an arrangement is linked to ACCOUNT , the account number and the arrangement ID can be used inter-changeably.


##### Alternate Account Number

It is possible to give alternate account numbers to MCY accounts. There can be account nick names indicated using Mnemonic field. The concept of alternate account number using Alt Id field is used when the legacy account numbers have to be linked to this account, previous IBAN account numbers. The Generate Iban field is used to generate the IBAN number automatically.

In practice, where our system has replaced an existing system, it allows the users to access customer accounts using the old account numbers. In order to allow this, ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER is set-up. This informs the system about the structure of the legacy system's account number (that is, how the legacy account number structure was defined). Once this is set up, it is possible to enter the old account number on the ACCOUNT record in the Alt Acct Type field.

- An index is kept in the ALTERNATE.ACCOUNT table.
- The ID in the external system account number and the single Globus Acct Number field contains the Temenos' system's equivalent.
- If the old account number is longer in length than the existing account number, it is possible to extend the maximum limit through the EB.OBJECT table.
- In the ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER application, alternative account formats can be specified, where the maximum length of fields is up to the number specified in the EB.OBJECT table
- In the Checkdigit Type field, a routine can be entered to validate the alternate account number.
- Multiple ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER records can be created, to allow multiple alternative account numbers.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Multi-Currency (MCY) Account Product Line available in AA allows the financial institutions to offer MCY account solutions to customers. This Product Line allows the customer to set up a base currency account and create multiple currency sub-accounts as per the allowed currency definition at any time.


##### Creating Multi-Currency Accounts

MCY accounts can be created from the Product Catalog by selecting an appropriate Product and triggering new Arrangement Activity.

The customers are defined at the time of the MCY account creation and can be added or removed anytime during the MCY account life cycle. All the customer(s) in the parent arrangement must be the customer(s) of the sub-arrangement(s) within the MCY account.

The MCY Product Line uses existing attributes enabled under Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class related to the Allowed Customers, Currencies and Products, with the following changes/amendments:

- The Customer attribute is set to Parent Customers and Required Customer set to All.
- The Currency attribute supports all the three options namely, Parent Currency, Allowed List or Any and the user can define the list of Allowed Currency . When defined as Parent, it results in MCY account currency auto populated in the AR account arrangement when currency is not specified.

Allowed Prd Group and Allowed Product store the allowed Retail Account products that can be linked to the parent multi-currency arrangement.

The Base Ccy Product field stores the Retail Account product under which the base currency sub-account creates automatically after the MCY account creation.

Correspondence .

Document and image management is not applicable in multi-currency (MCY) accounts, opened in the TBC. The event that the system publishes for a MCY account opening, can be consumed by an external solution applicable for Document and Image management.


##### Single Customer View (SCV)

It enables the banks to view the complete customer information using the Single Customer View (SCV). The Products tab in the SCV displays a list of all the customer accounts including checking, savings, CD, IRA, loan, safe deposit box. The MCY accounts are listed under the Accounts tab. It enables the user to view the MCY accounts for a specific customer.

The features related to opening a new multi-currency account for a customer using the single customer view screen are not applicable in the TBC.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Multi Currency Arrangement

Users can create a new Multi-Currency Account arrangement present in product catalogue, which collectively displays the balances of the Sub Arrangement accounts (of various currencies) by converting it into the base currency.

### 7.14  MultiCurrency Account Maintenance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In the life cycle of a multi-currency (MCY) account, the customer or bank initiates the changes in the account related information. The following are some of the MCY account maintenance activities:*
> 
> **Applications:** `PRINTER.ID`, `REPORT.CONTROL`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Alternative ID*, *Arrangement*, *Narrative*, *New Activity*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In the life cycle of a multi-currency (MCY) account, the customer or bank initiates the changes in the account related information. The following are some of the MCY account maintenance activities:

- Changing the customer
- Changing the account officer
- Changing the statement frequency
- Updating the limit
- Linking a card with charge to MCY arrangement

The features related to linking cards to a multi-currency (MCY) account are not applicable in the TBC.

When any of the other mentioned changes (that is, changing customer, officer or statement frequency) in a MCY account is requested from the front end, through an API, the system updates the respective details, using the corresponding activity in the underlying MCY account record in the TBC.

- During a change customer, the eligibility of the customer for that MCY account product is evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.
- Currently, the functionality pertaining to limits is not applicable for MCY accounts in the TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In an account life cycle, the customer or bank initiates the changes in the MCY account related information. These changes are achieved by initiating relevant activities in the system. Thus, the user can change the attribute values (features) of the different Property Classes in the multi-currency(MCY) account, subjected to negotiation rules, tracking setup, and periodic rules.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following are the multi-currency(MCY) account maintenance activities:


##### Changing the Customer

The Change Customer Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE-CUSTOMER) is used to change existing customers or add other customers to the MCY account. These customers are account owners and their eligibility rules are evaluated during the change activity.

The Update Customer Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE-CUSTOMER) is used to change or update the other parties of the account. The role of the other party needs to be indicated. For example, another customer can be added as a Guarantor.

Any change of customer in MCY account applies automatically for all sub-accounts in MCY account structure.

- In the TBC, when a change of customer is processed, The eligibility of the customer for that multi-currency account product is evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.


##### Changing the Account Officer

The Update Account Officer (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE-OFFICERS) details are used to change the account officer of the MCY account. This activity helps to include, change, or add account officers with specific roles and change the officers for a group of accounts.


##### Changing the Statement Frequency

It is possible to change the existing frequency (daily, monthly, quarterly, half yearly or yearly) at which the combined statement is being generated for a MCY account by editing the same with Update MCY Account Statement Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE-STATEMENT) as shown below.

When a new currency arrangement (AR) is created against a MCY arrangement and if the MCY arrangement’s statement condition has a statement frequency number flagged to produce a combined statement, then the same frequency number in the underlying sub-account arrangements is used for producing the combined statement.

As per the defined frequency, the system hands off the combined statement information to a print carrier solution. These combined statements can be printed using the PRINTER.ID and REPORT.CONTROL configuration. When the printing solution is not configured, the statements are held in &HOLD& folder.


##### Updating the Limit

During the life cycle of a multi-currency account, it is possible to increase or decrease the limit sanctioned for the multi-currency account by using the Update Limit Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE- ).

Currently, the functionality pertaining to limits is not applicable for multi-currency accounts in the TBC.


##### Linking a Card with Charge to MCY Account

The MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-ISSUE-CARD-ARRANGEMENT activity is used to issue a card and link the MCY arrangement. Any charges for the Issue Card Activity can be configured as an Activity Charge to MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-ISSUE-CARD-ARRANGEMENT Activity and applied to the MCY arrangement. This charge gets capitalised to the settlement account as per definition. The MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-ISSUE-CARD-ARRANGEMENT activity can be triggered directly from MCY Overview page under the Cards section.

The features related to linking cards to a multi-currency account are not applicable in the TBC.

Users can amend the customer details by triggering customer related activities. Similarly, the respective activities are to be triggered to amend the account details and so on.

### 7.15  PricingRules for MCY Accounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Financial institutions can impose special pricing for maintaining and servicing multi-currency (MCY) accounts.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Aa Pricing Rule Name*, *After Assessment*, *Credit Exceed One*, *Evaluation*, *Filter by Product*, *Logic*, *Multi Arrangement*, *On Assessment* ... +23 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Financial institutions can impose special pricing for maintaining and servicing multi-currency (MCY) accounts.

- Special pricing can be configured on an activity or scheduled charge, based on certain rules
- The discount on charges or premium on bonus is applicable only if specific balance or transaction count conditions (mentioned in the configuration section) are satisfied.
- A pricing benefit program can be added for the CHARGE property. It can be a complete waiver or adjustment of the charge after evaluation of the rule specified against that pricing benefit.

MCY arrangements can have the following pricing strategies, either independently of each other or in combination:

- Regional pricing
- Customer Related Arrangements pricing (CRA)
- Bundle pricing
- Package pricing

The pricing rules for the special pricing in a multi-currency account in the TBC can be defined and evaluated at TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In a multi-currency (MCY) arrangement structure, it is possible to define the rules governing the selection of appropriate relationship pricing plan at the MCY arrangement level. Banks can define the Pricing Rule condition for this purpose in the MCY account product.


##### Pricing Rule Property Setup

The property for which the pricing rule will be evaluated can only be any CHARGE property of the MCY account product, otherwise, the system raises a validation error.


##### Program Rules Setup

MCY pricing plans evaluate the rules each time a charge is triggered against a MCY account. Based on the evaluation results, the pricing is adjusted to the MCY arrangement accordingly. The following are the fields in the Program Rules and Benefits tabs:

- Program – Specifies the pricing program to which the pricing benefit rule belongs to. It is defined through the AA.PRICING.PROGRAM virtual table
- Rule Name – Specifies the name of the rule that needs to be evaluated. This is a free text field and is mapped to the Aa Pricing Rule Name field.
- Periodic Attribute – Specifies the periodic attribute that has to be used for the evaluation and is derived from AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE table. Only the periodic attributes that belong to Pricing Rules are allowed.
- Source - Specifies the rule source for the periodic attribute evaluation
- Value - Specifies the rule value that is used for the evaluation of the rule

- Filter by Product – It is used only if there is a need to define the product based on which the belonged related arrangements are subjected to rule assessment

The following screenshots display the setup and rules of MCY Pricing Programs.

- Pricing Benefit – Specifies the name of the benefit, the customer receives. It fetches value from AA.PRICING.BENEFIT virtual table.
- Pricing Property - Specifies the property for which the rule will be evaluated on. Only properties that belong to Charge Property Class are allowed.
- Trigger – Specifies when the rule starts running, that is, the trigger event. Allowed options are:
- Evaluation – Specifies when the pricing benefit is deemed as qualified. Allowed options are: Pass – When the specified rule is satisfied Fail – When the specified rule is broken
- Rule - Specifies the rule that is defined in Rule Name is allowed here.
- Logic – In case of multiple rules defined in PRICING.RULE.NAME, value in this field specifies whether all rules or any of the rule should pass to qualify for the pricing benefit
- Result – Specifies the resultant action to be taken on the pricing property. Allowed options are: Adjust - Adjusts the final value Override - Overrides the final value with a different value Waive - Waives the value altogether

> **⚠️ Note:** The following fields are restricted and made as no- input in the Pricing Rules Product Condition. Package Product Package Property Control Regional Product Regional Property Control Plan Select Type Plan Select Property Plan Reset Freq Plan Reset On Act Plan Select Method


##### Configuring MCY Periodic Attribute

The Periodic Attribute controls the attribute values of a MCY arrangement based upon periods of time. The following fields should be defined as follows in MCY periodic attribute setup:

- Multi Arrangement - Should be defined as MCY . When MCY is defined, the system lists the active MCY sub-accounts at the MCY arrangement creation level.
- Source Type - AC.BALANCE.TYPE or AA.ACTIVITY are the only allowed values.
- Satisfied by - Denotes if the periodic attribute has to be satisfied by all MCY sub-accounts combined or by at least one of the sub-accounts within the MCY structure. Options are Combined or Any .

The following MCY.BALANCE periodic attribute uses a Balance source type. It is evaluated on all active arrangements within the MCY account. The system uses a minimum allowed value comparison type and raises a rule error or override message when the rule is broken.

The following section describes different pricing strategies in MCY accounts.

Regional pricing helps the bank to specify a pricing plan for a particular branch in state of a region. This hierarchy is pre-defined in the organisation hierarchy setup. It is not customer or channel specific and it allows a bank to modify their MCY products pricing based on branch location.

Read Introduction to Regional Pricing for more details on Regional Pricing.

Customer Relationship Pricing can be enabled by grouping the related and unrelated arrangements of the customers.

Read Introduction to Household Pricing for more details on CRA.

A MCY arrangement can be part of the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS table (defined per customer), which defines the list of arrangements that receive special pricing benefits, charge waiver, etc based on the relationship of the family group or household with the bank.

A pricing rule with Multi Arrangement periodic attribute set as Cra can be used to evaluate the household’s services or products used. This setup can evaluate the households combined Product Count, Service Count or Product or Service based balances for the specified balance types.

If a MCY arrangement is part of a bundle with specific pricing rules, a special discount or premium can be offered to the MCY charge or bonus respectively. Also, the system considers the MCY balance in the evaluation of balance-based or number-of-products based criteria.

Read Introduction to Charges in Bundles for more details on Bundle pricing.

A pricing rule with Multi-Arrangement periodic attribute set as Bundle can be used to evaluate the household’s services or products used. This setup can evaluate the households combined Product Count, Service Count or Product or Service based balances for the specified balance types.

Package Pricing provides customers special pricing benefits in charges based on the package they use. This package can be any combination of customer service like the number of arrangements in different products or different services opted by the customer. In case of MCY arrangements in the package, pricing benefits are applied to the charges at MCY level.

The Property Control Property Class controls the behaviour of bundle properties and its impact on the participant arrangements. The Product Bundle Property Class allows definition of eligible product participants of the bundle product and minimum or maximum participants per product group and/or product.

Read Introduction to Package Pricing for more details on Package pricing.

Read Product Bundle Property Class for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

A scheduled charge or activity charge can be subjected to pricing rules when configured in the product. The pricing plan defined in the Pricing Rules condition offers a pricing adjustment when the condition is satisfied. The following are examples of how a discount is applied for activity charges and scheduled charges.


##### Activity Charge Discount

The charge under consideration is a USD10 activity charge – it is a charge on occurrence on the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE-CUSTOMER activity namely ADMINFEE.

Consider an example where an override charge amount of USD 5 is provided only when a minimum balance of USD 20,000 is maintained in the MCY account.


###### Periodic Attribute Setup

The pricing rules are configured in the MCY account using the MCY.BALANCE periodic attribute that is enabled by setting Multi Arrangement to MCY and is capable of evaluating eligible credit activities. The periodic attribute is configured as below:

- Period Attribute Class - BALANCE
- Source Type - AC.BALANCE.TYPE
- Multi Arrangement - Mcy
- Satisfied By - Combined (denotes the periodic attribute to be satisfied by all sub-accounts put together in the MCY structure)


###### Pricing Rules Evaluation

The Pricing Program Rules setup is on the MCY account using the MCY.BALANCE periodic attribute and a USD20,000 evaluation value.

The rule evaluation of maintaining the minimum balance value of USD 20,000 in all sub-accounts combined must pass for the system to raise the override on the USD 5 activity charge. The rule evaluation is triggered on assessment, that is, when the activity charge is to get raised and capitalised and the pricing benefit is applied for that instance of assessment.

The Activity Charge condition setup is shown below.

The user triggers the Change Customer Activity on the MCY account . Evaluation disqualifies, since the minimum MCY account balance of USD 20,000 is not maintained. Hence, the pricing benefit is not applied and the activity charge of USD10 is raised.

Consider another credit activity against the MCY account takes place as follows:

FT activity triggered to transfer 4000 USD to EUR sub-account

Consider the user triggers the Change Customer Activity on the MCY account. At this point, the evaluation should pass successfully since the balances put together of all sub-accounts involved in the MCY structure satisfy the minimum balance evaluation rule. Hence, the MCY arrangement gets the discounted activity charge of USD5 imposed.


##### Scheduled Charge Discount

Consider an example where a discount is given to a scheduled charge in case two or more credit transactions are executed against a MCY account. The charge under consideration is a USD10 scheduled charge namely ADMINFEE.


###### Periodic Attribute Setup

The pricing rules are configured in the MCY account, using the Credit Exceed One periodic attribute that is enabled by Multi Arrangement set to MCY and is capable of evaluating eligible credit activities. The periodic attribute is configured as below :

- Period Attribute Class - TRANSACTION.COUNT.TOTAL
- Source Type - AA.ACTIVITY
- Multi Arrangement - Mcy
- Satisfied By - Any (denotes the periodic attribute has to be satisfied by at least one of the sub-accounts in the MCY structure)


###### Pricing Rules Evaluation

The Pricing Program Rules setup is on the MCY account using the Credit Exceed One periodic attribute and an evaluation value of ‘one’ transaction.

The rule evaluation of maintaining a minimum of one executed credit transaction must pass for the system to provide a discount of USD4 on the USD10 scheduled charge. The rule evaluation is triggered on assessment, that is, when the scheduled charge is to get raised and capitalised and the pricing benefit is applied for that instance of assessment.

The evaluation takes place before first scheduled charge is triggered and gets disqualified since no credit transaction has been identified against the MCY account.

There are two credit transactions in the MCY arrangement before the next charge schedule.

As a result of this, during the pricing rule evaluation on the next schedule, the rule gets qualified and an adjusted amount of USD 4 is applied.

The following section describes different pricing strategies in MCY accounts.

When an MCY arrangement is created in a specific branch (ST.BRANCH in the arrangement creation), a discount can be applied on the charges at the MCY level based on the pricing rules.

Read Working with Regional Pricing for more details.

When a customer’s MCY arrangement is part of a household pricing, the MCY arrangement can contribute to the pricing evaluation based on the services and products used by the customer relationship arrangements. Further, the pricing rule condition can specify a discount on the charges at the MCY level.

When a customer’s MCY arrangement is part of a bundle, the MCY arrangement can contribute to the pricing evaluation based on the services and products used in the bundle.

Further, the pricing rule condition can specify a discount on the charges at the MCY level.

During a bundle creation, multiple arrangements including MCY can be packed together under the bundle page in the Arrangement Creation Activity. The bundled products are validated against the pricing rules and charge waiver or discounts are applied according to the setup.

This pricing rule definition at the bundle level is propagated to the individual arrangements based on the definition in the Property Control Property Class.

The Pricing Rules condition at the bundle level (that is, Package Pricing Rules) is merged with the condition of the primary arrangement. During rule evaluation, in addition to evaluating the rules of primary arrangement, the rules defined at bundle are evaluated and the details are stored in the AA.EVALUATION.DETAILS table.

The Package Pricing Property control is used to replace the charge condition or pricing rules condition. For MCY products, the charge or pricing rules condition that is triggered to be replaced should only be another condition that abides to the respective properties validations for the MCY product in place.

### 7.16  SubAccounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The user can create sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement for each allowed currency. These sub-accounts are created in the account arrangements created in the Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY product.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity Link*, *Allowed Product*, *Base Ccy Product*, *Currency*, *Effective Date*, *Master Arrangement*, *Product*, *Product Only*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The user can create sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement for each allowed currency. These sub-accounts are created in the account arrangements created in the Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY product.

There are no specific differences, related to the creation and update of sub-accounts under a multi-currency account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The sub-accounts are account arrangements created in the product defined in the Allowed Product field of Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY product. The linkage between sub-arrangements and a parent arrangement within a multi-currency (MCY) account is supported using the Master Arrangement field of AAA. In addition, information related to the connection between the two arrangements is updated in the Activity Link type field .

Refer to Configuration of AR Accounts for more details on the configuration of Sub-Accounts.

Further, the arrangement account product for the sub-account should have the Product Only field set as ‘Mcy’ in the AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER . This setup specifies that this product is for MCY sub-accounts only and it allows the bank to differentiate between the features of regular current, savings and MCY sub-accounts.


##### Automatic Creation of Base Currency Sub-Account

When the MCY arrangement is created, the system can be configured to create the base currency sub-account automatically. The automatic account creation can be configured by setting up the Base Ccy Product field in Sub-arrangement Rules condition of the MCY arrangement. The product should be a MCY only Product in AR product line. When the user gives this (Base Ccy Product) product in the Sub-arrangement of the MCY product configuration (or at MCY arrangement level), the base currency sub-account creates automatically in this product as part of MCY account creation.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can create sub-accounts for each allowed currency in the MCY arrangement. On creation of the MCY arrangement, the system can be configured to create the base currency sub-account automatically or manually.


##### Automatic Creation of Sub-Accounts

The system recommends to create the base currency sub-account automatically by indicating the ‘MCY only’ account product in the Base Ccy Product of the Sub-arrangement rules.

The following fields auto populate in the new sub-account:

- Effective Date - Displays the date which is same as the opening date of MCY account arrangement
- Currency - Displays the base currency indicated in MCY account arrangement
- Product - Displays the sub-account opened in the Mcy-only product given in Sub-Arrangement Rules based on the Base Ccy Product field definition
- Master Arrangement - The system defaults this value as the MCY Account Arrangement ID
- Customer - The system defaults the customer and customer role information from MCY parent account

Following the MCY account creation, the system automatically creates the base currency sub-account as shown below.

As soon as the MCY account gets authorised, both MCY parent and base currency account move to Current status.

When a sub-account is created under the master arrangement, the system automatically updates the links between the sub-account and master account in AA.ARRANGEMENT .

The MCY arrangement holds the sub account details as shown below.

The sub-account holds the MCY arrangement details as shown below.


##### Creating a Sub-Account under MCY Account

It is possible to create a sub-account from MCY Overview page. If the base currency sub-account is not created automatically, the base currency sub-account should be manually created using the same option.

> **⚠️ Note:** Until the base currency sub-account is opened, the MCY account is in inactive (AUTHORISED) status.

> **⚠️ Note:** The MCY account and the sub-accounts should belong to the same company. The system raises an error when the user tries to open a sub-account in a company which is different from the MCY arrangement account’s company.


##### Maintenance of Sub-Accounts

The sub-accounts are maintained similar to AR accounts.

Read Introduction to AR Account Maintenance for more information.

The base currency sub-account can be created manually by triggering the corresponding API. Similarly, the sub-accounts in other currencies are opened by triggering the corresponding API.

Users can create a new sub account arrangement with various currencies under the Multi Currency Arrangement Account.

### 7.17  SubArrangementRules


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for the Sub-Arrangements (sub-accounts) created and linked with the multi-currency(MCY) account. Customer, currency and product of the currency arrangements created under the MCY account are restricted.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allowed Arr Per Ccy*, *Allowed Product*, *Allowed Product Group*, *Base Ccy Product*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Product Only*, *Required Customer*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for the Sub-Arrangements (sub-accounts) created and linked with the multi-currency(MCY) account. Customer, currency and product of the currency arrangements created under the MCY account are restricted.

There are no specific differences related to defining conditions for creation of sub-accounts using sub-arrangement rules.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the Sub-Arrangement rule conditions for multi-currency accounts.


##### Currency Sub-Accounts

As defined in Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class , currency sub-accounts can be created with restrictions on:

- Customer – In Sub Arrangement Rules, the Customer attribute should be set as Parent Customer and the Required Customer attribute should be set as All in the MCY Product setup. All the customer(s) in the parent arrangement must be the customer(s) of the sub-arrangements in the MCY structure. When the sub-accounts are automatically opened by the system at the time of the MCY arrangement, the customer information in the sub-account is defaulted from the MCY arrangement. When the sub-account is opened manually, it is recommended that it should have same customer information as the MCY arrangement. Any change of customer in MCY account applies automatically for all sub-accounts in MCY account structure.
- Currency - Sub-accounts can be opened in any of the allowed currencies
- Allowed Product Group - This field specifies the Accounts product group under which the sub-account product should be created. The system evaluates this field at both the product proofing and the arrangement levels . It raises an error if more than one product group is defined for a MCY product.
- Allowed Arr Per Ccy – This field should be set to One for MCY Product line. No other values are allowed and this is a mandatory field.
- Allowed Product – This field specifies the Accounts product under which the sub-accounts can be created for the MCY arrangement. The allowed sub-account product should have the Product Only field in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER set to Mcy. The system evaluates this field at the product proofing and the arrangement levels. It raises an error if more than one sub-account product is defined for a MCY product.
- Base Ccy Product – This field indicates the product under which the base currency sub-account should be created automatically at the time of MCY arrangement creation. The Base Ccy Product , if defined, should be same as the Allowed Product defined in that condition. Else the system raises a proofing error.

> **⚠️ Note:** The sub-arrangement rules of an MCY product should not be set as a Product Only property.

Refer to Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class condition for the use of each option for Customer, Currency and Product.

- The customer number defined at the sub-account level is evaluated against the records in Party TBC.
- The currency details of a sub-account are evaluated against the values defined in Reference and Market Data TBCs.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Sub-Arrangement Rules are used for defining the rules for currency sub-accounts.The following section describes the processing of these Sub-Arrangement rules.


##### Creating a Multi-Currency Sub-Account

During a sub-account creation, the sub-arrangement rules defined at product level are validated and if the validation fails, errors are generated. These validations are applied since the sub-arrangement rules are being defined for MCY accounts and sub-accounts are created under a MCY account as a child arrangement.

The Sub-Arrangement Rules control the below actions in the sub-account:

- Change of customer

- Change of product

- Change of currency


##### Creating a Sub-Account with Base Currency

The base currency sub-account is the first sub-account that must be created by the user. The system can automatically open a base currency sub-account at the time of MCY account creation using a configuration or the user can manually open it after MCY account creation.

The MCY arrangement has the status as AUTHORISED (inactive) till the base currency sub-account is created. If the user tries to create any other currency account directly before creating the base currency sub-account, the system raises an error.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Multi Currency Arrangement

There are no Tasks available for Sub Arrangement Rules feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Sub Arrangement Rules feature.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`
