### 9.1  Block Creditors or AutomaticDebits from Account


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Under Single Euro Payments Area SEPA regulation, the debtors are allowed to:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account*, *Applied To*, *Applied to*, *Attrib Fmt Api*, *Clear Sys Ref*, *Customer Id*, *Direct Debit Service*, *Hook Api* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Under Single Euro Payments Area SEPA regulation, the debtors are allowed to:

- Block direct debit collections on specified accounts. For example, the debtor may request the bank to allow direct debit collections from his current account but not from the savings or deposit accounts.
- Define transaction stop for SEPA creditor restrictions.
- Define a maximum limit for payment against Direct Debit (DD) mandates.

New capabilities are added in the Transaction Restrictions module to allow the bank user or customer to blacklist or whitelist specific creditors, either at customer level or account level.

Moreover, the stop instructions will allow the bank user or customer to restrict DD collections initiated under a specific mandate reference and or creditor identifier to a maximum amount or an amount range, at customer level or account level. Payments processed through TPH will refer to the transaction stop instructions while processing the payment.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes blocking creditors or automatic debits from an account.


##### Blocking Direct Debit Collections on Specified Accounts

The debtor can request the bank to block direct debit collections on his account. For example, the debtor may want to allow for direct debit mandates to be set up for his current account and not for his savings and deposits accounts. Accordingly, the bank will decide the products for which the direct debit service is Opt-out by default and for which of them the facility is Opt-in. For example, the direct debit service for debtors will be Opt-in for current accounts but will be Opt-out for savings and deposits. This setup will be checked when a direct debit mandate is manually set up or automatically registered when a direct debit collection is processed (if the DD mandate auto registration is enabled in TPH). While parameterising the products, the bank can also setup activity restrictions to indicate that activities associated with the settlement of inward direct debit collections are not allowed.

The facility product conditions allows the bank to decide for which products the direct debit service can be Opt In or Opt Out, by default. The default option can be modified at the arrangement level, if it defined as ‘Negotiable’ at the arrangement product condition.

The following screenshot shows the FACILITY product condition attached to current accounts, in this condition the Direct Debit Service is setup as Opt-In.

The bank can use the Opt-Out option to stop the direct debit mandates being setup on the products like savings, lending, deposits, etc., where they can opt out of the Direct Debit service.

When the user tries to setup the Direct Debit mandate on an account for which the Direct Debit service is opted out, it will trigger an error as shown below:


##### Transaction Stop based on SEPA Creditor Restrictions

| Attribute | Allowed Operand |
|---|---|
| Creditor Identifier | Equal, Not Equal |
| Mandate Reference | Equal, Not Equal |

- The customer can instruct the bank to create transaction stop instruction at the customer level or account level.
- If the Customer Id field is updated with a valid customer Id, for which the restriction is setup, the restriction applies to all the accounts of the customer.
- If the Customer Id is defined in the Customer Id field and a specific account number of the customer is defined in the Account field, the restriction setup is applicable only for that specific account of the customer.
- If the customer is not defined, the Account field becomes mandatory, making the stop instruction apply only to the account specified.

In order to set-up restriction on creditor, following actions must be performed:

- The appropriate stop condition which has the attribute creditor identifier should be selected.
- Select the creditor identifier attribute with appropriate operand and define the creditor’s account number (also accepts IBAN) in the corresponding Value field.

The transaction stop instruction for creditor restriction can be configured to:

- Restrict DD collections from blacklisted creditors.
- Process DD collections from whitelisted creditors.
- Restrict maximum limit for DD collections for specific creditors.
- Restrict maximum limit for DD collections for specific creditors for specific DD mandate.

Here, the direct debit collection will be rejected.

##### Transaction Stop Check to be Triggered by TPH and SEPA Direct Debit

A Transaction stop mapping rule allows the bank to parameterise the sources for which the stop instructions can be checked and will allow to indicate how the stop attributes will be extracted from transaction.

The transaction stop mapping rule will allow fields which are in other tables than the main transaction table to be retrieved and used during the transaction stop check.

The following record in transaction stop mapping rules ( TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES ) will be parameterised for TPH and SEPA direct debit core.

A local API can be triggered if specific rules should apply before comparing the transaction field against the value of the attribute in the stop instruction. This API can be linked to the Hook Api field in TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES .

Core provides an API, TRANSACTIONSTOP.FORMATCHECK , which considers the creditor Id provided and if the creditor ID is for SEPA. It will replace the business code with ZZZ before the comparison.


##### Transaction Stop Instruction Applicable for the Next DD Collection Only

In the Transaction Stop Instruction application, the Applied To field is used to indicate if the stop conditions are applicable for the next payment only or for all the payments that match the instruction.

TPH checks the transaction stop instructions after validating the DD mandate. If the DD mandate check fails, the transaction is rejected or moved to repair and the stop instructions are not checked.

When TPH invokes the transaction stop check, the system evaluates all transaction stop instructions set up at the customer or account level:

- If at least one of the transaction stop instruction matches, TPH rejects the transaction.
- If a transaction stop instruction matches and the Applied to field is set to Next Payment Only, TPH rejects the transaction and the transaction stop instruction is automatically cancelled. Any other DD transaction posted after cancellation of the transaction stop instruction will be processed by the system.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Applied to field is not set, the system rejects all payments that match the transaction stop instruction.

- A Transaction Stop Condition record is set up in the system as follows:
- The TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION is set up for the Mandate Reference, Creditor Identifier, and Amount attributes.
- The Transaction Stop Type record is set up for SEPA Direct Debits posted by TPH.
- The Transaction Stop Map Rules record is configured in the system for Direct Debits posted by TPH ( POR.TRANSACTION ) to be matched with the Amount, Mandate Reference and Creditor Identifier attributes.
- A Direct Debit mandate is created in the system in the DD.DDI application with the following details:
- The DD mandate is created for account 11018 with the Mandate Reference MD-CORERCUR18 ( Clear Sys Ref field in DD.DDI ) and the Creditor ID CREDZZZ18.
- A Transaction Stop Instruction record is created in the system to stop only the next payment ( Applied to field) posted by a mandate that has the reference as MD-CORERCUR18, the creditor identifier as CREDZZZ18, if the amount in the transaction is greater than 400.
- TPH posts a Direct Debit transaction from the same Mandate Reference and Creditor Identifier for 500 EUR against account 11018.
- Because the transaction matches the transaction stop instruction, the system rejects the collection. As the instruction was configured to be applied only for the next transaction, after the collection is rejected, the system cancels the transaction stop instruction.
- If TPH posts other DD transactions for the same Mandate Reference and Creditor Identifier, they will be processed as there is no stop instruction in place.

#### 📖 Introduction

The TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.INSTRUCTION application allows the bank to capture a stop instruction on one account. Each record captures one instruction where multiple stop instructions can be captured on one account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.INSTRUCTION application allows the user to define the Transaction Stop Instructions for a particular account.

The screen below shows a sample TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.INSTRUCTION and the usage of the fields in this application.

- Stop Condition – This is an optional field, the bank can define various conditions to restrict the user to use a specific set of stop attributes. The stop condition is defined in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION .
- Transaction Type/Channel – This field allows the bank to indicate the instruction that applies only to specific transaction types or channels. This is assigned by transaction source and is indicated in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES in the Stop Type field. If the field is blank, then the stop instruction applies to transactions received via any channel or source.
- Stop Instruction Channel – This field indicates the channel through which the instruction has been setup (either online, in the branch or based on a letter sent by the customer). The values can be customised by the bank through EB.LOOKUP .
- Stop Reason – This field captures the reason why the stop instruction is created. The values can be customised by the bank through EB.LOOKUP application.
- The Stop Criteria allows the user to define the criteria for stop by specifying: One or more attributes (released through EB.LOOKUP ), the same attribute can be used only once in a stop instruction. For each attribute, an operand (fixed set of operands released by core) and the corresponding value is assigned One or more values for each attribute.

The attributes in the stop criteria are defaulted from the setup in the appropriate TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION record, if a Stop Condition is selected by the user. The user cannot add other attributes and cannot delete the defaulted attributes. For each attribute, the drop-down list for the operand only displays the operands which are defined in the Stop Condition record for that attribute.

The below screenshot shows the setup in the Stop Condition record Stop by Amount, where the only attribute is Amount and the allowed operands are Equal, Range and Less Than.

When the stop instruction is captured and the Stop Condition is populated, the attribute name from the Stop Condition record above and the operand drop-down list displays only the allowed values.

When the stop instruction is captured and no Stop Condition record is indicated, the user can select the attribute names. The drop-down shows only the attribute names defined in the DEFAULT record of TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION table.

Some details related to a cheque replacement can also be captured in the stop instruction. These are used for information only, and are normally captured when the stop instruction refers to a cheque for which a replacement has been issued. The user can indicate an expiry date for the stop instruction.

When a TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.INSTRUCTION is authorised and the user has not indicated an expiry date, Core Banking sets the Expiry Date to the current business date + default expiry days, if Default Expiry Days is indicated in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.PARAMETER. Once a Stop Instruction Channel is authorised, the status is set to Active.

A stop instruction once setup can be amended, if required. If the user wants to cancel a stop instruction, the Cancel Instruction flag is marked as Yes. When this is authorised, the status automatically moves to Cancel and the cancellation date is set.


##### Housekeeping Process for Expired and Cancelled Stop Instruction

An online service BNK/TRANS.STOP.ARCHIVE marks the stop instruction as Expired when the expiry date becomes less than or equal to the current business date. The same process moves the cancelled and expired stop instructions to history, based on the value in Days To History in TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.PARAMETER .

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Transaction Restrictions module allows the bank to define stop instructions for an account, which is evaluated when a payment or booking request is processed on the debit account. This module provides an exception approval flow when the stop instruction is triggered on a transaction.

The transaction stop instruction defined for the account can be specified to be in place for an indicated period of time. The stops can be defined using generic attributes such as cheque number, amount, party identifier and party name. The user can combine the attributes to define the stop criteria such as amount less than a specific value and cheque number in a specific range.

> **⚠️ Note:** A fixed set of operands are available in the Temenos Transact system and the bank can parameterise which of these can be used for a specific attribute.

- For amount, user can use the operands equal, range, less or equal and less than.
- For cheque number, user can use the operands equal and range.

The module has several parameterisation tables allowing the bank to:

- Define the transaction sources.
- Determine which are in scope of stop check.
- Customise what can be captured in a stop instruction.
- Define how to handle a transaction which matches at least one stop instruction.

Based on configuration, the Temenos Core Banking System verifies transactions initiated via Generic Account Interface (GAI also known as OFS clearing) to find if they are in scope of stop check. If it is in scope, the transactions are evaluated to verify if they satisfy the stop instructions set on the account:

- If the transaction matches a stop instruction and the default decision is to return, then GAI rejects the entry (SNP mode) or post this to suspense (SSS or SAO) and creates an AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION record as an investigation item.
- If the transaction matches a stop instruction and the default decision is to pay, then GAI processes the transaction further but creates an AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION record as an investigation item.
- If the transaction does not match any stop instruction, the entry is processed further.

Core Banking provides an enquiry to monitor the investigations items. The process to post or return the transaction raised by the GAI based on the outcome of the account or payment officer decision is covered by local implementations.

Other business applications (for example, Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) are linked with the Transaction Restrictions module. The stop instruction check is not triggered at the account layer. The sources, which are in scope of stop check are parameterised and the business application invokes a stop check API, provided by Temenos Core Banking, and handles the response returned for the stop check.

> **⚠️ Note:** Transaction Restriction module has not replaced the Payment Stop application and is not integrated with the Temenos Cheque Management System.


##### Product Configuration

The parameterisation of the Transaction Restriction module is covered using the following tables:

- TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.PARAMETER – It stores the main parameters that apply to stop instructions. For example: Default expiry days, the day after which cancelled and expired stop instructions are moved to history. Duplicate check criteria for stop instructions.
- TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.TYPE – It allows the bank to define stop types (usually per source or channel) and specifies various match type rules which meet the stop instruction. For each match type a decision on how to handle the transaction is specified. The transaction can be either returned or paid but an investigation process is triggered for the user to confirm the system decision.
- TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION – This can be used when the bank wants to impose limitations on the stop criteria, which can be captured by the user. For example, stop by cheque number and amount.
- TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES – It allows the bank to define the transaction sources for which the stop instructions are checked and how the value of the stop attributes can be extracted from the transaction.

| Transaction Stop TS1234 | Transaction Stop TS2354 |
|---|---|
| Account 12345678 Transaction Type = ACH Stop Instruction Channel = Bank Stop Reason = Stop ACH Attribute Name.1 = Amount Operand.1 = Equal Value.1.1 = 300 Attribute Name.2 = Party identifier Operand.2 = Equal Value.2.1 = ABC Company | Account = 12345678 Transaction Type = ACH Stop Instruction Channel = Mobile Stop Reason = Stop ACH Attribute Name.1 = Party Identifier Operand.1 = Equal Value.1.1 = ABC Company Attribute Name.2 = Amount Operand.2 = Equal Value.2.1 = 300 |

The TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.TYPE table allows the bank to define stop types (usually per source or channel) to specify various matching types. One or more matching types can be defined by combining attributes which once matched, the stop instruction is considered satisfied, irrespective if not all of its criteria are actually met.

For each matching type, a default decision on how to handle a transaction that matches at least one instruction are also defined here:

- Return – The transaction is rejected
- Pay – The transaction is posted

The rules defined here are evaluated in order. A stop is found when a match type is met. The default decision of the satisfied matched type is considered and the next match type rule does not get verified.

The bank has defined the following stop types for transactions associated with the ACH debits.

Consider that the stop instruction on Account 12345678 has the following stop criteria:

- Amount Equal 100.
- Party Name Equal ABC company.

An ACH transaction REF123 is received and evaluated against the rules defined in this. The transaction is on the Account 12345678, amount 200, party name is ABC Company and party identifier is AB123456.

The amount and the party identifier in the transaction does not match the amount in the stop instruction. Party identifier is not part of the stop criteria and therefore the first match type in the ACH record is not satisfied. The next match type is based on party name. As the party name in the transaction and stop instruction is equal, the second match type is satisfied and the default decision of this match type is to reject the transaction.

Another ACH transaction REF129 is received and evaluated against the rules defined in the ACH record. The transaction is on the account 12345678, amount 100, party name is XYZ Company and party identifier is XY123456.

The amount and the party identifier in the transaction does not match the amount in the stop instruction. Party identifier is not part of the stop condition and therefore the first match type in the ACH record is not satisfied. The party name in the transaction and stop instruction is different and therefore the second match type is not satisfied. The amount in the transaction and stop instruction is equal and therefore the third match type is satisfied and transaction is paid.

In both cases, an investigation item is created for the bank user to monitor the exceptions and take a decision.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the record in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.TYPE is blank, it means there are no matching conditions that override the stop instruction. In that case, the transaction satisfies the stop instruction if all criteria are met. The default decision is to reject the transaction.

TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION parameterisation table can be used when the bank wants to impose limitations on the stop criteria, which can be captured in the stop instruction. For example, stop by cheque number and amount. The stop condition, once indicated in the stop instruction, validates that the stop criteria input by the user is aligned with the rules imposed by the bank.

The following condition record indicates that for the stop criteria in the instruction, it is mandatory to have cheque number and amount and the operands allowed for each of them.

Based on this setup, when a stop instruction is initiated by the user and the Stop Condition is ’Stop by Check Number and Amount’, the Stop Criteria is auto-populated from the Stop Condition .

If the Stop Condition is left blank, the user can select the attributes from those which are defined in the DEFAULT record in TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION .

> **⚠️ Note:** Only one operand can be used at a time in one stop instruction, irrespective of the number of operands mentioned in the stop condition.

TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES parameter table defines the sources to which a transaction stop check applies.

The above record shows the setup for transactions initiated though the Generic Accounting Interface (OFS Clearing), posting rule for local clearing (LCLG – the ID of the AC.ENTRY.PARAM record).

A qualifier condition is added to indicate that only specific transactions received through this interface are checked against stop instructions (in this example, if Transaction Code = 1).

The channel or transaction type, which is assigned to these transactions, is defined in the Stop Type and are used:

- To identify the stop instructions that apply to these transactions. A Stop Instruction for a transaction type = ACH applies to a transaction received from this source. A Stop Instruction with transaction type left blank applies to all transactions received from all channels. A Stop Instruction for a transaction type different than ACH (for example, cheque and DD) cannot apply to a transaction received from this source.
- To identify the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.TYPE record which defines the matching criteria and the default decision.

The Account field indicates the field in the transaction’s business application (identified in Application Name ) from where the account is extracted.

In the above example, the account number in AC.INWARD.ENTRY table stores the account where the funds are posted, the active stop instructions on this account is retrieved. The matching attributes and rules on how to extract them from the transaction’s business application are defined in Matching Attribute and Attribute field Extract fields.

In the above example, Amount Lc y is a core field in AC.INWARD.ENTRY but Party Name and Party Id are local fields in the same application.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the high-level specifications required for the Transaction Restriction (TZ) module.

| S.No | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.PARAMETER | This application allows the user to define the default expiry days of the transaction stop capture instruction. If default date is not mentioned at the parameter level, then it has to be captured at each instruction level. Number of working days is also defined post which expired or cancelled instructions will be moved to HISTORY. The Dup Stop Criteri a field is defined to check if the transaction stop instruction captured is already entered or not. |
| 2. | TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.TYPE | This application allows the user to define Stop Type using various matching types. Different matching types can be defined by combining various matching attributes. For each matching type combinations defined in Stop type, Match Type field allows the user to define if the transaction must be rejected (return) or posted (pay) using matching attributes. |
| 3. | TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.CONDITION | This application allows the user to default or impose limitations on transaction stop criteria, which can be used to stop instruction. Different stop attributes like Cheque Number, Amount, Party Identifier, Party Name (values in Attribute Name field) and so on are available. Additional attributes can be defined in the EB.LOOKUP application in Model Bank. |
| 4. | TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES | This application allows the user to define the sources to which a transaction stop check applies. Mapping rules can be defined for the transaction initiated through different sources like OFS clearing, fund transfer, for all the incoming debits processed through TPH. |

#### 📖 Introduction

The Transaction Restriction module allows the bank to define the rules to filter and extract the relevant payments details and update them in the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT (Payment Regulatory Reporting table) application. This is consulted by the CRS and FATCA module to determine the indicator of the customer standing instructions.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic details the mapping rules for Payments Regulatory Reporting.

The Transaction Stop Mapping Rule with Purpose = RegReport is used:

- To define the criteria to determine if the payment is in scope of reporting.
- If payment is in scope, the user must define how the attributes of the TPH transactions are mapped into the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT application, considering TPH transaction details are stored in multiple.

- The Qualifier field, Qualifier Operand and Value fields define conditions to filter the transactions received from TPH which must update the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT table .
- The Match Attr field indicates the field in the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT which stores the value extracted from the TPH transaction.
- The Match Attr Ext field indicates the field in the TPH (in the application, POR.TRANSACTION ) from where the values are extracted.
- The Linked By field indicates the TPH-linked table from where additional details are extracted. The Linked Match Attr field indicates the field in the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT which stores the value extracted from the TPH transaction. The Linked Match Attr Ext field indicates the field in the linked TPH application identified in Linked By field. The Linked Match Cond Fld , Linked Match Cond Opr and Linked Match Cond fields are used when the details are extracted from a multi-value set to define the rule based on which the correct set of values are referred. The above record is released as part of the model bank configuration and is checked when TPH invokes the Update Payment Regulatory Reporting API.
- Checks if the transaction meets all the qualifiers criteria: It is initiated by a customer (CTRBTRIndicator = C). It is an outward payment (PaymentDirection = O). It is a credit transfer (ClearingTransactionType = CT (SEPA Credit Transfer) or BLANK (SWIFT Payment) ) It is an international payment (DomesticInternational = I).
- If a transaction is found, then it extracts its details and maps them into the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT table as follows: Execution Date = Processing Date in the POR.TRANSACTION table. Customer Number = Customer Id in POR.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO , from the set of values which has MAIN.OR.CHARGE.ACCOUNT.TYPE = D. Payment Country = Country Code in POR.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO , from the set of values which has the Party Role = ACWINS (Account with institution).

The POR.SUPPLEMENTARY.INFO record is identified through id of the transaction being processed (LINKED.BY – the ID of POR.TRANSACTION )


#### 🔧 Working With

The basic details related to any inter payment are extracted and reported duly under payment regulatory reporting.


##### Extract Payment Regulatory Reporting Details

All outward customer international payments, irrespective of whether they are cleared through market infrastructures (for example, STEP2, Equens) or through correspondent banking (SWIFT), are in scope of the CRS or FATCA regulation for standing instruction indicia. The basic details related to these payments are extracted and updated in the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT which are then analysed by the CRS and FATCA modules.

The process is as follows:

- After a payment is successfully processed (status = 999), TPH invokes the Update Payment Regulatory Reporting API exposed by the Transaction Restriction module.
- The Update Payment Regulatory Reporting API checks the parameterisation in the Transaction Stop Mapping rule for TPH.
- If a parameterisation is found with Purpose = RegReport, it then checks if the TPH transaction matches the qualifier conditions. If all conditions are satisfied, the details are extracted from the TPH transaction and are updated in the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT based on the extracting rules.
- The ST Indicia determination process (ST.CREATE.INDICIA services) picks the details of these transactions from the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT , verifies if they are in CRS and/or FATCA scope and then updates the status of the record as processed.
- After the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT is marked as PROCESSED it is immediately moved to history.

The parameterisation in the Transaction Stop Mapping Rule application is explained in the configuration section.

The screenshot below shows an outward SEPA Credit Transfer processed through TPH transaction details, classified as an international payment to GB:

Using the parameterisation in TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES with Purpose = RegReport, the following details are updated in the TZ.PAYMENT.REGULATORY.REPORT for the above transaction.

There are no Tasks available for Payment Regulatory Reporting feature.

There are no Outputs available for Payment Regulatory Reporting feature.

### 9.5  Transaction  Stop Check for Booking Requests


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Generic Accounting Interface (GAI) invokes the transaction stop check after the initial technical validation has passed (these are validated if the received entry is correct), the account has been identified and the duplicate check is performed for a clearing entry but before accounting.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Clearing Result*, *Error Message and Susp Reason*, *Original Trans Ref*, *Rel Instr Id*, *Request Code*, *Set Type or Orig Dec*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Generic Accounting Interface (GAI) invokes the transaction stop check after the initial technical validation has passed (these are validated if the received entry is correct), the account has been identified and the duplicate check is performed for a clearing entry but before accounting.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

In order to trigger the transaction stop check of booking requests generated through GAI the bank parameterises the source in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES .

The following parameterisation record is created for the GAI booking requests processed through the LCLG posting rule.


##### No Matching Type Rule Defined in the Stop Type Record

If no matching type rule is defined in the relevant stop type record, the default behavior is to evaluate the transaction against the Stop Instruction. If all the stop criteria are met, the default decision is to return the transaction and therefore the entry is rejected and an investigation item is created.

In the transaction source mapping rules, the ACH stop type record is used while booking entries with posting rule LCLG. The stop type record for ACH has no match type rules defined.

The following stop instruction is set on the Account 10995 and is active.

The following booking request is posted usingGAI.

Considering the above mapping rules for the LCLG source, transaction has been qualified for stop check (transaction code is 1). The stop instruction on the Account 10995 is active and therefore is considered as the booking request for the same account.

All criteria in the stop instructions are satisfied. As there are no specific match type rules, the default decision is to reject the entry. An error is raised and the entry is not posted due to the stop instruction.

The entry also indicates the investigation item (

ID) raised to monitor the failed payments due to stop instructions.

The user can look at the investigation item raised for this exception. The Original Trans Ref field refers to the AC.INWARD.ENTRY table. Request Source is CSM, which is the system Id for AC.INWARD.ENTRY and Request Code field is Transaction Stop, which indicates the reason why this item is raised.

The Set Type or Orig Dec field indicates the transaction is rejected (REJ) and the Rel Instr Id stores the id of the stop instruction and the decision against this (RETURN). The users can record their decision and finally decide if the entry is posted or rejected.


##### Matching Type Rule defined in the Stop Type Record

If matching type rules are defined in the relevant stop type record the system compares the transaction with the stop instruction but only considers the attributes indicated in the match type, and any other criteria in the stop instruction is ignored.

> **⚠️ Note:** Once a match type is satisfied its default decision applies. Therefore, the order in which the match types are defined in the stop type record is important.

Consider the following stop type record for ACH.

Based on this parameter, the transaction is evaluated against the stop instruction and if the amount and party name attributes match the default decision is to return, irrespective of other criteria in the stop instruction. If these attributes do not match then the next step is to verify if the transaction amount matches the criteria for amount in the stop instruction (if the criteria is defined). If this matches, the default decision is to pay. If the amount do not match, then transaction doesn’t match the stop instruction and the processing continues.

Consider the same stop instruction as in the previous example.

Consider that the following booking request is posted with the LCLG:CSM=BOOK,OFS/I/PROCESS///,INPUTT/123456/GB0010001////,LCLG,01,10995,THEIRREF012,100,1,ABC Companionway

Considering the above mapping rules for the LCLG source, the transaction has been qualified for stop check (transaction code is 1). The stop instruction on the Account 10995 is active and therefore the transaction is evaluated against the instruction as the debit booking request is on the same account.

The transaction amount and Party Name satisfy the criteria in the stop instruction but the Party Identifier does not satisfy. However, as the first match type in the stop type ACH is based on the Amount and Party Name only and these are matched the transaction is rejected as the default reason for the Match Type is Return. An investigation item is raised in AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION application for the user to review the system decision.

> **⚠️ Note:** In cases where Accounting Mode mentioned in the AC.ENTRY.PARAM application is other than SNP, the Clearing Result field in AC.INWARD.ENTRY application is updated with SUSP. Error Message and Susp Reason field is updated in the same and a FUNDS.TRANSFER is generated in Hold status.

Consider that another booking request is posted with the posting rule LCLG.CSM=BOOK,OFS/I/PROCESS///,INPUTT/123456/GB0010001////,LCLG,01,10995,THEIRREF012,100,1,XYZ Company,XYZ12345

According to the setup, the transaction has qualified for stop check (transaction code is 1). The stop instruction on the Account 10995 is active and therefore the transaction is evaluated against the instruction as the debit booking request is on the same account.

The transaction Party Name does not match the criteria in the stop instruction, therefore the first match type (Amount and Party Identifier) in the stop type record is not satisfied.

The next match type is amount only, as the transaction amount satisfy the amount criteria this match type is met, therefore the conclusion is the stop instruction applies and the default decision is to pay. In this case, the transaction is posted and the investigation item is raised for the user to review the decision.

The AC.FUNDS.AUTHORISATION record shows the decision against the stop instruction was to pay.


##### Matching Type Rule defined in the Stop Type Record – Multiple Stop Instructions On Account

The following screenshot shows that another stop instruction is setup on Account 10995.

Using the setup in example 2, the following booking request is posted:

CSM=BOOK,OFS/I/PROCESS///,INPUTT/123456/GB0010001////,LCLG,01,10995,THEIRREF014,100,1,ABC Company,XYZ12345

The entry satisfies the first stop instruction for the Match Type Amount and Party Name and the decision is RETURN. The second instruction is also satisfied as the amount is matched and the decision is PAY.

The overall decision is the worst case scenario, which means when at least a default decision is to return the entry is rejected.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Set Up Transaction Stop

The Transaction Restrictions module allows the bank to define stop instructions for an account for a certain period of time, which is evaluated when a payment or booking request is processed on the debit account. This module provides an exception in the approval flow when the stop instruction is triggered on a transaction. The stop instructions can be defined using generic attributes such as cheque number, amount, party identifier and party name.


##### Workflow

In Transaction Stop check for Booking Requests, the user can perform the following activities:

| SCREENS | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
|  | Search Transaction stop Instructions . |
| Transaction Stop Instructions List | Click the Amend icon corresponding to a record. |
| Transaction Stop Instruction | Enter values in the fields which needs to be amended. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. |


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Transaction Stop Check for Booking Requests feature.

### 9.6  Transaction Stop As A Facility


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An AA activity is triggered when a stop instruction is created or amended on an arrangement. This enables the bank to use the AA framework to send a notification to the customer and apply charges when a stop instruction is created or amended, if required.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

An AA activity is triggered when a stop instruction is created or amended on an arrangement. This enables the bank to use the AA framework to send a notification to the customer and apply charges when a stop instruction is created or amended, if required.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

Through the Facility product condition, the bank can parameterise, the products for which setup or amendment of the stop instruction are opted in or opted out.

With this setup in place, when a new current account arrangement is created, the ‘Setup’ and ‘Amendment’ for the stop instruction is automatically opted in.

To support this setup, an event type record TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.INSTRUCTION.SERVICE in EB.EVENT.TYPE application is triggered when a stop instruction is created and subsequently amended.

Through TEC.ITEMS application, different AA activities are triggered when a stop instruction is created or amended. Through the Activity Mapping Product Condition, the bank can indicate which service these activities correspond to.

After a stop instruction is created or amended on the arrangement, the appropriate activity is triggered.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Transaction Stop as a Facility feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Transaction Stop as a Facility feature.

---


### 9.7  Transaction Stop Check for FundsTransfer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A sample FUNDS.TRANSFER,TZ.STOP.INPUT version is available for the implementation projects. An input routine attached to this version ensures the transaction stop check is triggered when the fund transfer is input.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Trans Instr*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A sample FUNDS.TRANSFER,TZ.STOP.INPUT version is available for the implementation projects. An input routine attached to this version ensures the transaction stop check is triggered when the fund transfer is input.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This is covered as part of module configuration. There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

To trigger the transaction stop check the fund transfer source is parameterised in the TZ.TRANSACTION.STOP.MAP.RULES. The following parameterisation record explains how this can be setup:

A FUNDS.TRANSFER transaction is initiated with the above version. An override is raised to indicate that the transaction matches the first stop instruction. The Stop Instructions against which the funds transfer has matched is stored in a local reference Trans Instr field along with the default decision.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Set Up Transaction Stop
- Set Up or Execute Inward Entries

The Transaction Restrictions module allows the bank to define stop instructions for an account for a certain period of time, which is evaluated when a payment or booking request is processed on the debit account. The stop instructions can be defined using generic attributes such as cheque number, amount, party identifier and party name.


##### Workflow

Transaction Stop Check is achieved using FUNDS.TRANSFER, TZ.STOP.INPUT version. When the funds transfer is inititated, an input routine attached to this version triggers transaction stop check.

| SCREEN | WORKFLOW |
|---|---|
|  | Transaction stop Investigation Items . |
| Transaction Stop Investigation Items | Enquiry displays the list of Transaction Stop Instruction records. Click the Amend Investigation Item icon corresponding to a record. |
| AC Funds Authorisation | Enter values in the fields which needs to be amended. Click the Validate icon. Click the Commit icon. |


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Transaction Stop Check for Funds Transfer feature.

## Appendix B: Consolidated Field Reference


This appendix consolidates all field description tables from across the documentation, grouped by sub-module. This provides a single reference for all field definitions.


### Accounts - AC (AC)


**AccountCreation**

| Possible Values | Description |
|---|---|
| B | Indicates non-contingent interest to be reported in balance sheet. The interest and charge liquidation account needs to be a non-contingent account, in order to report the interest or charge as a balance sheet item. |
| C | Indicates contingent interest, which must not appear on the Balance Sheet. The interest or charge liquidation accounts can also be contingent accounts. |
| O | Indicates non-contingent interest but reported as an off balance sheet item. |
| I | Indicates an internal contingent account, which is used to counterbalance contingent accounts. This must not appear on the balance sheet |

**AccountInterestandCharges**

| Field Name | Details | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| Debit Int Addon | This is an add-on charge levied on the overdraft (OD) interest on the interest capitalisation date. Either this or highest debit charge can be taken on the OD interest but not both | Configured in DEBIT.INT.ADDON application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Government Margin | This is a supplementary charge on debit balances calculated by the system on debit interest capitalisation date and collected on behalf of the Government | Defined in GOVERNMENT.MARGIN application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Highest Debit | This is a charge calculated on the highest debit balance during each capitalisation period | Defined in HIGHEST.DEBIT application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Interest Statement | Some customers require a detailed interest statement each time interest is applied. The interest statement charge is a fixed amount which may be applied each time debit interest is applied | Defined in INTEREST.STATEMENT application and the key is linked to the GENERAL.CHARGE application |
| Int Chg Bal Type; Int Chg Def Bal; Int Chg Ccy; Int Chg Bal | These fields are used to specify a balance for waiving Debit Interest Addon , Highest Debit and Interest Statement Charges fields If the balance is based on minimum or average balance for the interest period as defined in Int Chg Bal Type field If this balance is greater than the Int Chg Bal or Int Chg Def Bal , the above mentioned charges will be waived |  |
| Calcul Step Period | Specifies whether charges in Bal Requirement , Number Of Credit , Number Of Debit , Turnover Credit , Turnover Debit , Highest Debit Chg and Statement Charge should be calculated once to cover the full charge period, as specified in the COMPANY record, or in MONTHLY steps If MONTHLY is specified, free, minimum and maximum amounts apply to charges calculated for each month, otherwise the free, minimum and maximum amounts are only applied to the total charges for the period |  |
| Bal Requirement | Maintenance charge depending on the balance in the account | Defined in BALANCE.REQUIREMENT application |
| Number Of Credit; Number Of Debit; Turnover Debit; Turnover Credit | Transaction charges can be levied either based on the number of debit or credit transactions or the turnover value of the debit or credit transactions | The charge is defined in NUMBER.OF.CREDIT , NUMBER.OF.DEBIT , TURNOVER.DEBIT , TURNOVER.CREDIT applications respectively |
| Statement Charge | Determines the charges for the issuing account statements | Defined in ACCT.STATEMENT.CHARGE application |
| Trans Code Charge; Comb Trns Chrg Cde | One or more transactions in the TRANSACTION application can be made chargeable by defining a TRANSACTION.CHARGE in the TRANSACTION application and is applied using these fields | Defined in the TRANSACTION application |

**AccountLimits**

| Field Value | Description |
|---|---|
| Null or Working | The update of available funds ignores unauthorised credits. Overdraft checks use only working balance. Future cash flow check uses the available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date of the transaction. |
| Forward | Same as above, except that overdraft uses the value in the Working Bal field (in the ACCOUNT ) plus current bank day forward movements. |
| Available | The update of available funds uses the Available Bal Upd field (in the ACCOUNT ) to decide how the available balance is to be updated. There is no overdraft check. Future cash flow check uses available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date. |
| Availwork | The update of the available funds uses Available Bal Upd field (in the ACCOUNT ). The overdraft check uses Working Bal field (in the ACCOUNT ) only. Future cash flow checks use available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date. |
| Availfwd | The update of available funds uses Available Bal Upd field (in the ACCOUNT ). The overdraft check uses Working Bal field (in the ACCOUNT ) plus today's forward movements. Future cash flow check uses available balance ladder as from the value or exposure date. |
| Blank | If this field is left blank the Working option is applied. |

**AccountMaintenance**

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| Exposure Date | Indicates the date on which a credit entry is included in the cleared balance of an account |
| Value Date | Indicates the date from which the entry is included for calculation of interest. Where there is no exposure date on the transaction, the value date is used as the date when the transaction affects the available funds |
| Booking Date | Indicates the date on which the transaction has been processed |
| Available Funds window | Contains the available funds balances for all forward dated and value dated account movements up to the number of calendar days forward from current bank day as specified on Cash Flow Days field in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER |

**AccountMaintenance**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Available Date | Indicates the date on which there is a projected movement. |
| Av Auth Db Mvmt | Indicates authorised debit movement for the date. |
| Av Nau Db Mvmt | Indicates unauthorised debit movement for the date. |
| Av Auth Cr Mvmt | Indicates authorised credit movement for the date. |
| Av Nau Cr Mvmt | Indicates unauthorised Credit movement for the date. |
| Forward Mvmts | Indicates authorised forward movements for the date. |
| Available Bal | Indicates the available balance for the available date. |

**AccountMaintenance**

| Override message | Description |
|---|---|
| Available balance excess | Raised if an account is linked to a limit and an online debit transaction has caused the overdrawn available balance on value date of the transaction to exceed its limit. |
| Available balance overdraft | Raised if an account is neither linked to a limit nor to a shared balance pool and if an online debit transaction causes the available balance to be negative as of the value date of the transaction. |
| Available balance limit excess | Raised if an account is linked to a limit and the available balances of all the accounts in limit falls below the limit amount. |
| Available balance limit expired | Raised if an account is linked to a limit and the transaction falls beyond the expiry date of the limit. |
| Available balance below locked amount | Raised if an account’s balance that has an AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record falls below the level of the locked amount. |

**AccountStatements**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| File | Indicates the file from which information is to be extracted to form the narrative. |
| Text Data | Indicates the element of text, or field whose content is to form part of the narrative that is defined. |
| Format | Indicates the special formatting to be applied to fields extracted from the specified file. |

**ACFA**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Update Activation File | This field is used to decide if the internal activation file must be updated or an external event must be emitted when the AC.FUNDS.AUTHOIRISATION record is authorised. It holds the following values: If set to Yes, the system updates the activation file with the status of the funds authorisation request. If set to No, the system does not update the activation file with the status of the funds authorisation request. If set to External, the system updates the IF.EVENTS.INTERFACE.TABLE application and an Integration Framework event is created. If set to BusinessEvent, a first-class business event is emitted. |
| Dda Funds Check | This field checks if ACFA performs the funds check when the record is committed. For example, when an ACFA record is created as an investigation item for transaction stop, the funds check is not required. |
| Allowed Funds Decision | This field decides if the funds authorisation request is to be manually approved and/or sent to the Recycler. For example, the funds authorisation requests for insufficient funds and/or posting restricts are normally sent to the Recycler, but those for transaction stop are manually reviewed by the bank staff. |
| Allowed Reservation | This field defines if funds are automatically locked on the account when an ACFA record is approved. When an ACFA record is created as an investigation item for the bank staff to review transaction stop or non-sufficient fund (NSF) decisions, it should not reserve funds. |
| Allow Approval Code | This field defines if the respective ACFA type can be manually authorised or authorised by the Recycler. |

**HVT Processing**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Deferred Balance Update | Switches the deferred balance updates on or off for the specific company or for all companies where ID is SYSTEM. |
| Deferred Ids To batch | Spcifies the number of pending deferred IDs to process in a transaction boundary. The default is 50. |
| Deferred Consolidate Ent | Specifies the AC.CONSOLIDATE.COND ID that is used to default the consolidation of statement entries if not defined for the account. |

**HVT Processing**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Deferred Balance Update | Switches the deferred balance updates on or off for the account. |

**HVT Processing**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Hvt No Lock | When set as ‘YES’, allows the debit transactions for HVT customer accounts to skip lock on ECB, provided a pre-reservation is created as part of the transaction. |
| Virtual Locked Time | Specifies the time in milliseconds until which the pre-reservation can be active in the system and can be considered during credit check. Any records that cross this time is deleted by a background service. Default time is 500 ms. |

**LockingFundsBlocked HeldAmounts**

| Field Value | Description |
|---|---|
| lock.funds.date | Indicates that only Active* debit reservations or debit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of an account. |
| credit.reserve.date | Indicates that only Active* credit reservations or credit-locked events are considered for calculating the available or usable balance of an account. |

**LockingFundsBlocked HeldAmounts**

| Field Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Account Link | If the user selects: Yes – Block is propagated to accounts. The propagation of funds reservation is related to the Parent Account and Linked Ac No fields in the ACCOUNT property. No – Funds are blocked only on a single account where the transaction is applied. |
| Check Notice | Allows the user to check any existing withdrawal notice request for the arrangement. |
| Expiry Type | Start of Day – Locked Amount is released at the next start of the day after the expiry date. Close of Business – Locked Amount is released on the expiry date before the close of business process. |

**Misc**

| Field Name | Usage |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash Flow Days | Specifies the number of calendar days forward for which the cash flow balances are to be maintained for the purpose of accounting overrides and cash flow processing. The number of days entered here determines the window period that cash flow balances are to be maintained on each account record. Each forward dated entry generated for an account impacts the cash flow balances, if the date of the entry falls within this period. If the number of days entered is 10, then any forward dated entry raised online that has the value date less than 10 calendar days from current date will update the accounts cash flow balances. If this update causes either a limit to be exceeded or an unauthorised overdraft to occur, then an override message appears on the transaction input. All entries raised online that fall outside the window do not update the account balances immediately and no override messages appear. But when their value dates fall within the window, the start of day process (SOD.CASH.FLOW) updates the account cash flow balances. If an exception occurs at this stage, then the CASH.FLOW.EXCEPTION table is updated to indicate this. If the value is not entered in this field, then only the nostro accounts have cash flow maintained and a default of 10 calendar days is used for this. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Value Dated Acctng | A switch to set value dated accounting as On or Off or Trade Dated General Ledger (TDGL). If a value dated accounting system is required, then this field must be set to Y. In trade dated accounting system, the cash based transactions update the customer’s account and the bank’s position on the date in which the transaction is processed in the system, irrespective of the value date assigned to the transaction. In value dated accounting system, the cash based transactions update the customer’s account and the bank’s position on the value date assigned to the transaction. It is held as off balance sheet until the value date. In TDGL accounting system, the cash based transactions update the customer’s account and the bank’s position on the value date assigned to the transaction. It is held under payable or receivable until the value date. Cash based transactions follow the accounting treatment based on this setup. However, the accounting treatment can be switched from one system to another and the system permits any of the following switch. Switching of Accounting System Treatment of cash based transactions can be switched from one system to another, any combination of the setup is possible. Original Accounting Setup Target Accounting Setup Trade dated Value dated Trade dated Trade dated GL Value dated Trade dated Value dated Trade dated GL Trade dated GL Trade dated Trade dated GL Value dated The new accounting system switch applies to new transactions only. The existing cash based transactions with a future date follows the setup applied when the transaction were raised. The Tdgl Details field in the STMT.ENTRY application holds the details of the accounting method followed for the transaction. Exceptions to the above is SEC.TRADE – Actual Settlement: If contract input is in existing setup and authorised in the modified setup, then the system follows the modified setup. | Original Accounting Setup | Target Accounting Setup | Trade dated | Value dated | Trade dated | Trade dated GL | Value dated | Trade dated | Value dated | Trade dated GL | Trade dated GL | Trade dated | Trade dated GL | Value dated |
| Original Accounting Setup | Target Accounting Setup |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Trade dated | Value dated |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Trade dated | Trade dated GL |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Value dated | Trade dated |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Value dated | Trade dated GL |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Trade dated GL | Trade dated |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Trade dated GL | Value dated |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Use Pay Receive | This field is used to flag the suspense processing at system Level, in the case of value dated or TDGL accounting setup. Under these accounting setup, the value of the transaction is suspended in a temporary account till the split value date is reached. The allowed values are : Yes – Suspended to GL accounts pay or receive as special entries and reported as on-balance sheet item in the general ledger (GL) report. No – This is the default setup where the suspense processing posts the entry to the internal suspense account. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Pay Rec Allwd | This field works in conjunction with Use Pay Receive . It is used when a customer wants to decide if payable or receivable are to be reported with account attributes or against underlying customer attributes based PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE application. Value in this field should be valid record ID of AC.DEFINE.PAY.RECV.ALLOWED application. This field is available at different levels such as System level, System Id (sub-system) level, Category level and System ID with Category level. In the AC.DEFINE.PAY.RECV.ALLOWED application, the users can create their own records using any of the following options in the Pay Recv Options field. The ID of the application record can be a meaningful alpha-numeric name. Broker – This option decides the customer to whom the payable or receivable is to be booked in the PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . If this option is set, the payable or receivable is booked against the third party customer (for example, broker) passed from the application. If this option is not set, the payable or receivable is booked against the customer passed in the original entry from the underlying application. Contract – If this option is selected, all the payables or receivables are reported under the PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . Customer – If the target account passed from the underlying application is a customer account and the Customer option is set, then the payables or receivables are reported under PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . Internal – This option works similar to Use Pay Recv set to Yes. If the entry is posted as an internal (suspense) account and the target account is passed from the application, then the original STMT entry to internal (suspense) account is converted to special entry with asset type as PAYSUS or RECEIVESUS. Nostro – If the target account passed from the underlying application is a NOSTRO account, and the Customer option is set, then the payables or receivables are reported under PR.CUSTOMER.BALANCE . NULL – If no option is set, then the system continues to work as usual. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Val Date Sys Id; Val Date By Sys ; Use Pay Rec Sys | Enables the definition of accounting treatment for specific cash-based applications, where it is different from the default accounting treatment. If the default accounting system is trade dated, for the application mentioned in Val Date Sys Id , a different accounting system can be defined. For example, if SEC.TRADE is to follow TDGL accounting system, the Val Date Sys Id is defined as SCTR and Val Date By Sys is defined as TDGL. The Use Pay Rec Sys field can be flagged as Yes or No, which is used in the suspense processing for the specific application. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Vd Cat Start; Vd Cat End; Val Date By Cat; Use Pay Rec Cat | Enables the definition of accounting treatment for specific category or range of categories, where it is different from the default accounting treatment and application specific (if defined) accounting treatment. The category level definition takes precedence over the system level and application level definition. The Use Pay Rec Cat field can be set to Yes or No, which is used in the suspense processing for the specific category. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Vd Cat Sys Id; Vd Cat Sys Start; Vd Cat Sys End; Val Date By Cat Sys; Use Pay Receive Cat Sys | If the accounting system for specific categories of an application is different from the default accounting system, it can be setup using these set of fields. The application can be defined in Vd Cat Sys Id , the category or range of categories can be defined in the Vd Cat Sys Start and Vd Cat Sys End fields. The accounting system applicable to this setup are defined in the Val Date By Cat Sys field. The Use Pay Receive Cat Sys field can be set to Yes or No, which is used in the suspense processing for the specific category. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Entry Category; Sus Category; Suspense Txn In; Suspense Txn Out; Suspense History | The format of Entry Category can either be CATEGORY-FX.POS.TYPE or CATEGORY, which determines the suspense account to be used when operating in a value dated accounting system. If the position type for the Entry Category does not exist, then the entry category alone is used to determine the suspense category. Else, the default suspense category is used. When a split value dated transaction is processed in a value dated accounting system then the first leg is balanced against a suspense account. This is washed out when the second leg reaches its value date. The suspense account that is used is determined by the category of the second leg entry. The Entry Category field and its associated field Sus Category defines this relationship. Example XX.1 ENTRY.CATEGORY YY.1 SUS.CATEGORY 19998 XX.2 ENTRY.CATEGORY 5000-XX YY.2 SUS.CATEGORY 19999 Entry Category is a start of range value. Hence in this example, second leg entries with a category in the range 0 - 4999 uses account LCL199980001 (where LCL is the local currency code) and entries with a category 5000 and above uses LCL199990001 for suspense processing. To define a default suspense account for all the entries, configure as shown below: XX.1 ENTRY.CATEGORY YY.1 SUS.CATEGORY 19998 The purpose of defining different suspense category is to allow the splitting of suspense movements, for value dated accounting, within the CRB. For example, it is possible to report suspense entries for nostro accounts separately from suspense entries for current accounts. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sys Code; Nostro Default; Def Override; Use First Acct; Default Order | These set of fields are used for defaulting the settlement nostro account applicable to the transaction defined in the Sys Code field. The Sys Code field is a combination of Application-Nature of transaction, for example, LD-PRIN or LD-INT. These values must be defined upfront in AC.SYS.CODES application. The Nostro Default field is used to specify how settlement accounts are defaulted when using a nostro account for the associated Sys Code . A null value implies that the nostro account is always defaulted. The following are the options in this field: AGENCY – Defaults only when agency conditions exist. NONE – No nostro account is to be defaulted. The Def Override field defines whether an override is required when the default account number does not match the account number entered on the deal. Additionally, if the account with bank, intermediary bank or beneficiary account number differs from the default derived from the information on the agency file, then an override is raised if this field is set to Yes. The Use First Acct field defines whether an account is to be defaulted when more than one possible default account exists. The following options are available in this field: Yes – First account of the customer in any company is defaulted. No – If more than one account is present in the current company, then no defaulting takes place. In a multi-book setup, the following additional options are available for this field: CUR – First account of the customer in current company is only defaulted. FRS – First account of the customer in the current company as first choice followed by first available account in any company is defaulted. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Cheque Register; Chq Dep Txn; Def Coll Susp; Chq Col Txn; Chq Ret Txn; Def Ret Susp; Return Txns; Return Susp Cat | The Cheque Register field indicates whether or not the cheque issue and management functionality within Temenos Transact has been activated. The Yes or No value entered in this field controls the defaulting of cheque type in DATA CAPTURE (DC) or FUNDS TRANSFER (FT) or TELLER (TT) application as well as payment stop processing. The list of transaction code for cheque on collection, clearing and returned cheque and the corresponding suspense accounts where the value of cheque needs to be parked in the clearing process can be defined in these set of fields. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Net Od Appl; Net Od Override; Net Locked Override | The Net Od Appl field specifies the Temenos Transact application for which debit and credit entries to an account in a transaction must be netted for displaying the overdraft and cash flow overrides. The allowed applications are LOANS AND DEPOSITS (LD), TELLER (TT), COLLATERAL (CO), FUNDS TRANSFER (FT), ARRANGEMENT ARCHITECTURE (AA) or ALL. When this field is set to ALL, the functionality is applied for all transaction irrespective of the application. The pre-condition for the suppression of overrides is to set the Net Od Override field as Yes. If Net Od Appl holds the value ALL, the system does not permit any other multi-value to be input. Either applications are manually input in a multi-value block or ALL value is used. For example, if the Net Od Appl field is set to ALL and the Net Od Override field is set to Yes and a transaction is made using the same account as both debit and credit account, no override is generated for any excess amount. Suppression of Unnecessary Overrides: If a single contract creates both credits and debits to an account, if the net effect of the contract is to credit the account, it is possible to suppress the override generated for the debit side of the transaction. Example If a discounted loan is arranged for a customer, whereby the customer has a balance of £10, receives a credit of $1000 for the loan, but also a debit of $100 for the upfront payment of interest. The system usually generates an override specifying that the customer is debited $100 and the customer is being overdrawn by $90. However, it is possible by configuring the Net Od Appl as LD and Net Od Override fields as Yes in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER to net off the differences, so as the credit of $1000 exceeds the debit of $100 and the override is suppressed. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Retain Ac Balances | Defines whether balances need to be maintained in ACCOUNT or not. When set to Yes the balances are updated in ACCOUNT and EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES . When set to N the balances are not updated in ACCOUNT , but updated only in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES . Default value is Yes. Changing this setup from Yes to No clears the existing account balances automatically. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Booked Balance | Defines which booked balance is recorded in the STMT.ENTRY record when the transaction is booked. The following are the options available in this field. Online Actual Bal – Records the account balance from the GL perspective, this means that future dated movements are not included. Traded Dated Gl Bal – Records the account balance from a customer perspective, which means that future dated movements recorded as PAY or RECEIVE are included. The enhanced transaction search uses the value in this field to display the output in Booked Balance column of the enquiries |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | ACCOUNT.PARAMETER | It has the information pertaining to cash flow, accounting method, generation of alternate identifier to account number, account level balance maintenance, netting and cheque issue management and so on. |
| 2. | CUSTOMER | To create a user account, the account holder should be registered as a customer in Temenos Transact . The information like name, address, age, residence, sector, language, industry, signature and so on, pertaining to the user is captured in the application. |
| 3. | CATEGORY | Based on the business needs, category codes defined in Temenos Transact has to classify financial transactions. Use of the codes together with personal customer characteristics enables the bank to produce balance sheets and returns reflecting a coordinated and structured view of its operation, by directing business transactions to their appropriate report. |
| 4. | CURRENCY | It allows the user to capture the operating currency of the account and it should be a record or value in the currency application. Account currency cannot be changed once the account is authorised as the balances are maintained in the currency. |
| 5. | ACCT.GEN.CONDITION | It allows the user to define the grouping condition for accounts for which the same conditions of interests and charges apply. Based on the business needs, category codes along with CUSTOMER attributes like Sector and Residence enable grouping of accounts. These attributes and their order of priority is defined in CONDITION.PRIORITY application for ACCOUNT record. |
| 6. | ACCT.GROUP.CONDITION | It allows the user to define the rules for accounts belonging to a group and specific currency mentioned in the table. Some examples for rules defined are Notice withdrawals, account violations, deferring interest and charges, rounding rules for interest and premium interest, automatic IBAN generation and so on. |
| 7. | ACCOUNT.DEBIT.INT | It allows the user to define special debit interest conditions when the corresponding group interest conditions are not suitable. The user can define Interest to be calculated on daily, average using value dated balance and interest rate to fixed or linked to basic rates. |
| 8. | ACCOUNT.CREDIT.INT | It allows the user to define special credit interest conditions when the corresponding group credit interest conditions are not suitable. Credit interest rates can be specified for different balance levels. Rates can apply to the entire balance or a part between the two-balance levels. |
| 9. | ACCT.CAPITALISATION | It allows the user to specify the next date and subsequent frequency of application of debit and credit interest capitalisation for a specific account. |
| 10. | GROUP.DEBIT.INT | It allows the user to specify the calculation method of debit interest for a group of accounts and provides the link to the GENERAL.CHARGE , where the charges applicable to the same groups of accounts are specified. The user can also specify negative interest and tax on interest. |
| 11. | GROUP.CREDIT.INT | It allows the user to specify the calculation method of credit interest for groups of accounts. The user can also specify second interest on the account with different capitalisation frequency. |
| 12. | GROUP.CAPITALISATION | It allows the user to specify the next date and subsequent frequency of application of debit and credit interest capitalisation for a group of accounts. |
| 13. | ACCOUNT.CLASS | It allows the user to define the account class records, which can be used by other Temenos Transact applications to construct account number or to check the account number for a particular group. |
| 14. | ACCOUNT.ACCRUAL | At company level, it provides the system with information on how and when to process accruals of interests and charges on customer accounts. Accrual process can be specified at Account Category and Account Group for which the associated interest accrual parameters are defined. |
| 15. | SAVINGS.PREMIUM | It enables the user to pay premium on the savings deposits if the savings account qualify the eligibility criteria defined in this table. |
| 16. | AC.FUNDS.DIVERSION.PARAM | The funds diversion is setup from the off-balance sheet Transaction Account to the on-balance sheet Diversion Account. The system provides flexible options that allows the bank to control the ability to suppress the funds diversion processing for specific transactions for Transaction accounts setup for funds diversion. The bank will be able to define the following options for funds diversion: The default funds diversion behaviour. To suppress Funds Diversion processing for specific activities by mentioning or defining the associated transactions code as an exception to the default rule. |
| 17. | ACSWIT.PARAMETER | This parameter table stores the validity period decided by the bank for the switch out service. The validity period can be defined in days or months. The ID of this record represents the Temenos Transact Company ID. |
| 18. | DDA.SERVICE.PARAMETER | This table helps the bank to decide whether the payment made by the account holder in a specific currency is allowed or not. Also, enables the Bank to change the core decision for Account Currency and to return the Payment Currency. |
| 19. | AC.ACCOUNTING.PARAM | This table helps to parameterise the accounting related processes based on the Max No Of Splits defined. |
